### 0.208 — v2.109-S220: command decisions, run / surrender / self-destruct (2026-11-18)
Owner (Chandley vs D-7 M, log 2026-11-18-21-23-58; won by total power failure and liked the adrift look): a crippled AI ship with no weapons kept "fighting"; wanted surrender, run-for-it, self-destruct for AI and player, dialogue boxes in faction voice, ending stories, ally awareness, difficulty and faction temper, and "are you sure" checks on the player's side.
- Code block "COMMAND DECISIONS" (all `cs*` functions) sits just before the opening-scene code. Hooks: `proceedFromPower` (calls `csAiDecide(cb)` BEFORE `aiAllocatePower`), `aiAllocatePower` (a runner / boom-armed ship puts its power in movement, weapons 0), `aiDoMove` (boom ship steers at the player via `csBoomApproach`), `advanceFromMove` (`csBoomCheck`), `checkVictory` (self-destruct ending panel), `scnFieldExit` (`csRunPara`), `buildDebrief` (`csDebriefLines`), `scnAiWantsOut` (now just `s._aiRun && sensors>0`).
- Assessment `csAssess(s)`: `csValue` = working weapons' firepower x hull x power; side ratio = own side (this ship + `GS.enemyAllies`) / other side (`GS.player` + `GS.playerAllies`). FLEET HOOKS: a future fleet mode only has to fill those two arrays. Triggers: nogun (no usable weapon, ratio<0.6), power, hull (both ratio<0.8), odds (ratio below the tier's limit AND the ship is hurt AND turn>=2, so nobody yields before a shot). Thresholds per tier in `CS_HULL/CS_POW/CS_ODDS`.
- Choice `csChoose`: weights by faction (`CS_FAC`: Fed/Ori yield, Kli/Rom scuttle, Gorn mixed) and tier (<=Ensign: run x2, scuttle x0.15; Captain: scuttle x1.5; Admiral x2; Legend x2.5, yield down). Run needs the Warp Out option and sensors; yield needs no scenario and the 2-turn cooldown after a refusal; boom needs power>=6 and no scenario. Scenarios keep only the old run (now at every tier).
- Boom: armed state `s._aiBoom`; it closes on the player and detonates when range <= `CS_BOOMRANGE[tier]` (4,4,3,2,1,1), or hull <=10%, or after 4 turns within range+2. Tiers 1-4 announce it with a hail; 5-6 are silent. Blast = the rulebook table via `calculateExplosionDamage` and `applyExplosionDamage` (works with Ship Explosions OFF too); recorded in `GS.blasts` (selfDestruct:true) and `GS.selfDestruct`.
- Player: sidebar button COMMAND (`csOpenCommand`): Demand Surrender (1 confirm, once per turn; the AI answers through `csChoose(.., demand)` only if it has a trigger), Make a Run (hint, needs Warp Out), Strike Colours and Self-Destruct (3 confirms: Are you sure / REALLY sure / REALLY, REALLY sure; NO is the default button and YES unlocks after ~1 s). Not offered in scenarios.
- Endings: `csEndYield`, `csShowEndPanel`, stories `csYieldStory`, `csBoomEnd`, run paragraph. Debrief: "Command:" lines.
- Tests: pt12.js (decision spread over tiers/factions), pt13.js (yield flow, command modal, triple confirm self-destruct, AI boom, allies, demand refusal).
- v2.110-S221 (owner chose option 2): a runner (`_aiRun`) with a cloak cloaks on purpose (p 0.85) only if `tot - cloakCost >= max(12, 0.6*tot)`; a cloaked runner decloaks when that no longer holds. Before this the old hurt-ship cloak odds ran independently of the run order. Test pt15.js.
- Not built / ideas: fleet mode itself; AI ending the fight when its OWN side is winning is unchanged; the surrendered ship is not shown "captured" on the map.

### 0.200 — v2.101-S212: end-of-battle stories now read the battle (2026-11-15)
Owner's play of v2.100: (a) warp-out test (log 14-39-16): ran flat out, took no damage, fired no shot, got a story that did not say so; (b) D-18C Gull win (log 14-44-14): Constitution took 12 hits on a live forward shield and lost one beam bank and 4 hull boxes, and the story did not mention the shields. Owner's rule, for ALL encounters: the ending must be told from the context of how the battle went (a quick undamaged escape is a different story from a long fight with a mauled ship).
Built: `endFacts()` (turns, shots fired and landed per side, hull % per side, systems lost per side from `GS.dmgLog`, closest range from `GS.debrief.snaps`, first damage, no-shots flag, and `ship._absorbed` = shield points that turned fire aside, now tracked at the four shield-absorption sites), `endLead(F)` (how the fight went), `endCost(F,winnerIsPlayer)` (what the winner paid: untouched / hits all turned aside / hull and systems lost, plus a "shields saved her" remark at >= 8 absorbed points), `fledStory(F,leaverIsPlayer)` (Free Battle warp-out: no shots; intact after a fight; hull >= 60%; 30-60%; under 30%). Used by: warp-out (`scnFieldExit`), destroyed win/loss (lead + the old killing-blow paragraph + cost), power failure (lead + the old preamble + cost + the old fate paragraph; `buildPowerKillNarrative` takes a 3rd argument), mutual destruction (lead + blast/kill text). The Big Bad Wolf's `scnNarrative` keeps its three-part form and gains: a warp-out with no shots, or an untouched ship, is told differently (both directions); the "fight" section no longer says "landed 0 of 0" when nothing was fired; a "deflectors stopped N points" line on a won fight.
Not done: the old text blocks (`buildKillNarrative`, `buildPowerKillNarrative` fates, `buildStressNarrative`) are unchanged and do not know the context themselves; the new lead and cost paragraphs carry it. Possible next: weave the facts into those blocks, add a Cadet/Ensign-friendly "what to try" line. Explosion note from the Gull log: the Gull went to 0 superstructure with 2 points below zero, the explosion roll was 10 (blows on 2 or less), so it held together: no blast. The explosion roll works as designed.
Tests (Playwright, real game, synthetic states): warp-out with no shots (turn 3), warp-out at 5 of 20 hull, a kill with 34 absorbed points, a power-failure surrender with no hits taken, a mutual blast, and the scenario warp-out with no shots. Please play it and tell me which stories read well and which do not.

### 0.198 — v2.99-S210: AI evasion safety, cloaked AI keeps moving, Warp Out option, Ship Explosions option (2026-11-15)
Owner's play of Reliant (Reliant Mk II) vs IKS Devisor (D-7 S), combat log 2026-11-14-17-53-20 (Lt. Cmdr per the debrief). NOT yet added to the combat log ledger (standing rule 2): do it next session. Owner feedback: the Klingon kept trying to evade at 2/22 and 1/22 superstructure (5 tries, 0 worked, each failure cost 1 stress), and sat still while cloaked (Move 0, Shields 24, Weapons 0 every turn). Owner's four requests, all built:
1. **AI Evasive Maneuvers safety gate** (`aiEvadeChoice`): from Ensign (D2) up, the AI never tries a dodge when superstructure <= 1 (a failed try costs 1 and would take it to zero); it keeps its shots. Cadet never dodges anyway. NOTE: the owner asked for "all difficulties except the lowest"; the lowest (Cadet, D1) already never evades.
2. **Cloaked AI keeps moving** (`aiAllocatePower`, after the overspend trim): while cloaking, Captain (D4) gets at least 60% of its post-upkeep power as Move, Admiral (D5) 85%; Legend (D6) was already all-Move. Lt. Cmdr and below unchanged. Cause of the old behaviour: shields were sized first (Lt. Cmdr: fixed 12) and ate the budget after the cloak upkeep. Movement points are still small because of the engine move ratio (a D-7 at 34 power, cloak 22, gets 12 spare: Move 8 = 1/1/0 points). The exploit layer (`aiPlanExploit`) already steers when the player is not cloaked. Open idea: choose WHEN to cloak by position, and decloak when losing (not built).
3. **Warp Out at the Map Edge** (new setup switch `warpout`, off by default; works in Free Battle; a scenario with `fieldExit:true` forces it on, and the setup panel shows it locked). `fieldExitOn()` = scenario flag, or (no scenario and `GS.rules.warpout`). Stepping off the edge opens the existing confirm window, reworded: "WARP OUT AND LEAVE THE BATTLE? ... Do you really want to do this?" with NO and YES buttons. Leaving = defeat for the leaver (victory for the other). The AI may run for the edge (`scnAiFlee`, Ensign and up, hull <= 30% or power <= 35% and worse off than the player), now also in Free Battle. A ship with sensors at 0% cannot warp out (rulebook: dead sensors, no warp), for both sides. `scnFieldExit` works with or without a scenario (own free-battle text). Click-to-move never offers off-map hexes: only the step buttons trigger it.
4. **Ship Explosions** (new switch `explosions`, Intermediate rules only, off by default; tooltip text in HOUSE_RULES). Before this the blast math (`calculateExplosionDamage`, `applyExplosionDamage`, the book's table) existed but was never called. Now: every superstructure loss goes through `ssLose()`, which records overkill (`ship._ssOver`); `resolveShipExplosions()` runs at the top of `checkVictory()`: a destroyed ship with overkill rolls d10 (explodes on a roll <= overkill; 10+ always; overkill 0 = no roll), worst-damaged first; a blast that kills the other ship gives it its own roll (up to 3 passes). Blast damage uses the exploder's `currentPower` and the rulebook range table, to the facing shield (same hex: split over all six). Both ships dead = MUTUAL DESTRUCTION with its own narrative (`buildBlastNarrative`, `GS.blastKill`). NOT built: deliberate SELF-DESTRUCT (the book's other cause), and a debrief line for explosions.

(2) A Scenario card at the top of the setup screen: drop-down (Free Battle default, then "★ The Big Bad Wolf"), side buttons, and a briefing (background, set-up, locked settings, both ships with power/hull/weapons/CE and a balance line, victory conditions, the book's notes). (4) `launchGame`: start hexes from the scenario: Hood at column 0, row 9 facing 0 (east), D-7M at column 23, row 9 facing 3 (west). **Facing note found while building:** `HEX_DIRS` and the sprite rotation make facing 0 = East; the free-battle start (facings 1 and 4) is therefore slightly diagonal (south-east / north-west). The scenario uses true east/west so the two ships head dead at each other (both start hexes are on odd row 9, same screen y). The free-battle start was NOT changed. `GS.scenario` ({id,name,fieldExit,playerSide}) is set; the header shows the scenario name; the log opens with a SCENARIO line. (5) "Driven from the field": in a `fieldExit` scenario `playerStep` off the map opens a confirmation (`scnConfirmExit`); LEAVE ends the battle (`scnFieldExit('player')`, DEFEAT); a log warning appears on an edge hex. Click-to-move still stays on the map (use ↑/↓). Free Battle still says "Cannot move: map edge". (6) AI side: `scnAiFlee` (called at the top of `aiDoMove`): difficulty 2 and up, hull at or below 30% or power at or below 35%, and worse off than the player: it runs for the nearest edge (nudged away from the player) and `scnFieldExit('enemy')` gives the player VICTORY. (7) Endings: `checkVictory` appends a one-line scenario epilogue to the narrative and the scenario name to the subtitle (`scnEpilogue`).

### 0.190 — Joachim's extrapolated stat sheet received, to be used as the need arises (first use: the Mutara Nebula scenario) (documents only, nothing built, game still v2.94-S205)

**Owner's message (2026-11-11), pasting the sheet into the chat:** "here is Joachim's stats as far as you're concerned. Use these as the need arises. example: The Mutara Nebula scenario we will later be building." **Saved as `/mnt/user-data/outputs/reference/Joachim_FASA_RPG_Stats_Extrapolated.md`** (written from the pasted text: it was not an upload; to keep it in future sessions it must be added to the Project's files, with the Khan sheet). **Standing label wherever it is used or displayed: "extrapolated, NOT FASA canon", until the owner marks an option as canon.** The owner's name for the scenario is now "the Mutara Nebula scenario" (the earlier notes call it the Wrath of Khan scenario).
**The sheet.** Attributes STR 87, END 100, INT 97, DEX 97, CHA 78, LUC 54, PSI 56; To-Hit 92 (modern weapons) and 90 (hand-to-hand), 2D10+10 bare-hand damage (the flat bonus is a judgement call), 13 AP. Starship skills: **Starship Helm Operation 90**, **Starship Combat Strategy/Tactics 84**, Damage Control Procedures 78, **Starship Weaponry Operation 74**, Deflector Shield Operation 68, Warp Drive Technology 60, Starship Sensors 50, Communication Systems 30; also Planetary Survival 92, Marksmanship 86, Leadership 82, Unarmed 82, Shuttlecraft Pilot 76, Small Unit Tactics 72, Security 60 and others. The option label is "Upper range, Systems officer, near-peer".
**Checked.** The sheet's stated formulas (AP = DEX/10 rounded down + 4; To-Hit = (DEX + weapon skill)/2 rounded up) reproduce KHAN's printed numbers exactly (AP 13, Modern 49 with no Marksmanship, HTH 84 from Unarmed 69) and Joachim's own (AP 13, Modern 92 from Marksmanship 86, HTH 90 from Unarmed 82): the arithmetic is sound. The film quotes in its "film evidence" bullet were not checked here.
**How it plugs into the Command and Control skills (§0.188).** The Helmsman role uses Starship Helm Operation AND Ship's Weaponry Technology Operation: **Joachim as helmsman has 90 and 74** (a 90% and a 74% Skill Roll, against 60% for an average generated crewman and Khan's own 35 and 21: Khan cannot fly or shoot his ship, Joachim can, as the film shows). The Science Officer uses Deflector Shield Technology, Damage Control, Sensors and Communications: Joachim has 68, 78, 50 and 30; the Chief Engineer uses Warp Drive Technology and Astronautics: Joachim has 60 and none listed. **Design points for the Mutara scenario (not decided):** (1) **Joachim's Tactics 84 is higher than Khan's 59**: if the captain's Tactics (plus a die) decides the initiative, the choice of who sits in the captain's seat matters; the film has Khan in command. (2) **In the film Joachim covers several stations at once** (the helm, the shields, the phasers, the damage report): the book gives each role to a different person, so letting one character hold two or three seats would be a scenario rule to design (for example a penalty for double-hatting, or the Reliant being short-handed). (3) With **no shields** in the scenario, his Deflector Shield 68 is moot, but his Damage Control 78 and Warp Drive 60 matter for repairing the half-power damage during the fight. (4) Joachim dies in the film (a collapsed bulkhead in the Enterprise's attack): a bridge hit could be the trigger for a casualty and the loss of his seat, which fits the Graduate bridge-hit and casualty rules.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Verify a supplied sheet's arithmetic against its own source numbers before using it. (2) A pasted sheet is not a file: save it where the project can find it, and say so.

**A Scenarios section: what it would take (from the code).** *What already helps:* the setup screen is built from cards (`sc-card`, ids `card-ruleset`, `card-terrain`) with room for a new "Scenario" card; `launchGame()` (about line 2842) already places the player at column 4, row 9 facing east and the enemy at column 19, row 9 facing west (flipped for a Klingon or Romulan player), close to the Big Bad Wolf set-up ("the centre of opposite short sides, heading straight at each other"); the map is 24 columns by 18 rows (`COLS=24, ROWS=18`, so the short sides are the left and right edges); the registry has the book's Basic ships: `Constitution` (for the Hood) and `D7_M`; the Basic ruleset exists. *What is missing:* (1) a `SCENARIOS` data table (id, name, the course it needs, background, ships and sides, start hexes and facings, speed, map and terrain conditions, victory conditions, notes) and `GS.scenario`; (2) the dropdown and a briefing panel (background, ships, which side you play, map, win conditions, the book's notes), with "Free battle" as the default; choosing a scenario would force the ruleset and the terrain options and fix the ships (the difficulty and the side stay free); (3) start positions from the scenario instead of the fixed ones (at the edge centres: column 0 and 23, row 9); (4) **"driven from the field"**: the game stops a ship at the map edge ("Cannot move: map edge", `inBounds` in about seven places), whereas the Basic rule re-centres the counters UNLESS the scenario makes leaving part of the victory conditions (rulebook lines 1496-1501), which The Big Bad Wolf does ("driven from the field"): so a scenario flag that lets a ship leave (with a confirmation) and a victory check that counts it (the AI never leaves because it uses `inBounds`); (5) the scenario's name in the log, the end screen and the debrief, and a scenario ending ("the convoy escapes"); (6) tests (the dropdown and the briefing, the forced settings, the start hexes, victory by destruction and by leaving for each side) and the regressions. **Resolved by the owner (2026-11-11): combat IS sub-light; warping out is only a captain's way of quitting a scenario; no movement mechanics change** (so nothing to verify there). Suggested phases: A the selector, briefing, forced settings, start positions and the name in the log; B leaving the map as a victory; C the scenario ending and debrief; later each scenario tagged with the course it needs and shown locked until that course exists (the Wrath of Khan: Graduate; the Kobayashi Maru: Command and Control).
**The new thread's handover and readme.** The owner's instinct is right: this HANDOVER now has about 190 numbered sections (every build and every answer), too long to read at the start of a thread. Proposed: a short "START HERE" handover (the owner's way of working and the standing rules; the current build and what is open; where everything is and how to run the tests; the roadmap and the decisions waiting; where the history lives) with this long file kept as the archive and a section index, plus a README refresh that adds the Scenarios section when it exists. Not yet written: awaiting the owner's go-ahead on when.
**Harness lessons.** (1) When the owner doubts a claim in a source file ("no one published stats"), check the web before agreeing, and report what was found and what was not. (2) Read the launch and movement code before estimating a feature: the default start positions and the two Basic ships already exist, but the map edge blocks the very thing the scenario's victory needs. (3) Say plainly when a candidate is a guess.

### 0.188 — Reference received: Khan Noonien Singh's FASA RPG stat sheet, kept for the scenarios and the Graduate and Command and Control work (documents only, nothing built, game still v2.94-S205)

**Owner's message (2026-11-11):** "for later use, (scenarios and graduate level applications) I'm including the MD for the kahn character using the FASA RPG stats." File: `Khan_Noonien_Singh_FASA_RPG_Stats.md` (copied to `/mnt/user-data/outputs/reference/`; **to have it in future sessions it must also be added to the Project's files: uploads last only for the conversation**). Source named in the file: FASA 2214, *Star Trek III Sourcebook Update* (1984), Star Fleet Personnel File, printed p.34, read from the page image (not OCR); the boxset entry has a shorter skill list.
**What the sheet gives.** Attributes STR 91, END 104 (above the 100 cap on purpose), INT 96, DEX 98, CHA 99, LUC 56, PSI 62; To-Hit 49 (modern weapons) and 84 (hand-to-hand), 2D10+11 damage, 13 AP; skills (percentile): Leadership 98, Planetary Survival 99, Psychology (human) 84, Terran Law 72, Administration 71, Unarmed 69, Negotiation 67, **Starship Combat Strategy/Tactics 59**, Environmental Suit 53, Political Science 52, Computer 42, Transporter 41, **Starship Helm Operation 35**, Communication Systems 24, **Starship Weaponry Operation 21**, **Deflector Shield Operation 11**. The file's own caveats: only "significant" skills are listed; **Joachim has no stat block** in any of the three books (if needed, build him as a lesser Khan, 70s to 80s, and label him an invention).
**How it plugs into the rulebook (checked against the Command and Control text, PDF p.41-44).** The course says it lets players of the RPG "reenact starship combats using the fully-developed characters from that game". The four roles use these skills: Captain: Starship Combat Strategy/Tactics; Chief Engineer: Warp Drive Technology and Astronautics; Helmsman: Starship Helm Operation and Ship's Weaponry Technology Operation; Science Officer/Navigator: Deflector Shield Technology, Damage Control Procedures, Starship Sensors, Starship Communications Procedures. Generated crews get each rating as three dice plus 45 (48 to 75, average 60). **So Khan as CAPTAIN has Tactics 59: an average captain by the book's own scale (60), and as I read lines 4588-4594 that rating (plus a die against the opposing captain's) decides the initiative, so only Kirk's number is needed to settle who moves last.** His Leadership 98 and Survival 99 are not used by the starship rules. His Helm 35 and Weaponry 21 would make him a poor helmsman or gunner (the file's note: Joachim flies the ship), and Deflector Shield 11 would make him a dreadful science officer, but shields are not allowed in the Khan scenario, so that one is moot. The names are close but not identical (RPG "Starship Weaponry Operation" and "Deflector Shield Operation", "Communication Systems Operation" against the book's "Ship's Weaponry Technology Operation", "Deflector Shield Technology", "Starship Communications Procedures"); the Chief Engineer's Warp Drive and Astronautics, Damage Control and Sensors are not on Khan's sheet (only significant skills are listed).
**Two facts in the file that support the owner's choices.** (1) The file gives the Reliant's data as superstructure 22, power 48, 4 x FH-10, 2 x FP-4, crew 336: **this is exactly the Reliant Mk I row in the FASA data** (`FASA_2302`: 22 / 48 / FH-10 x4 / FP-4 x2 / 336; the Mk II has 24 / 52 / FH-11 / 346): FASA's own sourcebook puts the Mk I in the film, as the owner chose. (2) The time line gives the events as RSD 2/2206.16 to 2/2206.20 (June 2222 by the project's conversion rule); the Enterprise "is crewed by Star Fleet Academy cadets on a training cruise": that suggests a LOW crew efficiency for the Enterprise in the scenario (and Khan's crew a mix of his own people and mind-controlled officers), which the Graduate and Command and Control rules can express. The file cites `FASA_2214_2216_DATA.md` §1.4 for the ship data; **that file is not in the project and was not seen**.
**For later (not decided).** Khan as a scenario persona for the AI (Tactics 59 as his captain's rating once the Command and Control skill rolls exist; an aggressive, predictable style); Joachim as an invented, labelled lesser Khan at the helm; Kirk, Spock, Scott and Saavik sheets would be needed for the Enterprise side if the owner has them; whether the scenario's crews use generated ratings or these named characters.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Check a supplied sheet against the rule that will use it (the Command and Control skill list) before saying how it plugs in: the names differ slightly. (2) A supplied document can confirm an earlier choice independently (the Reliant Mk I data): cross-check the numbers against the data file.

### 0.187 — Wrath of Khan scenario, second round: the ships (Enterprise Mk I against Reliant Mk I), starting at half power, and the order of work (discussion only, nothing built, game still v2.94-S205)

**Owner's reply (2026-11-11):** "the enterprise class mk I is the version of the enterprise in this scenario. The reliant is a mk I. I was thinking of taking away some power for the ships to simulate the fact they've damaged each other previously. I think going into the game each ship should be at half power. And the "damage" would be shown in the damage control panel and the corresponding visual effects being displayed as well. All these scenarios I think need to be available once we get the graduate section done as there's RPG elements that would best leveraged."
**Correction of Claude's earlier assumption (§0.186).** The first balance numbers used the CONSTITUTION class marks. The game (and FASA) has a SEPARATE "Enterprise class (movie-era refit)" (keys `Enterprise_MkI/II/III`, TMP era, Mk I `2/1704` = April 2217; the Constitution Mk I `1/8801` is a Four Years War ship with lasers and accelerator cannons, CE 801). **The owner's ship is the Enterprise class Mk I, which is playable.** **The Reliant Mk I (FASA `2/1507`, July 2215) is in the FASA data and the catalogue but is NOT playable: the game's registry has only `Reliant_MkII`;** adding it is a data job (a registry entry, `SHIP_CE`, `SHIP_ERA` (TOS by the project's date rule, since before 2217), the existing Reliant sprite).
**The two ships (from `FASA_2302_Federation_Ships_DATA.md` and the game's `shipRating`).** *Enterprise Mk I:* superstructure 26, crew 412, total power 60 (two warp engines of 26 + impulse 8), MPR 4:1, shields FSP max 16, beams FH-11 x6 in 3 banks (max 10 each), torpedoes FP-4 x2 (forward, damage 20), D 145.2, WDF 89.2, CE 12,952. *Reliant Mk I:* superstructure 22, crew 336, total power 48 (two warp engines of 20 + impulse 8), MPR 4:1, shields FSL max 14, beams FH-10 x4 in 2 banks (max 7), torpedoes FP-4 x2 (one forward, one aft, damage 20), D 105, WDF 63.8, CE 6,699. **The Enterprise rates about 1.9 : 1 over the Reliant Mk I (1.7 : 1 over the Mk II, 1.68 : 1 over the Mk III): the book's own ratings favour the ENTERPRISE, which is true to the film (a bigger ship, beaten by surprise and cunning), not the Reliant.** With no shields the headline ratio overstates the gap (the shields are a large part of D): without them the difference is nearer the hull (26 against 22, about 1.2 x) and the weapons (about 1.4 x); this is an estimate and should be measured by playing.
**Half power.** Total power is the sum of the warp engines and the impulse engine, and the game already models engine damage as reduced total power ("Engine hit: total power reduced to 40"). So "half power" can be shown as pre-battle ENGINE DAMAGE in the Damage Control panel: Enterprise Mk I total 60 -> 30 (each warp engine 26 -> 11, impulse 8 kept), Reliant Mk I 48 -> 24 (each warp engine 20 -> 8, impulse 8 kept). With no shields, all that power goes to weapons and movement (MPR 4:1: 12 power is only 3 movement points), so the duel plays slow and tense, which suits a nebula crawl. Halving both leaves the Enterprise ahead (30 against 24 power and more weapons); a per-ship starting fraction (for example the Enterprise 50%, the Reliant 65-70%), or other damage (crew casualties, a damaged beam bank), would even it; only play-testing can confirm.
**Visual effects (what exists, what is missing).** The Damage Control tab already shows the engine tracks and a ship image with hover regions, and the map sprite takes a "damaged" look below 60% superstructure. Whether ENGINE-only damage shows anywhere on the map or in the viewscreen was not checked; likely it does not, so a visible engine effect (dimmed or flickering nacelle glow, sparks, a thin smoke trail) would be new work, as would showing casualties and damaged weapons once the Graduate Course exists. A pre-battle briefing screen listing each ship's condition would also help.
**The order of work (owner: the scenarios should wait for the Graduate Course).** Agreed in substance: the Graduate Course supplies what the Khan scenario leans on: the Slim Chance table (the nebula's "lots of missing"), the detailed damage tables, weapons repair (Oper, Dmgd, Repd, Inop), crew casualties and efficiency, the engineering hits (shield grid, weapons grid, maneuver converter), repair difficulty, and shots while evading; the Command and Control Course adds the roles and skills (a Chief Engineer making repairs mid-battle is the heart of the film). Suggested tiers, each scenario tagged with the minimum course it needs: The Big Bad Wolf (Basic), The Wrath of Khan (Graduate), The Kobayashi Maru (Command and Control, plus several ships per side); the scenario FRAMEWORK itself (fixed starts, rule flags, victory conditions, a starting damage state) is separate work and could come first, with the Big Bad Wolf as its test, if the owner agrees.
**Open for the owner:** the same starting fraction for both ships or a tuned one; adding the Reliant Mk I as a playable ship; whether the framework and the Big Bad Wolf may come before the Graduate Course.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Before comparing ships, check the class names in the data: "Enterprise class" is not "Constitution class", and an earlier answer of mine used the wrong one. (2) A claim like "the weaker ship is the Reliant" must come from the numbers, and the numbers say the Enterprise is the stronger. (3) Say plainly what was not checked (whether engine damage has a visual).

### 0.186 — Design thoughts on a "Wrath of Khan" scenario: Reliant against an Enterprise class in a map-filling nebula, no sensor locks, no shields (discussion only, nothing built, game still v2.94-S205)

**Owner's idea (2026-11-11):** a scenario of his own, "The Wrath of Khan": Reliant against an Enterprise class in a specific nebula that fills the entire map; no sensor locks allowed; no shields allowed; "in the movie, it's really difficult to get a lock, there's lots of missing, not until each ship can get close enough to physically see one another in the murky nebula." He asked for thoughts.
**Findings that shape the design.** (1) **In the book a sensor lock is NOT needed to fire.** Advanced Course, Sensors (PDF p.26): "Vessels are in sensor contact when they are on the Starfield Mapsheet at the same time. Vessels in sensor contact will know each other's basic position, heading, and speed. They can fire on one another." A lock only buys INFORMATION (class, race, whether shields are down, and one of nine questions per Sensors Phase about power, shields, weapons, damage); the book calls sensors "the only method of obtaining information other than by visual observation". So "no sensor locks" alone would remove only intelligence, not accuracy: the film's "lots of missing" needs a separate rule. (2) **The book has no nebula rule** (searched the whole text); the game's nebula is a house rule (`HOUSE_RULES` entry `nebula`, hr:true). Today: a shooter inside a nebula takes -1 to hit and a target inside takes -1 (`terrainToHitPenalty`, about line 5750), so two ships both inside get -2; the legend also says "Sensors -30%, no sensor lock for ships inside" (the enforcement was not re-checked here). The cloaking rule already shows the mechanism for a bigger penalty (+3 moving, +5 stationary subtracted from the chart number). (3) **The Graduate Slim Chance table** (§0.185) gives a modified to-hit of 0 or less a second roll (needs 1-8 at 0, 1-6 at -1, 1-4 at -2, 1-2 at -3), which would turn "lots of missing" into a graded, never-zero chance; it is not built. (4) **Balance with the game's own ratings** (`shipRating`): Reliant Mk II (XI) D 110.8, WDF 67.8, CE 7,512; Constitution Mk II D 83.6, WDF 43.6, CE 3,645 (ratio 0.49: the Reliant is about TWICE as strong); Constitution Mk III CE 5,245 (ratio 0.70); superstructure 24 against 20 (Mk II) or 22 (Mk III). By the book's own balancing method the sides are uneven, in the Reliant's favour; the book also says a scenario states "their state of repair".
**Design suggestions given (none decided).** *Making the shots miss:* a to-hit ladder by range through the nebula (full visibility only at about 1-2 hexes, a growing penalty beyond, ideally with the Slim Chance table so it never reaches zero), built on the existing terrain and cloak penalty; optionally, a fog: the enemy shown only as an unlocated contact until it is within visual range (about 3 hexes), a bigger build. *No shields:* a scenario flag that gives shields no power and no points, so every hit penetrates and rolls a damage location (very deadly at 20-24 superstructure); the power freed from shields should be considered (a cap). *No lock:* removes the nine intelligence questions and the identity information; the AI needs a persona for a blind fight (close the distance, hold fire beyond visual range). *Balance:* use the Constitution Mk III as the Enterprise, and/or a handicap on the Reliant (state of repair, crew efficiency, a damaged bank), or asymmetric victory conditions, or an AI "Khan" persona that is aggressive and predictable; the film's "two-dimensional thinking" cannot be modelled (the game is 2D). Evasive Maneuvers could be forced on (with no shields every missile hurts more). *What the game lacks:* a scenario framework (fixed starts, per-scenario rule flags, a nebula filling every hex, victory conditions, a scenario name in the log and debrief); Big Bad Wolf would be the cheap first test of it.
**Open for the owner:** how much "cannot see each other" he wants (the to-hit ladder only, or also the fog), which ships and what balance, and whether to start with the scenario framework.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Before designing a rule around a game term ("lock"), check what the term does in the book: here it carries information, not accuracy. (2) Use the game's own ratings to check a scenario's balance before promising the film's drama.

### 0.185 — The Graduate Course summarised from the rulebook (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.94-S205)

**User request (2026-11-11):** "go ahead and summarize the Graduate Courses as well. just so they're all in front of me." Read in full from the rulebook text: PDF pages 34-40 (lines 3554-4240). **The Graduate Course contains NO published scenario; it adds only rules** ("Only additions to the rules are included here"); its one scenario-related section is Defense Outposts. Its one major change: **detailed Damage Location Tables.**
**1. Emergency heading change stress (p.35).** Each emergency heading change automatically gives 1 point of damage to EACH warp engine (instead of the Advanced Course's single point), marked off the Warp Engine Power Tracks and the Total Power Units Available Track. Extra damage comes from the Emergency Heading Change Stress Chart: cross the current warp speed with the ship's own stress columns (one for the warp engines, one for the superstructure, given in the Ship Data Tables and at the top of the Damage Control Display); the higher the warp speed the more damage, and it differs by ship type.
**2. Evading missile fire and "Fire from ship's evading missiles" (p.35, p.38).** The evasion procedure is the Advanced Course's, BUT the evader may still make the shots he declared, at a penalty: after the To-Hit Number is found, subtract 2. As in the Advanced Course the ORIGINAL heading is used for incoming damage from every weapon except the missile being evaded, and it ALSO determines the firing arcs of the evader's own shots. The book says the rule is there "so that players may re-create such sequences shown in the TV series and the movies".
**3. Against Impossible Odds (p.35): the Slim Chance table.** When a To-Hit Number or a repair number is modified to 0 or less there is still a slim chance: roll as usual; only a roll of 1 allows a second roll, with the number needed from the table: modified 0 needs 1-8, -1 needs 1-6, -2 needs 1-4, -3 needs 1-2, -4 or worse no chance (the OCR garbles the minus signs; this is the reading that fits the pattern).
**4. New or changed weapons (p.36).** Lasers: fired as beams, but a laser given more than its Maximum Power (up to twice) may fire TWICE in two different Firing Phases, each shot at half the power (rounded down) plus modifiers; unfired second shots are lost; the only double-firing weapon. Accelerator cannons: missile fire, may be evaded (§0.183). Romulan plasma: may be powered to HALF the power for half the damage, a graze doing half the graze damage. Lasers and accelerator cannons belong to Four Years War scenarios and certain civilian vessels.
**5. Damage results (p.36-38).** Damage is figured as before, but the LOCATION comes from one of three Detailed Damage Location Tables: Table A for ships with warp engines forward, B amidships, C aft (each ship's table is in the Ship Data Tables and at the top of the Damage Control Display); six columns, one per shield side penetrated; one die is rolled for EVERY hit that penetrates, whatever the damage. Effects: SHIELD GENERATOR hit: all its points are lost for the rest of the turn, and it does not work until repaired (repair attempts from the next phase). BEAM hit: a beam that can bear on the shooter is damaged, the TARGET's captain chooses which; if none can bear, half the damage goes to the superstructure; banked beams use the Banked Weapon Damage Table (a die against the damage). MISSILE hit: the same (plasma counts as a missile). SUPERSTRUCTURE hit: full or half damage depending on the location (halves round down). WARP ENGINE hit: the engine nearest the shooter takes it (a hit through Shield 2 or 5 may hit either, by die); when an engine's track reaches 0 the rest, and later damage, is halved onto the superstructure; repairable by a Crew Efficiency roll. IMPULSE ENGINE hit: the same pattern. SENSORS hit: the lock is lost at once and the ship cannot warp out or fire while they are out. BRIDGE hit: 1 superstructure point and casualties of damage x 2 (up to 20%); no Repair Rolls in the next Repair/Repower Phase. ENGINEERING hit: a second die on the Engineering Damage Table: 1-2 Shield Power Grid down (all shields drop until repaired), 3-4 Weaponry Power Grid down (no weapon may fire), 5-6 Maneuver Power Converter down (no heading changes, no holding station: the ship goes straight ahead at its movement rate), with combined results (SPG and WPG, SPG and MPC, WPG and MPC, all power systems) at the higher rolls whose die numbers the OCR lost. WARP ENGINE / SUPERSTRUCTURE hit: the damage is split in half between the engine and the superstructure (the engine takes the larger half if odd), and the crew casualties equal the superstructure damage as a percentage. CREW CASUALTIES (a C result): the percentage per damage point depends on the ship's ORIGINAL superstructure (a strength of 1 means 100% per point), times the damage up to a maximum of 5 points per hit; a 2C result (bridge and engineering) doubles it; an efficient crew may halve the casualties (a percentile Skill Roll at or under the Crew Efficiency Rating, rounding down); casualties lower the Crew Efficiency and, through the Casualty Modifier Track, the To-Hit and Repair rolls.
**6. Self-destruction (p.38).** Only to keep a ship from capture, and only for a ship with secret components or information that would endanger a government and its citizens (the book's example is the Romulan commander in the episode "Balance of Terror"). Romulans would do it only in extreme cases (few ships), Klingons feel it brings dishonour, and Federation, Gorn and Orions never do it.
**7. Systems repair (p.38-39).** Heavy damage makes repair harder: a hit marks one box on the Systems Status Track and, if the weapon is high-powered, more: (damage - 5) / 5 rounded down extra boxes (a 12-point hit marks 1 + 1); multiple hits on one system in the SAME Firing Phase add up (each hit costs one box, then the total damage minus 5 per hit, divided by 5, rounded down), hits in separate phases do not. A system already inoperable is unaffected by more damage. WEAPONS may now be repaired: each weapon's track has Oper, Dmgd, Repd and Inop; the first hit marks Dmgd (the weapon cannot fire until repaired); a Repair Roll of 1-8 mends a beam and 1-6 a missile weapon (marking Repd); a SECOND hit makes it permanently inoperable (Inop); a repaired weapon has -1 on its To-Hit Number (-1 per repaired weapon in a bank) and a repaired beam can be powered only to half its Maximum Power (rounded down).
**8. Defense Outposts (p.39): the one scenario-related section.** "In some scenarios, captains may encounter or be given command over space stations or defense outposts." Each outpost needs its own Master Control Panel. It may NOT leave its hex (an optional rule lets it drift one hex per turn, usually in the second Movement Phase) but may be rotated in place, never more than two hexsides per Movement Phase; its Movement Point Ratio is 10/1 (10 power points per movement point); it may never make emergency heading changes. Its firing arcs are THREE NUMBERED arcs, set by the small number on the Outpost Silhouette Counter (a vessel in a hex split by two arcs can be fired on by both arcs' weapons). Damage uses the Outpost Damage Table among the Detailed Damage Tables.
**In the game today (not rebuilt here):** as far as the logs show the game still uses the SIMPLIFIED damage location table; the Graduate items are on the wishlist as A19 (a separate setting), and of the list above only Evasive Maneuvers (an Advanced rule) is built, which already covers accelerator cannons; the evader's -2 shots, the detailed tables, the heading-change stress chart, the Slim Chance table, weapon repair, laser double fire, plasma half power, self-destruction and defense outposts are not built. Defense outposts would also need a scenario set-up to be useful.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A "course" that has no scenario still has scenario-related rules: read the whole course before saying so. (2) State a table's reading when the OCR damages it (the Slim Chance minus signs, the Engineering Damage Table's die numbers).

### 0.184 — The published scenarios of the rulebook, reviewed and summarised for the owner (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.94-S205)

**User request (2026-11-11):** "I already have a few scenarios to build out. For now, please review all the published scenarios out of the rulebook. summarize them here." **Finding: the rulebook PUBLISHES exactly TWO scenarios** (confirmed by the table of contents and by searching every "scenario" line of the whole 175-page text); everything else called a scenario is advice on designing one.
**1. THE BIG BAD WOLF: the Basic Course Scenario** (contents: book p.20; PDF p.21; introduced on p.9 as "a beginning scenario ... for use with the Basic Course rules"). *Background:* the USS Hood, a Constitution Class cruiser, is escorting merchantmen to Star Base 12 when it meets a Klingon D-7M Class cruiser bent on taking the convoy; the Hood engages while the convoy speeds away. *Set-up:* each captain has a prepared Master Control Panel; the two counters go at the centre of opposite SHORT sides of the Starfield Mapsheet, heading straight at each other; both ships have slowed to sub-light speed; each captain gets one Fire counter and one No Fire counter (p.9). *Victory:* the Hood wins if the Klingon is destroyed or driven from the field; the Klingon wins if he destroys the Hood or drives it from the field. *Notes:* the older Constitution is a match for the D-7M; keeping the forward armament on the Klingon lets the Hood fire everything; a Klingon who gets close can fly by and bring his aft weapons onto the Hood's usually unprotected, unarmed stern; the Hood has mobility and the longer beam range, the D-7M has photon torpedoes that can bring a shield down in one shot and aft-firing weapons; both captains should be told. **A discrepancy in the book:** the p.9 set-up text names the "Klingon D-10 cruiser" counter, the scenario itself says D-7M.
**2. THE KOBAYASHI MARU: the Command and Control Scenario** (contents: book p.53; PDF p.54; the book's own spelling, as OCR'd, is "Kobyashi"). *Background:* the Kobayashi Maru, in neutral territory patrolled by both the Federation and the Klingons, sends an urgent distress message; the Federation vessel must enter the neutral zone to rescue the crew, breaking the treaty and the uneasy truce. *Ship data:* one Federation vessel of any type against an appropriate Klingon battle group. *Set-up:* the Federation vessel on one narrow end of the mapsheet, the Klingon battle group opposite. *Victory:* the Federation players win if they EXIT THE KLINGON SIDE of the board in 15 turns or fewer with superstructure, engines and (the text) at least one-third intact; the Klingon player wins by preventing this; the Federation ship may not leave in any other direction or disengage by increasing warp speed: if it does, the Klingons win automatically. *Notes (the Academy test):* three or more battle groups against a single Enterprise Class Heavy Cruiser; the usual battle group is 3 D-7M Class Light Cruisers in tight formation; the first group enters on game turn 1, the second on turn 2, the third on turn 4; in later years a fourth group enters on turn 6 if necessary; "No one is intended to be able to survive this scenario: it is a test of character."
**NOT scenarios, but the book's guidance on making them.** *Introduction (p.9):* a scenario must say what the sides are and their goals, how many ships each side has, which ships, their state of repair, where they start, any planets, asteroid fields, suns, mines or other objects and where, when reinforcements arrive, and the victory conditions. *Advanced Course, "The Scenario" (PDF p.24):* captains will make up their own; decide the sides (two for beginners), the goals and victory conditions, how many ships of each type (one per captain for beginners; balance by the D and WDF values: the Constitution, D-7M and D-10 are nearly equal, the Reliant matches the L-9; in bigger battles make the total D and the total WDF of the sides equal), and where each ship starts (opposite edges); up to four mapsheets, laid out for the longest run in chase scenarios; planet, moon and asteroid counters take one to seven hexes, placed as the scenario says. *Command and Control, the gamemaster ("Instructor"), PDF p.50-51:* he designs the encounters (the goals for players and opponents, the ships and relative strength, the damage state, a background story that may come from a TV plot, a novel or "one of the adventures published by FASA"), the environment (planets, stations, asteroids, moons, mines; anything hidden and its movement), presents them as a Star Fleet Instructor and judges the action fairly. *Balancing Scenarios (PDF p.57-58):* Combat Efficiency = D x WDF; compare two ships directly (accurate head to head); for two sides FASA's own method adds up the Ds of each side and the WDFs of each side and compares both totals (balanced if both balance); the second method multiplies each side's total D by its ships' WDF and compares the total CEs (best with equal numbers). *Hooks in the rules:* a ship that leaves the mapsheet is moved back to the centre UNLESS the scenario makes leaving part of the victory conditions (Basic, p.17: this is what the Kobayashi Maru uses); the game ends when one side completes the scenario's victory conditions, and is a draw if both do at once or neither can (Advanced, "Ending the Game"); mines belong to "sub-light scenarios" (§0.183); lasers and accelerator cannons to Four Years War scenarios and certain civilian vessels (§0.183). The adventures FASA published separately are NOT in this book. **Not read in detail:** the Graduate Course's "Defense Outposts" section (contents: p.38), which looks scenario-related.
**What the game has today.** No scenario of any kind: "Big Bad Wolf" appears nowhere in the game or the documents, "Kobayashi Maru" only in four HANDOVER notes (§0.166 and §0.168) and two wishlist lines; every battle is a free set-up (ships, terrain, difficulty) with one ship per side and the end conditions destruction, surrender and power failure. **What each scenario would need:** The Big Bad Wolf needs only what exists (a Constitution as the Hood, the D-7 M, the two start positions facing each other at sub-light) plus a "driven from the field" ending (leaving the board) and fixed starting positions. The Kobayashi Maru needs features the game lacks: several ships per side (three D-7M per group, three or four groups), reinforcement groups entering on set turns (1, 2, 4, 6), formation movement for the AI, an exit-the-board victory with a 15-turn limit and a one-third condition on superstructure and engines, and a rule that leaving any other edge or warping away loses (the game has no warp-out action: §0.166).
**Harness lessons.** (1) "All the published scenarios" means checking the contents page and searching the whole text, not just the sections titled Scenario: the Advanced "Scenario" section is advice, and the Kobayashi Maru has no heading of its own in the OCR. (2) When a book contradicts itself (the D-10 against the D-7M), say so. (3) Say plainly what was not read (Defense Outposts).

### 0.183 — Rules answer: what the mines and accelerator cannon rules are for (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.94-S205)

**User question (2026-11-11):** "what are the mines and accelerator cannon rules pertaining to? Seems to be more scenario driven." **Answer: yes, both are scenario or era equipment, as the book itself says; neither is a general combat rule.**
**MINES** (Advanced Course, "Special Equipment", PDF p.30, rulebook OCR lines 3026-3094, next to the Romulan cloaking device): "Some sub-light scenarios may call for mines, which are very similar to immobile photon torpedoes." One side controls the area and has laid the minefield BEFORE the scenario; **the book has no rules for laying mines**. Each mine has the damage of a photon torpedo, never more than the laying side's torpedoes; the players agree the number beforehand for balance, and with a gamemaster no agreement is needed (the whole scenario can be threading a minefield). Positions are recorded by hex number (the Starfield Mapsheet hexes are numbered). Detonation: when a ship enters a mined hex the controlling player announces it and rolls one die: a 1 explodes against a FRIENDLY vessel, 6 or less against all others; the roll repeats every Movement Phase the ship stays in the hex, the chance rising by 1 each time; a detonated mine clears the hex. Damage goes to the part of the vessel that first entered the hex (the book's shield numbers: forward entry Shield 2, backing in Shield 5, sideslip from the right Shield 1, from the left Shield 3), resolved like a missile attack; **an emergency heading change evades 1 mine per Movement Phase.** The book's other mentions: the Advanced Course's contents list (line 2127), a table fragment (line 4098), and the Command and Control gamemaster's advice to place "planets, space stations, asteroids, moons, or mines" in the environment (line 5299). **In the game: no mine code; wishlist A1 lists "Mines (scenario-defined, photon-torpedo damage)" unchecked.** Because the book gives no laying rules, mines only make sense with a way to set up scenarios (a gamemaster or a scenario file): that fits the Command and Control roadmap (A20) better than the Advanced checklist.
**ACCELERATOR CANNONS** (Graduate Course, "Determining Weapon Hits", PDF p.36, OCR lines 3680-3735): they appear only "in scenarios taking place during the Four Years War, or where certain civilian vessels are involved", together with lasers; an accelerator cannon "fires a high-speed missile carrying a nuclear warhead", and neither lasers nor accelerator cannons "are generally as powerful as more modern beam and missile weapons". The whole rule is two lines: **"Treat accelerator cannon fire as missile fire. Accelerator cannon projectiles may be evaded."** (Lasers are the separate rule: a laser given more than its Maximum Power, up to twice, may fire two shots in two different Firing Phases, each for half the power.) **In the game:** the Federation cannons FAC-1 (damage 8, arm 3, chart F, range 8), FAC-2 (10, 4, G, 10) and FAC-3 (12, 4, H, 10) are defined from the p.47 design tables as MISSILE-type weapons (`FED_ACCELERATORS`, about line 1344; the weapon lookup at about line 1600 and the `FA` prefix at about line 1693), and three Federation hull rows in `FASA_2302_Federation_Ships_DATA.md` list them as the EARLIEST variant of the hull (later refits swap them for photon torpedoes); which playable ships carry them in the game was not checked. **Consequence: Evasive Maneuvers (v2.92-S203) already covers them, because it applies to every missile-type weapon**; strictly, the book's Advanced rule names only torpedoes and plasma and adds accelerator cannons in the Graduate Course (a harmless difference, the book says they are evadable anyway). **The wishlist note on A19 ("the game has the weapons but no two-shot or evasion code") was out of date for evasion and has been corrected; the laser two-shot rule is still unbuilt.**
**Open question for the owner:** whether mines wait until there is a way to set up scenarios.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A rules question about what a rule is FOR is answered from the passage and its neighbours (the course, the heading, the sentence that introduces it). (2) A search for one word can miss the game's own name for the thing (the code says FAC, the book says accelerator cannon): search both. (3) Reading a first grep's printed hits is not enough: count the thing on its own before saying whether anything uses it.

**What was built.** *The choice window:* the rules are a bulleted list, one sentence each; the first two bullets, "You take 1 point of hull stress (your superstructure: 20 -> 19)" and "You cannot fire this phase: ...", are bold and 12 px against 11 px for the rest; "half damage" and "full damage" are bold in the bullets and "HALF damage (9)" / "FULL damage (18)" are bold chips in every card; the odd "9: 0 gets through" notation became "(9): none gets through" and "(18): 6 gets through"; the missile line is one sentence ("KP-4 Tube 1 (torpedo, 18 damage) is aimed at your Fwd shield (12 points); it hits 70% of the time at this range"); the low-hull warning is kept. *The dodge:* the die really TUMBLES (a 3D transform about three axes with bounces, slowing to a stop on the pre-decided number; none with reduced motion or on a skip); a result BANNER names the shield, the kind of damage and the amount, and what it does to the shield: "FAILED: The torpedo hit your **Fwd shield** for **FULL damage: 18** / Shield 12 -> 0 · 12 absorbed · **6 gets through**" (before the impact: "will hit"); the same banner for a dodge that worked and for the enemy's dodge ("Your torpedo hit its ..."). *The firing screen (option on):* the committing button is the biggest thing on screen (15 px, bright orange "FIRE 2 SELECTED", or a calm blue "HOLD FIRE", or "CONTINUE" when nothing can fire); "NO FIRE" is hidden (HOLD FIRE replaces it); FIRE ALL is renamed "SELECT ALL READY (n)" and made small and quiet ("ALL READY SELECTED (n)" when done); the pair button is "SELECT A PAIR"; rows read "SELECTED · name"; the hover card says "READY — click to select" or "SELECTED — fires when you press FIRE (click again to cancel)"; the hint says "Click the weapons you want to fire, then press FIRE. (n selected) The enemy declares after you." and, once the fire is sent, "Your fire is sent. The enemy's answer and the results follow."; the log says "FH-3 Bank 1: selected", "SELECT ALL: 3 weapons selected", "Already selected: every ready weapon" or "Nothing ready to select", "You fire: ..." or "You hold fire.", and the enemy "IKS Devisor will fire: ..." or "will hold fire." The setup option's hover text was updated to match. With the option OFF the firing screen is unchanged.
**Verification (real Chromium).** New `testEv7.js` 14 checks (the bold bullets and the 12 px against 11 px, the bold chips, the sentence, the title, the 3D tumble sampled, the banners checked against the real log numbers, reduced motion) and `testEv8.js` 20 (the hierarchy by area, font and gradient, every label state, the log wording, the one-place wording table, the cost fix in all three situations, the plural); `testEv1/2/5` updated for the new words and the two-missile test split into identical (one row) and different (two rows, pick the second) = **171 evasion checks** (27 + 35 + 33 + 25 + 17 + 14 + 20). Played-through battles at three settings: no stalls. Regressions on this build: every-weapon sound comparison against v2.93-S204 (0 of 14 kinds changed), reverse rule 24, armed-now line 17, plasma loading 11, torpedo flight 12, faction torpedo paths 20, the 246-weapon look scope (0 wrong), Damage Control 66 of 66, entry window, explosions, Federation volley (0 clipped), bridge beds 27 + 15, bridge levels 10, bridge end 6. The new windows were LOOKED at (screenshots in `evade_windows_review_v2/`); the tumble was caught by running the animation clock at 15% speed.
**Two flaky tests, not regressions.** `testPlasmaFire.js` failed its check "the shot is still held until the bolt lands (0 pending at 0.7 s)" in 3 of about 13 runs on this build; compared run for run alternately with the previous build, the PREVIOUS build failed the same check once in 4 runs and this one passed 4 of 4: it measures a 0.7 s wall-clock window around a 0.96 s bolt, so it flakes with machine load (cause not pinned down further). `testReverseFlow.js` (two real turns, random events) failed 2 of 4 checks again in one run and passed in others, as on earlier builds.
**Bugs of Claude's found by the tests and by looking, fixed before delivery.** (1) The big orange button's colour was OVERRIDDEN by the older `.action-btn.primary` (it loads later with equal specificity): the size was right but the fill was not; now `.action-btn.primary.ev-main`. (2) After pressing FIRE with the enemy declaring last, the hint still said "Click the weapons you want to fire": now "Your fire is sent...". (3) The missile row, a flex box, broke into pieces instead of one sentence: now a block. Also found and fixed in my screenshots: two shots were bad (the die "tumbling" frame was taken after the roll had finished, and the "worked" banner after the window had closed), re-shot with a slowed clock and straight after a skip.
**Known limits / not built.** The wording set is not chosen (Plain is in; Bridge talk would be an edit of `FW`); the D-7 artwork is untouched; the shield-arc tie rule (§0.177) is still open; the sounds are still placeholders (C10); the enemy's dodge is still a blocking overlay. **Not verified:** how the tumble FEELS in real time (only its transform and slowed frames were checked), the layout on very small screens, Firefox and Safari.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A style that "looks right in the size" can still lose to an older rule on colour: test the computed colour, not just the box. (2) A screenshot of a timed animation needs the clock controlled (slow it, or freeze it): a capture is slower than the animation. (3) When a test fails only sometimes, run old and new builds alternately: running them in separate batches can mislead.
