### 0.179 — Combat log review (third playtest); the owner's takeaway; the firing-stage proposal v3 (FIRE ALL stays a select-all) and a wording table (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.93-S204)

**User message (2026-11-10), with `combat_log_2026-11-10-22-10-05.txt` (ledger row 32):** "played again to get the feel of this evasive maneuvers rule. The one thing I've taken away from this rule is to fire missile weapons to get shields down and/or dodges out of the way so that beam weapons cut into the target. I still feel the firing weapons labeling needs more intuitive wording/phrasing."
**The owner's takeaway is the intended play of the rule.** A missile is worth firing because it strips a shield or forces a dodge (a dodge costs the dodger its own fire and 1 hull point and can only evade one missile), after which beams cut in. In the log: the torpedoes killed the D-7's Fwd shield generator and its superstructure fell to a torpedo; the one dodge by the Admiral AI was FREE (it had declared no fire, so nothing was replaced), which is what the AI policy (§0.175) is built to find. Candidate for the option's hover text or the tutorial (not decided, not added): a one-line tip, "Torpedoes strip shields or force a dodge; beams then cut in".
**The evidence that changes the proposal.** In turn 5 the owner used FIRE ALL as a SELECT-ALL: FIRE ALL (4 weapons), then clicked both torpedoes OFF, then locked in the two beams (and fired the torpedoes the next phase). Proposal v2 (§0.178) made FIRE ALL fire at once, which would have broken exactly this habit. **Proposal v3 (replaces v2; NOT decided, NOT built):** FIRE ALL stays a way to SELECT, renamed so it says so (SELECT ALL READY (n)); the weapon buttons toggle SELECTED; ONE main button carries the action with a live label; the rest as in v2 (step strip, status line, log wording, the cost fix). 7 of 14 lock-ins in this log had no shots, so the main button's "nothing can fire" and "nothing selected" states are used half the time.
**The wording table offered to the owner (his words are the test; he has not chosen):** *weapon, ready*: "READY" (now) / "READY" (plain) / "STANDING BY" (bridge talk); *weapon, selected*: "DECLARED, fires when you lock in" (now) / "SELECTED" (plain) / "LOCKED ON: awaiting your order" (bridge); *select all*: "FIRE ALL" (now) / "SELECT ALL READY (n)" / "ALL WEAPONS ON TARGET (n)"; *main button*: "LOCK IN FIRE" (now) / "FIRE 2 SELECTED", "HOLD FIRE", "CONTINUE" (plain) / "FIRE!", "HOLD FIRE", "STAND BY" (bridge); *hint*: "Declare your shots: click the weapons, then LOCK IN FIRE" (now) / "Click the weapons you want to fire, then press FIRE." (plain) / "Select your weapons, then give the order: FIRE." (bridge); *the log, yours*: "You lock in your fire: ..." (now) / "You fire: ..." and "You hold fire." (plain) / "Weapons free: ..." and "Hold your fire." (bridge); *the log, the enemy's*: "IKS Devisor declares fire: ..." (now) / "IKS Devisor will fire: ..." and "will hold fire" (plain) / "IKS Devisor is charging weapons: ..." (bridge); *a repeat or empty click*: "FIRE ALL: 0 weapons declared" (now) / "Nothing ready to select" and "Already selected" (plain and bridge). The book's word "declare" stays in the rules text and the pop-up.
**Bugs found in the log (Claude's, not yet fixed).** (1) The debrief says "The enemy evaded 1 of your missile (1 worked)": the plural is wrong for 1 (`missile${s(...)}` at about line 6158): it should always read "of your missiles". (2) The cost counting when the player declares first (§0.178) is still to fix.
**Observations about the AI (recorded here only; the owner has not asked for a change).** The Admiral-rated D-7 declared only beams in all 4 declarations in this battle and never a torpedo, even before its torpedo tube was destroyed in turn 3; it dodged exactly once, when dodging was free.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Look for the way the player actually uses a control before changing what it does (FIRE ALL as select-all). (2) A wording question needs the words side by side in every state, not an abstract choice between options.

### 0.178 — Combat log review (second Evasive Maneuvers playtest); a bug in the evasion cost counting; the firing-stage proposal v2 (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.93-S204)

**User message (2026-11-10), with `combat_log_2026-11-10-16-30-00.txt` (ledger row 31):** "that was interesting. looks like the evasion works. has correct art. does seem to have correct sound too. Do wish the firing weapons stage was more intuitive. Have uploaded the combat log for your review." **The owner's own check of the v2.93-S204 animation: it works, the artwork is right, the sound seems right** (the first confirmation by ear of the placeholder sounds; the levels were never heard by Claude).
**The log.** The Constitution lost to a Captain-level D-7 in 8 turns (ledger row 31). Evasion: 3 offered, 2 taken, both failed (rolls 7 and 8), 1 declined. The Tactical Advantage appeared in both orders: when the enemy declared first (twice) the pop-up came at the start of the phase; once the player declared first, the log shows the faithful order exactly: "You lock in your fire ... / IKS Devisor declares fire ... / You decline to evade". The player's two evasions cost 2 hull points and the shots of those phases; the second came in the very phase where the enemy then landed 30 points of torpedo damage and the hull went from 10 to 0 (the final dodge failed): the dodge was a poor trade again (30% odds, one of two torpedoes). The Captain-level AI never dodged the player's torpedoes (its policy is cautious: HANDOVER §0.175).
**BUG (Claude's, found from this log; not yet fixed): the cost of a dodge is overstated when the player declares FIRST.** In the order "the enemy declares last" the player has already locked in when the pop-up appears, yet (a) the pop-up's cost line lists every READY weapon as one that "would stay silent", and (b) `GS.debrief.evasion.given` counts every ready weapon as a shot given up. Reproduced (`dbgCost.js`): 4 weapons ready, none declared and locked in: the pop-up said all four would stay silent and the counter recorded 4. Right answer: in that order the cost is the shots the player DECLARED (the queue), which a dodge replaces; in the other order (the enemy declares first, the player has not declared) the ready weapons are the right count. In this log the debrief's "8 shots you could have fired" is therefore too high (the player had locked in no shots in the second dodge). **Fix (to bundle with the firing-stage change if the owner agrees):** use the queued weapons when `GS._ev.locked`, and the ready weapons otherwise, in both the cost line and the counter.
**The firing stage: the evidence.** The first log showed 7 "FIRE ALL: 0 weapons declared" lines and 6 cancelled declarations; in this one there is a single zero-weapon FIRE ALL and no cancellations: the owner has learned the flow, but still finds it unintuitive. In this log 9 of 17 lock-ins had no shots at all (an extra click in every such phase), and each real volley needed FIRE ALL and then LOCK IN FIRE: two clicks for what used to be one. **Proposal v2 (builds on option A of §0.176; NOT decided, NOT built):** (1) **FIRE ALL does what it says: it selects every ready weapon AND fires them in one click** (the old muscle memory); (2) the per-weapon buttons toggle SELECTED (not DECLARED); (3) one main button with a LIVE label: "FIRE 2 SELECTED →", "HOLD FIRE →" (nothing selected but something could fire), "CONTINUE →" (no weapon can fire this phase); (4) a small step strip in the weapons panel, "1 SELECT · 2 FIRE · 3 ENEMY DECLARES", with who declares first ("the enemy declares after you" or "the enemy has declared: 2 torpedoes"); (5) a status line after firing when the enemy still has to declare ("Fire locked in: the enemy is declaring"); (6) log wording: "You open fire: ..." / "You hold fire", and "FIRE ALL: 0 weapons declared" becomes "Nothing ready to select" or "Already selected"; (7) the cost fix above. The two-step (declare, then the AI answers, then resolve) stays underneath, because the AI must see the player's declared missiles before it decides to dodge.
**Not decided:** whether FIRE ALL should fire at once (the main question for the owner); the rulebook's shield-arc tie rule (§0.177) is still open too.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A cost shown to the player must be computed for the order the player is actually in (declared first or last), not from the general state. (2) The debrief's numbers are worth reading against the log's own lines: "8 shots" for two dodges was the clue. (3) Reproduce a suspected bug in a tiny script before reporting it.

### 0.177 — What changed in v2.93-S204 (the dodge is SHOWN: the Sensor Scope animation, the ship's own artwork, the existing sounds)

**User messages (2026-11-09):** "I like the animation of 4 but the sound 3. Also, this should be using the target ships provided top down artwork. Also, make note, the sound will get replaced eventually. We already have the sounds for the weapons. Use that. I can get you a sound for when it "hits" the shield too. But for now, go with the current sounds." Then "Continue" (to finish the regression suites, deliver and document).
**How it was read.** Animation: style 4 of the Evasion Animation Lab, the SENSOR SCOPE. "Sound 3": read as STYLE 3's whoosh (the thruster burst, whoosh B), not the third whoosh in the list (the glide, which is style 4's own); Claude asked the owner to confirm; swapping is one function (`evWhoosh`). "The target ship's provided top-down artwork": the evading ship's own sprite, drawn with the game's own `drawShipAuto`, the function the tactical map uses. "Use the weapon sounds": the missile in the animation plays the shooter's EXISTING launch sound.
**What it does.** After the player chooses, the pop-up shows a scope (400 x 330): the six shield arcs with their REAL strengths and the shooter's REAL bearing; the die tumbles for 1.1 s (the same d10 that was already decided); then the evading ship's artwork turns one hex-side, the red arc and the "REVISED" label follow the shield that would take the missile, the missile blip (in the attacker's faction colour) arrives, and the impact shows. **A dodge that WORKS ends with the ship turned about 60 degrees and the missile on the NEW shield (half damage, a glancing spark); one that FAILS shows the missile landing while the ship has turned less than half a hex-side, still inside the original arc (the ORIGINAL shield, full damage), and never past that arc's edge.** The enemy's dodge plays the same scope in an overlay ("THE ENEMY EVADES", the enemy's colours and artwork, no choice buttons) and the phase waits for it (a default chosen by Claude, not decided by the owner). Skipping: Space, Enter, Esc, a click on the scope or the SKIP button jumps to the result (no sounds); a second press closes; left alone it plays about 3.3 s and closes itself about 1 s later (4.4 s in all); with "reduce motion" it jumps to the result and closes after about a second. A lethal stress point shows the hull failing (flash, cracks, shards), the missile flying on through the wreckage and no impact sound, then the existing defeat or victory with the stress ending.
**The sounds (ALL PLACEHOLDERS; the owner: "the sound will get replaced eventually").** (1) The WHOOSH is generated (the lab's style 3 thruster burst: two noise bursts and a low thump), at the start of the dodge, level 0.7 (peak about 0.7; NOT heard by Claude). (2) The MISSILE plays the shooter's existing launch sound exactly as `triggerWeaponFX` picks it (a Federation, Romulan or Gorn torpedo: its recorded clip via `playSfxFor(faction,'torpFire')`; a plasma bolt: the recorded "flame roar and spit", `plasma_fire`; otherwise the generated `torpedo`), when the missile appears. (3) The IMPACT plays the game's existing generated `shieldhit` if the shield took it all, otherwise `explosion`, as the game does. **The owner will supply a recorded shield-hit sound later** (wishlist C10). Because the real shot still plays its own launch and impact sounds when it fires after the pop-up, each of those is heard twice (once in the animation, once in the real shot).
**Finding: the rulebook's tie rule is not implemented, and evasion makes it visible (NOT changed; the owner to decide).** The book says: "The shield arc determines the shield side struck unless a firing ship is on the line between two shield arcs. In this case, it is always the target ship captain's choice of which of the two possible shield sides is struck" (FULL_OCR line 1751, with an example at line 1758). The game has no such rule: `getHitFace` picks by floating-point rounding. Measured on random positions: the shooter is exactly on such a line in about 7% of positions (285 of 3,990; 120 of 1,495), and there the game's choice is an accident. For evasion: in about 1% of dodges (17 of 1,495) a working dodge moves the shield by two places or not at all (always and only when the shooter was exactly on a line). **The animation always shows the face the game resolves (0 differences in about 10,000 random cases) and its impact point always lies inside the arc shown.** Options: (A) implement the book rule everywhere (the AI picks its stronger of the two shields; the player is asked, or the game picks his stronger), which changes combat balance a little in about 7% of positions; (B) leave as is. Not added to the wishlist (ask first); recorded here.
**Verification (real Chromium).** New files `testEv5.js` 25 checks and `testEv6.js` 17 checks, plus the earlier ones: `testEv1` 27, `testEv2` 31, `testEv3` 33 (now checking the enemy's overlay instead of a note) = **133 evasion checks**. They cover: the ship's own artwork drawn and turning (0 to -60 degrees for port, to +60 for starboard); all 66 registered ships in both outcomes at four moments with no fallback needed and no errors; 1,495 random positions, facings and directions against the game's own `getHitFace` (0 differences; every working dodge ends turned 60 degrees, every failing one lands under 30 degrees; the impact point inside the arc shown in every case); the animation's shield equals the shield the log then reports, for a working and a failing dodge; the sounds in order and once each (whoosh about 1.1 s, the missile's launch sound about 1.7 s, the impact about 2.2 s; the explosion when no shield; none when skipped; the Federation clip, the plasma clip and the fallback); skipping by Space, Enter, Esc, the button and a click; reduced motion; a 380 px window; the enemy's overlay (its colours and artwork, the phase waiting, the missile then firing); both lethal endings. Played-through battles (`testEv4`) at difficulties 2, 3, 4 and 6: no stall, bookkeeping consistent. Regressions on this build: every-weapon sound comparison against v2.92-S203 (0 of 14 kinds changed), reverse rule 24, armed-now line 17, plasma firing 12 and loading 11, torpedo flight 12, faction torpedo paths 20, the 246-weapon look scope (0 wrong), Damage Control 66 of 66, the entry window, explosions, the Federation volley (0 clipped), bridge beds 27 + 15, bridge levels 10, bridge end 6. Frames from the real game were LOOKED at for a Federation, Klingon, Romulan, Gorn and Orion ship.
**A flaky test, not a regression.** `testReverseFlow.js` (two real turns played with random events) failed 2 of its 4 checks in 2 of 10 runs on v2.93-S204 and in 1 of 4 runs on v2.92-S203: the failing runs show duplicate phases (`repower, repower, power, power`), a double-click race in the test's own rapid button pressing. It does not use the evasion option. It should be made robust one day.
**Mistakes of Claude's found and fixed on the way (none shipped).** (1) A leftover `closed=false` hack in the pop-up, removed before it ran. (2) A forced minimum turn of 2.4 degrees put a failed dodge's impact point about 2 degrees past the arc edge when the shooter sat on the edge: now the impact never passes the original arc's edge (zero turn if the margin is zero). (3) A test picked a Romulan ship key the selector does not offer, so the game quietly fell back to a Klingon D-7 and the frame looked wrong; the test now reads the real options. (4) A wrong assumption that the Federation torpedo clip would not be decoded in a test browser. (5) A geometry test first demanded agreement at exact arc lines, where the game itself has no rule; it now tests the real invariants and reports the ties. (6) A played-through script passed a plain number where a pair was expected.
**Known limits / not built.** The "Lock in fire" wording is unchanged (the owner has not chosen A, B or C). The enemy's dodge is a blocking overlay by default. Ship sizes vary with the provided artwork (the Klingon D-7 is visibly small, as on the map); the game's content-box helper measured only 1 of 47 sprites when asked, so an auto-fit would need its own measuring step. In the played-through battles the AI never actually dodged (covered by the scripted tests instead). The Evasion Animation Lab still draws a generic ship (it is only the proof of concept). **Not verified:** the sounds by ear (Claude cannot hear: the whoosh level of 0.7, the balance of the three sounds, the double launch and impact sounds), how the pace FEELS in play, Firefox and Safari.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A test that selects things by name must check that the selection took (the Romulan key; the AI difficulty earlier). (2) Test the invariant you actually need (the picture equals the rule) and measure the edge cases separately instead of asserting them away. (3) When a regression test fails, run it on the previous build too before drawing any conclusion. (4) A measuring helper that only works on already-analysed data is not a reliable basis for a feature.

### 0.176 — Combat log review after the first Evasive Maneuvers playtest; the Evasion Animation Lab (a proof of concept, a separate tool); the owner's answers (tool and documents only, game unchanged, still v2.92-S203)

**User messages (2026-11-09):** a combat log (`combat_log_2026-11-09-16-46-22.txt`, build v2.92-S203, IKS Devisor against USS Andor) with: "did some playtesting. Will need to do some more. But for now, please review the combat log and my comments. need a visual representation of the target ship evading. For cinematic purposes. The "lock in fire" verbiage does not seem as intuitive as needed. Do not build anything yet. Let's discuss first." Then the answers to the discussion: "1. Yes // 2. yes. It should be skippable but perhaps an animation of the evading ship making the move in the popup window. (I think this would answer your questions for 3 and 4 and 5 as well) Have the arcs in the hex marked and animate the ship doing the "dodge". A whoosh sounds would be fine. Do a proof of concept of a variety of animations for me to make the judgement call."
**The log review (ledger row 30).** The rule behaved as designed: 4 evasions offered and taken, rolls 3, 1, 3, 2 (all successes: a 0.8% run; the roll is the plain `d10()` and the 30 to-hit rolls in the same log are spread normally, so luck). Cost against benefit: about 12 damage points saved for 4 hull points and 12 shots given up; the Andor fired four identical torpedoes and only one can be dodged (in turn 1 the dodged one missed while three hit). After each evasion the ship points 60 degrees off and the log shows the player rotating back every time. **Evidence for the wording problem:** 7 "FIRE ALL: 0 weapons declared" lines and 6 "declaration cancelled" lines: the player clicked FIRE ALL repeatedly and toggled weapons, expecting a shot to fire; the screen mixes verbs (FIRE ALL READY, READY TO FIRE, DECLARED, LOCK IN FIRE). **Proposals (not decided):** (A, recommended) weapons toggle SELECTED, FIRE ALL becomes SELECT ALL READY (n), the End Phase button shows what it will do ("FIRE 2 SELECTED WEAPONS" or "HOLD FIRE"), a repeat click says "already selected", the hint says "Select your shots, then FIRE"; "declares" stays for the enemy and the pop-up; (B) a visible "1 Select, 2 Fire" indicator; (C) a flavour name such as ENGAGE. Also proposed: group identical missiles in the pop-up ("4 x FP-7 torpedo, you may evade ONE") and add an "expected damage saved" line. The owner has answered the animation questions but NOT yet chosen the wording.
**The owner's decisions on the animation.** (1) It applies to BOTH ships. (2) It is SKIPPABLE and plays inside the pop-up window: the arcs of the hex are marked and the ship is animated doing the dodge; a whoosh sound is fine; this settles the questions about the camera, the option (it belongs to the Evasive Maneuvers option) and the sound. (3) A PROOF OF CONCEPT of a variety of animations first, for him to judge. (The enemy's evasion has no pop-up today: the same animation would need an overlay: blocking or not is still to decide.)
**What was built: the Evasion Animation Lab** (`evasion_animation_lab.html`, 39 KB, published at https://claude.ai/artifact/VdvgrAu4WtdSqmxKfTXtTu, with the "Download this tool" button; NOT part of the game). Six styles, each in a mock of the pop-up with the six shield arcs marked (strengths shown), a faction-coloured d10 that rolls, the dodge, the missile arriving and the result text: (1) SCHEMATIC (dotted old heading, solid new heading, the red arc follows the shield facing the missile); (2) BANK AND SLIP (sideways slide, ghost trail, thruster puffs, glancing sparks, shake); (3) THRUSTER BURST (attitude jets fire at the bow and stern on opposite sides, a springy settle); (4) SENSOR SCOPE (sweeping scope, wireframe ship, a predicted-impact marker that is REVISED when the shield changes); (5) ARC DIAL (the ship stays fixed and the threat pointer swings round the dial: the clearest answer to "which shield takes it"); (6) SLOW-MOTION CINEMATIC (letterbox, a gentle push-in, slowed time, long ghosts, a shield ripple). Controls: your ship or the enemy's, port or starboard, the roll works or fails, torpedo or plasma bolt, the shooter's bearing (six), the evading and the firing faction (the game's six palettes), speed, whoosh, volume, and an ending where the hull is at 1 and the stress tears the ship apart (flash, cracks, shards; the missile then flies on through the wreckage and the text says so). Every card has Play, Skip (Space skips all) and a scrubber. **A failed dodge is shown "too late" on purpose:** the missile lands when the ship has turned 15 to 30 degrees, still inside the original arc, so it hits the ORIGINAL shield for FULL damage, as the rules say; a success shows the full 60-degree turn and the missile on the NEW shield for half. **Four whooshes** made by the page (A air sweep, B thruster burst, C glide, D Doppler pass that sweeps across the stereo field in the direction of the dodge), level-matched (rms 0.023 to 0.032, peaks 0.3 to 0.42); I cannot hear them.
**Verification (real Chromium; 22 checks).** The shield geometry for ALL 24 combinations of direction, outcome and bearing against independent arithmetic (port: bearing+1, starboard: bearing-1, failure: the original face); every style's impact at the right moment for 96 combinations (works: turned about 60 degrees, new shield; fails: 15-30 degrees, original shield); every style draws a full picture at six moments; the six faction palettes give six different pictures; the enemy version, the plasma bolt and the hull-at-1 ending render; Space skips; the scrubber seeks; Play runs in real time and stops; 2x speed; the four whooshes render without clipping and D pans the right way for each dodge; the Download button saves a working copy; no sideways scrolling at 420 px; 0 JavaScript errors. The frames were also LOOKED at (contact sheets of every style for a success and a failure).
**Mistakes of Claude's caught and fixed while building it.** My own re-reading caught two muddled pieces before they ran (the thruster jets would both have fired from the same side; the dial's pointer angle had a confusing offset). Testing and the pictures found: the scope's label hidden under the footer; the cinematic zoom cropping the top of the hex; whoosh B at peak 0.99 and the four whooshes at very different loudness (D about ten times quieter than B), which would have made the comparison by ear unfair; the page scrolling sideways at phone width; and the hull-at-1 ending still saying "HIT: half damage" after the ship was already gone. One test threshold (a whoosh's tail length) was my own arbitrary number and was corrected.
**Still to decide (the owner).** Which style, or which parts of several; which whoosh; how long; whether the enemy's evasion blocks play for a moment; the wording option (A, B or C); grouping identical missiles and the expected-damage line. **Not verified:** the whooshes by ear; how the animation FEELS at the game's pace; how it looks with the game's own ship sprites (the lab draws a generic ship, not the game's art).
**Harness lessons.** (1) A proof of concept for a visual decision must be LOOKED at, not only tested: the checks passed while three layout flaws and a contradictory caption were visible in the frames. (2) A comparison by ear needs level-matched sounds. (3) When an animation shows a rule (a late dodge hitting the original shield), derive the picture from the same geometry and test every combination. (4) A standing rule (a ledger row for every combat log) is easy to miss when the message says "discuss first": apply it anyway, in the same session.

### 0.175 — What changed in v2.92-S203 (the optional rule Evasive Maneuvers)

**User messages (2026-11-07):** "the aI difficulty settings for the evasion is good to me. Let's build it." then "Continue" (to finish the regression suites, deliver the build and update the documents). The spec was settled in §0.170 to §0.174 and the wishlist's evasion notes (A1). The owner's go-ahead is also taken as approval of the corrected defaults for the three rule gaps (§0.171).
**What it is.** A new option on the setup screen beside the terrain options: **Evasive Maneuvers** (`HOUSE_RULES` entry `evasion`), **OFF by default**, available only under the INTERMEDIATE rules (greyed out in Basic with "NEEDS INTERMEDIATE" and the reason in the hover text), and **ALL ON does not switch it on** (ALL OFF does turn it off). Hover text: the rule from the book (no movement points; the ship turns one hex-side but does not move; 1-3 on a d10 = half damage on the shield now facing; failure = original shield, full damage; 1 hull point either way; no firing that phase; one missile per phase; fire is declared then locked in; off by default; the AI may evade). With it OFF **nothing changes at all** (instant fire, no pop-up, same sounds, same results).
**The flow with it ON (every firing phase).** The Tactical Advantage winner declares fire last. *If the player has the advantage* the AI declares first (`aiDeclareShots`: which weapons fire is fixed at declaration, not at resolution), its declaration is announced in the log, and if any MISSILE (torpedo or plasma bolt; never a beam) is aimed at the player the pop-up appears at the START of the phase. *If the AI has the advantage* the player declares first, locks in, then the AI declares (announced), then the pop-up. **The player's weapon clicks only DECLARE (queue) shots in both cases; End Phase is relabelled LOCK IN FIRE (also the No Fire button locks in with no shots); this is a refinement of the §0.172 spec, which kept instant fire when the player had the advantage: the declare-then-resolve step is used in every firing phase so that the AI can pick which of the player's declared missiles to dodge, as the book's order requires.** After the lock-in the AI may evade one of the player's declared missiles; then the declared shots fire (staggered) and the AI's declared volley resolves as before. FIRE ALL declares all ready weapons; clicking a declared weapon again cancels it.
**The pop-up (`showEvasionPopup`).** The player is asked EVERY time (never decided for him): the incoming missile(s) (name, kind, damage, hit chance, the shield they are aimed at and its points; with several missiles he picks which to evade, by click or Up/Down); EVADE TO PORT (key 1), EVADE TO STARBOARD (key 2), TAKE IT (key 3 or Esc), each showing what happens if it works (30%: the shield now facing, half damage, how much gets through) and if it fails (70%: the original shield, full damage); the cost line (1 hull point with the current hull; the weapons that would be locked); a red WARNING at 1 hull point ("would DESTROY your ship"); the rules text from the book (plus the book's plasma hint). Evading rolls the d10 AT ONCE (decided first) and shows it as a faction-coloured d10 (`evDieSvg`: `TA_FACTION` accents, the crystal die for the independents) that tumbles for about 1.1 s; Space or Enter skips and continues; it closes by itself after 2.4 s; `prefers-reduced-motion` skips the tumble. The pop-up takes the player's faction colour.
**The rules as built (`doEvasion`, `getHitFace`).** Roll d10: 1-3 = success. The ship turns one hex-side (port = facing -1, starboard = +1; it does not move), loses 1 superstructure point (logged and in the damage log), and CANNOT fire this phase (queue cleared; `getWeaponBlockReason` says EVADING). Success: that missile hits the shield NOW facing the shooter, damage `ceil(half)` (a plasma bolt too: the book's graze numbers are not in the data). Failure: it hits the original shield for full damage. **Every other weapon still hits the original shield** (`ev.orig`). Only one missile per phase. The new heading stays after the phase; `_evade` and `GS._ev` are cleared when the phase ends. Cloaked ships may evade; a ship with no movement left may evade; a lethal stress point is allowed.
**The AI (`aiEvadeChoice`, `aiEvasionStep`).** It evades by difficulty (approved): Cadet never; Ensign about 1 time in 4; Lt. Commander when the shield facing the missile holds less than half its damage; Captain, Admiral and Legend when the expected damage saved beats the cost (its own declared volley's expected damage plus 2 for the hull point). It picks the most dangerous missile and the direction whose new shield is better; its declared fire is then replaced (counted); the player sees a log line and an on-screen note (no dice animation for the AI). **Note: at Captain and above the saving is at most about 15% of a missile's damage, so it evades only against big missiles at a good hit chance with a weak facing shield; the threshold (+2) is easy to tune.**
**Endings.** New `GS.debrief.evasion` counters (offered, taken, worked, failed, declined, hull points, shots given up, damage saved, and the AI's tried, worked, shots given up, damage saved); debrief lines ("Evasive Maneuvers were ON", "Evasive action: you were offered N ... took ... declined ...", cost and savings, "Every evasion failed ...", "You never evaded ...", "The enemy evaded ...", and the stress-kill lines); the end-screen stats line adds "Evasions: you tried X (Y worked) · the enemy tried ..."; a kill by a missile the victim had tried to dodge adds a clause ("had tried to dodge: the evasive turn came too late" / "...halved the blow; half was still more than ... had left"); **a ship destroyed by its own evasive turn has its own ending (`buildStressNarrative`, faction voice, from either side, `GS.killBlow.stress`), and the kill-blow records for ordinary hits now carry `evasion`.**
**Verification (real Chromium).** New files: `evHarness.js` (a controlled board, known shields, scripted dice via `window.d10`), `testEv1.js` 27 checks (the setup option: default off, greyed in Basic, hover text, clicking in Basic does nothing, ALL ON/OFF; option OFF changes nothing; the ON flow: pop-up at the start, the three choices, key 3, declare and cancel, LOCK IN FIRE), `testEv2.js` 31 (evade to PORT with success: the die, Space/Enter, the new face F-Stbd and half damage 18 to 9, the weapons locked; STARBOARD by real click with a failure: original face, full damage, counters; a torpedo dodged while beams still hit the original shield; two missiles with the pick; beams only = no pop-up; the AI-has-the-advantage order: nothing fires until lock-in, the log order, evading cancels the declared shots, taking it fires them), `testEv3.js` 33 (the AI policy for every difficulty, the AI really evading with its fire replaced, the Cadet never, the LETHAL STRESS endings for the player and for the AI, the debrief lines, the narratives, the dice colours), `testEv4.js` (played-through battles through the game's own buttons with random answers to every pop-up, at difficulties 2, 3, 4 and 6: no stall, no errors, the counters balance, pop-ups = offers). Shield faces were checked against independent geometry (a port turn puts a head-on shooter on F-Stbd, a starboard turn on F-Port). Regressions on the build: every-weapon sound diff vs v2.91-S202 (0 of 14 kinds changed), reverse rule 24 and 4, armed-now line 17, plasma firing 12 and loading 11, torpedo flight 12, faction torpedo paths 20, the 246-weapon look scope (0 wrong), Damage Control 66 of 66, the entry window, explosions, the Federation volley, bridge beds 27 + 15, bridge levels 10, bridge end 6; 0 JavaScript errors anywhere.
**Mistakes of Claude's found and fixed along the way (all in tests or the patch, none shipped).** (1) The patch first left a dead copy of `getHitFace`; caught before it ran. (2) The test harness set the AI difficulty BEFORE launch, but `launchGame()` reads the slider and overwrote it (the AI was Ensign): one early "the AI evades" ending passed partly by luck (an Ensign evades 1 time in 4); the harness now sets it after launch and every test really has the difficulty it names. (3) A timing race (an evasion record read 500 ms later, after the phase had cleared it) is now recorded as it happens. (4) A wrong end condition in the played-through test (the Legend AI can win in the first phase).
**Known limits / not built.** The Graduate rule (the evader may still fire at -2) and accelerator cannons; plasma grazes and the 5-point blocks (A1); a sound for evasion (silent; C10); the AI's evasion has no dice animation; with the option ON the enemy's "Target not in arc" log lines for weapons that cannot bear are not printed (only declared shots resolve); the tutorial cards do not mention the new flow; the Captain-and-above policy is cautious (above). **Not verified:** how it FEELS in play (the pace of declare, lock in and pop-up; the length of the dice animation), the layout of the pop-up on very small screens, Firefox and Safari.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A test harness must prove its own settings took effect (print the difficulty the AI actually had). (2) Record events at the moment they happen instead of reading state later. (3) Judge shield faces against independent geometry, not the code under test. (4) A played-through test that forces the situation (the AI armed with torpedoes) finds deadlocks that scripted scenarios cannot. (5) A refinement of an approved spec (declare-then-lock-in in every phase) must be flagged to the owner, not slipped in.

### 0.173 — Evasion: why an "immobilised" ship may evade (the book gives no reason; the default was wrongly worded); evasion in the end-of-game narratives (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.91-S202)

**User message (2026-11-07):** "is there an explanation as to why "an immobilised ship may evade"? It does not make sense to me. if there's an explanation in the rule, then it's probably good to add that in the pop up tool or narrative/description. Speaking of which, don't forget to add these decisions to the end of game narratives."
**The answer.** **No explanation in the rule, and the default was wrongly worded.** The only text is: evasion "does not cost any movement points, and it may be attempted even if a vessel has no movement left in the combat turn" (Advanced Course, PDF p.28). That is about the movement ALLOCATION of the turn (none made, or all spent), stated without a reason. Claude's wording "an immobilised ship may evade" blurred it with a ship immobile BECAUSE OF DAMAGE, which the evasion rule never mentions; the book mentions damage-immobile ships only for plasma grazes ("Ships immobile due to damage take full damage ... no grazes are possible"), where the reason is given: a graze means the captain "maneuvered his vessel out of the direct path of the bolt". **The game has no damage-immobilised state** (grep: none; an engine hit lowers total power, and zero power ends the battle), so the damage case cannot arise today. Corrected default: "a ship with no movement left may evade (the book says so)". If a damage-immobilised state is ever added (Graduate engine rules), the graze logic suggests such a ship should not evade: decide then. The wishlist notes now say all this, and say the pop-up must state the rule without inventing a reason.
**Pop-up and option text from the book.** Written into the wishlist notes with a draft pop-up text: no movement points needed (even with none left); the ship turns one hex-side without moving; 1-3 on a d10 (30%) = the missile hits the shield now facing it for half damage, failure = original shield, full damage; 1 point of stress either way; no firing that phase; one missile per phase; for plasma, the book's hint that it is worth it mainly when the facing shield is down or low; Graduate later: -2 shots.
**End-of-game narratives.** Read as: the player's evasion choices and results (and the AI's) must appear when the battle ends. How the end is built today: `buildDebrief` (the Tactical debrief, from `GS.debrief`), `buildKillNarrative` (destruction), `buildPowerKillNarrative` (adrift or surrender), shown on the end screen and written into the combat log and its export. The wishlist now lists what to track (offered, attempted, succeeded, failed, declined, hull points spent, shots given up, damage avoided, the AI's evasions), example debrief lines, and **a finding: a lethal stress point is a kill with no weapon, so it needs its own narrative (for either ship) and the kill narrative and debrief, which expect a shooter, a target and a weapon, must be checked so they do not break.** Interpretation to be confirmed with the owner.
**Harness lessons.** (1) When the owner asks "why", look for the reason in the book and say plainly when there is none; do not defend a default. (2) A vague word ("immobilised") can hide two different cases (no allocation versus damage); name the case the text actually covers. (3) A rule decision can create a new case elsewhere (a lethal stress point needs a narrative): follow it to the end screen.
**Not verified:** that "end of game narratives" means the debrief and kill narratives as read here.

### 0.172 — Evasion: the owner's final design decisions; what is still to confirm before building (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.91-S202)

**User message (2026-11-07):** "I'd like to keep this as faithful as possible. the "Ask only when it matters" - I don't think that should fall to you to decide. The player may have shields set handle it but may not want to "just take it" and leave the ship open to beam weapon damage. Let the player make that decision."
**Decisions now recorded in the wishlist (evasion notes):** (1) the pop-up at the start of the firing phase, honouring the Tactical Advantage; (2) the AI evades, depending on difficulty; (3) the option defaults to OFF and is chosen on the setup screen beside the terrain options; (4) **the FAITHFUL ordering**; (5) **Off / On only: when On the player is asked EVERY time a missile is aimed at his ship; there is NO "ask only when it matters" setting and the game never decides for him.**
**The faithful flow as it will be built (to be confirmed).** With the option OFF nothing changes (fire stays instant). With it ON, in every firing phase: *If the player has the Tactical Advantage* (the AI declares first): the AI's declared shots are shown at the start of the phase; if any missile is aimed at the player the pop-up asks (Evade port / Evade starboard / Take it, with the odds, the two shields, the costs); choosing to evade locks the player's weapons; otherwise the player fires as today (instant clicks), and when he fires a missile the AI decides, by difficulty, whether to evade it (which cancels its own declared fire that phase). *If the AI has the advantage* (it declares last): the player's shot clicks only DECLARE (queue) his shots; a "Lock in fire" step (proposed: the End Phase button, relabelled) ends his declaration; then the AI declares knowing them; then, if a missile is aimed at the player, the pop-up (evading cancels his declared shots); the AI also decides whether to evade the player's declared missile; then everything resolves in the game's usual order. The AI therefore needs `aiDeclareShots()` (which weapons, chosen at declaration, not at resolution) and an evasion policy.
**Still to confirm before building:** (a) the three rule gaps (§0.171) with the proposed defaults: a cloaked ship may evade, an immobilised ship may evade, a lethal stress point is allowed with a warning; (b) the AI's evasion policy by difficulty (proposal: Cadet never; Ensign about one time in four; Lieutenant Commander when the facing shield is weak against the missile; Captain and Admiral compare the expected damage with the cost: 1 hull point and the loss of its own fire); (c) the "Lock in fire" screen (End Phase relabelled, declared weapons highlighted, the AI's declaration shown when it goes first). **Awaiting the owner's go-ahead: nothing is built.**
**Harness lessons.** (1) A decision about WHO decides (the game or the player) belongs to the owner: offer the choice, do not default it away. (2) Write the final flow as numbered steps for each case so the owner can approve the behaviour, not just the idea.
**Not verified:** the exact feel of the two-step firing in phases where the AI has the advantage (only the flow is designed).

### 0.171 — The owner's answers before building evasion, and two clarifications (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.91-S202)

**User message (2026-11-07), answering Claude's pre-build questions:** "yes. pop-up at the start of the firing phase. When or if the AI has the advantage, let the AI declare as such then. // Does the AI evade in this build too? Yes. But it depends on the difficulty setting. // Default it to "off". Let the player opt in at the beginning of the game -- just choosing terrain options. // "How often does it interrupt? Ship just On/Off first, or also the "ask only when it matters" setting? (On/Off first, then add the middle setting once we've felt how often it stops play.)" not sure what you mean by this. Please clarify // The three cases you cite are for the graduate level right?"
**Recorded in the wishlist (evasion notes):** the three decisions (start-of-phase pop-up; the AI evades by difficulty; default OFF, chosen on the setup screen beside the terrain options) and the open items.
**Clarification 1: "ship just On/Off first".** "Ship" meant "release" (a poor word choice by Claude). The question: once the option is ON, the pop-up appears EVERY time an enemy missile is aimed at the player; the first version could offer only Off / On (every time), and a third setting, "ask only when it matters" (the pop-up appears only when evading could plausibly matter: for example the missile would get through the shield, or could kill), could be added after the owner has felt how often play stops. How often: in the 2026-11-06 22:25 log (Romulan against the Gorn SS-3) the Gorn fired a missile in 2 of 21 firing phases, so it would have stopped play twice in 7 turns; a Federation or Klingon ship with several torpedoes armed and in arc could trigger it nearly every firing phase. **Status: Claude will start with Off / On only unless the owner says otherwise.**
**Clarification 2: "the three cases are Graduate level?" No.** Cloaked ship, ship without power, lethal stress point: all three are GAPS in the ADVANCED Course rule (evasion is an Advanced rule, PDF p.28). Verified in the text: neither Advanced nor Graduate mentions them; the Graduate Course changes only the -2 fire for evaders (arcs from the original heading) and makes accelerator cannons evadable. **Claude's earlier default "a ship with no engine power cannot evade" was wrong against the text**: the book says evasion "may be attempted even if a vessel has no movement left in the combat turn" (and a ship with no power at all cannot exist, because the game ends at zero power). Corrected defaults: a cloaked ship may evade; an immobilised ship may evade; a lethal stress point is allowed with a warning.
**A conflict found in the owner's answer 1 (raised, decision pending).** "Pop-up at the start of the firing phase" and "when the AI has the advantage, let the AI declare then" pull in different directions: the winner of the Tactical Advantage declares fire LAST, so if the AI has it the player declares first and cannot yet know the AI's missiles at the start of the phase. Faithful design: if the player has the advantage the pop-up comes at the start (the AI has declared first); if the AI has it, the player's shots are only DECLARED until a "Lock in fire" step, then the AI declares, then the pop-up, then everything resolves (only with the option ON; OFF stays instant). Simple design: always at the start whoever has the advantage. Recommended: faithful (more work). Both are written in the wishlist.
**Harness lessons.** (1) When the owner's answer pulls two requirements in different directions, say so and lay out the options before building. (2) Re-read the rule text for the cases you proposed defaults for: one default contradicted the book. (3) Clarify jargon that sounds like a typo ("ship") in plain words and with an example from a real log.
**Not verified:** how often the pop-up would stop play for other ships (only the Gorn log was counted).

### 0.170 — Evasion design notes written into the wishlist; the faction colours confirmed from the record (documents only, game unchanged, still v2.91-S202)

**User messages (2026-11-07):** (1) the owner's design idea for evasion: "as a 'missile' is fire, all action/animation is stopped with a pop up window stating that 'evasive maneuvers' can be chosen. Given the dice roll options explaining the likelihood with an animation of rolling (using the corresponding faction color). Does that sound doable? I also feel this should be a selectable option to play with by the player before the game. Some players may not want a stoppage of play/action in the game. There should be a mouse explanation for this option as well before it is selected. Am I missing anything?" (2) "yes. write all of this into the wishlist as design notes under evasion, with nothing built. But also, I thought we'd already come up with faction colors? Blue - fed, Red - Klingon, Green - Romulan, Orange - Gorn, for the orion and independant merchant you even did a mock up of colors for me to pick from. I even stated I liked all of them and told you to remember them for later use."
**What was done.** Design notes written under the evasion bullet of the Advanced Course checklist (wishlist A1): the rule, the proposal, the verdict, the TIMING finding and recommendation, the pop-up contents, the other rules to honour, interruption control, the dice, what else is needed, the open rules, the scope warning; a pointer added to C9. **Nothing was built.**
**The timing finding (the one design decision to make first).** Found by reading the code: the game resolves fire in sequence. The player's shots resolve the instant they are clicked (`fireAllWeapons`, staggered 130 ms; `fireWeapon`); the enemy's volley resolves when the phase is ended (`endPhase` calls `resolveShipFiring`); `aiDecideFire` only records WHETHER the AI will fire (`GS.enemyFireDeclared`), and the AI picks its weapons at resolution. So a pop-up at "a missile is fired at you" would come after the player has fired, while the book says an evading ship cannot fire that phase. Recommended: the pop-up at the START of the firing phase (the AI's missile shots fixed at that moment); the AI evades when the player fires a missile, which cancels its own volley that phase.
**The faction colours: the owner was right, and Claude had missed it.** They are recorded in §0.124 and §0.125-0.126 and in wishlist C9, and live in the game as `TA_FACTION` (about line 3959): Federation blue `#4499ff` / `#2764b8`; Klingon crimson `#e23a52` / `#a01c30` (red); Romulan green `#33bb66` / `#176a3c`; Gorn burnt orange `#c97a3a` / `#8b4a1a`; Orion purple `#aa55cc` / `#74309a`; the independent merchants Obsidian (a dark see-through crystal die, accent `#9bb0d0`), chosen from SIX crystal styles that were presented as a mock-up for the independents (Clear Quartz, Smoky Quartz, Moonstone, Aquamarine, Rose Quartz, Obsidian); the owner liked all six and asked for them to be kept: they are saved in the game (`TA_CRYSTAL_STYLES`) and in `neutral_dice_styles.json`, ready for dice personalisation. (The mock-up was for the independents; Orion's purple came from the original palette choice.) **The catch, already on the wishlist (C9):** only the initiative dice use this palette; the start-screen buttons and ship database (CSS `--kli:#ff6622`, an orange Klingon, and an olive-gold Gorn) and the scan sweeps and viewscreen use two OTHER palettes that disagree with it, so a Klingon is crimson on the dice and orange on the start screen; unifying them is open (C9).
**Correction to an earlier answer.** In the previous reply Claude said the faction colours "exist (I only confirmed Federation blue and Klingon orange)" and that the dice animation "would be new work". Both were wrong or incomplete: it had read one CSS variable instead of searching for the owner's decisions. The faction-coloured d10 drawing exists (`TA_D10_FACES`, `taCrystalDie`); whether the initiative screen's number animation can be reused was not checked.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Before saying what the game "has", search HANDOVER and the wishlist for the owner's earlier decisions, not just the code; the owner's memory was right. (2) When the owner proposes a feature, read how the code orders the events it would interrupt before agreeing to the placement (the timing finding changed the answer). 
**Not verified:** whether the initiative screen's roll animation is reusable; the rules the book leaves open (cloaked or immobilised ships evading).

### 0.169 — What changed in v2.91-S202 (reverse movement needs a stand-still, Intermediate rules); a plasma question answered; one older movement quirk found

**User message (2026-11-07):** "reviewing what's built and what's not, I feel some of this might be appropriate to build make it optional for the player. Just thinking outloud for that. Some of the items are easy to integrate now and I have a question on one: * Reverse movement: it requires standing still the phase before. Built, but the stationary-first rule isn't enforced. --easy to implement. Let's do this. question here: * Romulan plasma: damage drops with range. Built, but simplified (see the difference below). Does this part refer to this: "Plasma: it can be fired at half power."" (An explicit request for the game change; the question about plasma was answered, no change.)
**The plasma question, answered.** No: they are two different rules. "Romulan plasma: damage drops with range. Built, but simplified" is the ADVANCED Course plasma rule (A1): the game has the damage-by-range table (RL), but not the grazes, not evasion, and applies ONE damage-location roll to the whole bolt where the book divides it into 5-point blocks. "Plasma: it can be fired at half power" is a separate GRADUATE Course rule (A19): arm the bolt at half power for half damage; the game has no half-power arming (a plasma weapon always arms at its fixed cost).
**The idea of making rules optional (recorded, not a decision).** The owner is thinking of offering some of the not-yet-built rules as OPTIONAL switches for the player. The setup screen already has house-rule switches (Planets & Moons, nebula, gravity wells); the new Advanced and Graduate rules could be offered the same way before their full settings exist. Noted in the wishlist roadmap; nothing built.
**The change.** The rulebook (Advanced Course, "Moving in Reverse", PDF p.27): "Ships may move in reverse, but they must have remained stationary during the preceding Movement Phase to allow the engineers to make the systems change-over ... In order to go forward again, the ship must remain stationary for one Movement Phase while the original engine configuration is re-established." Now: the player's ship has a drive configuration (forward or reverse); changing it needs the previous Movement Phase to have been a stand-still, and the two cannot be mixed within one phase. **"Stood still" = did not change hex (the meaning the cloak's moving/stationary penalty already uses): turning on the spot does not break it.** A battle starts with the ship at rest; the turn boundary counts (the last Movement Phase of the previous turn is "the preceding phase" of phase 1). **Intermediate ruleset only; Basic keeps its free reverse (the Basic Course has no reverse at all in the book, so this is the game's own choice, unchanged).** Both ways of moving obey it: the arrow keys (`playerStep`) and clicking a hex (`highlightMoveHexes` only offers the allowed hexes; `playerMoveTo` re-checks): a clicked hex is judged by where it lies: on the straight line astern = a reverse move, anywhere else = forward-type (this also stops the click search, which can route around by turning, from slipping behind the rule). Refusals say why in the log ("Cannot reverse yet: the engineers need one Movement Phase standing still ... You moved in the previous Movement Phase." / "...already moved this phase." / "Cannot go forward yet: after reversing ..."), and the movement hint shows the drive ("Drive: forward (reverse available)", "Drive: forward (reverse locked: you moved last phase)", "Drive: REVERSE (forward locked: you reversed last phase)"). Undo restores the drive state with the position. **The AI never reverses** (its code says "Ships cannot reverse"), so nothing changed for it; the player is still the only ship that can back up.
**What was NOT done (and why).** The book's next sentence says "forward and reverse movement may not be made in the same combat turn": stricter than the explicit rule in one case (forward, stand still, reverse inside one turn). The explicit rule is implemented; say if the stricter reading is wanted. Also not done: reverse is still not limited to one hex per phase ("Maximum speed in reverse costs 1 movement point" is ambiguous), heading changes in the same phase as reversing are still allowed (the book says a heading change needs a separate Movement Phase), and emergency heading changes are not in the game at all.
**Verification (real Chromium).** New `testReverse.js`, 24 checks: Basic unchanged (reverse straight after forward still allowed, no drive text); Intermediate: the hint at a battle's start, reverse after a stand-still, carrying on in reverse, forward refused straight after reversing (with the reason) and allowed after a stand-still, reverse refused after a forward move (with the reason) and allowed after a stand-still phase, no mixing within one phase in either order, a phase spent only turning counts as standing still, Undo restores the rule, the hexes astern are NOT offered after a move even with 5 points to route around, a REAL mouse click on the hex astern does nothing while locked and reverses the ship when open, forward hexes vanish after reversing, the previous turn's last movement phase counts, 0 JavaScript errors. New `testReverseFlow.js`, 4 checks: two complete turns in Intermediate through the game's own buttons (Power tab, Commit, Proceed to Combat, the initiative screen's SKIP, End Phase): the phase rollover ran exactly once per Movement Phase (6 for 6), a ship that only held position stayed in forward drive, 0 errors. Regressions on the new build: Damage Control 66 of 66, the entry window, the armed-now line 17 of 17, plasma firing 12 of 12, and the every-weapon sound diff against v2.90-S201 (0 of 14 kinds changed).
**Finding (older, NOT changed, the owner is asked): click-to-move charges only the straight-line distance and does not turn the ship.** Measured on v2.90-S201 (before this change): with 5 movement points, a click on a hex 120 degrees off the bow (not ahead, not a sideslip, not astern) is offered (the search includes routes that turn first), costs 1 point and leaves the facing unchanged: a free one-point step in any direction whenever the ship has spare points. The book's one-point options are forward, sideslip and a heading change; turning first would cost more points. This also means the reverse rule above governs the straight line astern but not the rear-diagonal hexes. Candidate fix: charge the real route cost and apply its turns, or restrict clicks to forward, sideslip and astern hexes.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A rule that can be broken through two input paths (keys, clicks) needs both guarded, and the click path needs a classification that cannot be bypassed by the search's turning routes. (2) Drive the REAL flow in a test: my first flow test stalled three times (the power panel needs its tab opened, Commit then Proceed, the initiative screen needs SKIP); each stall was a flaw in the test, found by printing the game's state, not by guessing. (3) A test must not re-enter a phase: entering it twice rolls the rule's memory twice (one check failed for that reason and was fixed in the test, not the game).
**Not verified:** the book's diagram of reverse movement options (a picture, not in the text); Firefox and Safari; feel in play.

### 0.168 — Owner decision: the ruleset roadmap (Advanced, Graduate, Command & Control as official stages); the Command & Control course broken down (game unchanged, still v2.90-S201)

**User message (2026-11-07), from the desktop:** "I think the advanced section should probably be officially added to the wishlist. Looks like we're already working through it anyway. might as well make it official. The Graduate part should also. (what I was referring to as advanced with the RPG elements and the like.) For now though, keep the intermediate setting. No change to the game at this time. We'll use "intermediate" as a place hold up until finally we advanced fully built out. And then the graduate section will be a totally separate setting. Finally, please break down the Command & Control course (officers and skill rolls) as well. Final goal here is to build out the game in its entirety. We just have to do it in stages."
**Decisions recorded.** (1) Advanced Course = official item **A1** (rewritten from "Advanced ruleset tier"), with the book's sections as a checklist and their status. (2) Graduate Course = official item **A19**, **a totally separate setting**. (3) **Intermediate stays as it is, a placeholder, until Advanced is fully built; then Advanced replaces it.** (4) **No change to the game at this time.** (5) The final goal is the whole game, built in stages. (6) Command & Control is listed as **A20** so that the roadmap is complete; the owner asked for its breakdown but did not yet say it is a setting: **to be confirmed**. The wishlist now opens section A with a "Ruleset roadmap" table (stages 0 to 4) and tags A4 to A13 with their courses.
**Where the "RPG" parts really are (a clarification given to the owner, to be confirmed by him).** The owner called the Graduate part "advanced with the RPG elements". In the book: the captain's Skill Rating and the crew's Crew Efficiency, with victory points and advancement, are in the ADVANCED Course's campaign rules; the bridge officers with their own skill rolls and DEX are the COMMAND & CONTROL course; the GRADUATE Course is the detail tier (detailed damage tables, stress charts, weapon repair, lasers, outposts), not an RPG layer. The book also builds each course on the one before: Command & Control assumes the players know Advanced Starship Tactics and the gamemaster Graduate Starship Tactics; its text twice says "Expert" where the Graduate Course is meant (an older name, by inference).
**THE COMMAND & CONTROL COURSE (book pp. 40-53), broken down from the rulebook text.**
*What it is.* A role-play course: three players and a gamemaster (the "Instructor"). Each player plays one bridge officer; the Instructor plays the enemy ship and everyone else, and judges. The combat systems (power, movement, fire, damage) are the Advanced Course's; the Instructor runs his ships with the Graduate Course's Master Control Panel. It also lets players of the FASA Star Trek role-playing game re-enact ship combat with their full characters.
*Roles.* **Captain** (the three players pick one of themselves; the Captain also plays one of the other roles; he has no panel): decides when to raise shields, open fire and how to manoeuvre, gives general orders, asks for status reports; the Helmsman never arms or fires without his direct order. **Chief Engineer**: finds Total Power Units Available, allocates power to movement, weapons and shields; powers systems down after engine damage. **Helmsman**: calculates movement points, moves the counter, arms, targets and fires weapons (counts the range, rolls the die), makes emergency heading changes and warp-speed changes. **Science Officer/Navigator**: sensors and their questions, energises the shields, rolls hit locations on the Detailed Damage Location Charts, records stress and crew casualties.
*Panels.* Three two-page Command Control Panels: the Engineering Panel (power), the Helm and Weapons Panel (movement points, warp speed, stress charts, firing charts, weapon tracks with Unarmed / Armed / Damaged), the Sensors/Damage Control Panel (sensors track, superstructure track, crew casualty tracks with the die-roll modifiers they cause, the six shield tracks); the Instructor uses a Master Control Panel for each ship he controls. Engine damage forces the Chief Engineer to power systems down (movement or weapons or shields, his choice, no reallocation).
*Skills and ratings.* Every skill and the DEX rating is created by rolling three dice and adding 45 (48 to 75, average 60). Rolls are PERCENTILE: equal to or below the rating succeeds. Captain: Starship Combat Strategy/Tactics. Chief Engineer: Warp Drive Technology, Astronautics. Helmsman: Starship Helm Operation, Ship's Weaponry Technology Operation. Science Officer/Navigator: Deflector Shield Technology, Damage Control Procedures, Starship Sensors, Starship Communications Procedures. Everyone: DEX.
*The skill rolls (what each gives).* **Captain, Tactical Advantage:** each turn the Captain rolls one die and adds his Strategy/Tactics rating; the Instructor does the same for the enemy captain; the higher total has the Tactical Advantage. **Chief Engineer, once a turn in the Skill Roll Phase, one of three:** Extra Power (Warp Drive Technology: +1 power point, or +2 on a roll of 05 or less); Engine Repair (Astronautics: repair 1 damage point on an engine, 2 on 05 or less, effective from the next turn; includes stress damage); Emergency Warp Speed Change (Warp Drive Technology: lets the Helmsman change warp speed by two steps instead of one; the opposing Chief Engineer must roll to follow a fleeing ship). **Helmsman:** To-Hit Bonus (twice a turn, roll against Ship's Weaponry Operation; success makes that Firing Phase's die rolls count one lower, +1 to hit, applied to one weapon or bank); Emergency Heading Change (once a turn, against Starship Helm Operation: success cuts the stress by 1 point and figures the extra damage as one warp factor slower; the book's example: Enterprise at warp 8, 6 power units lost becomes 3, superstructure damage 3 becomes 1). **Science Officer/Navigator, one roll in the Skill Roll Phase against Deflector Shield Technology OR Damage Control, applied to one of four things:** Extra Shield Protection (+2 shield points anywhere, even above the maximum but never more than 2 over it; +4 on 05 or less; lasts that turn); Damage Control (reduce penetrating damage by half a die roll rounded up, 1 to 5, split as he likes, decided after targets are declared and before the die; it does not reduce casualties or repair anything); Superstructure Repair (1 point, 2 on 05 or less); Reducing Casualties (5%). In the Sensors Phase: Starship Sensors roll for the lock (with a 20-point penalty to scan for a cloaked Romulan, which only lets him scan one firing arc each Movement Phase); questions per Movement Phase = skill / 10 rounded up (more than three: the extra ones spread over later phases), and EACH question needs another Starship Sensors roll to interpret the answer. Other: Preventing Ship Explosions (when superstructure damage would go below 0: roll against Damage Control with +10% for each point below zero; failure kills everyone aboard and may hurt nearby ships); Difficult Communications Tasks (Starship Communications Procedures; failure means try again next turn).
*Bridge hits and DEX rolls (end of the Firing Phase in which the location is rolled).* For every 5 damage points or part, the Science Officer rolls one die twice: first which officers are shaken (1-3 none, 4-6 Science Officer, 7-9 Helmsman, 10 both), then which combat systems (communications/damage control, sensors, shields, helm, weapons; high results shake several: reroll 2 to 4 times; the OCR of this table is partly garbled). A shaken officer rolls percentile against DEX: failure means he cannot work the next Movement/Firing Phase and may reroll at the end of the next Firing Phase; a shaken Science Officer asks no questions, reduces no damage, rolls no hit locations; a shaken Helmsman fires nothing and the ship moves straight; an officer still shaken at the next Power Allocation cannot reset his panel (no new shields or lock; no new weapons or speed change). A shaken system is repaired by its officer over the next Movement and Firing Phases and a skill roll at the end of the next Firing Phase (failure: reroll the following phase with +5%); meanwhile it counts as unpowered. **Engineering out** (engine-room hit): the Chief Engineer rolls against DEX; failure also means power cuts are random; and all power is withdrawn for the next Movement/Firing Phase (no shields, weapons or movement; movement points and locks lost until next turn) until he rolls against Astronautics (then back after one phase; else another phase, reroll at +5%); the settings are kept.
*Sequence of play (22 steps).* **Skill Roll Phase first** (the Chief Engineer and the Science Officer roll); Power Allocation (Chief Engineer allocates and applies any bonus power; Helmsman calculates movement and arms beams; the Captain gives general orders; Science Officer energises shields and applies any bonus shield points); Tactical Advantage (Captain's roll); Sensors Phase (the Science Officer's lock roll); then three rounds of Movement (questions asked; stress damage assessed; Helmsman's skill roll to reduce it) and Firing (targets declared, the Tactical Advantage holder last; the Weapon Firing Sequence for outgoing fire; the Damage Sequence for incoming fire; power-down decisions by the Chief Engineer; panels adjusted); panels reset at the end of the turn; the game ends when the gamemaster's goal is reached or he judges it cannot be.
*Information model.* **Without a sensor lock, a hit is resolved in secret by the gamemaster** (the shield result and the hit location are not told to the target's captain); with a lock, the Science Officer is told whether the shield was penetrated and rolls the location himself.
*Expanding.* Four players: the Captain as his only job, or split Helm and Weapons (the Captain steers, a Weapon Officer fires). Five players: two ships head to head, three players each, no gamemaster; or also split the Science Officer's job (sensors and damage control; the Navigator takes the shields). Six: also a Communications Officer (damage control and communications). Further splits are not recommended.
*Campaigns and scenario.* Use the Graduate Course campaign rules; no initial advancement points (the initial skill ratings stand); victory points are divided equally among the roles (the Captain's go to Strategy/Tactics, the others' to whichever skill each chooses); a ship that must be abandoned: the officers may ask to move to another ship as a unit, or create new characters; rotate the roles. Scenario: The Kobayashi Maru (a Federation vessel against a Klingon battle group; exit the Klingon side within 15 turns with superstructure and engines at least one-third intact).
*What it would need in the game* (inference, for the later design): named officers with skill and DEX ratings and a place to keep them; a Skill Roll Phase and percentile rolls; the bonuses above wired into power, shields, to-hit, stress and repair; the Graduate detailed tables (bridge and engineering locations) as the source of bridge hits; per-role panels (or one view per officer); an Instructor (the AI, or a human); hot-seat or multiplayer (A12) to give each human an officer; and A4 and A5 as the first pieces.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A request to "make it official" is a roadmap change, not a game change: record the decision verbatim, change only the documents, and say so. (2) When the owner's term ("advanced with the RPG elements") does not match the book's structure, say where the parts really are instead of silently re-labelling them. (3) Read the whole course before breaking it down (the skill rolls are in three separate places: the roles, the skill-roll sections and the sequence of play).
**Not verified:** the exact die ranges of the "Combat Systems Shaken" table (garbled in the text); the Command & Control course's own Kobayashi Maru scenario notes beyond what is quoted; whether the owner wants Command & Control as a separate setting (A20 is listed pending his confirmation).

### 0.167 — The book's courses broken down (Basic, Advanced, Graduate) against what the game implements; a plasma difference found (game unchanged, still v2.90-S201)

**User message (2026-11-06):** "In a bullet point fashion break down each version of the game. Basic, Advanced and graduate." Answered from the rulebook text (its contents page, the RULES_DATA summary, and the passages themselves) and from the game code.
**The structure.** The book has four courses, each adding to the one before: Basic (pp. 6-21), Advanced (pp. 22-33), Graduate (pp. 34-39) and Command & Control (a role-play course: officers and skill rolls); an Expert Course is mentioned only in passing (stress damage). **The game offers two rulesets: BASIC ("Fast play ... Cloak is simplified (homebrew)") and INTERMEDIATE ("Adds a Sensors Phase, sensor locks + intel, and faithful FASA cloak detection with to-hit penalties"). Intermediate is the game's own name for a CUT of the book's Advanced Course; there is no Advanced or Graduate ruleset (A1 is the Advanced tier).**
**Basic Course (all built):** two ships, a Master Control Panel each; three Movement and Firing rounds a turn; Tactical Advantage by movement points (fewest moves first and declares fire first); power split between movement, shields and weapons with no carry-over; 1-point moves (forward, rotate, sideslip, hold; no reverse); changing warp speed loses the game; Fire/No Fire counters; d10 to-hit by range and chart; beams do the power put in (+ close-range modifier), missiles a fixed damage for a fixed arming cost; six shield faces; the Simplified Damage Location Table; no repairs.
**Advanced Course (partly built, as Intermediate):** BUILT: the Sensors Phase, locks and the nine questions, sensor shadows (planets, moons), the cloaking device with detection and the +3/+5 to-hit penalty, reverse movement, Romulan plasma (range-based damage). NOT BUILT: emergency heading changes and their stress, tactical heading changes, evading missile fire, mines, ship explosions hurting nearby ships (the maths exists, never called: A6), systems repair (A5), Romulan plasma grazes and evasion, dividing plasma damage into 5-point blocks, the campaign rules (captain Skill Rating, Crew Efficiency, advancement, victory points), rescue by beaming to a ship within 4 hexes, self-destruct (A7).
**Graduate Course (not built):** the three Detailed Damage Location Tables (A forward, B amidships, C aft engines; six columns by shield face) with warp, impulse, bridge, engineering (Shield Power Grid, Weaponry Power Grid, Maneuver Power Converter) and crew-casualty effects; engine stress by warp speed (A8); evaders may still fire at -2; the Slim Chance table when to-hit falls to 0 or less; lasers (power up to twice the maximum buys two shots in separate phases) and accelerator cannons (missile fire, evadable); Romulan plasma at half power; heavy hits make repairs harder; weapon repair (A18); self-destruct rules; defense outposts (A13). The game has the Federation lasers and cannons as weapons but I found no two-shot or half-power code.
**DIFFERENCE FOUND (nothing changed; the owner is asked):** the Advanced Course says plasma damage that gets past the shields is divided into 5-point blocks, each with its own roll on the Simplified Damage Location Table, and that the target may graze (Skill Rating roll: half damage) or evade (half damage on another shield, no firing that phase). **The game applies the table damage with ONE location roll for the whole bolt**: in the 2026-11-06 22:25 log a single roll (6, engine) put all 30 penetrating points into the SS-3's engine and cut its power to 6, where the book would have rolled six separate 5-point blocks. Also not found: enforcement of the book's rule that a ship must have stood still in the previous Movement Phase before it may reverse (movement is by arrow keys: forward and reverse are always available).
**Harness lessons.** (1) A "break down the versions" question must separate the BOOK's tiers from the GAME's tiers: they differ in number and in name. (2) Reading a rule next to a real log exposes differences a code search alone does not (the single plasma location roll). (3) A note in HANDOVER that "the book names only two tiers" was wrong for weeks: check notes that say "the book has no X" against the contents page.
**Not verified:** the Command & Control course in detail; whether the game's reverse movement has a stationary-first rule hidden in the movement code (I found none); lasers' two-shot rule in play.

### 0.166 — Rules questions answered from the rulebook (sensor lock, warping out, weapon repair); weapon repair added to the wishlist as A18 (game unchanged, still v2.90-S201)

**User messages (2026-11-06):** "what are the rules for weapon lock?"; "for the 'warp out' part, are there any qualifiers as to when such an action should take place? Or is it totally up to the player's judgement?"; "Are there any rules to allow fixing of damaged weapons?"; then "Yes. Add weapon repair to the wishlist". Each was answered from the rulebook text in the project and from the game code (not from memory); only the last asked for a document change (wishlist A18, nothing in the game). Recorded here so a later session does not have to look it up again.
**Sensor lock (there is no separate "weapon lock").** *Rules (pp. 26-27, 31):* a lock is needed for INFORMATION, not to fire at a visible ship ("vessels in sensor contact ... can fire on one another"). Each Sensors Phase one lock roll: d10, 1-6; range is the whole mapsheet; a planet or moon in the way blocks it (mutual sensor shadow); the lock stays until the sensing ship tries another target, its sensors are knocked out, or the target's weapons hit it; a lock gives class, race, name, whether the target is locked on you, and one of nine questions per Sensors Phase. Cloaked ships: the scan REPLACES the lock; choose a shield arc, roll d10 against the Cloak Detection Table (range 1-10: stationary 3 / lock 6, moving 5 / lock 8; 11-20: 2 / 5, 4 / 7; 21-30: 1 / 4, 3 / 6; none beyond 30; the "lock" columns are the +3 for having detected it last phase); success gives the position and a firing solution with a to-hit penalty of 3 (moving) or 5 (stationary); failure loses it. *The game (Intermediate ruleset only; the Basic ruleset has no Sensors Phases): `playerAttemptLock` (d10 <= 6, one roll per phase, `losBlocked` for planets), `askSensorQuestion` (one of the nine per phase), `playerScanCloak` and `cloakDetectThreshold` (the table above, `CLOAK_DETECT`), `aiDoSensors` (the AI's lock roll, and its chance to scan the right arc against a cloaked player by difficulty: 15%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 100%, 100%); a hit on the locking ship drops its lock (Intermediate only); engaging a cloak drops every lock on it; a cloaked ship cannot fire; in the Basic ruleset a cloaked ship cannot be fired on at all.* **Differences from the book found (nothing changed; the owner was asked and has not decided):** (1) the rulebook says damaged sensors stop the ship firing weapons or warping out; in the game a sensor hit lowers `ship.sensors` by 3 per damage point (percent), at 0 you cannot lock or scan, but NOTHING stops weapons firing; (2) the book says a lock is lost immediately when sensors are hit; the enemy's is dropped at its next Sensors Phase (`aiDoSensors`), but no code drops the PLAYER's existing lock.
**Warping out.** *Rules:* in the Basic Course, changing warp speed is "a valid tactic" but the captain "has abandoned the field to his opponent", removes his counter and LOSES THE GAME; no condition on when (no phase, damage or range limit was found). Hard blocks: damaged sensors (the ship "cannot warp out or fire weapons", lock lost, until repaired); superstructure at 0 or below (the ship cannot fire or move; "usually" the captain surrenders or self-destructs). Scenarios override: the Kobayashi Maru may be left only by the Klingon edge within 15 turns with superstructure and engines at least one third intact, and leaving any other way or "by increasing warp speed" is an automatic Klingon win; a ship that drifts off the mapsheet is re-centred unless the scenario makes leaving a victory condition. Alternative: abandon ship by beaming to a friendly ship or base within 4 hexes (counts as an opposing victory; the captain keeps his Skill Rating, the Crew Efficiency Rating is lost). Flavour, not a rule: "Federation, Gorn, and Orions will never destroy their own vessels, for they all believe that to 'run away and live to fight another day' is a good proverb." *The game has NO warp-out or disengage action* (the only "disengage" in the code is the cloak); a battle ends by destruction or by power loss (the "adrift" ending). **Open (the owner was asked, no answer):** whether to put a warp-out option on the wishlist (the simplest version follows the Basic rule: leaving ends the battle as a loss).
**Weapon repair (the rules behind A18).** Graduate Course only ("In the Graduate Course, weapons may be repaired"). Before it the book lets you repair sensors and shield generators (Systems Repair Rolls) and engines and superstructure (Crew Efficiency roll), not weapons. Status track Oper / Dmgd / Repd / Inop; first hit = Dmgd, unusable until repaired; Repair Roll in a Repair/Repower Phase instead of another system (one per phase): d10 1-8 beams, 1-6 missiles; success = Repd; a second hit = Inop for the rest of the combat; no roll in the phase right after the hit (one Firing Phase without damage to that system must pass); repaired weapons: -1 to the To-Hit Number per shot (banked: -1 per repaired weapon in the bank) and repaired beams powered to at most half their Maximum Power (rounded down).
