The general failed-roll bonus (+1 to the next roll on that system) probably applies. *The game:* a hit weapon is destroyed (`alive=false`, chosen by `pickWeaponLoss`: the cheapest weapon that bears on the shooter); the Damage Control tooltip says "Crew repair is not in the game yet, so damage is permanent for this battle"; the Repower phase only re-energises shields. Added to the wishlist as **A18** (rules, what it would take, six open design questions); A5 now points to it.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A "what are the rules" question gets the rulebook text AND the code, because the two can differ (two differences were found this time). (2) Search the book for every qualifier before saying there are none (the sensors-down block on warping out is in the damage rules, not the warp section). (3) Do not add a difference to the wishlist until the owner says so: ask, and record the finding in HANDOVER meanwhile.
**Not verified:** the Advanced Course may hold further warp-out or repair wording that the text search did not return (the OCR of this book is imperfect in places); the page numbers are the ones the game's own comments use (pp. 26-27 and 31 for sensors).

### 0.165 — What changed in v2.90-S201 (new bridge sounds: Romulan, Klingon and the Federation Motion Picture-era Enterprise bridge)

**User message (2026-11-06), with three recordings (`03romulanbridge.mp3`, `29_klingon_bridge.mp3`, `01enterprisebbridge.mp3`):** "I'm providing new bridge sounds. Right now all you have is procedurally generated ones and one for TOS bridge. for any romulan player they hear '03romulanbridge'. For klingon they will hear '29_klingon_bridge'. for any ship that is of the TMP era for the federation, they will hear '01enterprisebbridge'. As for the other factions, we'll leave them alone for now." (An explicit request for the game, so the standing rule is met.)
**What plays now.** Every Romulan player (12 ships) hears the Romulan bridge; every Klingon player (18) the Klingon bridge; every Federation ship of the Motion Picture era (14 of the 28: Enterprise refit Mk I to III, Federation II Mk I and II, Chandley Mk II and III, Excelsior Mk I and II, Reliant Mk II, Baker Mk IV, Andor Mk II, Northampton Mk II, Gagarin Mk I, by `SHIP_ERA`) the Enterprise bridge; the other 14 Federation ships (original series: Constitution Mk I to III, Chandley Mk I, Loknar Mk II, Baker Mk II, Larson Mk VII, Remora Mk III, Federation I Mk I to VI) keep the TOS bridge; the Gorn (3) and Orion (2) players are unchanged (the generated Federation bed). A bed behaves exactly as the TOS bridge always did: it starts at Engage, plays under the Tactical and Power Allocation tabs, fades out on Damage Control where the recorded hum replaces it, fades back in, and fades out and stops at the end of the battle. The generated beds and the Power tab pad no longer play for these players. The new beds fade in over 3 s at Engage; the door swoosh (a TOS bridge sound) stays with the TOS bed only. If a bed cannot be decoded, the game falls back to the generated bed (tested).
**How it was built.** The whole recordings were NOT embedded (60 s, 131 s and 192 s; 1.9, 2.1 and 3.1 MB of audio: about 9 MB more in a 12.7 MB game). Each bed is a seamless LOOP cut from its recording, found by searching for the steadiest stretch whose end continues best into its start (searched at a low sample rate, refined at the full rate to 30 ms), blended at the seam with a CONSTANT-POWER crossfade whose gains are computed from the measured correlation of the two overlapping pieces (g = sqrt(1 + rho sin 2θ)), peak-normalised to -3 dBFS, and encoded as MP3 **64 kbps joint stereo** (measured against the loop: waveform correlation 0.9974 to 0.9996, every band within 0.02 dB, stereo width unchanged, decoded length exact; 96 and 128 kbps were not needed because the beds are almost all below 500 Hz). Romulan: 18.72 s from 27.0 s of the file (rho 0.65, crossfade 1.5 s, 150,300 bytes); Klingon: 18.87 s from 36.0 s (rho 0.86, 1.5 s, 151,554 bytes); Enterprise: 21.75 s from 138.0 s (rho 0.51, 2.0 s, 174,541 bytes; very wide stereo, left and right correlation 0.01, preserved). Total +639 KB; the game is 13,300,407 bytes. A loop is played whole (`ls 0`, `le null`), which relies on the decoder honouring the MP3's gapless header: tested (the decoded length is exact and the first and last 20 ms are not silent).
**Seams (the thing most likely to be heard).** Judged against how the loop itself varies, not against zero (the beds wobble by 1.5 to 3 dB over 0.1 s): the deepest dip within 2 s of the wrap against the same measure elsewhere in the same loop, in the browser's own decoder: Romulan -3.70 dB (median elsewhere -4.32, worst -5.99; 84% of other places dip as much or more), Klingon -4.05 (-4.04; 48%), Enterprise -3.22 (-3.27; 58%); the spectrum across the wrap matches as well as it does inside the loops. **The first design failed this:** a linear or equal-power crossfade left dips of -3.8, -3.6 and -2.4 dB against wobbles of 2.9, 2.2 and 1.5 dB; the correlation-aware law fixed it. The Romulan loop's peak had also overshot full scale (+0.3 dBFS) in the blend, found on the first run and fixed by the normalisation.
**Level (the owner may want to change it).** Each bed's RMS is matched to the TOS bed's, which plays at -30.8 dBFS RMS: gains **Romulan 0.205, Klingon 0.230, Enterprise 0.218** (`BRIDGE_BEDS[...].gain`); all four measure -30.8 dBFS RMS as played in the browser. That is also close to the Klingon and Enterprise files' own level (-29.3 and -30.5 dBFS). **But the Klingon and Enterprise beds are mostly deep rumble (83% and 73% under 120 Hz), so by A-weighting (how loud they sound) they come out about 16 and 15 dB below the TOS bed, and the Romulan (mid-bass, centroid 316 Hz) about 6 dB below.** Matching by A-weighting instead would take gains of 0.41, 1.50 and 1.30, which would put the two rumbles near -15 dBFS RMS (overpowering on a subwoofer), so the RMS match was chosen; if the Klingon or Enterprise bed is too quiet, raise its `gain` in `BRIDGE_BEDS`.
**Verification (real Chromium).** New `testBridge.js`, 42 checks over six captains (Romulan V-8 Type 4; Klingon D-7 S; Federation TMP Enterprise refit Mk I; Federation TOS Constitution Mk II; Gorn SS-3; Orion Wanderer), each pressing the real Engage button and using the real tab buttons: the right bed starts; one looping source of the right recording, looped whole; the level after the fade; the door timer only for the TOS bed; no generated bed under it; Damage Control fades it to 0 and the hum replaces it; Power Allocation brings it back with the generated pad off; the Tactical Map never restarts it; the Gorn and Orion have no recorded bridge and still hear the generated bed. New `testBridge2.js`, 10 checks: levels as played, durations, edges, seams, **the Federation TOS bridge buffer is identical to v2.89-S200 sample for sample (998,600 samples, equal checksums)**, and a corrupted Klingon bed falls back to the generated Klingon bed. New `testBridgeEnd.js`, 6 checks: the bed fades out and stops at the end of the battle (Klingon, Romulan, Federation TMP). Regressions: the every-weapon sound diff against v2.89-S200 (0 of 14 weapon kinds changed), plasma firing 12 of 12, plasma loading 11 of 11, the armed-now line 17 of 17, Damage Control 66 of 66, the entry window, explosions, torpedo paths 20 of 20, the 246-weapon look scope (0 wrong) and the Federation enemy volley; 0 JavaScript errors anywhere.
**Findings and mistakes (all in my tests, none in the game).** (1) My first restart check counted every looping source, but the Damage Control hum is one too; the check now counts the bed's own recording. (2) My first fallback test corrupted the file after the faction had already been chosen, which had triggered the early decode of the good copy; it now corrupts first. (3) A helper function was spliced into page code from the wrong side. Each was fixed in the test and the game was not touched to make a test pass.
**Notes.** A Federation TMP ship still hears the TOS console chirps on Commit and Proceed (those are Federation sounds) and no door swoosh; the Klingon and Romulan players still hear nothing on Commit and Proceed. The Federation TOS bed is prefetched when a Federation player is chosen (the ship is not known yet); the TMP bed decodes at Engage (a small file, no audible delay expected). The Power tab's generated hum (48 and 180 Hz, scaled by the allocation) still plays for everyone; the generated Power pad now plays only for the Gorn and Orions.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Judge a loop's seam against the same statistic elsewhere in the loop, not against zero. (2) Choose a crossfade law from the measured correlation of what is being blended. (3) When beds differ in spectrum, level them by RMS AND report the A-weighted gap. (4) Test a fallback by breaking the input BEFORE anything decodes it early. (5) Count only the sources you mean when asserting "never restarted". (6) Prove an unchanged bed is unchanged by a checksum of its decoded samples.
**Not verified:** how the beds SOUND in play and whether the levels feel right (the A-weighted gap above); the Enterprise, Klingon and Romulan beds on a real device or in a browser other than Chromium; the era classification of the Federation ships relies on `SHIP_ERA` (section 6 of FASA_TOS_to_TMP_Timeline.md). **Open:** the Gorn and Orion bridges (waiting for recordings); the levels; Klingon and Romulan console chirps (still silent); whether TMP-era Federation ships should keep the TOS chirps.

### 0.164 — A full AUDIT of the game's sound, the "replace all procedurally generated sounds" project, and a documentation catch-up (game unchanged, still v2.89-S200)

*Status as of v2.89-S200. v2.90-S201 (§0.165) then replaced the Klingon, Romulan and Federation Motion Picture bridge beds with recordings: the ambience figures below are from before that change (now 6 ambience recordings and 4 generated ambience systems).*

**User message (2026-11-06):** "works great! sounds solid! please update all doc. for the wish list i want to take care of all sounds -replacing all procedurally generated sounds." (about the plasma firing sound of §0.163).
**How the audit was done (from the code, not from memory).** Read `snd()` and every call of it; searched the whole file for every other function that creates oscillators, noise buffers or filters; listed every embedded base64 recording; traced which ambience each faction gets; read the commit, proceed and arming call sites. Game v2.89-S200, 2026-11-06.
**RECORDED or designed (done).** The 13 clips of `UI_SFX_B64` (audio sizes): `plasma_fire` 76 KB, `gor_torpedo` 29, `rom_torpedo` 22, `plasma_load` 29, `gorn_beam` 19, `kli_tos_disruptor` 24, `fed_door` 10, `fed_phaser` 13, `ship_explosion` 10, `fed_torp_load` 17, `fed_torp_fire` 28, `fed_commit` 16, `fed_proceed` 20; and three ambience recordings: `SETUP_AMB_B64` 22 KB (setup screen), `FED_BR_B64` 132 KB (the Federation TOS bridge, for Federation players only: `startFedBridge` is called when `playerFaction==='fed'`), `DMG_HUM_B64` 54 KB (the Damage Control hum bed).
**GENERATED (to replace): 10 one-shot sounds in `snd()` and 6 ambience systems, 16 families.** *One-shots:* `phaser` (0.3 s sine sweep 800 to 200 Hz; used for every beam without a clip: Romulan RB 62 weapons on 12 ships, newer Klingon KD 82 on 15 ships, Orion OD 10 on 2 ships, via `WEAPON_SFX`); `torpedo` (0.6 s, sine 200 to 80 Hz plus saw 150 to 60 Hz; Klingon KP 19 weapons on 9 ships, Orion FP 4 on 1 ship, and the fallback); `explosion` (0.6 s low-passed noise burst: the impact of any hit that goes through via `impactFX`, plus shield-generator-destroyed ~5337, engine hit ~5363, superstructure hit ~5378, and the fallback of the destruction clip ~8107); `shieldhit` (0.25 s saw 300 to 150 Hz: a shield absorbs a whole hit, `impactFX` ~4939); `miss` (0.15 s 220 Hz; the only `snd` a deferred shot still plays itself, `rsnd` ~5233 and ~10330); `move` (0.1 s blip 440 to 880 Hz; 5 call sites); `phase` (two tones 330 and 440 Hz; 3 call sites); `tactical` (three tones 220, 330, 440 Hz; ~4099); `victory` and `defeat` (~5703). *Ambience (6 systems):* (1) the Power tab hum `initHum` (sines at 48 and 180 Hz scaled by the allocated power); (2) the Power tab pad `startPwrAmb` (36 and 108 Hz); (3) the Federation procedural bed `startTacAmbFed` with the sensor sweep ping `doSweep`, which is also what GORN and ORION players hear on the Tactical tab; (4) the Klingon bed `startTacAmbKli` with irregular blips `doKliBlip`; (5) the Romulan bed `startTacAmbRom` (a dark sawtooth drone with a slow sweep; its chirp `doRomChirp` is defined but NEVER CALLED: dead code); (6) the Damage Control reactive layers `startDmgAmb` and `updateDmgAmb` (groan 58 Hz, formant "voice" chatter 280, 340 and 420 Hz with a random cadence, buzz 880 Hz, alert tones 660 and 880 Hz square, silent until critical) laid over the recorded hum bed. (In the wishlist table (1) and (2) share one row.)
**SILENT (not generated, missing).** Commit and proceed for every faction except the Federation (`playFactionSfx` has only a Federation table); arming sounds for everything except Federation weapons and plasma-type weapons (a Klingon, Romulan, Gorn or Orion beam or torpedo makes no sound when selected).
**Who hears what, by player faction.** Federation: the recorded chirps, bridge bed, door and hum bed, with the generated Power tab hum and pad, impacts, movement and Damage Control layers. Klingon and Romulan: the generated tactical bed (and blips) instead of the bridge recording, no chirps. Gorn and Orion: the generated Federation bed and sweep, no chirps.
**The method and a proposed order** are in wishlist C10 (design in a tool, check it is distinct, encode at a bitrate chosen by content, level by measurement, hook by faction, weapon type or event, test with the every-weapon diff, natural volleys and the regressions; ONLY when the owner asks). Proposed order, by how often a sound is heard (the owner decides): 1 the Romulan, newer Klingon and Orion beams, 2 hit, shield and miss, 3 the Klingon and Orion torpedoes, 4 move, phase, tactical, victory and defeat, 5 the silent interface events, 6 ambience beds.
**Documentation catch-up (the owner asked for all documents to be updated).** *README:* three wrong counts corrected against the game (**63 playable ships, not 44; 103 catalogued hulls (Federation 35, Klingon 23, Romulan 40, Gorn 3, Orion 2), not 78; 40 front-view portraits, not 22**), the Sound bullet (which stopped at v2.73) rewritten, bullets added for the weapon looks and the Armed-now line, the Klingon weapons bay and Sound tools sections updated (six looks; the plasma bank recording; Fire pops; Download this tool; the plan). *HANDOVER:* the header's stale "TOOLS (...game unchanged)" clause replaced (tool links, the sound project, a second standing rule), a SOUND PROJECT block in the master state, a sound and effects bullet in section 1, the sound and effects code locations in section 5, **eleven missing rows (19 to 29) in the combat log ledger**, and the turn counts of §0.157 corrected. *Wishlist:* the header's build and date, C10 rewritten as the all-sounds project with the full inventory table, D10 (keep the ledger current), a Completed entry. *FASA_TOS_to_TMP_Timeline.md:* a note on where its table is used in the game (`SHIP_ERA`). The project's own copies of these documents in the owner's Claude project are OLDER than these and should be replaced (HANDOVER's hand-off checklist).
**Mistakes of mine found and corrected.** (1) **The ledger rule (2026-09-24: every combat log gets a row in the same session) had not been followed for eleven logs (2026-11-01 to 2026-11-06); the ledger ended at row 18 (2026-10-05).** Fixed: rows 19 to 29 (rows 19 to 25 retrospective, facts from the logs themselves). (2) **Turn counts in §0.157 were wrong by one:** the 2026-11-06 12:04 log has 9 turns, cloaked 1 to 7, decloaked 8, won 9 (the debrief's 21 cloaked windows are 7 turns x 3); the section said 6, 7 and 8 and "won on the eighth turn", and the owner was told "six turns" in conversation; corrected in place, and the ledger row has the right numbers. (3) Three README facts had been stale for many builds (above).
**Harness lessons.** (1) An inventory of a sound system must come from the CODE: grep every audio node constructor and every call site, and list the embedded recordings; the generated sounds live in two layers (`snd()` and the ambience functions) and some events are simply silent. (2) Re-read the STANDING RULES before closing a review of a log: the ledger rule exists to be applied. (3) Check every number in a document against the game before repeating it (three were wrong). (4) A parser's "outcome unknown" must be settled by reading the log (the SS-3 win was a cascade hit that the pattern missed); count turns by listing the Power Allocation blocks with their cloak lines.
**Counts checked against the game on 2026-11-06 (playable ships only; a registry-only base entry adds 1 RB, 2 KD and 1 KP that nobody can fly):** Federation FH and FL 158 weapons on 28 ships; Federation FP 66 on 23 and FAC 6 on 3; Gorn GBL 18 and GP 12 on 3; older Klingon D-7 bolt beams 8 on 3 ships (D-7 A 2, C 4, G 2); Klingon KD generated 82 on 15; Klingon KP 19 on 9; Klingon RPL 2 on 2; Orion OD 10 on 2 and FP 4 on 1; Romulan RB 62 on 12, RP 14 on 4, RPL 5 on 5 (plus 1 registry-only). **An earlier summary to the owner gave RB 63, KP 20, KD on "about 17 ships" and 10 older-D-7 beams: those counts included the registry-only entries or were rounded; the figures here are the exact ones.**
**Not verified:** the README's long list of hulls with artwork (written at an earlier build; only the count was replaced); what the sessions behind ledger rows 19 to 25 concluded (the rows carry the log's facts and the debrief's tier, not those sessions' findings); the ambience and the Gorn and Orion use of the Federation bed were read from the code, not heard; the proposed order is a judgement. **Open:** the owner chooses the order and sends the next recipe; the combined lab (C13).

### 0.163 — What changed in v2.89-S200 (the plasma weapons' FIRING sound: "flame roar and spit")

**User message (2026-11-06):** "option b is best in my opinion. 'flame roar and spit'. let's add that for all plasma firing." So candidate B of §0.162 is the firing sound of the plasma weapons, in the game. (Explicit request for the game, so the standing rule is met.)
**Where it plays.** `plasma_fire` in the `plasma` branch of `triggerWeaponFX` (replacing the synthesised `snd('torpedo')`, which stays only as the fallback if the clip is not decoded yet): **every plasma-TYPE weapon, either side: the Romulan bolt tubes (RPL-2 and the others, 6 weapons) and the Klingon D-7 G and R (RPL-1, 2 weapons): 8 weapons in all.** NOT the Romulan RP and Gorn GP torpedoes (they have their own sounds, §0.160), not the loading sound (§0.160, untouched), no beam, no look.
**The sound.** Recipe `recipe_sound_plasma_firing_B_flame_roar_and_spit.json` (§0.162: a sine ignition thump 120 Hz down to 42 Hz under a pink-noise roar, band-pass sweeping 2.6 kHz to 450 Hz, with 70 pops a second of 6 ms at level 230%, noise bed 75%, light crunch, drive and a small space; 2.4 s, stereo), rendered by the lab's own engine and encoded as MP3. **Encoding choice, measured:** the 128 kbps encode (38 KB) blurred the pops (13.9 abrupt pop onsets a second against 16.7 in the original render, 17% fewer; correlation 0.9931); 192 kbps kept 15.6 (0.9982); **256 kbps (77 KB) keeps all 16.7 with the same irregularity (0.86) and kurtosis, correlation 0.9994, so 256 kbps stereo is what is in the game** (about 40 KB more than 128 kbps in a 12.7 MB file; the other clips are tonal and sound the same at 128 kbps). Decoded in the browser: 105,840 samples, same as the render, offset 0, correlation 0.99938 and 0.99935. Not onset-trimmed (the clip begins with the thump), voice cap 3.
**Level: PLEASE NOTE it is quieter than the sound it replaces.** Gain 0.46: the loudest 300 ms matches the Federation torpedo LAUNCH (-19.0 dBFS; an exact match needs 0.484, trimmed 0.6 dB for consistency with the Gorn and Romulan torpedoes, which were trimmed 0.8 dB). Single shot: **peak -9.4 dBFS and loudest 300 ms about -19.4 dBFS, against -3.0 and -17.1 for the old synthesised plasma sound: about 2.3 dB quieter by loudness and 6 dB lower in peak.** Natural volleys on the real audio output (peaks, new against old, none clipped): player Romulan V-8 Type 4 (6 volleys) **0.40-0.55 against 0.68-0.96**; player Klingon D-7 G (5) **0.60-0.67 against 0.74-0.95**; enemy Romulan V-8 Type 4 (5) **0.37-0.50 against 0.72-0.81**; enemy Klingon D-7 G (5) **0.62-0.78 against 0.76-0.96**. If the owner wants the plasma bolt as LOUD as it was, one number does it: `UI_SFX_GAIN.plasma_fire` 0.46 to about 0.60 (loudest 300 ms -17.1 dBFS, peak about -7 dBFS).
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) **A diff of what every weapon of every ship plays against v2.88-S199: exactly 2 of 14 weapon kinds changed (Romulan plasma 6 and Klingon plasma 2, from the synthesised torpedo sound to `plasma_fire`); the other 12 are identical**; 0 JavaScript errors. (2) Real fire paths, 12 of 12: the Romulan V-8 Type 4 and the Klingon D-7 G as PLAYER (the weapon armed by clicking its name: the loading sound plays once; FIRE: ONE firing sound, 0 synthesised torpedo sounds, the old plasma effect once, no spoke torpedo, the result still held until the bolt lands) and as ENEMY of a Federation player (one firing sound per plasma shot, 0 synthesised, the phase completes). (3) The plasma loading tests, 11 of 11, untouched. (4) Regressions: the 246-weapon torpedo look scope (0 wrong), torpedo flight, kill and AI tests (12 of 12), the Romulan, Gorn and Orion torpedo paths (20 of 20), the 17-ship bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn beam scope, arming sounds for all factions, the Federation enemy volley (3 phaser and 2 launch clips, none synthesised), the armed-weapons line (17 of 17), Damage Control (66 of 66), explosions and the entry window.
**Findings.** (1) A noisy, popping sound needs a higher MP3 bitrate than a tonal one: always compare a pop-heavy clip's pop count before and after encoding, not just its correlation. (2) The plasma ships fire one bolt per volley, so the loudest plasma volleys are small; the new sound's lower peak removes the (small) clipping risk the old hot blip had. (3) `plasma_fire` and `plasma_load` are both from the owner's Torpedo Lab and distinct from each other (the loading swells and is dark, the firing hits first and crackles).
**Harness lessons.** (1) After an encode, test the property the sound is CHOSEN for (the crackle), not only the waveform match. (2) State the level change against the sound being replaced (peak, loudest 300 ms and natural volleys) and give the one number that undoes it.
**Not verified:** how it SOUNDS in play (the level is matched by measurement, not by ear) and whether the owner wants it louder (see above). **Open:** the level choice; if the owner retunes candidate B in the Torpedo Lab, it must be re-encoded (256 kbps) and re-levelled; sounds for the Romulan, newer Klingon and Orion beams and the Klingon and Orion torpedoes (still synthesised); the plasma LOOK (the reference pictures show a roiling fireball ball; the game's plasma is still the old orange effect).

### 0.162 — The Torpedo Lab gets a FIRE POPS control; three "crackling bolt" candidates for the plasma weapon's firing sound (game unchanged, still v2.88-S199)

**User message (2026-11-06), seven screenshots of the original-series Romulan plasma weapon:** "watching videos of the plasma has that 'crackling bolt' with flaming sounds gives that vibe to me. just take a look at the visuals." (an answer to the question in §0.161 about the firing sound's character).
**What the pictures show.** A roiling plasma BALL, not a streak: a seething yellow-white core with swirling tendrils inside a ragged orange-to-red shell (images 1 to 4), which then swells into a large soft red mass (image 5) and finally floods the whole viewscreen red (image 6); images 4 and 7 are the same frame. So the sound is FIRE: crackle and flame roar, with the heat growing as the ball swells. (Note for later: this reference differs from the game's plasma LOOK, which is still the old orange effect; no look was changed.)
**The lab change (a tool, not the game).** The Torpedo Lab's "Crackle rate" only gates the noise on and off at REGULAR steps (up to 150 a second), which makes a rattle, not a fire. Layer 5 (roar and crackle) now has four new controls: **Fire pops** (0 to 300 per second: sparse, irregular pops laid on the noise, a Poisson stream of short decaying noise bursts of random size and sign, fixed random seeds so a sound repeats), **Pop length** (1 to 40 ms), **Pop level** (0 to 300%) and **Noise bed level** (0 to 100%: turn the hiss down to hear pops alone). Defaults: 0 pops, bed 100%: the code is skipped and every existing sound is unchanged. Older recipes without the four settings load with those defaults (tested); new recipes carry them.
**Preservation check (sample by sample, previous published lab against this one, 13 sounds: every preset and the owner's three sound recipes):** 12 bit-identical or identical apart from the reverb's own float noise (below -80 dBFS, which appears on a different preset on each run). The 13th, the owner's **Romulan torpedo recipe, differs by one step (0.0039) in about 190 of 119,072 samples, but the PREVIOUS lab differs from ITSELF by exactly the same** when the recipe is rendered twice: it is the reverb's float noise flipping a step of that recipe's 9-bit crunch (0.0039 = 1/256), inaudible at -48 dBFS against a -3 dBFS peak, and was there before this change.
**The three candidates (presets in the lab, just before Blank; recipe files `recipe_sound_plasma_firing_A_crackling_bolt.json`, `..._B_flame_roar_and_spit.json`, `..._C_plasma_bank_with_fire_pops.json`).** *A, crackling bolt:* your explosion recording (high-passed 150 Hz, low-passed 3.5 kHz, 4 semitones up, 60%) for the flame body, plus a noise layer of bright pops (85 a second, 5 ms, level 190%, bed 18%, band-pass sweeping 3.8 kHz to 1.5 kHz), a little drive and a small space; 2.3 s. *B, flame roar and spit:* a sine ignition thump (120 Hz down to 42 Hz) under a pink-noise roar (band-pass sweeping 2.6 kHz to 450 Hz) with pops (70 a second, 6 ms, level 230%, bed 75%), light crunch (10 bits), drive and space; 2.4 s. *C, plasma bank with fire pops:* the plasma bank's surge and ring at 38% (high-passed 300 Hz, low-passed 7 kHz) under pops ONLY (150 a second, 3 ms, level 300%, bed 0, high-pass sweeping 2.2 kHz to 5.2 kHz); 2.3 s. **Measured (offline, the lab's own renders):** audible length (within 30 dB of the peak) 2.05 s, 2.15 s and 2.05 s against 1.75 s for the Gorn torpedo and the Federation launch; all LOUDEST in the first 0.05 s (front-loaded, unlike the loading sound's swell at 1.1 s); **abrupt crackle onsets per second (a sharp jump in the 2 kHz+ level within a few ms): A 42, B 17, C 66, against 10.6 for the Gorn torpedo, 5.0 for the Federation launch, 0.6 for the Romulan torpedo and about 1 for the loading sound**; spacing irregularity 0.58, 0.86 and 0.65 (1.0 is random like a fire; a regular pulse is near 0; the old synthesised sound scores 0.30). The zoomed spectrograms show dense vertical streaks (pops) for all three and none for the Federation launch (`plasma_firing_candidates.png`). **Distinct from everything in the game and from each other (21 pairs; correlation at best lag, spectrum difference):** the highest correlation is 0.211 (B against the Romulan torpedo: both carry a low sine thump sweeping down), all others 0.136 or lower; spectrum differences 5.7 to 21.5 dB (A is closest to the Federation launch in tonal balance at 5.7 dB; C is farthest, 12 to 21.5 dB); C against the loading sound (both from the plasma bank) has correlation 0.004 and a 21 dB spectrum difference.
**Verification (real Chromium).** New `testPops.js`, 13 of 13: a layer with 0 pops and bed 0 is silent; the pop RATE (10, 20 and 40 a second give 15, 28 and 48 separate pops in 1.8 s against 16, 28 and 45 expected from a random stream with a 15 ms merge window); Pop length sets how long a pop lasts (2.0 ms against 17.0 ms for 2 ms and 30 ms settings); Pop level 200% against 100% is exactly 2.00 x; Noise bed 50% is exactly 0.50 x; rendering with pops is repeatable sample for sample; the three presets render exactly the sounds measured (largest difference 0.0000); an old recipe loads with pops 0, length 8, level 100, bed 100; a new recipe carries and restores the four settings; the four sliders exist, the keyboard moves Fire pops (85 to 90) and the Layer 5 reset returns it to 85. Earlier suites on the new build: UI 15, layout 12, reset 14, export 13, plasma bank 13, Download this tool 13 (the saved copy renders the identical sound), and the 35-case feature render sweep (slowest 659 ms), 0 JavaScript errors. The lab is republished at its existing link (downloads enabled) and is in outputs.
**Findings and corrections.** (1) **My first crackle test was misleading and I replaced it:** counting peaks in the 1.5 to 8 kHz envelope scored the Federation launch recording at 29 a second (above candidate B) because its pulsing texture makes peaks; crackle is SUDDEN and IRREGULAR, so the test now counts abrupt onsets and the irregularity of their spacing. (2) **My first candidates failed my own checks:** C was drowned by the bank's bright tone (1.7 pops a second), B's pops passed through a filter sweeping down to 320 Hz and came out as low thumps (1.7 a second), and all three were over in about a second despite 2 s files (the lab's decays are exponential): fixed by quieting the tone and raising the pops, opening B's filter, and slowing the noise decays so the sound is present for the whole flight. (3) **Pop length changes how long a pop lasts (a tick or a puff), NOT how bright it is** (a decaying noise burst is white at any length): my first test assumed otherwise and was wrong. (4) The old "Crackle rate" is a regular gate: it will still sound like a buzz or rattle; use Fire pops for fire. (5) B and the Romulan torpedo share a low sine thump (correlation 0.21): if B is chosen and should be more different, move its thump pitch.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Calibrate a new metric on KNOWN sounds first (the Federation launch scoring as "crackly" exposed the first test as wrong); (2) check what a layer's filter does to the new content before trusting it (B's pops); (3) a sound file's length is not its audible length: measure the time within 30 dB of the peak; (4) when a tool is changed, prove the OLD sounds are unchanged sample by sample AND compare the old tool with itself, or a difference may be blamed on the change when it was always there.
**Not verified:** how any of the three SOUNDS (I cannot hear; the pops, length, front-loading and distinctness are measured, the character is the owner's call); the plasma firing sound is NOT in the game (the plasma weapons' firing still plays the synthesised torpedo sound). **Open:** the owner auditions A, B and C in the Torpedo Lab (it is the preset list; Fire pops, Pop length, Pop level and Noise bed are in Layer 5), tunes one and sends the recipe; then it is encoded, levelled against the Federation launch (-19.0 dBFS loudest 300 ms) and hooked into the `plasma` branch of `triggerWeaponFX`, as for the loading sound, but only when the owner asks.

### 0.161 — Review of the owner's Romulan-against-Gorn session, and a design brief for the plasma weapon's FIRING sound (game unchanged, still v2.88-S199)

**User message (2026-11-06), with a combat log (BUILD v2.88-S199):** "just played a romulan bird of prey against the gorn. I won! That was fun! The load plasma weapon was solid for the romulan. The sounds from the gorn firing weapons worked well. I need to find a good firing sound for the plasma weapon though. review the combat log provided." So the loading sound (§0.160) and the Gorn torpedo and beam sounds are liked; what is still wanted is a sound for the plasma weapon FIRING (it still plays the synthesised torpedo sound, 0.9 s).
**The session.** Player: RIS Talon (V-8 Bird of Prey Type 4: hull 15 boxes, shields up to 11 a face, RB-6 beam max power 6 arcs F / F-Stbd / F-Port range 18, **RPL-2 plasma arc F only, range 14, arming cost 15**, cloak cost 15). Enemy: SS-3 Class VI Destroyer (AI rated CAPTAIN; hull 20 boxes, shields up to 12 a face, four GBL-3 beams max power 3, range 15, two GP-3 torpedoes cost 2 each, range 14). Won on turn 7. *Turns 1 and 2:* cloaked (6 cloaked windows), Move only (13 to 4 move points), closing from hex 19,8 to 14,8. The Gorn detected the cloak in turn 2 (windows 2 and 3) and fired GBL-3 x2 and GP-3 at range 4: with the +3 moving penalty the bands were 1-4 and 1-2 (not impossible, unlike the Constitution's 1-0 in the earlier log), and **one beam hit for 3: engine hit, the Talon's power 28 to 25** (later 23). *Turn 3:* cloak off, RPL-2 armed (15; the game auto-reduced a manual shield setting that no longer fitted the lower power); the Talon turned twice (facing 2, then 1) and **fired in the second window at range 3 from the Gorn's aft quarter: hit (needed 7 or less, rolled 1), RL-2 = 32 damage, the aft shield absorbed 2, 30 penetrated, location roll 6: ENGINE: the SS-3's power fell to 6.** The Gorn's return fire that turn found only 2 of its 5 weapons in arc (the rest said "Target not in arc"); a GP-3 hit for 8 was absorbed by the shield, a GBL-3 hit for 2 hit the Talon's engine. *Turns 4 to 7:* **the crippled Gorn allocated Move 4 to 1, Shields 2, Weapons 0 every turn and never fired again.** Turn 4: RPL-2 armed (15 points) but NOT fired (no fire line; the RPL-2 covers only the forward arc and the Gorn was rotating; the log cannot say whether it was out of arc or held; 15 points spent for nothing). Turn 5: RB-6 armed (6), fired at range 4: miss. Turn 6: RPL-2 at range 5: hit (6 or less needed, rolled 2), 24 damage (shield absorbed 1), location 1: the F-Stbd shield generator destroyed. Turn 7: RB-6 and RPL-2 (21 points): RB-6 hit for 6 (destroyed a GP-3 tube), **RPL-2 hit at range 5 for 24, location 9: hull -24 against 20 boxes: destroyed.** Debrief (the game's own): 13 open windows, all answered; the enemy's blind side held for 4 windows; the 3 hits taken all landed on the forward shield; average range 4.2 hexes.
**Plasma use in numbers.** Armed 4 times (60 power points), fired 3 times, **3 of 3 hit (chart M gave 70%, 60% and 60%), 80 damage in all (32 + 24 + 24)**; the RB-6 fired twice: 1 hit, 1 miss. All three shots were at range 3 to 5, from outside the target's arcs or into its weaker faces. As in §0.157, the engine hit was the decisive effect of the first bolt: **one plasma hit through 2 shield points crippled a whole ship for the rest of the fight** (power 6: no weapons).
**NOTES FOR THE AI, added to C14 (nothing built).** (1) **A crippled AI does nothing.** With power 6 the SS-3 allocated Move 4 and Shields 2 and nothing to weapons for four turns while the player sat at range 4 to 5: its two GP-3 torpedoes cost only 2 each and a GBL-3 beam works on 1 point, so it could have armed both torpedoes (4) or a beam; an AI with little power should spend it on something that can still hurt (or run), not on 1 point of movement and 2 points of shield spread over six faces. (2) **Shields cannot save a ship from the RPL-2 up close**: the Gorn's whole shield (12 points over six faces, about 2 a face) absorbed 2 of 32; even a full 12-point face leaves 20 of 32 through, as much as the SS-3's hull: only range, arc and engines matter (the owner's play again: close under cloak, strike from the target's blind quarter). (3) **The AI's detection of a cloaked ship works at CAPTAIN** (it fired at range 4 with a real chance and scored an engine hit): the difference from ENSIGN is that its shots had a chance. (4) **A tip for players (not a bug):** the RPL-2's 15 points are spent at commit; if the bolt cannot bear that turn (forward arc only) they are lost (turn 4).
**BRIEF for the plasma weapon's FIRING sound (from the log and the game's rules).** *When it plays:* once, at the instant the bolt is fired (player or AI), in the `plasma` branch of `triggerWeaponFX`; the impact explosion is a separate sound at landing, and the owner's LOADING sound already plays when the weapon is armed (a 1.8 s slow swell, loudest near 1.0 s). *How long the bolt flies* (the plasma effect, 60 frames a second): **0.48 s a hex: range 1 = 0.5 s, 2 = 1.0 s, 3 = 1.4 s, 4 = 1.9 s, 5 = 2.4 s, 6 = 2.9 s, 8 = 3.8 s, 10 = 4.8 s, 14 = 6.7 s.** In the owner's session the shots were at range 3, 5 and 5 (1.4 s, 2.4 s, 2.4 s); the old synthesised sound lasts 0.9 s and is over well before the bolt lands, so a firing sound of **about 1.5 to 2.5 s** would cover the typical shot (a 3 s tail would cover range 6); a plasma bolt is also much SLOWER than a torpedo (2.1 hexes a second against 5.4), so its sound should not be the same size as the torpedo's. *Shape:* the loading sound swells; the firing sound should be front-loaded (a clear launch at 0 s) so the two are not confusable; it must also stay distinct from the Gorn torpedo (loudest at 0 s, 383 Hz centroid), the Romulan torpedo (46% under 120 Hz) and the Federation launch (smooth decay, 590 Hz): the §0.160 comparison method (correlation, third-octave difference, loudness shape) can check any candidate. *Material the owner already has in the Torpedo Lab:* the plasma bank (its surge-and-ring part is the source "Plasma bank: the surge and ring"), the torpedo launch and explosion recordings, the TOS disruptor, and the synthesised layers. *Level:* match the loudest 300 ms to the Federation torpedo launch (-19.0 dBFS) as for the other sounds, then check the biggest plasma volleys (the Romulan V-8 and the Klingon D-7 G and R carry only one or two RPL tubes, so a volley is small).
**Harness lessons.** (1) Read a log for what was ARMED against what was FIRED (turn 4: 15 points armed, nothing fired). (2) The weapons' ranges and the effects' speeds decide how long a sound should last: compute the flight times before choosing a length. **Not verified:** that a 1.5 to 2.5 s firing sound is what the owner wants to hear (it follows the flight times; the character is the owner's call). **Open:** the plasma firing sound itself (the owner is looking for one; candidate presets can be built in the Torpedo Lab, which is tooling, on request); C14.

### 0.160 — What changed in v2.88-S199 (three new sounds from the Torpedo Lab: the Gorn torpedo, the Romulan torpedo, and a LOADING sound for plasma weapons); the difference check

**User message (2026-11-06), with three Torpedo Lab recipes:** "here is a solid sound for the gorn torpedo weapon" (recipe 1); "Here is a good sound for the 'loading' sound for any plasma weapon. before encoding, make sure recipes actually differ from one another" (recipe 2); "for any romulan torpedo firing, use this" (recipe 3); "again do a difference for these recipes confirming I've given you distinctive sounds and not accidentally duplicated any of them." The owner asked for these sounds in the game ("use this"), so they are in; the recipes were checked for duplicates BEFORE encoding, as asked. Saved as `recipe_sound_gorn_torpedo.json`, `recipe_sound_plasma_loading.json`, `recipe_sound_romulan_torpedo.json` (exactly as pasted). All three carry the lab's default name field "tos-torpedo" (a label only).
**THE DIFFERENCE CHECK (settings, then sounds). VERDICT: all three are distinct sounds; none is an accidental duplicate; Gorn and Romulan are RELATED.** *Settings:* Gorn and plasma loading differ in **3 settings, and only ONE can change the sound (`L1.src`: `launch` against `bank`)**; the other two (`L2.drop` 380 against 1670, `L4.ratio` 1.41 against 5.44) are on layers switched OFF in both. Gorn is a one-layer sound (L1 only), plasma loading likewise; **Romulan has all five layers on** and differs from each of the others in 28 settings. The lab accepted all three recipes without changing a single setting on loading (0 changed). *Sounds (rendered by the lab's own engine; mono mix; peaks all -3.0 dBFS by the lab's normaliser):* **Gorn:** 1.80 s, centroid 383 Hz, energy under 120 Hz 16.2%, 120-800 Hz 72.6%, 800-3200 Hz 11.2%, loudest at 0.0 s (hits hard, then decays). **Plasma loading:** 1.80 s, centroid 333 Hz, 23.7% / 65.8% / 10.2%, loudest at 1.0 s (a slow swell, then fades), left and right identical (the bank is mono). **Romulan:** 1.35 s, centroid 374 Hz, **45.9% under 120 Hz** / 40.0% / 14.0%, loudest at 0.0 s. *Pairs (an identical pair would be correlation 1.00, spectrum difference 0 dB, loudness-shape match 1.00):* **Gorn / plasma loading: correlation -0.010 (best within +-100 ms 0.085), third-octave spectrum difference 3.8 dB on average and 23.1 dB in the biggest band, loudness-shape match -0.45 (opposite shapes: one decays, one swells): clearly different, though they share a similar tonal balance because the processing is the same.** **Gorn / Romulan: correlation 0.428, 4.0 dB, 13.5 dB, shape 0.85: distinct but related: the Romulan contains the Gorn's pitched-down launch recording as its first layer plus four more, so it is the Gorn's cousin, heavier in the bass, shorter, with a tail of space.** **Plasma loading / Romulan: -0.028, 4.0 dB, 18.9 dB, shape -0.88: unrelated.** *Against what the game played before:* every one is near zero correlation with the Federation torpedo launch (-0.007, -0.019, -0.020) and with the old synthesised torpedo (Gorn -0.020, plasma loading -0.057, Romulan 0.245 because both have a sine sub sweep), with 8.6 to 11.5 dB of average spectrum difference; plasma loading against the raw plasma bank correlation 0.005 (centroid 333 Hz against 2128 Hz: the bank slowed and darkened). Picture: `sound_recipes_compared.png`.
**The encoding.** Each lab render written losslessly and encoded with LAME at 128 kbps: Gorn and Romulan STEREO (the launch recording is wide stereo: left and right differ by about as much as they share), plasma loading MONO (identical channels). 29,719, 22,613 and 29,719 bytes (about 108 KB of base64 in the game). Decoded in the browser each MP3 has the **same length as the lab render (79,380, 59,536, 79,380 samples), offset 0, correlation 0.9987, 1.0000, 0.9988** (the gapless header is honoured).
**What plays where (`UI_SFX_B64` keys `gor_torpedo`, `rom_torpedo`, `plasma_load`).** (1) **`gor_torpedo`: every Gorn missile-type weapon (the GP-2 and GP-3, 12 weapons), either side**; (2) **`rom_torpedo`: every Romulan missile-type weapon (the RP-2 and RP-3, 14 weapons), either side**: both through the existing per-faction clip mechanism (`FACTION_SFX.rom` and `.gor`, only `torpFire`; `playSfxFor(shooter.faction,'torpFire')` in the missile branch of `triggerWeaponFX`); (3) **`plasma_load`: when the PLAYER arms a plasma-type weapon (the RPL tubes of the Romulans and the Klingon D-7 G and R), any faction, by weapon type** (`togArm`; played once on arming, nothing on disarming; the AI has no arming sound). **NOT changed: the plasma-type weapons' FIRING sound (still the synthesised torpedo sound), every beam, the Klingon KP and Orion FP torpedoes, the Federation clips, every look.** Gains (single-shot loudest 300 ms matched to the Federation torpedo LAUNCH at -19.0 dBFS and LOAD sound at -20.5 dBFS): matched gains 0.64 (Gorn), 0.66 (Romulan), 0.51 (plasma loading); the two torpedo gains were then **trimmed 0.8 dB to 0.58 and 0.60** because the Gorn BH-2 (8 beams and 4 torpedoes at once) clipped in 1 volley of 22 at 0.64 (peak 1.01); onset trim on for the two torpedo clips (onset 9 ms and 0 ms), OFF for the plasma loading (its quiet swell would be cut); voice caps 3, 3 and 2; no limiter.
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) **A diff of what every weapon of every ship plays against v2.87-S198 (clips identified by their audio object, because two of the new clips are the same length): exactly 2 of 14 weapon kinds changed (Gorn GP 12 from the synthesised torpedo sound to `gor_torpedo`, Romulan RP 14 to `rom_torpedo`); the other 12 are unchanged** (including the plasma tubes' firing sound, the Orion and Klingon torpedoes, all beams). (2) Plasma loading, 11 of 11 checks with real clicks on weapon names: a Romulan RPL-2 and a Klingon RPL-1 play it once on arming, nothing on disarming; a Romulan RB-4 beam, a Romulan RP torpedo tube and a Federation torpedo tube do not (the Federation still plays its own load clip once); five in quick succession never keep more than 2 alive; the clips load whole (79,380 mono, 79,380 stereo, 59,536 stereo samples). (3) Volleys on the real audio output, new build against the previous synthesised sound, **no clipping at the final gains**: player Romulan Nova (6 torpedo clips, 12 beams) peaks 0.77-0.80 at gain 0.66 against 0.81-0.88 before, and 6 volleys at 0.60 max 0.89; enemy Romulan Nova 6 volleys max 0.72; player Gorn BH-2 (4 torpedo clips, 8 beams) 12 volleys at 0.58 max 0.88 (at 0.64: 14 volleys, 1 clipped at 1.01); enemy Gorn BH-2 6 volleys max 0.74. Every volley shows 0 synthesised torpedo sounds left. (4) Regressions: the 246-weapon torpedo look scope (0 wrong), torpedo flight, kill and AI tests (12 of 12), the Romulan, Gorn and Orion torpedo paths (20 of 20), the Federation enemy volley (3 phaser and 2 launch clips, none synthesised), the 17-ship bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn beam scope, arming sounds for all factions (the Federation load clip x0 for the others, as expected), the armed-weapons line (17 of 17), Damage Control (66 of 66), explosions and the entry window.
**Findings.** (1) The Gorn and plasma-loading recipes are one setting apart (the source recording): a check by SETTINGS alone would have flagged them as near-duplicates, and one by SOUND shows them to be unlike (the loudness shapes are opposite); the check needs both. (2) The Gorn and Romulan torpedoes share a first layer, so they are family by design. (3) The Gorn and Romulan sounds are stereo because the launch recording is; keep that in mind for any later re-encode. (4) The Gorn BH-2 is the loudest case in the game (8 Gorn beam clips and 4 to 8 torpedo clips): measure it, not a small ship, when levelling a sound. (5) Harness: two clips of the same length must be told apart by identity, not length (`testSfxPathsId.js`).
**Harness lessons.** (1) Compare recipes by settings AND by rendered sound; list which differing settings sit on switched-off layers (they cannot matter). (2) Split a long regression run into batches that each fit the 300 s tool limit and write results to a file (one combined run timed out and lost its output). (3) A single clipped volley in a small sample needs more volleys before a decision: 22 volleys showed it was rare, and a 0.8 dB trim removed it.
**Not verified:** how the three sounds SOUND in play (the levels are matched by measurement, not by ear); that a Romulan or Gorn player hears nothing when ARMING an RP or GP torpedo tube (unchanged from before: only the plasma weapons now have an arming sound). **Open:** a sound for the plasma weapons' FIRING (still the synthesised one); sounds for the Romulan, Klingon and Orion beams and the Klingon and Orion torpedoes (see the sound map in the conversation of 2026-11-06 and wishlist C10); an arming sound for torpedo tubes of the Romulans and the Gorn if wanted.

The corrected recipe differs in ONE number: **`hue` 16** (everything else the same: `len` 40, `flare` 100, `rot` 180, `bright` 25, `tspeed` 265, `count` 8, `irr` 80, `thick` 40, `core` 65, `twinkle` 0, through-the-core ON).

On the map the Gorn torpedo is now a **golden amber** star (picture `game_romulan_gorn_orion_torpedoes.png`: Romulan green, Gorn amber, Orion blue). **About the colour number:** 0 is the film's orange-yellow, positive values go greener (88 is green) and negative values go redder (the K'tinga at -29 is red), so 16 is slightly yellower than 0; a deeper orange would be about 0 to -10 in the tool.

**What went wrong (mine).** The owner said the plasma bank recording was "good audio to incorporate into the weapon audio settings"; that meant the sound TOOLS (the Beam Lab and the Torpedo Lab). The lesson is recorded as the STANDING RULE at the top of this file. The tool changes of §0.155 (the recording as a source in both labs) were wanted and stay.
**The revert (v2.85-S196).** Built from the exact v2.83-S194 file with new version labels only: **3 lines differ from v2.83-S194 (the title, the header label and the startup message); no plasma bank code remains; 12,444,329 bytes** (v2.84-S195 was 12,517,077). Verified: a diff of what EVERY weapon of EVERY ship plays against v2.83-S194 shows **0 weapons changed**, so the 34 plasma-family weapons (Romulan RP and RPL, Gorn GP, Klingon D-7 G and R tubes) play the synthesised `snd('torpedo')` again (a Romulan Nova volley: 0 plasma-bank clips, 6 synthesised torpedo sounds, no clipping); the 246-weapon torpedo look scope (0 wrong), torpedo flight, kill and AI tests (12 of 12), the 17-ship bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn scope, the 17 real-click armed-weapons checks and the Damage Control sweep (66 of 66) all pass. The v2.84-S195 change is fully described in §0.156 (a clip table entry, `isPlasmaWeapon`, gain 0.46, 3 voices, two hooks) should the owner ever ask for it; no patch file is kept.
**Tools: "Download this tool" in the Beam Lab and the Torpedo Lab** (the Klingon weapons bay had it since §0.149). A button in each Export row; the page keeps a clean copy of its own source taken BEFORE its script builds anything (`SELF_HTML`, with any scripts, base tag, policy tags or iframes a host added removed), and saves it: in the viewer through the `downloads` capability (`.html` is allowed; the viewer asks the person to confirm; an `extension_not_enabled` answer is reported in words), opened as a file as a plain download. **Verified in real Chromium, 13 of 13 for each lab:** the download is `beam_lab.html` (143 KB) or `torpedo_lab.html` (362 KB), the same size as the original; the saved page is complete and its markup holds no controls (no cards, no preset options); the saved copy opens by itself with no errors and builds the same controls (5 cards and 10 presets, 8 cards and 10 presets) in the same starting state; **the copy renders the IDENTICAL sound to the original (the TOS recording and the plasma bank match to the last digit)**; a real preset click works in the copy; **downloading again from the copy gives a byte-identical file (146,172 and 370,490 bytes)**; in a stand-in for the viewer, `save()` is called once with the right name and a `text/html` Blob and the page says so; declined, not enabled and no-permission cases give a message, a message and a disabled button; a test host that injects its own script, base and policy tags does not get them into the saved file (6 of 6). Earlier suites pass: Beam Lab UI 15, layout 12, reset 14, export 13, plasma bank 15, "Game now" against the game's beam sound 0.999996; Torpedo Lab UI 15, layout 12, reset 14, export 13, plasma bank 13. Both labs republished at their existing links; all three tool files are in outputs (`beam_lab.html`, `torpedo_lab.html`, `klingon_weapons_bay.html`). Picture: `lab_download_buttons.png`.
**THE SESSION (read from the log, then checked against the game's rules and code).** *Ships:* the Talon (V-8 Type 1: hull 15 boxes, shields up to 8 a face, RB-4 beam max power 6 arcs F / F-Stbd / F-Port range 10, **RPL-2 plasma bolt arc F only, range 14, arming cost 15**, cloak cost 15); the Constitution Mk I (hull 20 boxes, shields up to 9 a face, **FL-6 x3 arcs F / F-Stbd / F-Port, FAC-3 x2 arc F only, all range 10, nothing covers its sides or rear**). *The cloaked approach:* turns 1 to 7 under cloak (7 turns x 3 windows = the debrief's 21 cloaked windows) [corrected 2026-11-06: this said turns 1 to 6], every cloaked turn Move only (11 to 3 move points), Shields 0 (11 to 22 once), Weapons 0, "Armed: nothing". The AI detected the cloaked ship in three windows and fired **10 shots (FL-6 x3 and FAC-3 x2, twice) at "need 1-0"** (the cloak's +3 moving or +5 stationary penalty pushes the success band to nothing): certain misses. Its power was the same every turn (Move 8 to 2, Shields 10 to 10, Weapons 18) whatever happened, and it flew straight east (facing 0) and then stopped near hex 13 to 14, 10. *The strike:* the Talon closed to **range 1 on the Constitution's blind quarter**, where all five of its weapons answered "Target not in arc" in the first window. Turn 8 [was written as turn 7]: cloak off, Weapons 21 (RB-4 at 6, RPL-2 at 15); plasma shot 1 missed (needed 8 or less, rolled 10); RB-4 hit for 6 and destroyed the A-Stbd shield generator; the Constitution rotated (facing 3) and, in the second window, hit twice with FL-6 (sensors to 91%, RB-4 destroyed). Turn 9 [was written as turn 8]: **RPL-2 re-armed (15 points: plasma must be armed again every turn)**, shields 2 to 4, move 9 to 3; first window: hit (needed 8 or less, rolled 8): **RL-2 gives 32 damage at range 1; the shield absorbed 2; 30 penetrated; hull -30 against 20 boxes: destroyed.**
**Why range 1 is the whole game for the RPL-2 (numbers from the code: chart M and the RL-2 damage table).** Hit chance and damage by range, and the EXPECTED damage per shot (hit chance x damage): range 1 to 2: 80% x 32 = **25.6**; 3: 70% x 32 = **22.4**; 4: 70% x 24 = 16.8; 5 to 6: 60% x 24 = 14.4; 7 to 8: 50% x 20 = 10.0; 9 to 10: 40% x 16 = 6.4; 11: 30% x 12 = 3.6; 12: 20% x 12 = 2.4; 13 to 14: 10% x 8 = **0.8**. So a shot at point-blank is worth about 30 times a shot at the bolt's maximum range, and 32 damage minus a FULL 9-point shield still leaves 23, more than the Mk I's whole hull (if the location roll sends it to the hull: here it did, roll 7). The owner's play (cloak, close in under it, into the blind arcs, decloak, arm plasma, shoot at range 1) is the way to use it.
**NOTES FOR THE AI (recorded as the owner asked; NOTHING in the AI was changed).** *What the AI already does (from the code):* the sustained-cloak pattern (a cloaked AI spends turns on Move only, then decloaks to strike: Legend decloaks with chance 0.90 at range 3 or less and 0.08 beyond; the other levels decloak at 55 to 75% at range 4 or less, 10 to 20% while still closing, 5 to 12% if the hull is under 40%), the point-blank strike turn (at range 3 or less it arms every usable weapon to its cap), hunting a cloaked target (movement 70%, weapons 10%), and difficulty-dependent tracking of a cloaked ship (last known position at Cadet and Ensign, perfect at Admiral). So at the broad level the AI already plays the pattern the owner played. *Gaps I can see (my reading, not confirmed by the owner):* (1) **no notion of ARCS when closing**: the owner ended on the target's blind quarter and took no return fire in the first window; an AI Romulan could choose its closing and decloak hex by which of the target's weapons bear on it. (2) **Nothing plasma-specific**: the strike rule is range-based but does not use the damage-by-range table above (decloak at 3 or less, plasma first priority on the strike turn, the beams with what is left, the plasma re-armed every turn). (3) **As a DEFENDER at ENSIGN the AI is passive against a cloaked plasma ship**: fixed power split every turn (Shields 10 against a 15-cost plasma bolt), 10 shots at 0% chance, straight-line movement, no turning to put its forward arcs on the last known position, no keeping its distance from it (plasma damage is small beyond 7 hexes). *Possible AI behaviours, for the owner to approve (not built):* AI Romulan: close under cloak into the target's blind arcs, decloak at 3 hexes or less, arm the plasma first on the strike turn, fire in the first window, keep 15 points for re-arming; AI defender: when a cloaked contact is detected or lost within about 6 hexes, do not fire shots with no chance, turn its arcs toward the last known position, move the shields to that side, and stay away from it. Wishlist C14.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A message that mentions a tool's result and "incorporate" is about the TOOL until the owner says otherwise: ask before touching the game. (2) Keep v2.83-S194's exact file as the revert base and prove "nothing else changed" with a line diff (3 lines) and the every-weapon sound diff (0 changed): the reverted build was verified in minutes. (3) The sound diff test's "expected change" list must be flipped when the change is reversed: its four FAIL lines this turn were the OLD expectation. (4) Compute a table of expected values (hit chance x damage) in code rather than by hand before writing it into notes.
**Not verified:** the reverted game was tested in Chromium only; the plasma sound in the owner's real sessions is only what the owner reports (the sound changed, which is what was wanted back); the AI notes are my reading of the code and one log and need the owner's judgement before anything is built. **Open:** C14 (the AI notes above); the owner's decision on the combined lab (C13); the earlier open items.

### 0.156 — What changed in v2.84-S195 (PLASMA WEAPONS PLAY THE OWNER'S PLASMA BANK RECORDING)

**User message (2026-11-05):** "Continue", after the labs were updated and the owner was asked whether the recording should go into the game and for which weapons (§0.155). Read as: go ahead and put it in the game. **The weapons were chosen by me: the PLASMA family only** (the owner had said it works "for either plasma weapon or beam weapon", but beams are a different decision, see Open). The owner may correct this.
**Which weapons (34 in all, found by listing every weapon of all 66 registered ships).** `isPlasmaWeapon(w)`: type `plasma` (the Klingon D-7 G and R tube RPL-1; the Romulan bolt tubes RPL-1, RPL-2, RPL-3: 8 weapons) OR a designation starting `RP-` (the Romulan plasma torpedoes, typed `missile`: 14) or `GP-` (the Gorn plasma launchers, typed `missile`: 12). By faction: Romulan 20, Gorn 12, Klingon 2. The biggest volleys: the Romulan Nova (8 RP-3) and the Gorn BH2 (8 GP-2). NOT in the family: the Klingon KP photon tubes (typed missile), the Orion FP tubes, the Federation torpedoes, every beam.
**The change.** The recording (`plasma_bank`, 53,960 bytes, 71,948 characters of base64, audio identical to the owner's file, §0.155) is in `UI_SFX_B64`; `UI_SFX_GAIN.plasma_bank` = 0.46; `UI_SFX_MAXVOICES.plasma_bank` = 3 (the oldest of a pile-up fades out over 40 ms); NO onset trim (it plays from its first sample) and NO limiter. It plays at the instant the shot is fired, in the two places the old synthesised `snd('torpedo')` was: the `plasma` branch of `triggerWeaponFX` and the `missile` branch when `isPlasmaWeapon(weapon)`; if the clip is not decoded yet the old synthesised sound is the fallback. Either side's ship uses it (the player's or the enemy's). Visuals are UNCHANGED (the old plasma and torpedo effects).
**How the level was chosen (measured on the decoded clips at their game gains).** Loudest 300 ms RMS and peak: the recorded Federation torpedo launch (gain 0.55) -19.0 dBFS / -6.9; the OLD procedural plasma sound -17.1 / -3.0; the raw plasma bank -12.2 / -0.6 (mono decode). **Matching the Federation launch needs a gain of 0.458**, so 0.46 (peak -7.4 dBFS for a single shot).
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) **A diff of what every weapon of every ship plays, previous build against this one: exactly 4 of 14 weapon kinds changed (Romulan RP 14, Romulan RPL 6, Gorn GP 12, Klingon RPL 2, all from the synthesised torpedo sound to `plasma_bank`); the other 10 are unchanged** (the Klingon KP and Orion FP tubes still synthesised; every beam keeps its sound; the Federation and Gorn-beam and old-D-7 clips unchanged); 0 JavaScript errors. (2) Natural volleys on the real audio output, previous build to this one, 4 volleys each, **none clipped**: the player's Romulan Nova (6 plasma tubes bearing plus 12 beams) peaks 0.83-0.90 to 0.75-0.85; the player's Gorn BH2 (4 plasma tubes plus 8 beams) 0.84-0.94 to 0.73-0.80; the enemy Romulan Nova 0.82-0.87 to 0.71-0.87; the enemy Gorn BH2 0.78-0.83 to 0.72-0.79. Every volley shows 0 synthesised torpedo sounds left. (3) The recognition rule: RP-1, RP-3, rp-2, GP-2, GP-3, RPL-1, RPL-2, RPL-3 and the type `plasma` count; KP-4, KP-6, FP-4, FP-1, FAC-3, OD-3, RB-1, RB-4, FH-11, FL-6, GBL-3, KD-8, an empty designation, a missing weapon and a beam without one do not. (4) The clip loads whole (145,774 samples, 3.31 s, mono), plays from offset 0 at gain 0.46, and an eight-tube volley starts all 8 sounds but never keeps more than 3 alive. (5) Regressions: the 246-weapon torpedo look scope (0 wrong), torpedo flight, kill and AI tests (12 of 12), the 17-ship bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn scope, the entry window, explosions and kills, the Damage Control sweep (66 of 66), arming sounds for all other factions, the Armed-now line (17 real-click, 11 style checks, 63 of 63 ships), and the Federation enemy volley (3 phaser and 2 launch clips, none synthesised).
**When the surge lands (CALCULATED from the code at 60 frames a second, not measured: the headless browser redraws slowly).** The recording has a quiet swell for 0.72 s and then a surge. The RP and GP torpedoes use the torpedo effect (0.09 hexes a tick, 5.4 hexes a second), so on a 6-hex shot (1.1 s) the surge lands about 0.4 s before arrival, at about 3.9 hexes out; the RPL bolts use the plasma effect (0.035 hexes a tick, 2.1 hexes a second), so a 6-hex shot takes about 2.9 s, almost exactly the clip's length, with the surge near the start of the flight and the ring carrying to the impact.
**Harness lessons.** (1) The game's clip table is declared with `let` (not a property of `window`): a wait written as `window.uiSfxBuf&&...` can never succeed, and a silent `.catch` had hidden that in an earlier script; name the variable directly and call `prepUiSfx()`. (2) A per-weapon diff of "what plays" over every ship (previous build against new) is the fastest proof of "only these weapons changed". (3) When a sound is far longer than the one it replaces (3.3 s against 0.9 s), measure volleys of the biggest ship, not one shot.
**Not verified:** how it SOUNDS in play (I cannot hear; the level was set by measurement against the Federation launch), the swell-then-surge timing on a real 60 fps screen (calculated, not measured), browsers other than Chromium. **Open:** (a) **BEAMS:** the owner said it works for a beam too; the beams that still use the synthesised sound are the Romulan RB (63 weapons [corrected 2026-11-06: 62 on playable ships, the 63rd is on a registry-only entry]), the Klingon KD (82 on the newer D-7s and others) and the Orion OD (10), while the Federation, Gorn and older D-7 beams have recordings; which beams, if any, should use it is the owner's call; (b) if the quiet 0.72 s swell is unwanted on fast shots, the clip can start at the surge (one small code change); (c) a plasma LOOK (the visual is still the old effect; the owner's Weapon FX Foundry has a plasma type); (d) the combined lab (C13).

### 0.155 — The owner's plasma bank recording added to the Beam Lab and the Torpedo Lab (game unchanged, still v2.83-S194)

**User message (2026-11-05), with `sound-effects-plasmabank.mp3`:** "this is good audio to incorporate into the weapon audio settings. works good for either plasma weapon or beam weapon." Read as: add it as a source in the sound tools (the Beam Lab for the beam use, the Torpedo Lab, titled "photon and plasma sound design", for the plasma use). The GAME was not touched. The owner may correct that reading.
**The recording (measured).** 3.306 s as decoded (3.344 s in the file), mono, 44.1 kHz, 128 kbps, 56,903 bytes, with an embedded picture. Peak -3.6 dBFS, RMS -21.9 dBFS, crest 18.3 dB. **Shape:** a quiet rising swell from the start (about -48 to -31 dB by 0.5 s), a further gradual rise from about 0.60 s, a **surge starting at 0.721 s (+10.3 dB over 40 ms, to about -12.5 dB by 0.77 s)**, a ring that holds near -12 dB to about 1.0 s then fades about 10 dB across 1.1 s (-12.2 dB at 0.8 s, -22.8 dB at 1.9 s), steady bright bands near 3.7, 5.4 and 6.5 kHz to about 1.9 s, then upward-sweeping tones fading out by about 2.9 s. **Spectrum:** 18% of the energy under 120 Hz (strong tones at 33, 79 and 124 Hz), 63% between 800 and 8000 Hz, centroid 2128 Hz, 90% below 4314 Hz. Picture `plasmabank_analysis.png`. **A correction to my own first description:** I said the sound "jumps 17 dB in an instant at 0.72 s"; it actually swells from about 0.60 s and the steep part is about +10 dB over 40 ms from 0.72 s.
**The asset.** The embedded picture was removed WITHOUT re-encoding and WITH the gapless-playback header kept (`ffmpeg -map 0:a -c:a copy -map_metadata -1`, the Xing/LAME header kept): 53,960 bytes (`plasma_bank_recording_clean.mp3` in outputs), decoding **sample-for-sample identical** to the original in ffmpeg and in the browser (145,774 samples, same hash). Removing the header too (`-write_xing 0`) shifted every sample by 1,105 and was rejected.
**What was added, in BOTH labs.** Three choices in the recorded layer's Source list: **"Your plasma bank (whole, 3.3 s)"** (`bank`), **"Plasma bank: the charge-up swell"** (`bankcharge`) and **"Plasma bank: the surge and ring"** (`bankburst`); the split is found from the audio itself at load (`findBurst`: the biggest rise in level over 40 ms between 0.3 and 1.5 s; it finds 720.9 ms, 31,790 samples), as the Torpedo Lab does for its torpedo recording. Two presets in each, **"Plasma bank: your recording, as it is"** and **"Plasma bank: the surge and ring only"**, inserted just before "Blank" so Blank stays last. The test hooks `__lab.src()` and `__lab.srcData()` were extended (no effect on use). Sizes: Beam Lab 69,447 to 144,404 bytes, Torpedo Lab 295,325 to 368,719 bytes. **Beam Lab only: stretchy sliders.** That lab's Layer 1 Trim start (400 ms), Length (1000 ms) and the Total length (2000 ms) were made for short phaser sounds and would cut this recording off, so `applyLimits()` keeps those three ranges for the short sources and stretches them (3300 / 3400 / 3500 ms) only while a plasma bank source is selected; the schema holds the long maxima so recipes keep long values; switching to a short source pulls the long values into the short ranges. **Mutate was fixed:** it picked from the widened schema regardless of source, so it could propose a 2.5 s length for the 60 ms blip; it now uses the selected source's range and clamps at the end. The Torpedo Lab needed none of this (its ranges already reach 2 s trim, 10 s length).
**Verification (real Chromium).** Torpedo Lab 13 of 13 and Beam Lab 15 of 15 new checks: the Source list and presets; the whole source sample-for-sample the browser decode of the owner's file; the split at 720.9 ms with charge-up plus surge (31,790 + 113,984) exactly the whole; **"as it is" reproduces the file at correlation 1.000000 at a steady 0.5 x (the labs' layer gain), error to the last sample**; the surge preset matches the surge slice (1.000000); Pitch +12 st halves the sound (2544 ms to 1272 ms); Reverse moves the loudest moment from 826 ms to about 2480 ms; Trim 720 ms starts on the surge (-23.6 against -49.7 dB in the first 50 ms); Sustain holds the ring (-18.1 dB in the last 200 ms against -125.8 dB); the Beam Lab's sliders keep 400 / 1000 / 2000 for the TOS phaser, stretch to 3300 / 3400 / 3500 for the bank and narrow again on the real dropdown, the End key reaches 3400 ms, a recipe with the bank keeps its long values while the same values on a short source are pulled in; **600 mutations from the bank and from the phaser all sit inside their own source's limits (0 outside; moves on and off the bank 14 and 10 times)**. Earlier suites still pass: Torpedo Lab UI 15, layout 12, reset 14, export 13, determinism, the 35-case feature render; Beam Lab UI 15, layout 12, reset 14, export 13, and "Game now" against the game's own beam sound still 0.999996. Both labs republished at their existing links.
**Test repairs (not product changes).** (1) Tests picked "Blank" by list position (now 9 in the Torpedo Lab, last in the Beam Lab): they pick by label. (2) The Torpedo Lab UI pitch-slider check read a result after a fixed 500 ms wait: it **failed 4 of 4 times on the PREVIOUS published lab** on this slower machine (it had passed 15 of 15 before), so it was timing, not my change; it now waits for the re-render (passes 5 of 5). (3) The old Mutate range test hard-coded the short ranges; it now uses the source's own.
**Findings.** (1) **A sustained loop of the ring is NOT an easy win, and no sustained preset was made:** the ring fades about 10 dB across 1.1 s and even the steadiest 300 ms window (0.90 to 1.20 s) drifts 0.8 dB with only a 0.75 spectral match between its two ends (a shimmering texture, not a flat tone); I cannot judge by ear whether a loop of it sounds smooth, so the Torpedo Lab's Sustain control (loop starts at 900, length 300, smoothing 100) is left for the owner to try. (2) Beam Lab Layer 1's Source dropdown is narrow and shows "Your plasma bank" truncated; the full label is in the list. (3) The labs play layers at half gain (0.5 x) at the 100% level setting; the preset peaks at -3 dBFS through the Output normaliser.
**Not verified:** how any of it SOUNDS (I cannot hear; everything above is measured), the real viewer's saving for the republished pages (tested against a stand-in earlier). **Open:** whether the recording should go INTO THE GAME (for the plasma tubes, which still use the old synthesised torpedo sound, and/or for beams) and for which factions, done as for the Gorn beam (clip, gain and a limiter set by measurement); a plasma look for the visual tools; the combined lab (C13), which should carry it as a source.

### 0.154 — The owner's "Weapon FX Foundry" v0.1 (a plasma weapon tool NOT made in these sessions); a correction to §0.153 item 3

**User message (2026-11-05), with the file `weapon_foundr.html`:** "here's the plasma weapon tool. Does this look familiar?" Kept in outputs as `weapon_fx_foundry_v0.1_owner_upload.html` (43,684 bytes; picture `foundry_three_types.png`).
**Familiar? NO.** Searched the three transcripts, the outputs folder and the game for "foundr": nothing (the game has no `WEAPON_FX` table, 0 hits, and no mention). It was not built in any session I can see; it may come from another conversation or tool, and it is NOT recorded who made it. **This corrects §0.153 item 3**, which said no plasma tool existed: none was made in THESE sessions, but the owner has one.
**What it is (read in full, then run in real Chromium: no JavaScript errors).** Title "Weapon FX Foundry — Star Trek: Tactical Command", header "torpedo test range · tune · save", v0.1, one 595-line page, no external files. A **test range** canvas (1148 x 420) with PROCEDURAL placeholder ships (a wedge aggressor and a saucer target) and a Fire button plus auto-fire. **Projectile type: Torpedo, Beam, Plasma** (segmented control). Sliders: colour (hue, with a swatch), white-hot core, size, speed, opacity, beam length; **glow and trail** (flare, flicker, trail length, trail fade); **impact** (explosion or shield ripple; size, flash, particles). **Sound, three layers:** Launch Kick, Soaring Flight, Impact Blast; each can load a real audio file (level, pitch, tone cutoff, trim start and end, loop, length) with a synthesised fallback (kick pitch and punch; flight tone, air rush, movement; blast crack, concussion, sub pitch, debris, grit, brightness, rumble); Layered or Samples-only mode; master volume and stereo width. **Presets:** a name box, **Save preset (.json)**, **Load preset**, **Copy game config** and **Bake stereo WAV**. How the three types differ: the torpedo is a blue glowing disc with a trail; **plasma is the same drawing at 1.5 x size, 0.7 x speed, with a sideways wobble**; the beam is a straight glowing line for `beamlen` seconds with a ripple at the target.
**What was measured.** Save preset downloads `<name>.json` (878 bytes, 54 numbers; **no audio inside**: only the sample file NAMES go in the "game config", so a reloaded preset needs its sounds loaded again). **"Copy game config" writes `WEAPON_FX['<name>'] = { type, hue, whiteHot, size, speed, opacity, flare, flicker, trail, trailFade, impact, impactSize, flash, particles, mode, dry, width, samples, sound:{kick, flight, impact} };` a table the game does not have**: the game keeps torpedo looks in `TORPFX.recipes` and sounds in its own tables, so the block cannot be pasted in as it stands.
**How it relates to the plan (wishlist C13, the combined lab).** It already has a plasma type, per-layer sample loading, sound baking and presets saved by name as files, so it is a real starting point for the Plasma tab and the Sound tab. It does NOT have: an in-page library to review and reload (the name only becomes a file name); samples stored with a preset; the game's own ship art; the spoke look of the owner's torpedo recipes (its projectile is a glow disc with a trail). Nothing was changed in the game; the plasma tubes (Romulan, Gorn, the D-7 G and R) still use the old effect. To use the Foundry's plasma in the game the owner designs a look and sends the preset .json (and the audio files separately), and it is then built into the game like the spoke torpedoes (new drawing code for the glow-and-trail look, a table entry, the ship era and faction rules).
**Harness lessons.** (1) Say "I have no record of this, it may come from another conversation" rather than guess who made it. (2) Read AND run an unfamiliar tool before characterising it, and check what its export targets in the game (here a table that does not exist). **Open:** the owner's decision on whether the combined lab should start from this tool's plasma type and sound layers; a plasma look designed in it.
