NO, and I looked.** Searched all three transcripts and the owner's list of published artifacts (10: Klingon weapons bay, Torpedo Lab, Beam Lab, The Maru Gambit, The Maru Gambit Story Skeleton, Hull Parts Kit, Nebula Render Lab, Gravity Well Render Lab, Viewscreen Starfield, Federation Console Dossier-Plaque): there is no plasma tool. The closest thing is the **Torpedo Lab, titled "photon and plasma sound design", which has a plasma SOUND preset**; a plasma VISUAL has never been designed in a tool, so the game's Romulan (and Gorn, Klingon D-7 G and R) plasma tubes still use the old effect, and the Gorn plasma launchers GP-n and the Romulan plasma are unchanged.
**4. PROPOSAL (nothing built; waiting for the owner's go-ahead): one combined "weapons and sound lab" with tabs and named recipes.** Tabs: **Beams** (the Beam Lab's sound plus a beam VISUAL), **Bolts** (the TOS D-7 disruptor from the Klingon bay), **Torpedoes** (the Klingon bay's spoke torpedo, three looks to start from), **Plasma** (NEW: starts from "the game's plasma now" and the Torpedo Lab's plasma sound), **Sound** (the Beam Lab and Torpedo Lab layer engines) and **Recipes** (a library). **Recipes with names:** Save as (name, kind such as torpedo look, beam sound, bolt, plasma look; faction and era as optional tags), a list to review, Load, Rename, Delete, Export and Import a file. One recipe format for every kind: `{name, kind, faction, era, params, saved}`; the existing recipes (K'tinga x2, Federation TMP and TOS, the Gorn beam sound) would be imported as the first entries. **"Would this write to disk?" Not literally, and this is the honest picture.** A published page cannot silently write a file to the owner's computer or to Claude's disk (browser safety). There are three real ways: (a) the **`db` capability** keeps the recipes in the artifact's own storage: they survive closing the page, work on any device signed in to the same account, and **Claude can READ them back in any later chat (Artifact `read_db`) and write them (`write_db`)**, so "use the saved recipe 'ktinga 3'" needs no pasting; (b) the **`downloads` capability** lets the page offer a .json file the owner saves (the viewer asks for confirmation each time; `.json` is allowed); (c) **browser storage** (`localStorage`, private to that browser) as the fallback when the page is opened from a downloaded copy (where `db` and `downloads` do not exist). The GAME itself is a local file and cannot read the lab's storage: recipes reach it by Claude baking them into the game (as for the torpedoes and the Gorn sound) or, later, a "load recipes file" button in the game. **Decisions for the owner:** the tab list; whether the OTHER proofs of concept (Nebula Render Lab, Gravity Well Render Lab, Viewscreen Starfield, Hull Parts Kit, Console Dossier) belong in it (they are graphics rather than weapons or sound; the proposal leaves them out); the Plasma tab's reference look (the old TOS plasma bolt is a glowing ball); that a merged page is large (the three tools are about 0.3 to 0.4 MB each with embedded sound, so roughly 1 to 1.2 MB, far under the 16 MB limit) and is the one thing to maintain instead of three.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Never put a `//` comment inside a one-line statement sequence in a test file: it swallows the rest of the line (twice this turn: use a block comment). (2) A test that hard-codes a number the game holds (the K'tinga speed) goes stale on the next recipe: read it from the game. (3) Check a "markup is escaped" test is armed on the SAME item it renames. (4) Before answering "do you remember X?", search the transcripts AND the published list, then say which came back empty.
**Not verified:** how the larger, coloured line reads on the owner's own screen and ship; how the small new K'tinga reads in a real fight (it is much smaller and dimmer than before). **Open:** the combined-lab decisions above; the Federation looks may be tuned later; looks for the Klingon TOS torpedoes, the Romulan, Gorn and Orion missiles and the plasma tubes; a Klingon torpedo sound; the master limiter; a longer minimum flight or brighter Federation looks at 2 to 3 hexes if needed.

### 0.152 — What changed in v2.82-S193 (the Power tab shows what is armed; a combat-log review)

**User messages (2026-11-05), with a combat log of the USS Enterprise (refit) Mk III (the player) against the IKS Devisor D-7 S (K'tinga look), won in three rounds by total power failure:** "played as the Enterprise class against the klingon k'tinga. I may be mistaken, but I did not see all the torpedo effects match up with the number fired. Particularly in the beginning. I thought I'd charged two but only saw one. The visual effects for the federation torpedo seemed adequate. There may be some tweaking down the line but for now, it works. Review the combat log please." After the review, which offered two changes, the next message was cut off ("let'"); it was read as "let's do it" and the two changes were made. The owner may correct that.
**The review (from the log, then replayed in the game).** The opening volley says "FIRE ALL: 2 weapons firing": **FH-11 Bank 4 (a phaser) and FP-4 Tube 1, one torpedo**, so one effect was right. The power line that round, "Weapons 2", is Bank 4 at 1 point plus Tube 1 at 1 point (a torpedo costs `armCost` 1; a beam costs the points the player sets, up to `maxPower` 10; round 2's "Weapons 3" was three torpedoes, round 3's "Weapons 13" was Bank 1 at 10 plus three torpedoes). In that position (Enterprise 7,10 facing east, D-7 at 19,9, range 13) **every weapon was in arc and in range** (beam arcs 0,1,3,5, torpedo arcs 0,3; beam range 24, torpedo range 16), so Tube 2 was not blocked: it was not armed. Whole fight: the player fired 7 torpedoes (1, 3, 3), the enemy 4 (2, 2). Replayed through the real fire paths, every shot made an effect: **opening volley 1 effect (1.6 s on screen); the three-torpedo volley at range 3 made 3 (about 0.55 s each, all three on screen together); the K'tinga's volley made 2 torpedo effects and 3 beam flashes** (launched about 110 ms apart through one large glow; two distinct bright cores). At 2 to 3 hexes a Federation torpedo is a small dim point crossing about one hex in the 0.30 s minimum flight, and three overlap, so they are easy to miscount; the owner called the Federation look adequate.
**Why "charged two, saw one" was possible.** (1) Only the **16 x 16 px arm circle** armed a weapon: a click on the weapon's name, the middle of the row or the arc text did nothing, silently. (2) The torpedo rows sit BELOW the four phaser banks at the bottom of the weapon list (Tube 1 at y=875, Tube 2 at 921, Tube 3 at 967 in a 900 px window: Tube 2 and 3 need scrolling). (3) Nothing on screen or in the log said which weapons were armed; "Weapons 2" is only a number of points. Arming itself is correct: real clicks armed exactly the clicked weapon, no row moved after a click, and the committed armed set matched the clicks.
**The change (three parts).** (1) **The weapon's NAME arms and disarms it, like its circle** (`.wpn-nm` has its own `onclick` calling `togArm` on the row's circle, so a circle click never fires twice). The name cell is wide (about 860 of the row's 1196 px at 1500 px), so a click in the empty middle of the row arms too: that is the bigger target, and the new line below is the feedback; the arc text, the power slider and the hit-chance tag still do nothing; a knocked-out weapon's row is unchanged. The help line now says "click its name or its circle". (2) **A live line `#armed-now` above the rows**: "ARMED NOW: 3 weapons — FH-11 Bank 4 (1 pt), FP-4 Tube 1 (1 pt), FP-4 Tube 2 (1 pt)" in blue; orange "ARMED NOW: nothing. Click a weapon's name or its circle to arm it." when none. `armedList()` reads the buttons and the inputs, `updArmedSummary()` fills it, called at the end of `updPwr()` (every arm click and power change) and at the end of the row build in `initUI()`. (3) **At commit, an "Armed: ..." line** built from the COMMITTED weapon state (`w.armed`, `w.poweredWith`) goes into the combat log (so the exported log names them), the allocation log (`addPlog`) and the confirmation line under the Proceed button ("Armed: nothing" in the combat log when none; with no power at all the confirmation keeps the existing, more urgent "NO POWER ALLOCATED" warning). Picture: `power_tab_armed_now.png`.
**Verification (real Chromium, real mouse clicks).** 17 of 17 checks: the line starts at "nothing"; a click on a NAME arms it and the line says so, a second click disarms; the CIRCLE still toggles exactly once per click; the arc text and the hit-chance tag do nothing; the name cell is a wide target; a beam armed by name starts at 1 point and the line follows its power (5 points); **the owner's scenario (Bank 4 + Tubes 1 and 2 armed by name) reads three weapons, the commit logs "Armed: FH-11 Bank 4 (1 pt), FP-4 Tube 1 (1 pt), FP-4 Tube 2 (1 pt)" matching the game's own armed list, the points add up to "Weapons 3", the allocation log and the confirmation carry it, and FIRE ALL fires all three and makes two torpedo effects**; the arming sound plays once for a name click; "Armed: nothing" for an empty commit; a knocked-out row's name has no click; no JavaScript errors. **Sweep: all 63 playable ships** arm every weapon by name, the line matches the count and the exact points the commit would spend, and disarm back to "nothing" (63 of 63; knocked-out rows inert 62 of 62). Phone emulation (the page lays out at 980 px): the line is 656 x 23 px in the 676 px weapon column. Regressions: arming sounds for all four other factions, Federation torpedo and phaser sounds, **a diff of what every weapon plays against v2.81-S192 (0 changed)**, the 246-weapon torpedo look scope, torpedo flight, kill and AI tests, the 17-ship bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn scope, the entry window, explosions, and the Damage Control sweep (66 ships) all pass.
**Findings.** (1) Shrinking a DESKTOP browser window to 390 px made the weapon column 130 px wide (the line 254 px tall); real phones (mobile emulation) lay the page out at 980 px and are fine: judge phone layout with mobile emulation, not a narrow window. (2) The Power tab arms weapons only through the circle or the name; it is NOT possible for a click to land on the wrong weapon (checked), so a missing second torpedo means that weapon's button was not pressed. (3) At very short range the Federation looks are brief and dim by design (recipe brightness 35% and 30%, the 0.30 s minimum flight); not changed, the owner will tune later.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A report of "N effects for M shots" starts with the log: the FIRE ALL line and the "Weapons N" power line say how many weapons were ARMED, before any visual is investigated. (2) Never arm in a test by setting flags and then pressing Commit: Commit rebuilds the armed list from the buttons and disarms everything (a blank film cost a retry). (3) A test must aim at the ELEMENT it means (the arc text), not a position in the row, once a neighbouring element has been made larger. (4) Do not double-escape regular expressions in a plain JavaScript test file (they silently match nothing: "0 of 63"). (5) The Tactical Advantage overlay covers the tabs after Proceed; earlier tests never press Proceed. (6) Forcing the game into the fire phase and then calling `revisePwr()` is ignored by design; use a fresh game.
**Not verified:** which button the owner pressed in round 1 (the log cannot say; the game only arms what is clicked); how the larger click target and the new line FEEL in play. **Open:** the owner's better K'tinga recipe (the K'tinga was also "a bit too bright", §0.151) and later tweaks to the Federation looks; a longer minimum flight or brighter Federation looks at 2 to 3 hexes if the three-torpedo volley is still hard to count; the earlier open items (looks for the Klingon TOS torpedoes, the Romulan, Gorn and Orion missiles and the plasma tubes; a Klingon torpedo sound; the master limiter; the Federation laser sound).

### 0.151 — What changed in v2.81-S192 (ENEMY Federation ships play the recorded phaser and torpedo sounds)

**User message (2026-11-05), with a combat log of the Klingon D-7 S (the player) against a USS Constitution Mk II (the enemy), which the player won:** "The torps from the klingon ship are a bit too bright. will provide a better recipe later. But what's interesting is the sounds of the phasers from the connie firing at me were the procedurally generated sounds not the ones I've provided for you to use."
**Two observations.** (1) **The K'tinga torpedo is a bit too bright:** noted, NOTHING CHANGED; the owner will send a better recipe. It is one entry (`TORPFX.recipes.ktinga`, its `bright` is 100) in the game and will be replaced by the owner's numbers when they arrive. (2) **The enemy Constitution's phasers played the synthesised sound.** This was a known limit, not new: in v2.73-S184 (§0.138 D) the recorded phaser was attached only when `shooter === GS.player`, and the Federation torpedo launch of v2.72-S183 has the same gate. It was listed as an open item in two earlier summaries (§0.145 and §0.146) but never put in front of the owner, who found it by ear when a Federation ship was the ENEMY for the first time.
**The change.** A new `playSfxFor(faction, ev)` looks up a faction's recorded clip by the SHOOTER's faction; `playFactionSfx(ev)` (the interface sounds: commit, proceed, arming) is now a one-line call to it with the PLAYER's faction and is otherwise unchanged. In `triggerWeaponFX`: **every Federation beam** (the phaser FH, the laser FL, and the two undesignated banks of the registry-only base "Constitution" entry, which is not playable) now plays `fed_phaser`, and **every Federation missile** plays `fed_torp_fire`, whichever side fires it. Only the Federation has recorded clips (`FACTION_SFX` has one entry), so every other faction still falls through to its own sound exactly as before. The player's Federation sounds are unchanged.
**Verification (real Chromium; the player is a Klingon, as in the owner's game).** (1) A diff of what EVERY weapon of EVERY registered ship plays on the previous build and on the new one: exactly three kinds of weapon changed, **158 Federation FH/FL banks and 2 undesignated ones (synthesised phaser to the recorded phaser) and 73 Federation missiles (synthesised torpedo to the recorded launch)**; the other 11 kinds are identical (Gorn beams still the Gorn clip, the older D-7s' bolts still the disruptor clip, every other Klingon, Romulan and Orion beam, and every Klingon, Romulan, Gorn and Orion missile and plasma tube still synthesised). (2) The owner's situation through the AI's own fire path (`resolveShipFiring`), an enemy Constitution Mk II (3 FH-3 phasers and 2 FP torpedoes, all bearing) at a Klingon D-7 S, 4 natural volleys: **previous build: 0 phaser clips, 0 launch clips, 5 synthesised sounds (this is what the owner heard); new build: 3 phaser clips, 2 launch clips, 0 synthesised.** (3) Loudness, natural volleys on the recorded output, previous build to new build: Constitution Mk II peaks 0.72-0.84 to 0.70-0.84 (none clipped); Federation I Mk I (4 lasers, 2 cannons bearing) 0.71-0.74 to 0.57-0.67; Excelsior Mk II 0.70-0.83 to 0.58-0.69; Enterprise refit Mk III 0.78-1.02 (1 of 4 clipped) to 0.69-0.88 (none); **Andor Mk II (6 of its 10 weapons bearing) 0.77-1.02 to 0.88-0.98 and one volley in four flagged at the edge in BOTH builds (as for the player's own Andor volley, §0.150)**. (4) Regressions: the 246-weapon torpedo look scope, the torpedo flight, kill and AI tests, the 17-ship bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn sound scope, the entry window, explosions and kills, arming sounds and the Damage Control sweep all pass; 0 JavaScript errors.
**Findings.** (1) The two "ENEMY (AI)" lines of the old sound tests (`testPh`, `testW`) still show synthesised sounds and are still RIGHT: in those tests the player is Federation, so the enemy is never Federation (a faction is excluded from the enemy list); they test a Klingon enemy. The Federation-enemy case is the diff and the fed-AI run above. (2) The enemy's Federation volleys are mostly QUIETER than before: the recording's average level is below the synthesised phaser's sustained burst when several overlap. (3) The Andor's ten-weapon volley is at the clipping edge either way; a master limiter (wishlist C10) would remove it for good.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A feature scoped to "the player" silently excludes the enemy: test the ENEMY side with a player of a DIFFERENT faction, because a faction never meets itself. (2) Say, in the summary, WHO a scoping choice leaves out and put it in front of the owner; listing it as "open" in a long section was not enough. (3) A diff of one behaviour over every weapon of every ship (previous build against new) proves "nothing else changed" better than spot checks. (4) A test's expectation can go stale when a change is intended: say so and update it, do not loosen it.
**Not verified:** how the enemy's recorded volleys SOUND in play (the owner's ears; I measured peaks only); the real viewer is not involved. **Open:** the owner's better K'tinga recipe; the earlier open items (looks for the Klingon TOS torpedoes, the Romulan, Gorn and Orion missiles and the plasma tubes; a Klingon torpedo sound; the master limiter; the Federation laser sound).

I've come up with torpedo effect for klingon k'tinga, Federation TMP era and lastly the TOS era for the federation too!" followed by three settings blocks. **The three recipes (verbatim numbers; the files `recipe_torpedo_klingon_ktinga_tmp.json`, `recipe_torpedo_federation_tmp.json` and `recipe_torpedo_federation_tos.json` hold them as the tool saves them; the game's table `TORPFX.recipes` was checked against them: 11 of 11 numbers identical in each).** They were made with the tool as of v. "even spokes" (the spoke layout of HANDOVER §0.149), which is the layout the game uses.
**K'tinga (Klingon TMP):** `{"len": 13.5, "flare": 50, "rot": 117, "bright": 100, "tspeed": 240, "count": 5, "irr": 80, "thick": 40, "core": 150, "twinkle": 52, "hue": -31, "bspeed": 135, "bsize": 50}`
**Federation TMP:** `{"len": 6, "flare": 50, "rot": 117, "bright": 35, "tspeed": 250, "count": 3, "irr": 80, "thick": 30, "core": 70, "twinkle": 51, "hue": -45, "bspeed": 135, "bsize": 50}`
**Federation TOS:** `{"len": 2, "flare": 16, "rot": 117, "bright": 30, "tspeed": 250, "count": 3, "irr": 80, "thick": 30, "core": 55, "twinkle": 78, "hue": -180, "bspeed": 135, "bsize": 50}`
**Where each applies (checked against `FASA_TOS_to_TMP_Timeline.md` section 6, not against the game's own table).** The look is chosen by the SHOOTER's faction and era (a new table `SHIP_ERA`, keyed by registry key, leaves `SHIP_REGISTRY` untouched) and applies to MISSILE-type weapons only. **K'tinga look** (Klingon, TMP era): D-18C Gull, K-22 Bird of Prey, D-7 S, D-32 Stronger Bird, L-42 Great Bird, L-24 Ever-Victorious (22 torpedo shots over 6 ships; the L-9 and K-23 carry none). **Federation TMP look:** Chandley Mk II and III, Enterprise refit Mk I to III, Reliant, Andor, Northampton, Baker Mk IV, Excelsior Mk I and II, Federation II Mk I and II (13 ships with torpedoes; the Gagarin has none). **Federation TOS look:** Constitution (all marks), Loknar, Larson, Baker Mk II, Chandley Mk I, Federation I Mk I to VI (14 ships; the Remora has none). **Unchanged, still the old torpedo:** the Klingon TOS-era torpedo carriers (D-7 M dated 2211, D-2 Stingtongue, D-10 D), and every Romulan, Gorn and Orion missile. Plasma (the D-7 G and R tubes, Romulan plasma), beams and bolts are unchanged. **The Federation's FAC accelerator cannons (the Constitution Mk I, Federation I Mk I and Mk II) are missile-type in the game and use the Federation TOS look too;** it is a one-line change if they should keep the old dot. Either side's ship uses its recipe (the player's or the AI's).
**Scale onto the map (a judgement call; two constants).** The tool measures size and speed against its own picture, the map is a different size, so (1) **`TORPFX.unit` = 1.25** world units per tool "S unit": a torpedo is the same size on screen as in the tool at its usual window size (1 S unit = 0.86 px in a 1400x860 window; 0.85 px on the map at default zoom; K'tinga core radius 9.0 px in the tool, 8.95 px on the map); (2) **`TORPFX.hexPerSec100` = 4.1** hexes a second at a travel speed of 100%, the tool's pixels a second on the map (147 px/s in the tool; a hex is 35 px): the K'tinga's 240% is 9.8 hexes a second and the Federation's 250% is 10.3, between today's old torpedo (5.5) and the disruptor bolts (11); a shot never takes under `TORPFX.minFlight` = 0.30 s. The map is much smaller than the tool's ships, so the K'tinga's long spokes (13.5 core radii, about 135 px) reach about 4 hexes: that is the recipe at the tool's size. **`TORPFX.flash`** = 1 scales the launch flash (1 = the tool's; 0.5 half; 0 none): it can look large over a small Federation ship because the map's ships are small.
**The effect (`sptorp`).** `addSpokeTorpFX` / `drawSpokeTorp` are the tool's drawing code on the map (halo, spokes as a soft band with a bright centre line, core, muzzle flash); `torpSpokeLayout` is the tool's `spokeLayout`, line for line (spokes shared out evenly, never leaving a half-circle bare). It flies in REAL time (`tickFX`'s `_dt`, as the bolts do) and the spokes turn at the recipe's rotation in real time. The missile branch of `triggerWeaponFX` uses it when `torpRecipeFor(shooter, weapon)` finds a recipe and the old `addTorpFX` otherwise; the result posts when the torpedo lands (or passes, on a miss) through the SAME `onArrive` / `pass` handshake as before, so the launch sound (the player's Federation recorded clip, otherwise the synthesised one), the impact explosion (still orange for every look), the log order and the phase waiting are unchanged. The Klingon KP tubes' red colour of the OLD torpedo (an earlier request) is still used for the Klingon TOS-era ships.
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) Scope: all 246 missile weapons on all 66 registered ships, each fired as a hit and as a miss, make the look the era document says and nothing else (0 wrong); no non-missile weapon makes one. (2) Player path: a Federation TMP ship's torpedo is created as `sptorp`, nothing is logged at launch, one result is pending, the result posts on landing (590 ms for a 6-hex hit, 563 ms for a miss); the spokes have turned 39 degrees after 0.34 s at 117 degrees a second (expected 39). (3) AI path: an enemy K-22 fires a K'tinga-look torpedo, the result posts on landing and the phase completes after it (625 ms). (4) A killing blow from torpedo 1 with torpedo 2 in flight: the fight is over, nothing pending, the destruction animation starts, no effect left, and torpedo 2 reports "the fight is already decided". Filmed with a hand-stepped clock the destruction runs about 4.4 s in the old and the new build alike (a nebula in that game's random map made the "light at the target" numbers differ; it was in the first frame). (5) Flight time = hexes / (4.1 x speed%) exactly for 1, 4, 8, 12 and 16 hexes on all three recipes: K'tinga (240%) 4 / 8 / 12 hexes take 0.41 / 0.81 / 1.22 s; the Federation looks (250%) 0.39 / 0.78 / 1.17 s. (6) Regressions pass: the 17-ship disruptor-bolt scope, the 11-ship Gorn sound scope, the entry window, Federation torpedo and phaser/laser sounds, explosions and kills (incl. the mutual kill), and the Damage Control sweep (66 ships); 0 JavaScript errors. Pictures: `game_spoke_torpedoes.png` (the three looks in flight on the real map).
**Findings.** (1) **The Andor's full volley (6 torpedoes + 2 phasers at once) was ALREADY at the clipping edge**: on v2.79-S190, 3 of 6 volleys clipped (peaks 0.85 to 1.03); on v2.80-S191 0 of 6 (0.81 to 0.98); the other big-volley ships peak 0.67 to 0.87. A master limiter would remove it (see the wishlist). (2) The old torpedo effect advances one small step per map REDRAW, so in a slow browser it flies slowly; the new effect uses real time (clamped to 0.05 s per redraw, so under 20 frames a second it runs slower than real time). (3) The Federation's two small looks are subtle by design (brightness 35% and 30%, small cores): at 0.85 px per tool unit the TOS look is a dim blue spark about 7 px across. (4) **Sounds are unchanged:** the Klingon and the AI's torpedoes still use the synthesised torpedo sound and the Federation player's the recorded launch.
**Harness lessons.** (1) A comparison against the OLD build needs a hand-stepped clock: the old effect is redraw-driven, so a real-time film of it in a slow headless browser shows it still in flight when the new one has landed. (2) "Force a kill" by overriding `d10` depends on the order of dice rolls, which differs between builds; force every roll to the minimum and kill the shield generators instead. (3) A brightness metric around a target is confounded by random terrain (a nebula): look at the frames. (4) Time the flight from the effect's own speed (`1/pps`) at distances beyond the weapon's range; the fire path itself is tested separately.
**Not verified:** how the three looks FEEL in play (the owner tuned them in the tool, where the picture is bigger than the map's ships; `TORPFX.unit` and `TORPFX.flash` are the two numbers if they read too big or too small); that the owner wants the FAC cannons to share the Federation TOS look and the Klingon TOS-era torpedoes to stay as they were; sound with the new timing beyond the volley peaks measured. **Open / for later:** recipes for the Klingon TOS-era torpedoes (D-7 M, D-2, D-10 D), the Romulan, Gorn and Orion missiles and the plasma tubes, using the same tool; the impact explosion is still orange whatever the look; a Klingon torpedo sound; the other items in wishlist C12 and C10.

### 0.149 — Klingon weapons bay: the spokes shared out evenly around the core, and "Download this tool" (the game is unchanged, still v2.79-S190)

**User message (2026-11-05), with a screenshot of a torpedo whose spokes all fan out toward the upper left:** "I need this file downloadable. the spokes come from only one source, the spokes need to be more evenly distributed. see how they're not pointing in other directions? Allow for them to rotate - that part is good."
**Readings (the owner may correct them).** "Come from only one source ... not pointing in other directions" was read as: all the spokes bunch on one side of the core. The other possible reading, that each spoke should continue through the core out the other side (a star-filter look), is offered as an OPTIONAL tick box ("Spokes pass through the core"), off by default. "This file downloadable" was read as the tool itself, the Klingon weapons bay. Rotation is unchanged.
**Cause (measured, not guessed).** The old angle formula blended an even position with a RANDOM one (`u = (1-irr)*(i/N) + irr*random`), so at the default (5 spokes, irregularity 80%) the angles were mostly random and could clump. Replaying it over 2,000 random seeds: **39% of torpedoes left a whole half of the circle empty at the defaults** (5 spokes, 80%), 79% with 3 spokes, 12% even with 8 spokes, and the emptiest gap was up to 319 degrees. On real renders (40 torpedoes, spokes found from the pixels): **17 of 40 left a half-circle bare, the worst with 300 degrees empty.** Also the two long spokes were assigned to neighbouring positions, so the long ones sat on one side.
**The fix (`spokeLayout`).** Every star now has its spokes shared out EVENLY (spoke i at i/N of a turn) with a random starting turn per torpedo; **irregularity now only nudges each spoke inside its own share** by up to `J = min(0.40, 0.22*(N-2))` of an even share (so two can never merge and a half-circle can never be left bare; for 2 spokes J is 0 and they are exactly opposite), and it varies the lengths. The two long spokes are spoke 0 and spoke round(0.4*N), which are far apart, and every other spoke is capped at 0.8 of full length so the two longest are always that pair. Optional **"through the core"** draws each spoke again at +180 degrees (an odd count gives a new direction for each; an even evenly-spaced count lands on its own spokes and just brightens them). Rotation is untouched (the spokes still turn at the rotation setting).
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) 66,000 random layouts (2 to 12 spokes, irregularity 0, 40, 80 and 100%, 1,500 seeds each): **0 leave a half-circle bare**; every gap stays inside the design bounds; 0% irregularity is exactly even; at the default the biggest gap between neighbours is at most 118 degrees (median 95; an even star is 72); the two longest spokes are never closer than 69 degrees. (2) On real pixels at the old defaults, 40 renders: **old build 17 bare (biggest empty gap 300 degrees), new build 0 (biggest 116 degrees)**, all 5 spokes found every time. (3) "Through the core": 3 spokes become 6 and 5 become 10, always in exact opposite pairs. (4) The tick box starts off, a real click turns it on, Reset all and the torpedo group's reset turn it off, Copy / Load settings round-trip it, a wrong type is ignored (8 of 8). (5) Regressions: the 20 control measurements, 31 UI checks, 45 layout checks, 7 sound checks and the 24-frame pixel match with the old TOS disruptor page all still pass. Picture: `klingon_spokes_before_after.png` (the same 12 torpedoes, same seeds, before and after).
**Download this tool.** A button in the control bar. The page captures its own source (`SELF_HTML`) at the very top of its script, before it builds anything, and sanitises it (drops other scripts, a base tag, policy meta tags and iframes a host might have added), so the saved file is only the tool. In the viewer it uses the `downloads` capability (`.html` is on the second allowlist, so it can in principle come back `extension_not_enabled`; the page then says so; ordinary saves have no size limit) and shows the viewer's own confirmation; opened as a file it does a plain download. **Verified:** the button downloads `klingon_weapons_bay.html` (425 KB, the same size as the original); the download is a complete page (doctype, title, all four pieces of ship art, both sounds, the code) taken before the sliders were built (no doubled controls); the saved copy, opened in a fresh browser, has no JavaScript errors, all art and sounds loaded, exactly 11 + 2 sliders, the identical starting state and **pixel-identical pictures** (torpedo salvo tactical, torpedo viewscreen, TOS disruptor); in the copy FIRE launches a torpedo and the sliders move; downloading again from the copy gives a **byte-identical** file (434,888 bytes both times); in a stand-in for the viewer the page calls `save()` once with `klingon_weapons_bay.html` and a `text/html` Blob of 425 KB and says it saved; the declined, `extension_not_enabled` and no-permission cases are handled (message, message, button disabled); and a test host that injects its own script, base and policy tags before the page runs does NOT get them into the downloaded file (14 + 1 checks).
**Harness lessons.** (1) A "randomness" control that picks angles at random will clump; make it a bounded nudge inside an even share. (2) A test that samples at fixed angles breaks the moment orientation is randomised: read the angles from the layout. (3) A search of a downloaded file for the word "http-equiv" finds the sanitiser's OWN source: check the markup, not the whole file. (4) "Mirroring" an evenly spaced EVEN number of spokes does nothing visible: test it with an odd count.
**Not verified:** the download in the real viewer (the real host's wrapper may add things I cannot see; the sanitiser is a defence against that, tested with a stand-in host; the viewer's confirmation step is the host's); that the owner's reading of "one source" is the one meant. **Open:** the owner's answer on that; the other two tools (Beam Lab, Torpedo Lab) have no download button yet and could get the same one; the earlier open items (rotation and twinkle in the film, crossing time, bringing the torpedo into the game, wishlist C12).

### 0.148 — The Klingon torpedo of the Motion Picture era, and the KLINGON WEAPONS BAY (a visual tool; the game is unchanged, still v2.79-S190)

**User requests (2026-11-04/05).** (1) "Just as I asked about klingon TOS beam weapons, describe the klingon torpedo from the motion picture era. to assist i'm providing some screenshots. And yes, I will ask you to build out a poc tool for the torpedo as well. you can use the architecture you have from the beam weapon tool. just combine both of them into one tool." (2) "what you're calling spokes, I'd like the ability to adjust the length and flair and rotate speed of them within the tool. I'd want to adjust the brightness too. Also, make the speed at which they travel adjustable as well."
**Readings (the owner may correct them).** "Both" = the TOS D-7 disruptor proof of concept and the new Motion Picture torpedo, in ONE page with an era switch; the two sound labs stay separate. "Flair" was read as FLARE: the glow around the core. Because the word could also mean variety or style, the tool also offers spoke count, irregularity, thickness, core size, twinkle and colour. The tool replaces the old disruptor page at the same link (`tos_d7_disruptor_poc.html` stays in the outputs folder, unchanged).
**The tool:** https://claude.ai/artifact/JnHEhPA1wja6fMR68uX5zn , source `klingon_weapons_bay.html` (432 KB, one self-contained file).
**The torpedo as it appears in the owner's two frames (measured).** A small, soft, near-white pale-yellow core (centre colour about RGB 255/234-252/150-167; core radius 10 to 13 px in frames 725 and 1,005 px wide, i.e. 1.3 to 1.8% of the width) with a warm halo, and no visible body or trail. Thin, straight, pale-yellow rays radiate at IRREGULAR angles (no pair on a straight line through the core in frame 1; angles in frame 1's big core 2, 78, 285 and 304 degrees), brightest at the core and fading outward, 9 to 26 core radii long (up to 336 px, about a third of the frame width, in frame 2), one or two dominant. Frame 1 holds three torpedoes at three sizes (radius 13 px, 10 px and a tiny distant dot with a short horizontal streak). The rays are soft glowing bands with a thin bright line down the middle. The backdrop is the V'Ger cloud: orange-red in the middle with purple streaks above and below. The rays were measured with a detector (the average blue-channel contrast along each direction, checked by drawing the detected rays over the frames: `klingon_tmp_torpedo_frame_analysis.png`); counts are MINIMUMS because fainter rays exist.
**The scene and the sources (secondary; none seen on film by me).** Three K't'inga-class cruisers (the IKS Amar, Commander Barak) approach the V'Ger cloud and the Amar fires three photon torpedoes into it to no effect (Memory Alpha); the cloud's plasma bolts destroy them. How it was made: TrekCore (a fan site) says a 20 W argon laser was used for the photon torpedoes; a longer account (Cinemore, English edition) says argon lasers with motion-control cameras, with the original blue-green changed to orange in optical processing; a 1989 magazine (START) says the effects company (Apogee) mounted a chunk of crystal on a rotating lucite rod; forum posts say the Enterprise's torpedoes in the same film used the same effect in another colour and that the long rays were shortened in later films. Launch point: the large port at the front of the K't'inga's bulbous forward hull (an old Wikipedia mirror and a forum), disruptors from the engine area. **Inference (unconfirmed from stills): a laser through a rotating crystal would throw spokes that sweep and sparkle, which fits the irregular angles.**
**Not known (nothing in the stills says):** speed, flight time, whether the rays rotate or twinkle, how they change on approach, the launch flash, the impact, the sound. The tool's defaults for these are ESTIMATES (rotation 12 degrees a second, twinkle 25%, crossing the screen in about 2.5 s tactical and 3 s viewscreen). **Questions put to the owner, not yet answered:** do the spokes rotate or twinkle in the film, and how long does a torpedo take to cross the screen?
**What the tool does.** An era switch: TOS (the grey D-7, the green disruptor bolts exactly as in the earlier proof of concept, your disruptor file with the trimmed tail) and TMP (the game's green-hulled D7RSM art standing in for a K't'inga, the torpedo). TMP launch points: the tip of the head in the top-down view (sprite pixel 127.5, 50) and, in the head-on view, the tube position the owner tuned for the game (`TORPEDO_GLOW_POS.D7RSM`, x 0.499, y 0.500). Torpedo sliders (starting values): **Spoke length** 2 to 40 core radii (20); **Flare** 0 to 100% (50); **Spoke rotation** -180 to +180 degrees a second, positive clockwise (+12); **Brightness** 20 to 200% (100); **Travel speed** 20 to 300% (100; the readout shows the time to leave the screen); Spokes 2 to 12 (5); Irregularity 0 to 100% (80; 0% is an even, equal star); Spoke thickness 25 to 300% (100); Core size 40 to 300% (150); Twinkle 0 to 100% (25); Colour -180 to +180 degrees (0 = the film's orange; the sources say the laser was blue-green, about +130). Also a salvo of three (sizes 1, 0.72, 0.5, 0.55 s apart, like frame 1), a space or cloud backdrop, tactical or viewscreen views (the torpedo grows as it drifts across the viewscreen), Slow 1/4, film grain, auto-fire, a muzzle flash, **Reset all** and a per-group reset, and Copy / Save (.json) / Load settings. The disruptor sliders (bolt speed and size, 25 to 200%) now START at the owner's game choices, 135% speed and 50% size. The torpedo sound is the owner's recorded Federation torpedo launch, a STAND-IN until a Klingon one exists. Look sliders act on torpedoes already in flight; travel speed is fixed at launch; spoke rotation integrates over time so changing it never makes the spokes jump.
**Calibration against the frames.** The first draft was far too timid (hair-thin spokes about 14 core radii long, a halo invisible on an orange backdrop). Compared with frame 2 at the same size, the spoke was rebuilt as a wide soft glow band plus a thin bright centre line fading slowly, the halo was enlarged and made yellower, the cloud was darkened so the torpedo's own flare does the lighting, and the default spoke length was set to 20. Measured with the same detector at core radius 13 px: spoke length 14 gives rays up to about 11 core radii, 24 gives up to 26 (the film's longest, 25.8). **The settings closest to the frames were spoke length about 36 and flare about 90, with thickness left near the default (200% looked too fat against the film's thin lines).** The tool's spokes still read stronger in contrast than the film's, partly because its backdrop is darker. Picture: `klingon_torpedo_tool_vs_frames.png`.
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) Every torpedo control measured on real renders against a black backdrop, 20 of 20: spokes drawn = 3, 5, 8 and 12 asked for, evenly spaced to within 1 to 2 degrees at 0% irregularity; irregularity 0% gives equal spokes, 100% gives angle spread 62 degrees and length spread 26%; the longest spoke measures 66, 132 and 186 px at 10, 20 and 30 core radii; rotation through the LIVE animation loop turns the spokes exactly +139 and -135 degrees in about 1.5 s at +90 and -90 degrees a second, and 0 at 0; drawn phase moves the longest spoke exactly 30 degrees for 30; brightness rises at every step; thickness 2.0, 4.0 and 6.0 px at 50, 100 and 200%; core radius 4.5, 7.0 and 14.5 px at 60, 100 and 200% with the halo off (ratio 2.07); glow radius 27, 53 and 114 px at flare 0, 50 and 100%; the colour shifts move the measured outer-spoke hue by exactly the shift; twinkle 0% gives identical pictures at two moments and 100% differs; 200% travel speed covers exactly twice the distance (ratio 2.00) and halves the time to leave the screen (2.52 s to 1.26 s); the drawn torpedo sits on the path to within 1 px. (2) The TOS side is pixel-identical to the old disruptor proof of concept: 24 of 24 frames (2 views, 3 nacelle settings, 4 moments) with both at 100%/100%, largest difference 0. (3) UI 31 of 31 with real clicks, keys and downloads: the era switch, FIRE (1 or 3 torpedoes, 2 or 1 bolts), Space, tap, all 13 sliders by keyboard, **Reset all** (every slider and option, on-screen controls agreeing, era and view staying) and the group resets (only their own group), Copy / Load (exact round trip; garbage and wrong kinds refused; out-of-range values clamped; wrong types ignored), Save settings (a plain `.json` download; in the viewer the exact `save()` call, the declined and unavailable cases), the panel toggle, Slow 1/4 (0.25 s of picture per second) and auto-fire. (4) Sound 7 of 7 on the recorded output: the disruptor shot peaks -6.0 dBFS; one torpedo -9.8 dBFS; a salvo of three -6.7 dBFS with 0 clipped samples; the three launches 0.55 s apart (2.2 s in Slow 1/4); the sound tick box and volume 0 give silence. (5) Layout 45 of 45 on 1280x800, 1024x600, 1280x520 and a 390x844 phone at 2x, both eras. 0 JavaScript errors.
**Findings and harness lessons.** (1) On a phone the settings panel starts closed because with it open the picture shrinks to a thin strip; on a short window the panel is open by default and leaves about 180 to 200 px of picture (the Settings button collapses it). (2) The old page's `fireAt(t)` does NOT render and fires at time t: the right way to capture frame t is `fireAt(0)` then `freeze(t)`; a page that only re-measures its canvas on a window `resize` event needs that event after CSS changes, or a comparison is against a stale canvas. (3) A visibility check must test whether the element takes up space (`getClientRects`), not its own `hidden` flag, because a hidden PARENT hides its children. (4) Hue cannot be measured at the bright core: the red and green channels clip at 255 and every hue from 40 to 100 degrees reads as the same yellow; sample the dimmer outer spoke. (5) "Which spoke is longest" changes when a long spoke hits the canvas edge; use a short length when tracking one spoke. (6) The first viewscreen path dropped off the bottom within 1 s; it now drifts right and slightly down for about 3 s while growing 2.4 times. (7) Comparing against the film is only meaningful by running the SAME detector on both pictures.
**Not verified:** how the motion feels (the owner's call; every motion value is an estimate); the real `downloads` save in the viewer (tested against a stand-in); Firefox and Safari; that "flair" means flare; sound in the viewer. **Open / for later:** the owner's answers about rotation, twinkle and crossing time; then bringing the TMP torpedo into the GAME. That needs decisions: which ships (the Motion Picture-era Klingon ships that carry torpedoes by the era rule are the D-7 S, D-18C, K-22, D-32, L-42 and L-24; the D-7 M carries two KP-3 but is dated 2211, so it is the owner's call), the scale onto the map (the way `TOSBOLT.unit` scaled the bolts: a D-7 is about 25 px tall on the map), whether the effect is the game's existing missile effect redrawn (results already post when a missile lands), and a Klingon torpedo sound; wishlist C12.

### 0.147 — The sound tools: Reset added to the Beam Lab, and the new TORPEDO LAB (the game is unchanged, still v2.79-S190)

**User request (2026-11-04):** "in similar fashion as you did for the beam weapon, build a poc for the torpedo/plasma weapon. Using your generated sound and the provided sound from me. I'd like more options, more bass. more ability to make the sound last. More other worldly in addition to what you did for the beam weapon. Also, for both tools, there needs to be a reset back to starting point. so really, you're augmenting the beam weapon one and building a new plasma/torpedo poc tool."
**Both pages are published (the links stay the same when updated), and their sources are `beam_lab.html` and `torpedo_lab.html` in the outputs folder.** Beam Lab: https://claude.ai/artifact/HNWZK8AZp9Jkq85CUt6kgM . Torpedo Lab: https://claude.ai/artifact/QYSyASirfLDQfZzDFHv5Wk . Each page is one self-contained file that renders in an offline audio context (so the preview is exactly the export), shows a waveform, a spectrogram and measured numbers, has A/B slots, Mutate and Wild, Undo, reference buttons, a recipe (every setting as JSON) and Export (a plain `.wav` when opened as a saved file; a `.zip` holding the WAV and the recipe inside the viewer, because the `downloads` capability does not allow `.wav`).
**RESET (both tools).** "Reset to starting point" restores every control, and the name, to the **starting point = the preset or recipe last loaded** (the page's first preset at page start; choosing another preset or loading a recipe makes THAT the starting point; Mutate and Undo do not move it). Each card also has a small ↺ that restores just that section. Reset is itself undoable. Tests (real keyboard, dropdown and checkbox events): changes then Reset restores every setting and the on-screen controls; Undo after Reset brings back exactly the settings from just before it; the per-card ↺ restores only its section; the starting point follows a new preset and a loaded recipe; Mutate then Reset; resetting with nothing changed is harmless. Beam Lab 14/14, Torpedo Lab 14/14. Beam Lab regression after the change: export 13/13, UI 15/15, layout 12/12, "Game now" fidelity unchanged (correlation 0.999996).
**What the owner's recordings and the game's torpedo sound ARE (measured before designing anything).** The game's torpedo sound (`snd('torpedo')`, used for EVERY torpedo and EVERY plasma bolt, and for any weapon that is not a player's Federation torpedo) is two oscillators: a sine sliding 200 to 80 Hz and a sawtooth sliding 150 to 60 Hz, both through one gain that falls from 0.4 to 0.001 in 0.6 s: 88% of its energy is under 250 Hz, brightness 304 Hz, audible 0.47 s. The owner's `torpedo_load_fire_short.mp3` (2.85 s) is a charge-up (0 to 1.075 s, a bright whine, brightness 2,414 Hz, only 0.2% of energy under 250 Hz), a gap of digital silence (about -90 dBFS), then the launch (1.075 s on, brightness 695 Hz, **only 0.9% of its energy under 120 Hz** and 16% under 250 Hz). `smallexplosion1.mp3` (1.99 s) is the opposite: **47% of its energy is under 120 Hz** and 72% under 250 Hz (brightness 418 Hz), so it is a real sub-bass source. The phaser tone and the disruptor clips have no bass (they are 99.9% and 67% above 1 kHz). That is why the owner hears the recorded launch as lacking bass.
**The Torpedo Lab.** Sources (all the owner's): the torpedo launch, the charge-up (the recording is split where its silent gap is, found from the audio itself so it is right whatever the browser's decoder does; the lab reports launch 1.775 s and charge-up 1.075 s), the whole torpedo recording, the explosion, the phaser tone and the disruptor. **Five layers:** (1) recorded: pitch -36 to +12 semitones, trim, length to 10 s, fade, **sustain** (loops a section with a smoothed seam so a short recording can last: the unit's first stretch cross-fades in from the audio just after it, so the seam is continuous), high-pass, low-pass, reverse; (2) **sub-bass boom**: a tone dropping 300 to 20 Hz with attack, hold, duration to 10 s and a "small-speaker" control that blends in a saturated copy so the bass is audible on laptop speakers; (3) synth voice: the game's procedural voice grown up (rising or falling, warble); (4) **FM texture** (the other-worldly one): a carrier shaken by a modulator, with the shake and the pitch both moving over time; (5) roar and crackle: white, pink or brown noise through a low-pass, band-pass or high-pass whose cutoff sweeps. **Movement and colour:** throb, ring modulation, flanger, crunch (bit and sample-rate reduction), drive. **Echo and space:** echo up to 1 s with repeats to 90%, reverb up to 8 s with a brightness control. **Bass and output:** bass shelf up to +18 dB, rumble filter, high cut, stereo width, length up to 10 s, final fade, peak level, mono or stereo. 73 sliders. The spectrogram runs 20 Hz to 16 kHz (a 4,096-point window for sounds over 1.5 s) and the numbers shown include the share of energy under 200 Hz and under 80 Hz. Mutate never touches the Output section.
**Presets (starting points; I could not hear them).** Game now (the game's procedural sound, exact); TOS torpedo (the recorded launch as the game plays it); Photon torpedo, heavy launch; Plasma bolt, other-worldly whine and throb; Long-range plasma lob (8.5 s: the phaser tone two octaves down, sustained); Charge-up; Detonation rumble; Blank. **They were rebalanced by measurement:** my first versions were almost all sub-bass (the heavy launch 68% of its energy under 80 Hz, the plasma bolt 92%, the detonation 94%), which would be inaudible on small speakers and would bury the owner's recordings, so the sub-bass levels were cut until the measured shares were: heavy launch 55% under 200 Hz (the recorded launch alone: 6%), plasma bolt 50%, lob 62%, detonation 82% (56% under 80 Hz).
**Verification (real Chromium).** (1) "Game now" vs the game's own `snd('torpedo')` rendered offline: correlation 1.000000, peak identical (0.70747), error 61 dB below the signal. (2) "TOS torpedo (recorded)" vs the clip the game plays for Federation torpedoes (`fed_torp_fire`): correlation 0.9885 after alignment (the game's clip is a re-encoded, trimmed copy). (3) Every new control measured on a real render, 21 of 21: the +12 dB bass shelf lifts 40 to 100 Hz by 9.5 dB and leaves 1 to 4 kHz alone; the sub-bass layer at 60 Hz peaks at 60.0 Hz; the small-speaker control raises the harmonics 2,046 times; sustain turns a 637 ms recording into a 2,972 ms sound and the loop seam is 0.54 times the loudest ordinary jump (no click; with the 5 ms minimum smoothing it is 1.04); FM shake 0 gives one spectral peak and shake 10 gives 16; ring modulation 440 Hz x 100 Hz gives 340 and 540 Hz and removes the 440; throb at 5 Hz pulses at 5.0 Hz; the flanger changes the sound (correlation 0.71); crunch at 4 bits leaves 13 distinct values and a rate drop of 8x holds each value for 8 samples; echo bursts land at 0, 300 and 600 ms; the reverb lengthens the audible sound from 457 ms (1 s) to 3,070 ms (6 s); stereo width 10 ms delays the right channel by 441 samples; the rumble filter cuts 20 to 50 Hz by 16.6 dB and 50 to 80 Hz by 5 dB; the 2 kHz high cut cuts 4 to 10 kHz by 19 dB; noise under 200 Hz is white 4%, pink 38%, brown 59%; pitch -12 semitones halves the main tone exactly (1,314 to 657 Hz; the stretched spectrum correlates 1.000); hold at full keeps the level (0.300 against 0.044 at 1 s). The longest, heaviest sound (10 s, reverb 8 s, echo, FM) renders in 0.76 s. (4) Export 13/13 (local `.wav`, the exact `save({filename, data})` call and a `.zip` against a stand-in for the capability, declined and unavailable cases) and the zip's CRC and contents checked with Python. (5) UI 15/15 (73 sliders mutated 300 times, all in range), layout 12/12 (desktop, 2x, phone). 0 JavaScript errors anywhere.
**Findings.** (1) **Rendering with the reverb is repeatable only to about -99 dB below full scale:** presets without a reverb render 100% identically every time, but presets that use the convolution reverb differ by floating-point rounding (worst 1.2e-5, below one 16-bit step); two exported WAVs of the same recipe differ by at most 1 LSB in 2.5% of samples. So a recipe reproduces a sound to inaudible precision, not bit for bit, when a reverb is involved. (2) **Web Audio's low-pass and high-pass "Q" is in decibels** (the height of the resonance bump), not a linear Q; the labs use 0.707 for a plain filter (a 0.7 dB bump) and the Layer 5 "Narrowness" is a resonance amount for those filters but a true Q for the band-pass. (3) Energy share overstates how audible bass is: the ear is far less sensitive below about 80 Hz and small speakers cannot reproduce it, so judge sub-bass on headphones or with the small-speaker control.
**Harness lessons.** Measure band energy straight from the spectrum, not with a band-pass filter, when the band is far below the loud part of the signal (the filter's skirts leak energy from above and hid a working rumble filter); judge a pitch shift by the frequency of the main tone, not by the spectral centroid; `Math.max(...bigArray)` overflows the call stack on a 194,000-sample WAV: use a loop; a "same file" comparison must allow for the reverb finding above.
**Not verified:** how any preset sounds (I cannot hear; the owner will); the real `downloads` save in the viewer (tested against a stand-in); other browsers (Chromium only: the filters and saturation are each browser's own, and an exported WAV from the owner's own browser is the exact record of what they heard). **Open / for later:** the owner has not yet designed a torpedo or plasma sound in the Torpedo Lab, so the GAME still plays its procedural torpedo sound for plasma and every non-player-Federation torpedo; when one is chosen it needs integrating the way the Gorn beam sound was (§0.146: a clip, a gain and a leveller bus, with volleys measured); the Federation laser sound is still open; wishlist C10.

### 0.146 — What changed in v2.79-S190 (the BEAM LAB, and the owner's Gorn beam sound in the game)

**The Beam Lab (new, published page; source `beam_lab.html` in the outputs folder).** Requested 2026-11-04 after the owner found the game's beam sounds "procedurally generated" and wanted "a hybrid combo" of the generated sounds and the recorded TOS phaser, "with the ability to augment the sound" and "an export function". It is a single self-contained page: three layers (1: the recorded TOS phaser, either the tone the game plays or the 60 ms opening blip the game cuts off, with pitch, trim, length, high-pass and low-pass, reverse; 2: the game's procedural voice grown into an oscillator with wave, pitch slide, envelope and a warble; 3: shaped plasma-crackle noise), then drive, echo and a generated "space" reverb, and an Output section (length, peak level, mono or stereo). It renders in an offline audio context, so what is heard is exactly what is exported. It shows a waveform, a spectrogram and measured numbers (peak, RMS, brightness, audible length); has A/B slots, Mutate and Wild buttons, undo and reference buttons (the game's current beam sound, and the recorded TOS phaser); and exports a WAV plus a recipe (every setting as JSON). **Export:** opened as a saved file it writes a plain `.wav`; inside the viewer the `downloads` capability does not allow `.wav` (its allowlist is gif, png, jpg, jpeg, webp, mp4, webm, mov, txt, json, md, docx, pptx, epub, csv, ttf, html, svg, pdf, xlsx, zip, fig), so it saves a `.zip` holding the WAV and the recipe, built by a small zip writer in the page. Verified: the "Game now" preset reproduces the game's own `snd('phaser')` code rendered offline to a correlation of 0.999996 (peak identical, error 51 dB below the signal); the exported WAV matches the preview to 16-bit accuracy and is byte-identical inside the zip (Python `zipfile` CRC check); a recipe round-trips exactly and bad or out-of-range recipes are refused or clamped; 300 mutations never leave a control's range; layouts on desktop, 2x and phone. The page is peak-normalised for fair comparison. **What the game's beam sound was:** every beam, laser or phaser, played one sine tone sliding 800 Hz to 200 Hz in 0.3 s (`snd('phaser')`, gain 0.3, a placeholder from the earliest builds); at equal peak it averages 7 dB quieter than the TOS phaser and sits at about 670 Hz against about 2,000 Hz. **Open:** the owner has NOT yet found a Federation laser sound with it (the Federation lasers use the recorded phaser for now, §0.145).
**User message (2026-11-04):** "This is one of the coolest tools we've come up with! While not finding the sound for lasers for the fed, I did come up with a good sound for the Gorn beam weapons! here's the recipe:" (the recipe below). It was read as a request to use it as the Gorn beam sound; the owner may correct that.
**The recipe (verbatim; load it with "Recipe, paste to load" in the Beam Lab; also saved as `gorn_beam_recipe.json`):**

 "tool": "beam-lab",
 "version": 1,

 "params": {
  "name": "laser-a",
  "L1": {
   "on": true,
   "src": "tone",
   "gain": 70,
   "pitch": -7,
   "trim": 20,

   "hp": 400,
   "lp": 2981.0347602582874,
   "rev": false,

  },
  "L2": {

   "wave": "sawtooth",
   "f0": 3200,

   "curve": "exp",

   "att": 27,

   "wdepth": 0,

   "gain": 55,
   "delay": 0
  },
  "L3": {
   "on": true,
   "kind": "pink",
   "fc": 4200,
   "q": 1.2,
   "att": 8,
   "dec": 45,

  },
  "FX": {

**What it is (measured).** Loading it in the lab holds every number exactly (0 differences); it renders to 960 ms, stereo, peak -1.00 dBFS, average level (RMS) -8.1 dBFS (a dense sound), brightness 1,551 Hz, first sound at 3 ms. Layer 1: the TOS tone pitched down 7 semitones, high-passed at 400 Hz, low-passed at 2,981 Hz; layer 2: a sawtooth sliding 3,200 to 420 Hz (the warble depth is 0, so the warble does nothing); layer 3: pink crackle at 68 Hz; drive 100%, echo 150 ms with 48% repeats at 10% mix, space 30% over 1.75 s (the 960 ms length cuts the tail). Rendered by the lab to `gorn_beam.wav` (stereo, 16-bit, 44.1 kHz).
**In the game.** The WAV was encoded to **MP3 44.1 kHz stereo 160 kbps, 20,420 bytes**. Bitrate was chosen by per-band ENERGY balance (a noise-heavy sound cannot be judged by waveform SNR, which is only 17.6 dB at 160 kbps): at 128, 160 and 192 kbps every band (60 Hz to 16 kHz) keeps its energy within 0.48, 0.44 and 0.26 dB and the amplitude envelope correlates 0.9989, 0.9997 and 0.9999 with the source. New key `gorn_beam`, played by `playUiSfx('gorn_beam')` in the beam branch of `triggerWeaponFX` for **every Gorn beam (`shooter.faction === 'gor'`: GBL-3 on the SS-3, GBL-7 on the MA-12, GBL-8 on the BH-2), whichever side fires it**; the beam's LOOK is unchanged. Unchanged: the Gorn plasma/missile launchers (GP-n, still the synthesised torpedo sound), every other faction, the older D-7 bolts and the Federation recorded phaser. If the clip cannot play, the old synthesised beam sound plays (tested).
**Level (the hard part: measured, not guessed).** The clip is DENSE (average -8.1 dBFS at a -1.0 dBFS peak) and a Gorn battleship fires up to 8 beams in a volley, so a plain gain clipped almost every volley (peaks 0.95 to 1.41 at gain 0.20 with 5 voices). Two findings drove the design. (1) **The game's own impact sounds alone already reach 0.71-0.86 in a six-beam volley** (measured by muting the clip; the old build's volleys were 0.75-0.85), so any extra loud sound goes straight into clipping. (2) A limiter at -4 dB holds everything near one ceiling, so lowering the gain only made a SINGLE shot very quiet without lowering the volley peaks. So the Gorn bus is a **leveller**: `UI_SFX_LIMITED.gorn_beam = {thr:-14, trim:0.25}` (a compressor with a LOW threshold of -14 dB, ratio 20, whose output is trimmed to 0.25), `UI_SFX_GAIN.gorn_beam = 0.30`, `UI_SFX_MAXVOICES.gorn_beam = 3` (at 4 voices the battleship clipped 1 volley in 4). The shared limiter code was changed to one limiter PER sound with an optional threshold and trim (`uiBus(ac,k)`, `UI_SFX_LIMITED[k]` = `true` or `{thr,trim}`); the D-7 bolt sound keeps `true` (threshold -4 dB, no trim) and is unchanged. **Result, real audio output, natural dice:** a single Gorn shot peaks -14.6 dBFS and averages -24.5 dBFS (the Federation recorded phaser: -12.8 / -24.9; the D-7 disruptor: -9.2 / -21.8; the old synthesised Gorn beam: -8.6 / -28.9); player volleys, 5 each: SS-3 0.72-0.96, MA-12 0.79-0.92, BH-2 0.85-0.94, **0 of 15 clipped** (the old build: 0.75-0.85); AI volleys (4 each): 0.25-0.49, none clipped. `UI_SFX_GAIN.gorn_beam` and the bus values are each one constant to change.
**Other checks.** Scope: 11 ships across all factions, every weapon fired: only the 18 Gorn beams play the new clip (0 wrong). AI path: an enemy MA-12 with 4 beams bearing plays the clip 4 times, no synthesised sound. D-7 bolts: scope (17 ships), hit, miss and kill, and D7_C volleys 0.74-0.89 unchanged. Federation phaser and laser sounds unchanged; entry window, explosions and kills, arming sound, Federation torpedoes and the Damage Control sweep (66 ships) pass; 0 JavaScript errors. Game now 12,430,727 bytes (+28,141 bytes against v2.78-S189: the 27 KB clip as base64 and the bus code).
**Harness lessons.** (1) `UI_SFX_GAIN[k] || 0.3` makes a gain of 0 fall back to 0.3: to mute a sound in a test use 0.0001 (my first "muted" run was the loudest). (2) A limiter's output ceiling makes loudness insensitive to gain once it is hit: measure a SINGLE shot and a VOLLEY separately before choosing the gain, and measure what the other sounds contribute alone. (3) Judge a noise-heavy sound's MP3 by band-energy balance and envelope, not waveform SNR. (4) The AI test needs a placement where the most of the enemy's beams bear (several Gorn banks face different arcs); a placement that requires ALL of them reports "placed false" and fires nothing. (5) Natural-dice volleys vary run to run by about 0.1: use 4-5 per setting.
**Not verified:** how the sound is perceived in play (the owner designed it by ear; I cannot hear); the Beam Lab's real `downloads` save in the viewer (tested against a stand-in for the capability: the exact `save({filename, data})` call and the zip it saves); a full 8-beam Gorn battleship volley with all 8 bearing (at the test placement 6 of 16 weapons bear); that the owner wants the sound on the AI's Gorn ships too (it is: any side). **Open / for later:** a Federation laser sound; a sound for the Gorn plasma launchers (GP-n) and other factions' beams; the owner's recipe can be refined in the Beam Lab and sent back; wishlist C10.

### 0.145 — What changed in v2.78-S189 (the Federation LASER banks use the recorded TOS phaser sound)

**User question (2026-11-04), after playing the oldest Constitution against a D-7 G (combat log attached; the player won; the disruptor sound "is good"):** "Why is the sound for the phasers on the old Connie procedurally generated as opposed to the TOS like sounds we should have addressed quite sometime ago?"
**The answer (verified by firing every weapon of the Constitution Mk I and recording which sound played).** The oldest Constitution carries **3 x FL-6 (lasers) and 2 x FAC-3 (accelerator cannons)**. The FAC-3 tubes are missile-type and already played the recorded torpedo-launch clip; the three FL-6 beams played the SYNTHESISED phaser sound, because in v2.73-S184 (§0.138 D) the recording `tos_ship_phaser_short.mp3` was attached only to banks designated `FH` (phasers). That was a deliberate scope choice (the recording is a phaser, and lasers are a different weapon), it was written down here and mentioned in that build's summary ("lasers keep the synthesised sound"), but it was **not flagged that two ships carry ONLY lasers**, so for the Constitution Mk I and the Federation I class the recording never played at all. That consequence should have been raised then.
**The change.** One condition in the beam branch of `triggerWeaponFX`: `/^FH/i` is now `/^F[HL]/i`, so the PLAYER's Federation laser banks (FL-n) play `fed_phaser` exactly as the phaser banks do (same clip, same gain 0.20, same onset trim). Affected playable ships (counted live): **Constitution Mk I (3 FL) and Federation I Mk I (10 FL)**, both lasers only. **Unchanged:** the AI's beams (an enemy Federation ship's beams still use the synthesised sound, as designed in v2.73-S184), every other faction's beams, the Klingon older-D-7 bolts, torpedoes and cannons (recorded torpedo clips), and any shot where the clip cannot play (the synthesised sound, as before). The same clip is used for lasers as for phasers because it is the TOS-like Federation beam sound the project has; a distinct laser sound can be chosen later.
**Loudness (natural-dice volleys on the real audio output, 4 volleys each).** Constitution Mk I (all 5 weapons bear): peaks 0.71-0.88, against 0.59-0.67 on v2.77-S188 (the recording is stronger than the old synthesised sound: about +2 dB); Federation I Mk I (6 of its 12 weapons bear at the placement tested): 0.70-0.91; Federation II Mk I (12 FH banks, already on the clip): 0.78-0.87. No clipping in any. **Not measured:** a Federation I volley with all 10 lasers bearing at once (at the test placement only 6 of 12 weapons bear; its banks face forward, port and starboard).
**Other checks.** Each weapon of the Constitution Mk I: 3 lasers -> recorded phaser clip, 2 cannons -> recorded torpedo clip, no other sounds. `testPh`: FH bank, FL bank, three banks 130 ms apart and the real `fireWeapon` all play the clip once per bank; the AI's beam and a Klingon player's beam are still synthesised. Torpedoes, the 17-ship bolt scope check, the entry window and the Damage Control sweep unchanged. 0 JavaScript errors. Game now 12,402,586 bytes (+111 bytes against v2.77-S188).
**Lesson.** When a feature is deliberately scoped to part of a family (here FH but not FL), check which SHIPS fall entirely outside it and say so in the summary: a scope choice that leaves a whole ship unserved is a finding, not a footnote.
**Not verified:** how it sounds (the recording is the owner's); a full 10-laser Federation I volley; that the owner wants lasers to share the phaser sound rather than a different one. **Open:** the AI's Federation beams (an enemy Constitution or Federation I) still use the synthesised sound; wishlist C10.

### 0.144 — What changed in v2.77-S188 (TOS D-7 DISRUPTOR BOLTS: a new weapon effect and sound for the older D-7s)

**User request (2026-11-04), after the proof of concept `tos_d7_disruptor_poc.html` (published page; built from one reference frame of the original-series D-7 and the supplied `tos_disruptor.mp3`):** "bolt size should be 50 percent. bolt speed should 135 percent. otherwise take the sound with trimmed setting and replace this weapon effect for the 'older' D-7s. The A's, C's and G's. Go ahead and update the game with these settings."
**Scope.** The older D-7s are the marks that use the grey `D7` sprite: **D7_A (2 KD-6), D7_C (4 KD-6), D7_G (2 KD-6 and 1 plasma tube)**. Only their BEAMS change (`isTosBolt(shooter,weapon)` = beam type and `shooter.spriteKey === 'D7'`). The D7_G's RPL-1 plasma tube, the M, R and S marks (the green `D7RSM` art, KD-8), and every other ship of every faction are unchanged: checked by creating 17 ships and firing every weapon's effect (0 wrong). It applies to EITHER side: an enemy D-7 uses it as the player's does.
**The effect (`TOSBOLT`, `addTosBoltFX`, `drawTosBolt`).** A soft bright head with a pale core, a short streak, and a trail of small round beads that shrink and dim (the look of the reference frame), plus a muzzle flash. Settings kept from the proof of concept: `TOSBOLT.sizePct = 50`, `TOSBOLT.speedPct = 135`. **Scale (judgement call):** the proof of concept drew a large ship, but a D-7 on the map is only about 25 px tall (default zoom ts = 0.68; a hex is about 35 px), so the whole effect (head, beads, bead spacing AND speed, together) is scaled by `TOSBOLT.unit` = world units per proof-of-concept "S unit". **`unit` = 1.4**, chosen by looking at four-bank volleys on the real map at scales 0.7, 1.0, 1.4 and 1.8: at 1.0 the beads were too fine to see, at 1.8 the glow hid the ships. At 1.4 the head is about half a hex wide and a bolt crosses 6 hexes in about 0.55 s (a torpedo takes about 1.1 s). `TOSBOLT.unit` is the one number to change to make every bolt bigger or smaller (and, being in the same units, faster or slower). **The bolt flies in REAL time** (`tickFX` now computes `_dt` from `performance.now()`; torpedoes still tick once per map redraw, which is an existing quirk: they run faster on a high-refresh display, bolts do not).
**Launch points: the nacelle pods.** Bolts leave the D-7's two nacelle pods, alternating bank by bank (`tosBoltMount`, `TB_PODS`: the pod front ends measured from the 256-px `D7` sprite's own pixels, rotated by the ship's facing the same way `hullExtentAlong` does), so a volley is two separate parallel streams like the reference frame. This is done INSIDE `computeWeaponAim`, so a miss line is still solved from the real launch point and can never clip the target's hull. (My first version used the generic hull-edge emitter: all four banks left from nearly the same spot and their trails stacked into one smear; found only by looking at a volley on the map.)
**Bolts are projectiles (deferred results).** Like torpedoes, a bolt's roll is made at launch but its result (the roll line, damage, shield text, the shield shimmer or explosion) posts when it lands on the hull or shield (a HIT) or as it passes the ship (a MISS): `isTosBolt` was added to the `deferred` test at BOTH fire sites (the player's `fireWeapon` and the AI's `resolveShipFiring`) and to the `pendingImpacts` watchdog line in `triggerWeaponFX`, and the effect uses the same `onArrive` / `pass` handshake as a torpedo in `tickFX`. The phase end already waits for pending impacts, so nothing else changed. Verified: a hit posts after a 0.50 s flight (5 hexes), a miss posts as the bolt passes, the AI's four-bank volley posts each result as its bolt lands (the last at about 1.0 s) and completes only after it, and a killing blow from bolt 1 with three more in flight gives "HIT but the fight is already decided; no further effect" for the others, starts the destruction animation, and leaves nothing pending or stuck.
**The sound.** `kli_tos_disruptor`: the supplied file cut where the proof of concept's Trimmed mode cuts it (starts at 0.100 s, skipping the leading silence; the echo tail fades out linearly between 1.38 s and 1.64 s of the original and is baked into the clip), 1.54 s, **MP3 44.1 kHz stereo 128 kbps, 25,539 bytes** (at 96 kbps it was 19,166 bytes with an SNR of 18.7 dB against the reference; at 128 kbps 22.8 dB, same pre-echo 28 dB below the attack: 128 was taken for a tonal, warbling sound). Played by `playUiSfx('kli_tos_disruptor')` in the bolt branch of `triggerWeaponFX`, once per bolt, with `UI_SFX_TRIM` (the runtime start offset is 12.8 ms into the decoded clip), a 6-voice cap, and **a limiter on its own bus** (`UI_SFX_LIMITED`, `uiBus`: DynamicsCompressor, threshold -4 dB, ratio 20; no other sound is touched). If the clip cannot play, the old synthesised beam sound plays instead. **Level: `UI_SFX_GAIN.kli_tos_disruptor` = 0.22**, set by recording the real audio output of natural four-bank volleys: 0.35 peaked at 0.92-1.00 and clipped in 2 of 6; 0.25 at 0.79-0.86; 0.18 at 0.58-0.69 (the range the game's volleys had before); 0.22 at 0.70-0.79 (player's volley) and 0.70-0.79 (enemy's volley), and 0.72-0.83 for the real sequence (the Federation volley, then the enemy D7_C's) against 0.72-0.85 on the previous build, no clipping in any.
**Findings to know.** (1) **The viewscreen never shows weapon fire** (`renderViewscreenInline` reacts only to the enemy's destruction flash and a glow when the enemy has a forward torpedo tube), so the proof of concept's Viewscreen mode was not ported: it would be a new feature. (2) **The game's synthesised impact sounds clip in a forced all-hits volley on EVERY build:** with the dice forced to hit and the target unshielded, the previous build (v2.76-S187) peaked at 2.16 / 1.68 / 2.27 (player volley / enemy volley / both at once; up to 16,551 clipped samples) and this build at 1.71 / 1.39 / 1.99. That is the existing 'explosion' (gain 0.8) and 'shieldhit' (0.25) sounds stacking; natural volleys do not clip. A master limiter on the whole game output would remove it for every sound; it was NOT built (it touches everything). (3) A Klingon player cannot meet a Klingon enemy (the enemy list excludes the player's faction), so two D-7s never fire at each other; the player's and the AI's volleys never overlap in the real phase order (the AI fires after the player's results have landed), so the same-instant test was unrealistic and is not the measure used.
**Measured results (real Chromium 141).** Scope: 17 ships, 0 wrong. Player path (D7_A, 5 hexes): effect `tosbolt`, 1 pending, 0 log lines at fire time, result at 0.50 s, clip once, 0 synthesised sounds; the M-mark control still fires a `beam` with the old sound. AI path: 4 bolts, 4 clips. Kill and miss cases as above. Regression: entry window, arming sound, explosions and kills (incl. the mutual kill), Federation torpedoes and phasers, the other factions' ambience (identical), the Damage Control suite (ship fit 0 of 63 overlapping, shield faces 6 of 6, 28 of 28 tooltip checks, all 66 ships draw the tab) and the torpedo-kill explosion visuals: all pass; 0 JavaScript errors. Game now 12,402,475 bytes (+43,795 bytes against v2.76-S187: the clip, 34 KB as base64, and the effect code).
**Harness lessons.** (1) A forced-hit test OVERSTATES loudness and can even reverse a comparison: on forced hits the old build looked louder than the new one, on natural dice the new build was louder until the gain was lowered. Measure loudness with natural dice over several volleys, on both builds. (2) To capture exact effect frames, override `performance.now` in an init script and step it by hand, calling `renderTac()` each step. (3) Look at the effect ON THE MAP at the real zoom before choosing a scale: the ship there is a fraction of the size it had in the proof of concept. (4) A `break` inside nested loops only leaves the inner loop; return from a function instead. (5) The proof of concept's sizes cannot be taken in ship-relative terms on the map (a bolt 10% of a 25-px ship is 2 px). (6) `String(1.0)` is "1": build filenames with care.
**Not verified:** how the sound or the bolts look and feel to a player (the owner's judgement; the scale 1.4 and the gain 0.22 are choices, each one constant); other zoom levels, window sizes and high-DPI screens for the bolt size; the effect on a very slow or very fast frame rate beyond the real-time clock. **Open / for later:** a master limiter (finding 2); whether other original-series Klingon ships or other factions' weapons should get their own effects; wishlist C10.

### 0.143 — What changed in v2.76-S187 (DAMAGE CONTROL REDESIGN: fit, labels, tooltips, repair-ready layout, and two old bugs)

**User request (2026-11-03), after a hard Chandley-vs-Winged-Defender win (combat log attached; the Admiral-tier Romulan cloaked and the cloak-scan mechanic worked as designed):** "The ship's silhouette overlaps the shield arcs (This is true for most ships I've played as) and there needs to be more labeling providing more information for the player as to what the bar graphs are. What is 46 percent on the left? Is that power? Is that weapon availability? better labeling and perhaps tool tip pop info too. Remember we're going to be getting to a point where there'll be an RPG aspect by bridge crew that will have the opportunity to repair damage. We should be going in that direction in our presentations."
**Answer to the question.** The left gauge is **POWER (engine output remaining)**: `currentPower / totalPower`, here 24 of the Chandley's 52 units = 46%. The right gauge is **SENSORS** (array condition, 0-100%). Both already had titles in the code ("PWR", "SNS"), but they were drawn ABOVE a column that was taller than the visible canvas, so only the percentage below each was ever on screen. The same quantity was also called "Warp Core" (sidebar and bottom status bar) and "total power" (the log); the game's own tooltips already said POWER, so POWER is now the one word on this tab and in the status bar.
**What was built.** (1) **Fit:** `dmgDrawShipArt()` (the ship-art drawing, now its own function) shrinks the art about the ring centre by `dmgFitK()` so that every non-transparent pixel sits inside the shield hexagon by `DMG_RING_MARGIN` (1.1 units) and above the superstructure caption; measured from the art's own alpha, once per art and track size, in unit space (so independent of window size). (2) **Gauges:** title, subtitle, a 100/50/0% scale on the outer side, the percentage, units ("24 / 52 units"; sensors "lock/scan: ON/OFF") and a condition word from `dmgCondition()` (NOMINAL 90+, REDUCED 61-89, IMPAIRED 31-60, CRITICAL 1-30, OFFLINE 0; the thresholds match the bar colours). Gauges now **fill from the bottom** like any gauge (they filled from the top), so the scale reads correctly. (3) **Face labels** sit outside the ring on each edge's outward normal and show live points ("F-PORT 16/16", or "F-PORT  DESTROYED", falling back to "F-PORT  ✕" when the window is too narrow). The old X drawn over the face name (it hid "FWD") is gone; the arc keeps its own X. (4) **Superstructure track** wraps into rows of at most 14 boxes (`DMG_SS`), sits inside the ring, and has a caption with the numbers ("SUPERSTRUCTURE  15/50  30%  ⚠ BREACH"). (5) **Legend** along the bottom explains the ring colours. (6) **Tooltips** (`dmgTipHtml`, shown in the existing `#ship-tooltip`, class `dc` for the wider body): gauges, every shield face (arc line or label), the track, the ship (weapons summary) and every System Status row. Each says what the system is, what damage does (checked against `applyDamage`, `checkVictory` and the sensor code: power 0 = total power failure and the battle is lost; a sensors hit costs 3x its damage in percent, 0 = no lock or scan, below 100% the enemy contact shows static; a destroyed generator lets full damage through and stays destroyed), and the **planned repair station**. (7) **System Status sidebar** is grouped (HULL, SHIELD GENERATORS, POWER, SENSORS, WEAPONS), each group with a condition word and its station tag; dead rows now read "DESTROYED" in a legible red. (8) The hull-warning text that used to be drawn on top of the left gauge ("ENGINES: 25% ... HULL BREACH") is removed; the information is on the gauges and the breach warning is on the track caption. One shared layout function `dmgGeom()` now serves the canvas, the spark spawner and the frame loop (they used to repeat the formula three times).
**Repair-ready layout (the RPG direction).** The tab now follows FASA's own Damage Control Display: the Superstructure Damage Track and the Systems Repair Status Tracks (rulebook p.11-12: one for sensors, one per shield generator, four for engineering functions, with the repair roll tied to an assigned officer). Every tooltip ends "REPAIR STATION (planned): X. Crew repair is not in the game yet, so damage is permanent for this battle." **The station assignments are a PROPOSAL for the owner to correct**, built on FASA's four control-panel displays (Engineering, Helm, Weapons, Damage Control) plus Science for sensors: Power = Engineering, Shield generators = Engineering, Sensors = Science, Weapons = Weapons, Hull = Damage Control. They live in one place (`dmgStn()` and the group headers in `renderDmgView()`); when wishlist A5 is built that sentence must change. A4/A5 are otherwise untouched.
**Two old bugs found and fixed.** (a) **Shield generator damage was drawn on the wrong faces** for three of the six (since v1.79-S90, HANDOVER §0.26; the original v2.67 upload has it too). The ring used the order FWD, F-P, F-S, AFT, A-P, A-S, but the game's order (`SHIELD_NAMES`, and every log line) is Fwd, F-Stbd, A-Stbd, Aft, A-Port, F-Port: a destroyed F-Stbd generator was drawn at F-Port, A-Stbd at F-Stbd, F-Port at A-Stbd (the charge colours likewise). Fixed with `DMG_FACES` in the game's order. Measured: 3 of 6 faces correct before, 6 of 6 after. (b) **The damage tint was drawn as a brown box.** `source-atop` onto the main canvas tints everything under the image because the canvas is already opaque, so every damaged dedicated-art ship (below 70% hull) had a brown rectangle around it. The art is now tinted on a private copy and that is drawn. Measured: the opaque pixel count of the damaged art equals the undamaged count for every ship.
