**Measured results (real Chromium 141, every ship through the real draw path).** Overlap: **57 of the 63 playable ships (60 of all 66) had art pixels outside the ring or on the track before (worst overshoot 5.6 units); 0 after.** Fit scale k: min 0.734, median 0.845 (the median ship is 15% smaller), 5 ships needed no change. Layout: 16 combinations (4 ships x window sizes 1500x900, 1280x720, 1024x640, 860x560, every generator destroyed to force the longest labels): 0 clipped or overlapping elements. Sweep: all 66 registry entries draw the whole tab and sidebar with no error. Tooltips (real mouse, 28 checks): gauges, all six faces by arc and by label naming the right face, track, ship, sidebar rows, empty-space hide, class reset, and the older stats-bar tooltip still working and not styled as `dc`: 28 of 28. Regression: entry window, hum on this tab, explosion sound and kills (including the mutual kill), arming sound, torpedo-kill explosion visuals: all pass. Game now 12,358,680 bytes (+12,065 bytes against v2.75-S186).
**Housekeeping in this pass.** The quoted user text in §0.141 and §0.142 had stray backslashes from a quoting slip in earlier turns; removed.
**Harness lessons.** (1) Reproduce the user's screen first (a scenario that sets the same damage), then compare before and after on the same scenario. (2) Do pixel analysis INSIDE the page and return numbers: my first shield-face test shipped about five million values out of the browser per face and timed out at 300 s. (3) A hover-region overlap check includes padding and the scale labels, so it flagged a layout that was only tight; make the check match what is visible, then fix the cause (the compact label fallback). (4) Check arithmetic in expected values: 13 of 22 boxes is 59%, not 60%. (5) The tutorial coach card (`#tut-coach`) covers the bottom of the screen in screenshots; hide it first. (6) `globalCompositeOperation='source-atop'` on a canvas that is already opaque tints everything: tint a private copy. (7) Write documentation scripts as files with raw strings: an escaping slip in an inline script silently skipped every edit once, and left stray backslashes before.
**Not verified:** how it looks on a real GPU or in Firefox/Safari (only headless Chromium); windows narrower than 860 px; a UI Scale above 100% (the new sidebar classes are not in the UI Scale list, like `.sys-nm` before them); touch devices (the hover tooltips have no touch equivalent); whether the median 15% shrink of the ships feels too small (an alternative is to enlarge the ring: a layout decision for the owner).
**Open / for later:** the baked-in lettering on the sprites (the Chandley art reads NCC-2301, its data says NCC-1838; HANDOVER entry of 2026-10-26); the owner's decision on the proposed repair stations; a weapons readout on the canvas itself (today weapons are in the sidebar and the ship hover); wishlist A4/A5 (crew and repair mechanics).

### 0.142 — Documentation only: the owner's era decisions for the ships FASA does not date (no game change; the game stays v2.75-S186)

**User decisions (2026-11-02), after reviewing the §0.141 classification:** "The Chandley can be a TMP era one. It has the stylings consistent with that era. The Gorn can stay unknown and straddle both era. So little is known about them. The Federation I has a TOS era look and the Federation II has a TMP era look."
**Applied (read the Chandley decision as Chandley Mk II, the ship that was flagged as straddling):** Chandley Mk II = **TMP**; Federation I Marks I-VI = **TOS**; Federation II Marks I-II = **TMP**; Gorn SS-3, MA-12, BH-2 = **both eras**. These are the owner's judgement calls on appearance and on how little is known, **not FASA dates**, and `FASA_TOS_to_TMP_Timeline.md` marks them as such. **Final classification of the 63 playable ships: 30 TOS, 28 TMP, 3 in both eras (the Gorn), 2 unassigned (the Orion Lightning and Wanderer).** 50 ships are placed by FASA date, 13 by the owner's decision.
**Recorded in the timeline file as an unverified hypothesis:** HANDOVER's "Federation I in service 2248-2268" (from the fasaststcs site) would convert to about 2191-2211 on FASA's scale if it is on the canon-aligned scale (56-58 years later), which is TOS era and would agree with the owner's call; if it is on FASA's scale it would be TMP or later, which would not. Not resolved.
**Open:** whether the whole Chandley class (so Mk I, December 2216, currently TOS by date) should be TMP; the Orion (could be treated like the Gorn); the four other refit-interval ships; the five ships dated 2217 itself. Still **nothing written into `SHIP_REGISTRY`**: populating an `introduced` or era field needs an explicit go-ahead (wishlist A10, §0.92).

### 0.141 — Documentation only: the TOS/TMP era rule, the FASA stardate conversion, and the ship era classification (no game change; the game stays v2.75-S186)

**User instructions (2026-11-02):** (1) the user was sure the rules contained a conversion for the timeline file ("read through the rules"); (2) "Go with FASA's published timeline to make the distinction between TMP and TOS era"; (3) update `FASA_TOS_to_TMP_Timeline.md` with all findings, as it "will be your source of truth in the project section"; (4) list every ship that falls in the TOS era and the TMP era for review.
**Outcome.** `FASA_TOS_to_TMP_Timeline.md` was rewritten (in the outputs folder; the project-folder copy is read-only, so the user must re-upload it). It now holds the conversion rule, FASA's published timeline, the corrections to the old file, the canon comparison, the classification of all 63 playable ships, the open decisions, and every dated mark in the three manuals converted. **Read that file before doing any era or date work; this entry is only the summary.**
**The conversion (found by web research; it is not in the rulebook scan, which only says dates are "in Stardates", p.57).** FASA Reference Stardate **C/YYMM**: year = 2000 + 100 x C + YY, month = MM (the Romulan manual prints only C/YY). Checked against FASA's own examples and against the project's Baker Mk II data (`2/1606` = June 2216).
**What it showed.** All dated marks in the Federation, Klingon and Romulan manuals convert to the **2180s-2220s** (Federation April 2187 to March 2223; the manual is stamped "published 2/2306" = June 2223). On that scale the Enterprise class is **April 2217**, the Excelsior **October 2222**, the Klingon L-24 **April 2222**, the Romulan V-30 **2217**.
**FASA's published timeline for the era hinge (Trekipedia FASA pages):** Kirk's five-year mission **2207-2212**; Admiral at Star Fleet Command 2212-2217; the refit Enterprise returns to duty and the **V'Ger Incident in 2217**; Enterprise-A launched 15 October 2222. **Era rule adopted: TOS era = entered service before 2217; TMP era = 2217 (RSD 2/1700) or later.**
**The old timeline file was wrong, and why.** It gave V'Ger / the Enterprise refit / the V-30 as **2271** (FASA: **2217**, the same two digits swapped; the V-30's `2/17` in the Romulan manual proves it), the end of the five-year mission as **2269** (FASA: **2212**; the old value is on the canon-aligned scale, about 56-58 years later), and two early anchors (`0/87` = 2121, `0/97` = 2139) that the formula turns into 2087 and 2097. Other old claims (L-13 refit, Gorn SS-3 detection, 2272 funding reversal, 2273 D-7 exchange and others) are **unverified** and listed in the file; do not rely on them. Some wiki pages show a canon-aligned year beside a stardate (for example "2/1104 (April 2269)" against "April 2211" in the text); always use the formula, never that display.
**Initial classification result (63 playable ships; superseded by the owner's decisions in §0.142): 24 TOS, 25 TMP, 1 straddling the line (Chandley Mk II), 13 with no FASA date** (Federation I x6 and II x2 are not in the manuals; the Gorn and Orion sheets print "Date Entering Service - Unknown" or are illegible). Five ships are dated in the refit interval 2213-2216 (Larson Mk VII, Remora Mk III, Baker Mk II, Chandley Mk I, Klingon D-10 D) and are listed as TOS with a flag; five are dated 2217 itself and are flagged as boundary-sensitive. **Nothing was written into `SHIP_REGISTRY`**: populating an `introduced` year on every hull (wishlist A10, HANDOVER §0.92) still needs an explicit go-ahead.
**Consequence for A9/A10.** The A10 example "no Excelsior in a 2250 scenario" was canon-scale thinking; on FASA's scale the Excelsior enters service in October 2222, so scenario years must be written in FASA-scale years (an Excelsior check would be "not before 2222").
**Lessons.** (1) Never state that a file is absent without listing the folder: the timeline file WAS in the project and I wrongly said it was not (my check had only covered the files I chose to open). (2) I cited the FASA module number 2217 (*Where Has All the Glory Gone?*) as if it supported the 2217 date; it is a catalogue number (like 2302, 2214) and is **not** evidence; the dates rest on the pages and manual data listed in the timeline file. (3) Two date scales coexist in the sources (FASA's and a canon-aligned one); label every year with its scale.
**Not verified:** FASA dates for the Federation I and II; anything about the Gorn and Orion; FASA timeline material after 2224; the ranking of the five refit-interval ships (a user decision).

### 0.140 — What changed in v2.75-S186 (BUG FIX: the ship-destruction visuals were missing on torpedo kills)

**User report (2026-11-02), after beating the IKV Ever-Victorious (L-24, CE ratio 1.3 : 1 against the player) in the USS Federation (Federation I Mk VI) using an asteroid field as cover (combat log attached, v2.74-S185):** "When the klingon blew up I heard the sound for explosion but the visual effect for it is gone. this had an ever expanding ring from the center. What happened to it?"
**Combat-log review.** Nothing in the log is wrong. The player won in round 5 with the last blow a TORPEDO ("FP-5 Tube 1 ... Superstructure hit -16 -> 0 boxes remain", with tube 2's torpedo still in flight: "FP-5 Tube 2: HIT but the fight is already decided"), which is exactly the case that triggers the bug below. The log also shows asteroid cover working ("+1 cover, beam weapons partially deflected" on all the enemy's beams), a planet blocking the sensor path in round 1, the Fwd shield generator lost twice over the fight (the player stopped shielding), and the debrief (adversary CAPTAIN, 9 of 9 hits on the Fwd shield, enemy lock held in 9 of 12 windows).
**Root cause (found, reproduced, and proven pre-existing).** The destruction animation (`playDestructionSequence`) runs its own `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`tick`): each frame it calls `renderTac()` to redraw the map and then paints the detonation flash, the hex-accurate shockwave ring and the fireball on top. But the tactical map ALSO has a permanent loop, `frame()` inside `initTac`, that calls `renderTac()` on every animation frame forever. Both loops draw to the same canvas in the same frame, so the explosion survives only if its loop runs AFTER the map loop; the order is fixed by which loop registered its next `requestAnimationFrame` first. When the destruction starts from event or timer code (a phaser kill: the beam's result is resolved inside `fireWeapon`) the map loop registered earlier, so it runs first and the explosion is painted on top: visible. When the killing blow is a TORPEDO, its result is deliberately held back until the projectile lands (v2.61-S172) and is then delivered from INSIDE the FX drawing, i.e. inside the map loop's own `renderTac()` call, so `playDestructionSequence` registers `tick` BEFORE `frame()` reaches the end of its callback and registers itself; from then on every frame runs `tick` first and `frame` second, and `frame`'s `renderTac()` repaints the whole map over the explosion before it is ever shown. Result: no flash, no ring, no fireball, while the sound (and the victory panel) still happened. The same applies to a torpedo (or any projectile) that kills the PLAYER. **It is NOT caused by the explosion sound added in v2.73-S184** (that call sits above the early return, and was checked): the identical torpedo-landing kill on the user's original upload (v2.67-S178) also shows no flash, ring or fireball. It went unnoticed because beam kills are unaffected and, until now, the user's kills (and the previous two logs') were beam kills.
**The fix.** `let destructionActive = 0` (next to `explosionImages`); `frame()` now does `if(!destructionActive) renderTac();` (it still advances its animation clock), so while a destruction animation runs, the map loop stands aside and the animation's own loop draws the scene and the explosion in one pass; `playDestructionSequence` increments the counter when the animation really starts (after the frames-empty early return) and `endDestruction()` decrements it exactly once, on normal completion OR from a safety timer `EXPAND_MS + 2500` = 3.8 s, so the map can never be left unrendered even if the animation loop were to die. The counter also handles two animations overlapping. No change to the animation itself or to any sound.
**Verification (real Chromium 141; screenshots, with the kill delivered the way the game delivers it).** (1) Reproduction: a real forced-hit `fireWeapon('fp5')` whose landing is made the killing blow (the game's own `checkVictory()` runs right after the weapon's result), screenshots at 0.12 / 0.32 / 0.52 s after the animation starts: BEFORE the fix (v2.74-S185) and on the user's ORIGINAL v2.67-S178 upload no flash, ring or fireball appears (only the torpedo's own impact glow), and the Victory panel arrives; a PHASER kill in v2.74-S185 shows the ring. (2) After the fix: the same torpedo-landing kill shows the ring sweeping out across the map and the fireball; the phaser kill still shows it; and the mirror case (the enemy's KP-6 torpedo landing and destroying the PLAYER, staged with `triggerWeaponFX(enemy, player, ...)` and a result callback that kills the player) shows the detonation glow at +0.12 s and the shockwave ring at +0.32 s where v2.74-S185 showed nothing (see `destruction_ring_before_after.png`). (3) Side effects: the map redraws at 57 per second idle, 47 per second during the animation (its own loop draws the scene, no gap), and 47-58 per second right after it ends; two overlapping animations count 2 and release to 0; with a SIMULATED dead animation loop (its first `requestAnimationFrame` swallowed) the map froze at 0 redraws per second and the safety timer restored it by itself after 3.8 s (56 per second). (4) Regression: the explosion sound (enemy, player, fallback, the real kill route, mutual destruction: still one clip each, the second 1.34 s after the first), Federation torpedoes and phasers, the entry window, the arming sound, the other four factions' ambience (identical to v2.74-S185). 0 JavaScript errors. Game now 12,346,615 bytes (+1,128 bytes against v2.74-S185).
**Also checked, no change needed:** the CLOAK effect has its own loop too (`triggerCloakFx`), but it only keeps `renderTac()` running while the effect, which is drawn INSIDE `renderTac`, animates, so there is no overlay that can be painted over. The viewscreen's destruction fireball (a separate canvas, `renderViewscreenInline`) is independent of this bug.
**Harness lessons (so they are not repeated).** (1) A kill started from `page.evaluate()` runs OUTSIDE the render loop and cannot reproduce this bug (my first reproduction showed a healthy ring): trigger the kill so it resolves INSIDE `renderTac`, i.e. through a real torpedo landing (force the hit with `Math.random = () => 0` and wrap `checkVictory` to zero the hull as the weapon's result lands). (2) The weapon ids differ per ship: query `GS.player.weapons` (the Federation I Mk VI has `fp5`/`fp5_1` torpedoes and `fh10*`/`fh8*` phasers, not the Constitution's `fp1`/`fh3`). (3) A pixel-counting "near-white pixels" metric on screenshots was unreliable (random terrain, the torpedo's own glow); a labelled contact sheet of frames at fixed offsets after the kill is the dependable proof. (4) Two loops drawing the same canvas in the same frame is an ordering hazard: when adding another overlay animation, draw it from inside `renderTac` (or suppress the map loop while it runs, as here).
**Not verified:** how the ring looks on the user's own display at other UI scales or on a real GPU (the screenshots are from headless Chromium at 100 percent); Firefox / Safari. **Open / for later:** nothing new.

### 0.139 — What changed in v2.74-S185 (AUDIO BUILD 7: the arming sound for every weapon)

**User request (2026-11-02), after playing another full session (combat log attached, v2.73-S184):** "Great sounds! and the combat was close! Almost lost! The 'enter the simulator' prompt is good as well. I'm thinking to add the load torpedo sound for even the phasers as well. I don't have another option for some kind of auditory feedback for the player when weapons are selected. Let's go ahead and add that sound for the phasers too. Otherwise good to go for now. Be sure to update all the MD files as well."
**Combat-log review.** Nothing in the log looks wrong; it is a legitimately close fight (the Constitution lost its Fwd shield generator in round 1, took engine hits down to 22 total power, put 0 points into shields for the later rounds, and won in round 6 with the enemy at 0 boxes; the AI was rated ENSIGN, CE ratio 1.0 : 1). It exercised the audio exactly as designed: FIRE ALL volleys of 5, 3, 4 and 4 weapons, a mid-volley kill ("the fight is already decided" shots after it), and 2 to 5 weapons armed per turn. The user played v2.73-S184 and reports the sounds, the swoosh change and the entry window all work as wanted (no complaint about the 13.5 s bed or the door swoosh frequency).
**What changed.** In `togArm()` (the only way a player turns a weapon on for charging) the load/charge sound was played only when `w.type === 'missile'`. It now plays whenever a weapon is switched ON (`if(on) playFactionSfx('weaponArm')`): phaser banks (`FH`), lasers (`FL`) and torpedo tubes alike, because the purpose is audible feedback that the selection registered and the user wanted no other feedback mechanism. **Switching a weapon OFF stays silent** (unchanged), and the sound is Federation-only via the faction table: `FACTION_SFX.fed.torpLoad` was RENAMED `weaponArm` (it is no longer torpedo-only; the asset is still `fed_torp_load`, the same 1.045 s clip, gain 0.40). Klingon, Romulan, Gorn and Orion hear nothing when arming, as before. (HANDOVER §0.137 and the §0.132-§0.138 text that say `torpLoad` refer to the old key name.)
**The pile-up problem found and handled.** Five or more of these 1-second clips can overlap when a whole ship's weapons are armed quickly, so peaks were measured on the AUDIO THREAD (worklet meter, real policy, bridge playing). Before any change: a hurried player (one weapon per 200 ms) peaked at 0.68 / 0.67 (USS Constitution 5 weapons / Federation2_MkI, the Federation ship with the MOST weapons: 14), a very fast clicker (100 ms) at 0.84 / 0.91, and a machine-gun 30 ms apart at 0.94 / **1.459 with 149 samples at or above 0.98 (clipping)**. Humans do not click 33 times a second, but a future "arm all" button would, so a small guard was added: `UI_SFX_MAXVOICES = {fed_torp_load: 4}` and `uiSfxVoices` in `playUiSfx`: at most 4 voices of that sound ring at once; when a new one starts the OLDEST is faded out over 40 ms and stopped, and `onended` removes finished voices. Every click still gets its sound. After: hurried 0.68 / 0.66, very fast 0.74 / 0.80, machine-gun 0.84 / **0.91 with 0 clipped samples**; with 14 weapons armed 30 ms apart, 14 clicks started 14 sounds, 4 were ringing right after, and 0 remained once they finished (no leaked voices). The same cap mechanism can be given to any other sound by adding it to `UI_SFX_MAXVOICES`.
**Verification (real Chromium 141, DEFAULT autoplay policy, real clicks).** Federation (USS Constitution, 3 phaser banks + 2 torpedo tubes): each of the five weapons switched ON plays the load clip once (48,384 samples at the 44.1 kHz context), switching a phaser bank or a tube OFF plays nothing, switching a bank back ON plays it again, and the armed state is correct afterwards; Klingon (5 weapons), Romulan (2), Gorn (6) and Orion (8): arming every weapon by real clicks plays NO load clip. Regression on this build: the entry window (all ten scenarios, real policy), Federation torpedoes (load x1 on arming a tube, fire clip x1 per launch with no synthesised torpedo, the AI's torpedo still synthesised), Federation phasers (FH bank plays the recording, an FL laser / the AI / a Klingon beam keep the synthesised sound, a three-bank volley plays it three times, the real `fireWeapon` plays it once per bank), explosions (enemy, player, fallback, the real kill route, mutual destruction), the other four factions' ambience identical to v2.73-S184 on every tab, the bridge edge cases (late decode, decode failure, double Engage), the console chirps, the hum, and a full FIRE ALL volley with a kill (4 runs: peaks 0.81-0.86, no sample at or above 0.98, against 0.76-0.96 last build). 0 JavaScript errors throughout. Game now 12,345,487 bytes (+883 bytes against v2.73-S184: no new audio, only the hook change and the voice cap).
**Not verified:** how the load sound feels on a PHASER (the user chose it and can judge; it is one clip at `UI_SFX_GAIN.fed_torp_load` = 0.40, one constant to lower if five in a row is too much), whether the 4-voice cap is ever audible (it only engages when more than 4 overlap, i.e. arming faster than about 4 weapons per second); Firefox / Safari (only Chromium was run); a real sound device. **Open / for later:** a different (shorter) arming sound for phasers if the long torpedo clip proves too much when arming many weapons; selection feedback for the other factions (they have none); the optional master limiter; per-faction recordings; roadmap item C10.

### 0.138 — What changed in v2.73-S184 (AUDIO BUILD 6: entry window, swoosh-free bridge, door swoosh isolated, Federation phaser, ship explosion)

**User request (2026-11-01), after playing a whole session (combat log attached, v2.72-S183; "The sounds played well"):** (1) the bridge door "shwoosh" is heard too often; (2) a new sound for any ship blowing up (`smallexplosion1.mp3`), "streamlined with your resources"; (3) use the earlier "click anywhere for sound" idea as a small window up front, "Click here to enter the Simulator"; (4) isolate and export the door swoosh like the torpedo clips, for the user's RPG project in another thread; (5) analyse `tos_ship_phaser_short.mp3` and use the appropriate audio when Federation phasers fire.
**Combat-log review.** Nothing in the log looks wrong. It shows what the audio has to cope with: volleys of up to FIVE weapons at once (3 phaser banks + 2 torpedo tubes, "FIRE ALL: 5 weapons"), kills that land mid-volley ("FP-1 Tube 1: MISS but the fight is already decided": the leftover shots still launch, so their sounds overlap the explosion), and 2 torpedo tubes armed most turns (two overlapping load sounds). That is why a peak/clipping check on a full volley with a kill was added (section G).
**A. The door swoosh (isolated, then removed from the loop).** *What it is.* In the bridge recording the door sound is a ~0.5 s broadband burst: hiss across ~1.5-5.8 kHz for ~0.45 s, a LOW THUMP below ~140 Hz at ~0.42-0.47 s, and a small upward blip at ~0.48-0.55 s. It adds nothing below ~1.2 kHz (burst vs the ambience beside it: 150-500 Hz +0-2 dB, 500-1200 Hz about 0, 1.2-3.5 kHz +12 dB, 3.5-9 kHz +23 dB). The 4:17 recording holds 27 broadband bursts in two kinds: ~0.5 s door swooshes (often in pairs ~3.9 s apart: open/close) and 0.2 s chirps. The OLD 22 s loop (9.45-31.54 s) contained THREE swooshes plus a chirp: about 8 per minute; the whole recording averages ~7 per minute. *Isolation.* An early "two families" reading was an artifact (instances "matched" at a lag of 0.8 s where they barely overlap, and correlation over a tiny overlap is spuriously high; a first alignment also had the lag sign wrong). Done properly (alignment bounded to +-100 ms around each burst start, burst-only comparison): a cluster of door swooshes at 113.3, 117.2, 153.1, 157.0, 186.4 and 190.3 s correlate 0.72-0.93 with a template; six instances were aligned and amplitude-normalised to the median burst level (an iterative template had collapsed the scale; fixed). Averaging alone only lifted the burst from +5.4 to +9.4 dB over the ambience (the instances are not sample-identical), so a two-layer clean-up: (i) HISS layer: 4th-order zero-phase high-pass at 1.1 kHz plus narrow notches (Q 40) at the ambience's weak steady lines inside that range (1556.4, 2632.7, 3236.9, 4823.7, 4833.3, 4859.6, 4867.3 Hz); (ii) THUMP layer: the average low-passed at 140 Hz and kept ONLY inside a raised-cosine window 0.34-0.58 s after the burst start (a plain high-pass would have deleted the thump). Result: the ambience-only band (130-1100 Hz) went from -47.6 to -64.8 dBFS (17 dB quieter) while the swoosh band moved by only 1.5 dB. Clip = 10 ms before the burst start to 0.62 s after (0.630 s), 4 ms fade-in, 60 ms fade-out; the original peak is -28.8 dBFS, so it is normalised to -3 dBFS (+25.8 dB, factor 19.54). **Delivered standalone as `bridge_door_swoosh.wav` (48 kHz stereo 16-bit, 0.630 s, peak -3 dBFS, 94% of the energy in 1.1-6.5 kHz, 4.4% in the thump band) plus `bridge_door_swoosh_before_after.png`.** *In the game:* `fed_door`, MP3 44.1 kHz stereo 128 kbps, 10,911 bytes; `UI_SFX_GAIN.fed_door` = 0.1024 = the bridge gain (2.0) / 19.54, which restores the ORIGINAL level relative to the bed; measured in the recorded output the door sits at -43.3 dBFS (3.5-9 kHz band) against -42.8 dBFS in the recording, and +23.5 dB above the bridge ambience on average (+21 to +23 in the recording; it varies with the bed's own HF level).
**B. The bridge bed rebuilt without the swoosh.** The loop now comes from a stretch of the recording with no door sound at all. The clip is [start-up | 1 s crossfade | bed loop] (16 kHz stereo MP3, 48 kbps, **135,909 bytes, 51,192 bytes smaller than before**). *Search (and two of my own mistakes):* a first search on audio low-passed to ~3 kHz reported a 0.936 wrap, but at FULL bandwidth that point scored only 0.31-0.61 (the low-passed search only saw the steady tones); a full-band (24 kHz) search found the real optimum, and refining with a +-30 sample window then missed it because I had rounded the points to two decimals of a second (the match is razor-sharp in time: up to +-240 samples lost); a +-400 sample refinement found it. Final: start-up ends at sample 455,128 (9.48183 s), loop 3,595,200 .. 4,243,880 (74.90000 .. 88.41417 s of the original, **13.5142 s**), full-band correlation **0.9675 for the wrap and 0.9677 for the join** (the other candidate, 31.40-44.82 s, scored 0.9649 / 0.9653). That the start-up end matches the bed this well says the recording repeats long stretches of its ambience. Join: 1 s crossfade, correlation rho 0.977, power-compensated law (near-linear); in clip time the loop is `FED_BR_LS` = 8.7448 s .. `FED_BR_LE` = 22.2590 s; `buildFedBridge` (unchanged) blends the last 1.0 s of the loop linearly into the 1.0 s before it. **Trade-off to tell the user:** the loop is 13.5 s instead of 22.09 s, because there are few swoosh-free stretches (26.6-47.6 s and 72.6-91.4 s are the only ones >= 18 s; the others top out near 13 s, and a 17.7 s loop in the first stretch only reached 0.84). The bed's own gentle pulse therefore repeats every 13.5 s; without the distinctive swooshes that is much less noticeable than before. The loop region contains three tiny ticks (single 20 ms windows at -58 dBFS in the 3.5-9 kHz band, ~11 dB below a door swoosh and 28x shorter): part of the ambience, not door sounds. *Verification:* unit test at 48000 / 44100 / 32000 / 96000 / 16000 Hz: loop 13.514 s everywhere, wrap jump 0.02-0.06x the largest nearby step (UNBLENDED control up to 0.79x, 6.7x the mean step), loudness through the blend identical to the raw tail (-47..-32 dB); real run recorded on the AUDIO THREAD for 40.65 s (real policy, tab switches, both wraps at 22.26 s and 35.77 s): the output equals 2x the looped buffer bit-for-bit (max difference 0.00 over 26.6 s), measured gain 2.00, ducking to ~0 on Damage Control and back, correlation 1.00.
**C. The door swoosh now plays rarely, from code.** `scheduleFedDoor()` (started in `beginFedBridge`, cleared in `stopFedBridge`): the first swoosh 18-34 s after Engage (`FED_DOOR_FIRST_S`), then one every 25-55 s (`FED_DOOR_EVERY_S`), mean about 40 s = **about 1.5 per minute (was ~8 per minute in the loop)**; it plays only while the bridge is audible (not on Damage Control), the game is not over and the context is running. Checked: over 4000 draws the delays span exactly 18.0-34.0 s (mean 26.0) and 25.0-55.0 s (mean 39.9); with the timers shortened to 2-5 s over 60 s the swoosh played 4 times on Tactical, 0 times during the Damage Control visit, 3 times after returning, and 0 after the victory.
**D. Federation phaser sound.** *The file (measured).* `tos_ship_phaser_short.mp3` is 4.68 s but holds only ~0.65 s of sound: a 38 ms blip at 4-42 ms (centroid 2.7 kHz, peak 0.48), 180 ms of digital silence, then ONE steady tone 0.250-0.886 s (0.636 s; a warble alternating ~1.35 kHz and ~2.6 kHz, amplitude-modulation depth 0.495, RMS -9.2 dBFS, peak 0.822, stereo L/R correlation 0.60), a HARD CUT at -9 dBFS (-9 to -61 dBFS in 10 ms), then 3.8 s of digital silence. *Clip:* the tone only, 0.248-0.900 s, 0.5 ms fade-in, 40 ms fade-out; the opening blip is LEFT OUT (it reads as an edit leftover and would sound like a stray tick 200 ms before every shot: tell the user, it may have been deliberate). MP3 44.1 kHz stereo **160 kbps**, 13,629 bytes (at 96 kbps the pre-echo before the attack was only 24 dB below it, at 160 kbps 45 dB). *Game:* only the PLAYER's Federation phaser banks (`desig` starting `FH`, 145 uses across the playable ships) use it, via `FACTION_SFX.fed.phaserFire`, in the beam branch of `triggerWeaponFX`; Federation LASERS (`FL-6`, 13 uses), the AI's beams, every other faction, and any shot where the clip cannot play keep the synthesised sound. Tested with forced misses so the impact sounds cannot confuse the count: FH-3 plays the clip once and no synthesised 0.35 s sine; an FL-6 bank, an AI shooter and a Klingon player's beam play the synthesised sound and no clip; three banks 130 ms apart play the clip three times; the real `fireWeapon('fh3'/'fh3_1'/'fh3_2')` each play it once.
**E. Ship explosion.** *Finding:* `playDestructionSequence()` played NO sound at all (only the weapon-impact thump and the victory/defeat jingle afterwards), so a ship blowing up was silent. *The file:* `smallexplosion1.mp3`, 1.99 s, mono (L = R), peak 0.905, RMS -17.8 dBFS, loud for ~1 s then a long decay (99% of the energy below 2.6 kHz, 99.9% below 5.35 kHz). *Clip:* 0.020-1.750 s (the last 0.24 s is below -60 dBFS), 80 ms fade-out, MP3 **22.05 kHz mono 48 kbps, 10,859 bytes** (envelope correlation 0.9994 at 48k; the constant 3.4 dB tonal "deviation" seen in the encode test was ffmpeg's mono-to-stereo upmix dropping 3 dB, which a browser does not do). *Game:* `if(!playUiSfx('ship_explosion')) snd('explosion');` at the top of `playDestructionSequence`, so EVERY hull destruction (either side, any faction, both ships in a mutual kill) plays it once, and if the clip cannot play the old synthesised explosion fires instead (never silent). Tested: enemy destroyed, player destroyed, clip unavailable (falls back to the 0.6 s synthesised noise), the REAL kill route (enemy hull to 0, the game's own `checkVictory()`: the clip plays once at the kill, never again, and the victory jingle follows after the animation), and mutual destruction (two clips, the second 1.34 s after the first).
**F. The entry window.** A small centred window, styled from the game's own tokens (amber #ff9900 title and 1 px frame, #030810 panel, #1a0800 amber-edged button, letter-spaced Courier New): "STAR TREK / TACTICAL COMMAND SIMULATOR / [ > CLICK HERE TO ENTER THE SIMULATOR ] / SOUND ON, BEST WITH SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES", over the dimmed setup screen (z-index 10000); the button has focus on load (Enter or Space work), the setup screen behind it is `inert` until it closes, and the button pulses softly (not with `prefers-reduced-motion`). It is the page's FIRST CLICK, which is what lets the browser play the start-screen sound at once. It closes on the button's `click` (fade 0.4 s), or BY ITSELF in a browser that allows sound with no gesture. It deliberately does NOT close on the unlock alone: closing on the PRESS would let the release land on whatever lies underneath. **Bug found by testing and fixed:** it first closed on the press (and on a bare Tab key), because the load-time probe leaves a `resume()` request pending that resolves at the first real gesture and its closure looks like "no gesture needed"; fixed with a `gestureSeen` flag set by the first real press/key/touch. Verified under the REAL autoplay policy: load = window shown, focus on the button, screen inert, audio refused; click, Enter and Space = window closed, sound running, loop playing; a mouse press held down = sound starts at once but the window waits for the release; Tab alone = sound starts, window stays; hover and scroll = nothing; a permissive browser = window closes itself and the loop plays; after closing a real click on a faction button works and nothing under the window was triggered; Engage afterwards fades the loop out. A New Mission (page reload) shows the window again, which is also needed for the sound.
**G. Clipping (found, caused by this build, fixed).** A full Federation FIRE ALL (the game's own `fireAllWeapons`: 3 phasers + 2 torpedoes 130 ms apart, bridge playing) was measured on the audio thread. **Previous build v2.72-S183: peaks 0.63-0.85, no clipping. This build with my first gains (phaser 0.30, explosion 0.50): peaks up to 1.145 (+1.2 dBFS), 3-7 samples at or above 0.98 per volley** (the recorded phaser is a steady loud tone and three overlap; the game's own impact explosion plays at gain 0.8 on top). Fix: lowered ONLY the gains added here (phaser 0.30 to **0.20**, explosion 0.50 to **0.40**; the torpedo gains the user approved are unchanged). Result over 8 volleys with a kill: peaks 0.758-0.960, **no sample at or above 0.98**. The margin is thin on the worst case (0.96, versus 0.85 before this build) because the impact explosions stack unpredictably with the hit rolls. An optional safeguard, offered and NOT built: a master DynamicsCompressor limiter on the output (a global change to every sound).
**Sizes.** Game now 12,344,604 bytes (-15,820 bytes against v2.72-S183: three new clips +35,399, entry window and scheduler, minus the 51,192 saved on the bridge clip). New clips: door 10,911, phaser 13,629, explosion 10,859 bytes.
**Harness lessons (so they are not repeated).** (1) Any script launched with `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required` sees the entry window close itself (correct behaviour) so a click on `#enter-btn` times out: test under the DEFAULT policy, entering as a player would (click the button; on builds without the window click a bare spot). (2) When the entry window is open, real mouse clicks on anything else are intercepted (and the screen is `inert`): enter first. (3) `testH` counted bridge sources by buffer length > 1,000,000 samples; the new bed decodes to ~998,600 samples, so it silently reported 0 (a stale filter, not a failure): derive such thresholds from the data. (4) Search at FULL bandwidth when the criterion is full-band (a low-passed search can report a match that is not there), and never round loop points between steps (a razor-sharp match tolerates ~1 sample). (5) A correlation over a tiny overlap is spuriously high: bound the lag. (6) ffmpeg's `-ac 2` upmix of a mono clip drops 3 dB; a browser does not. (7) Python `%` formatting breaks on text containing a percent sign: use placeholders (again).
**Not verified:** how any of it SOUNDS (I cannot listen: the door's naturalness after clean-up, the phaser level 0.20, the explosion level 0.40, whether a 13.5 s bed repeats noticeably in a long session, whether dropping the phaser's opening blip was right); the clipping margin at the worst case (0.96); Firefox / Safari (only Chromium was run; Safari has the strictest autoplay rules); a real sound device. **Open / for later:** the optional master limiter; recordings for the other factions' phasers, explosions-as-faction and bridges; the enemy Federation AI's phasers and torpedoes still use the synthesised sounds by design; roadmap item C10. Keep `tos_ship_phaser_short.mp3`, `smallexplosion1.mp3` and `tos_bridge_1_activate.mp3` in the project folder (sources; NOT embedded).

### 0.137 — What changed in v2.72-S183 (AUDIO BUILD 5: a user-reported start-up problem, and the Federation torpedo sounds)

**User request (2026-11-01):** (1) "there does appear to be an issue, I did not hear the sound until i selected something. In this case I selected the recognition manual section and that's when it started to play." (2) "here's a file that has two distinct sounds [`torpedo_load_fire_short.mp3`]. I need you to separate them out. The first one would be anytime as a federation player selects torpedoes in the power allocation section to be charged. The second sound is when they are fired during combat."
**PART 1 — the start-up problem.** *What was really going on.* Browsers allow a page no sound before a user gesture. The setup-screen sound starts at the first gesture, so on a freshly loaded page it is silent until the first click, which is what the user saw (the first thing they clicked was the Recognition Manual). **Nothing can make a page play with zero interaction in a normal browser** (verified: an AudioContext created by the page's own script at load stays `suspended`, and Chrome logs "The AudioContext was not allowed to start"). That part is a browser rule and is NOT fixable; if the user wants a visible cue, an unobtrusive "click anywhere to enable sound" hint on the setup screen is an option (offered, not built, because it is a UI change).
*What WAS wrong (and is fixed).* The hook waited for a completed `click` or a `keydown`, each registered with `{once:true}`. Measured under the real autoplay policy: a mouse PRESS that never completes as a click (a drop-down, a drag) did not start the sound at all, and activation actually becomes true at `pointerdown`, about 750 ms before a click completes in a test, so the sound started later than it could; a single non-counting event would also use up the only chance. **New hook:** `unlockAudio()` is registered, in the capture phase, for `pointerdown`, `mousedown`, `touchstart`, `touchend`, `keydown` and `click`; it creates/resumes the context and, once `ac.state === 'running'`, removes itself and calls `startSetupAmb()`; until then it retries on every such event (a context that was refused earlier does NOT wake by itself: verified, the pending `resume()` promise from load never resolved after a gesture, so a new `resume()` must be made inside a gesture). It is also tried once at load (`setTimeout(unlockAudio,0)`, after the whole script has run, because the later `let`/`const` declarations are in the temporal dead zone before then): that succeeds only where the browser allows sound without a gesture (verified with the permissive flag: the loop starts by itself, gain 0.15, zero interaction). The AudioContext is therefore now created at load (suspended; Chrome logs one harmless warning); the decodes that used to wait for the first click now happen at load (the hum, the console chirps, the torpedo clips, the Federation bridge for the default faction, the setup loop). Result under the REAL policy (11 first-interaction types, default Chromium): starts on a click, a tap, a key (Tab / Shift / Escape), a click on a `<select>`, and now on a mouse PRESS without release; stays silent, correctly, with no interaction, a wheel scroll, or hover (none of those count as activation).
*Testing flaw this exposed (important).* **Every audio test before this one launched Chromium with `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`, which disables the very rule behind this bug, so the tests could not have shown it.** Run audio tests with the DEFAULT policy. Also: **Playwright's `page.evaluate()` runs script with a simulated user gesture** (`navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive` was already true; an AudioContext created inside `evaluate()` is "running"), so an `evaluate()` can grant the permission under test; create the AudioContext from the page's own script (`addInitScript`) when testing autoplay, and use real `page.mouse` / `page.keyboard` / `page.touchscreen` for the gesture.
**PART 2 — the torpedo sounds.** *The file (measured).* `torpedo_load_fire_short.mp3`: 2.85 s, 160 kbps, 48 kHz, stereo with real stereo content (L/R correlation 0.80), RMS -14 dBFS; the decoded float peak is 1.123, so the source MP3 overshoots full scale (3 samples; a 16-bit conversion clamps them). It holds two sounds with a true digital-silence gap between them (max(|L|,|R|) < 1e-4 for 10.3 ms, 1.0500-1.0603 s): **sound 1** 0.010-1.050 s (loud, about -10 dBFS RMS, 99.9% of its energy below 7.6 kHz, centroid 2.3 kHz, fading to -71 dBFS by its end) and **sound 2** 1.073-2.850 s (loud, 99.9% below 7.2 kHz, centroid 0.67 kHz, and CUT OFF by the end of the file while still audible). *The split.* Cut in the middle of the gap (1.0551 s). Sound 1 = 1.045 s, starting 1 ms before the first sample above -66 dBFS; sound 2 = 1.775 s, same rule; fades: 0.5 ms in, 10 ms out (sound 1) and a 150 ms raised-cosine out on sound 2 (it was truncated, so the natural decay is finished instead of clicking). **One common gain** (-2.0 dB) so the louder true peak lands at -1 dBFS and the two sounds keep the relative loudness the user made them with (sound 1 peak 0.726, RMS -15.0 dBFS; sound 2 peak 0.891, RMS -16.6 dBFS). Delivered standalone as `torpedo_1_load_charge.wav` and `torpedo_2_fire.wav` (48 kHz stereo 16-bit, 200,696 and 340,880 bytes).
*In the game (Federation only, `FACTION_SFX.fed.torpLoad` / `.torpFire`; gains `UI_SFX_GAIN` 0.40 and 0.55).* **Load/charge sound:** in `togArm()` (the ONLY way a player turns a weapon on for charging; the other two code paths only turn it off), when the toggle goes ON and `w.type === 'missile'` (Federation photon torpedoes are `missile`; beams make no sound, disarming makes no sound; each arming click plays it). **Fire sound:** in `triggerWeaponFX()`, the missile branch, where the synthesised `snd('torpedo')` played: `if(!(shooter===GS.player&&playFactionSfx('torpFire'))) snd('torpedo');`, i.e. the PLAYER's torpedo launch uses the recorded sound if the player's faction has one, and otherwise (the AI's torpedo, every other faction's torpedoes, or if the clip cannot play) the synthesised sound plays exactly as before, so the two are never doubled and a failed decode never makes a torpedo silent. `playUiSfx` and `playFactionSfx` now return true/false. Plasma torpedoes (Romulan) are untouched.
*Why MP3 here, and how its start-up delay is removed.* Unlike the 38 KB of chirps (kept as PCM WAV), these clips are long and wide: as 22 kHz stereo WAV they would add ~720 KB. As **44.1 kHz stereo 128 kbps MP3: 17,599 + 28,884 bytes = 46,483 bytes (61,980 base64 characters); the game grew by 63,559 bytes (now 12,360,424)**. Settings were chosen by measurement on a transient-heavy sound (settings tried: 22.05k/64k, 22.05k/96k, 32k/96k, 32k/128k, 44.1k/128k): envelope correlation 0.9997-0.9998, tonal balance within 0.5 dB mean (0.8 dB max), and the pre-echo before the attack 53-63 dB below it at 44.1k/128k (40-53 dB at the cheaper settings, which saved only 11-23 KB). The waveform SNR is only 14.0 / 18.5 dB, which is normal for a noisy sound re-encoded from an MP3 source and is not what the ear judges here. **An MP3 decoder pads the front of a clip** (measured 26.8-28.6 ms), which would delay a sound that has to land on a click or a shot: `UI_SFX_TRIM` marks the two clips, `firstAudibleSec()` finds the true onset in the DECODED audio (first sample above -50 dBFS in either channel, minus 1 ms), and `playUiSfx` starts playback there (`src.start(0, offset)`). Measured at 22.05 / 32 / 44.1 / 48 / 96 kHz: **play() to first audible sample = 0.0-0.3 ms**; the game plays the clip from 1.8-3.5 ms into the original (it skips only the faint lead-in); the played audio correlates 0.979 / 0.989 (L) and 0.981 / 0.997 (R) with the original clip, the attack (first 80 ms) 0.96-0.98.
*Verification (real Chromium 141, DEFAULT autoplay policy, real clicks).* Power Allocation on the USS Constitution (3 phaser banks FH-3, 2 torpedo tubes FP-1): arming a phaser = no clip, no synthesised sound; arming tube 1 = the load clip x1 (decoded length 48,384 samples at the 44.1 kHz context) and no synthesised oscillators; clicking it again (disarm) = nothing; arming it again = x1; arming tube 2 = x1. Combat, with the enemy placed on a hex the GAME's own `getWeaponBlockReason` accepts (in range, in arc; a first attempt at guessing the geometry was refused by the game and tested nothing): the real `fireWeapon('fp1')` and `fireWeapon('fp1_1')` each play the fire clip x1 (79,488 samples) and NO synthesised torpedo sound; a phaser bank is unchanged (synthesised); `triggerWeaponFX(shooter = GS.enemy, ...)` with a missile uses the synthesised sound and no clip. Other factions (Klingon IKS Devisor KP tube, Romulan ChR Winged Defender RP tube, Gorn SS-3 GP tube, Orion Wanderer): arming plays no clip and firing plays the synthesised sound with no clip, IDENTICAL to the previous build (checked with no-action controls: the "2 oscillators" seen at arm time were the tactical ambience's own pings). Regression on this build: the other four factions' ambience on every tab identical to v2.71; the Federation bridge edge cases (late decode, decode failure, double Engage); the hum seam and tab logic; the console chirps; the setup-screen scenarios under the real policy (first click, key press, decode still pending, Engage while decoding, decode failure); and a Federation player whose very FIRST interaction is pressing Engage (bridge running, setup sound correctly locked out). 0 JavaScript errors throughout.
**Harness lessons (so they are not repeated).** (1) The permissive autoplay flag hides autoplay bugs (above). (2) `evaluate()` grants user activation (above). (3) The game's tutorial coach card (`#tut-coach-body`) sits over the Commit button and swallows real mouse clicks in tests; trigger `document.getElementById('commit-btn').click()` or dismiss it. (4) When aligning a recording against a reference, search BOTH directions: the loader deliberately starts a few ms INTO the original (it skips the faint lead-in), and a one-directional search reported a nonsense correlation of 0.1 for audio that actually correlates 0.98. (5) A guessed hex offset is not a legal shot: use the game's own `getWeaponBlockReason()` to find one. (6) `AudioNode.frequency.value` read at `start()` time is the default (440), not the scheduled value: count oscillators, do not read frequencies. (7) Python `%` formatting breaks on text containing a percent sign (it did again): use placeholders.
**Not verified:** how the two sounds SOUND in play (I cannot listen: the levels `UI_SFX_GAIN` 0.40 / 0.55, and whether the load sound is too long when two tubes are armed in quick succession, since each arming click plays the full 1.1 s clip and they overlap); the AI's Federation torpedoes (e.g. a Klingon player against a Federation AI) use the synthesised sound by design; Firefox / Safari (only Chromium was run; Safari has the strictest autoplay rules and is the likeliest to behave differently); a real sound device.
**Open / for later:** torpedo (and other) sounds for the other factions; a visible "click for sound" hint; whether the enemy's torpedo launch should also get a recording; roadmap item C10. Keep `torpedo_load_fire_short.mp3` in the project folder: it is the source and is NOT embedded (the two MP3 clips in the game were made from the delivered WAVs: `ffmpeg -ar 44100 -ac 2 -b:a 128k -write_xing 0`).

### 0.136 — What changed in v2.71-S182 (AUDIO BUILD 4: the setup / start screen gets the stationary-ship loop)

**NOTE (§0.137): the first-gesture hook described below (`click` / `keydown` with `{once:true}`) was REPLACED in v2.72-S183 by a more robust unlock (earliest press/key/touch, retried until the context really runs, plus a probe at load). Everything else here stands.**

**User request (2026-11-01):** "I want this sound to replace the procedurally generated sounds at the very beginning of the game where the player is choosing ships, factions and settings. I may use it elsewhere too. But for now, just replace the 'start' of the game sound."
**Finding first: there was NOTHING to replace.** In v2.70-S181 the setup screen is silent. Verified on the real page with the audio start calls instrumented: no AudioContext exists until the first click, and after it no oscillator or buffer source starts, through all five faction buttons, the difficulty slider (1-5), the ship pickers, every checkbox, and the Ship Recognition Database button; `ambTab` stays null, 0 nodes; there is no `<audio>`, `<video>`, `new Audio` or `.play()` in the file, and every audio call site (`createOscillator`, `createBufferSource`, `snd(...)`) is inside gameplay code. So this build ADDS a start-screen sound (and said so to the user) rather than replacing one; if the user hears something there, ask what and when. Nothing else was removed: every procedural bed keeps working for the factions that use it.
**What was built.** `SETUP_AMB_*` constants and `snapExtremum`, `buildSetupLoop`, `prepSetupAmb`, `startSetupAmb`, `beginSetupAmb`, `stopSetupAmb`. The loop (the ping-pong from §0.135) plays on the setup screen at gain `SETUP_AMB_GAIN` = 0.15 (the loop is -11.6 dBFS RMS; measured output after the fade-in: RMS -28.0 dBFS, peak -18.6 dBFS; about the level of the engineering hum, which the user approved) with a 2.0 s fade-in. **Browsers refuse to play before a click or key press**, so it starts on the FIRST click or key press anywhere on the page (the existing first-gesture listeners now also call `startSetupAmb()`); until then the page is silent, which cannot be avoided. It is NOT in `ambNodes` (so tab switching never touches it). **Engage:** `launchGame()` calls `stopSetupAmb(1.0)` first (1.0 s fade, then stop) and sets a `locked` flag so it can never start again (New Mission reloads the page). The order matters: the Engage button's own handler runs BEFORE the document-level first-click listener, so if Engage is the very first click the lock must already be set or the setup sound would start just after Engage; tested (scenario S3). It stops for every faction on Engage, and the Federation bridge or the other factions' beds start as before. The decode happens when the audio engine is created (the loop is tiny); if the first click arrives while it decodes it starts by itself, once; if Engage arrives while it decodes it never starts; if decoding fails the screen stays silent exactly as before and the game is unaffected.
**The asset.** `SETUP_AMB_B64`: the loop's forward half plus `SETUP_AMB_PAD_S` = 0.05 s of REAL audio beyond each end, as an **8 kHz mono 16-bit PCM WAV, 22,530 bytes (30,040 base64 characters); the game grew by 35,076 bytes (now 12,295,793)**. Everything audible is below 1 kHz: the 48k->8k->48k round trip is 65 dB below the signal in 15-1000 Hz and every band level is identical to 0.1 dB. **PCM, not MP3, deliberately:** the ping-pong's turn-around points must land on waveform PEAKS, and an MP3's start padding (up to ~70 ms, decoder-dependent) would shift them off the peaks (the hum and the bridge tolerated such shifts because one is periodic and the other is crossfaded; this method cannot). `SETUP_AMB_HALF_S` = 62652/48000 s is the forward half. **Runtime:** the browser resamples the finite 8 kHz clip to the sound card's rate at decode time and damages its first and last samples (§0.135); the pads absorb that and the loop is cut from the clean interior. The two turn-around points are then SNAPPED to real peaks of the DECODED audio: within +-1 ms of the nominal position, the real peak (slope changes sign) with the least curvature (smallest sum of the three second-differences around the apex; ties go to the nearest). Because the snap works on the decoded audio, it is exact at any output rate. The cycle comes out at 2.6104-2.6105 s on every rate tested. **Rebuild recipe:** from the original `stationaryship1.mp3` (mono; 48 kHz): samples [a-2400, b+2400] with a = 8595 and b = 71247, times the gain `10^((-slope x (t - t_mid))/20)` with slope = +1.36 dB/s measured over [a, b] (the gain is held constant in the pads), then `scipy.signal.resample_poly(x, 1, 6, window=('kaiser', 9.0))` to 8 kHz, 16-bit WAV.
**The loop was re-cut (found by testing, before it shipped).** The first runtime test showed the wrap junction reading a +2.7 sigma high-frequency burst at EVERY sample rate: a value identical at every rate is a property of the chosen point, not of resampling. Investigation: the recording has a small natural HF event at that spot (offline, the chosen peak scored +3.7 sigma, its only neighbour +4.6), and a mirror doubles whatever is next to it. My §0.135 selection had scored smoothness, kink, sharpness and band levels but never HF content. **Fix:** add the HF-burst z (energy above 500 Hz in 2 ms windows around the junction, versus the same quantity over the loop) as a selection criterion and re-pick both points among the peaks with kink under 10 percent of a normal step and a flat apex. Trade-off table: HF z <= 1.0 leaves only a 2.1 s cycle; HF <= 1.5 / level <= 1.5 gives 2.11 s; **HF <= 2.0 / level <= 1.6 gives a = 0.1791 s, b = 1.4843 s, cycle 2.61 s (chosen)**; HF <= 2.0 / level <= 1.8 gives 2.69 s. Result at the junctions: wrap +1.4 to +1.5 sigma (was +2.7), turn +0.5 sigma (was +0.6), curvature at the 47th-82nd percentile (ordinary), step 0.00-0.05x a normal step, at 48000 / 44100 / 32000 / 96000 / 24000 Hz. I changed the points AND the snap rule (the first runtime snap took the smallest slope step, which can pick a sharper peak) in the same step, so I cannot say how much each contributed. The standalone `stationaryship_loop.wav` delivered with §0.135 had the same flaw and was rebuilt and re-delivered (cycle 125,304 samples = 2.6105 s).
**Verification (real Chromium 141, Playwright; ffmpeg/scipy offline).** (A) The shipped asset through the game's own loader, decoded and looped at 5 sound-card rates: junctions as above, no JS errors. (B) The real page: before any input AudioContext = none and nothing plays; the first click creates it, the loop starts (one looping source, gain 0.034 at 0.5 s, 0.15 at 2.7 s); switching factions, the slider and the other controls does not restart it (still ONE source); a KEY press as the first gesture starts it too; Engage as the very first click: it never starts; first click while the decode is slowed 1.5 s: starts by itself once; Engage while decoding: never starts; decode failure: silent, 0 errors, the game starts; Engage after it was playing: gain 0 within 0.4 s and the source stopped, and the Federation bridge starts. (C) The REAL OUTPUT recorded (11.6 s): level RMS -28.0 dBFS; buffer matched at NCC 1.0000, 1.000x level; 3 wraps and 3 turns after the fade-in, identical readings at each; the audio after a wrap and after a turn lines up with the buffer at lag 0 samples (NCC 1.00000). (D) Regression on this build: the other four factions' ambience on every tab is IDENTICAL to v2.70 (oscillator sets; the Damage Control formant oscillators are continuously modulated by design and are masked in the comparison); the Federation bridge edge cases (late decode, decode failure, double Engage), the hum seam test, the hum's tab logic and the console-chirp tests all pass unchanged; the long Federation bridge run (57 s, both loop wraps, tab switches, victory) matches the model BIT-FOR-BIT (max difference 0.00 over 43 s) when recorded with an audio-thread recorder.
**Harness lessons (so they are not repeated).** (1) **A `ScriptProcessor` recorder can DROP samples.** In one long run the output matched the model exactly (lag 0, residual -240 dB) until ~35 s, then sat at a constant lag of exactly 384 samples (3 x 128, the render quantum) with correlation still 1.00: the content was intact, the recorder had skipped data; the v2.70 run of the same test had been clean. Re-recorded with an **AudioWorklet** recorder it was bit-exact. On a `file://` page the worklet module must be loaded from a **`data:` URL** (a `blob:` URL fails with "Unable to load a worklet's module"). Use the worklet recorder for any long timing claim. (2) **I printed a hard-coded sentence, "the detector does flag a real click", that the control did not support** (a planted 6x-median step left the wrap reading unchanged). Measured properly: the HF-burst detector clearly flags a planted step of 25x the median step (-41 dBFS; z +4.2, +6.5 at 100x, +8.2 at 400x) and cannot see 6x (-53 dBFS, inside the sound's own HF texture); the real junction steps are 0.01x (wrap) and 0.02x (turn) of the median step, about -109 dBFS, hundreds of times below the smallest click it can see. Never hard-code a conclusion into a test's output. (3) `Math.max(...bigArray)` overflows the stack on ~100k elements; use a loop. (4) Two `.sc-launch` buttons exist; select Engage by `button[onclick="launchGame()"]`. (5) Python `%` formatting breaks on text that contains a literal percent sign; use placeholders.
**Not verified:** how it SOUNDS (I cannot listen: the level, whether a 2.6 s cycle shows as faint breathing in a long listen, and that the rumble suits a start screen are taste calls; note it is almost entirely below 300 Hz, which small laptop speakers barely reproduce, so on those it may be quiet or inaudible: `SETUP_AMB_GAIN` is one constant); Firefox / Safari (only Chromium was run; Safari's autoplay rules are the likeliest difference); a real sound device.
**Open / for later:** the user "may use it elsewhere too" (candidates: a stationary / holding ship in battle; the Recognition Database; the end-of-battle screens); the sound is the same for every faction on the setup screen; roadmap item C10. Keep `stationaryship1.mp3` in the project folder: it is the source and is NOT embedded.

### 0.135 — Analysis only (no game change): stationaryship1.mp3 turned into a seamless loop

**CORRECTED in §0.136 (same day, found by testing before wiring it in): the loop points recorded below (a = sample 6291) put a natural high-frequency event of the recording right at the wrap junction (+3.7 sigma; my selection had not looked at high-frequency content). The loop was re-cut: a = sample 8595 (0.1791 s), b = sample 71247 (1.4843 s), forward half 62,653 samples (1.3053 s), full cycle 125,304 samples = 2.6105 s (the numbers below say 2.7065 s). The delivered `stationaryship_loop.wav`, the x4 preview and the picture were rebuilt. The method, the findings about the sound, and the browser/padding result below are unchanged.**

**User request (2026-11-01):** "analyse this sound. Can you cycle it so there are no seams and it just plays continuously with the same sound?" (`stationaryship1.mp3`). The user did not say where it plays; the name suggests a stationary-ship sound. **Nothing was changed in the game (still v2.70-S181); the loop exists as files only.** Ask where it should play before wiring it in.
**The file (measured).** 1.944 s, 77,793 bytes, 320 kbps, 48 kHz, stereo but the two channels are IDENTICAL (dual mono); peak 0.901 (-0.9 dBFS), RMS -11.6 dBFS; 99.6% of the energy below 300 Hz (52% at 20-60 Hz); spectral flatness 0.22; strongest lines near 23, 44, 69, 97, 144 Hz. **Why a plain repeat seams:** the first ~20 ms is digital silence (-91 dBFS) and the last ~10 ms is a hard cut to digital silence, so every repeat has a ~30-40 ms drop-out (measured as a -3.5 sigma to -4.2 sigma level dip in every band at the seam). The clean steady region is 0.04-1.93 s. **Character:** the "lines" are NOT steady tones: the 23 Hz line's instantaneous frequency wanders 20.7-28.9 Hz and its level swings ~9 dB, the others likewise; it is a narrow-band random rumble (resonant noise) with beating. Consequently no splice matches well: the best crossfade splice correlates only 0.33-0.53 (the bridge recording scored 0.96; random splices on this material ~0.0 +- 0.1), so a crossfade loop blends mismatched phases (level wobble or cancellation of the low band) and is the wrong tool.
**Method: ping-pong loop** (forward, then backward, then forward...), mirrored about waveform PEAKS so the junctions are smooth (a mirror about a point where the slope is ~0 is continuous in value, slope and curvature). It is legitimate here because the sound is time-reversible: envelope-derivative skewness -0.08 (a decaying-burst control: +0.57), waveform time-reversal statistics ~0 (+-0.015 at short lags; control up to 3.8), and the level statistics are identical forwards and backwards. **Point selection (the part that took iterations):** (1) a first pick by waveform smoothness alone left the 18-48 Hz band 2 sigma low at the mirror points (they sat in natural low-band troughs); (2) a mirror junction DOUBLES the audio next to it, so the quantity that matters is the level of the ~50-100 ms either side of the junction in every band (18-48, 48-120, 120-320 Hz, broadband); points were scored on that, plus peak sharpness (curvature and jerk percentile) and kink (slope step at the mirror, <= 10% of a typical sample step); (3) the longest cycle (b = 1.80 s) left a +2.6 sigma broadband bump at the turn, and no candidate past ~1.5 s was clean (>= 1.63 sigma), so the cycle is the longest one that stays within ~1.7 sigma. **Final: a = sample 6291 (0.1311 s), b = sample 71247 (1.4843 s) at 48 kHz; forward half 64,957 samples (1.3533 s); full cycle 129,912 samples = 2.7065 s** (the original file is 1.944 s). Kinks 0.000 and 0.000 of a typical sample step. A slow level trend in this region (+0.87 dB/s; its standard error is ~0.5 dB/s, so it is borderline-real) was flattened symmetrically (+0.59 dB at the start, -0.59 dB at the end) so the average level and the peak stay put (peak 0.783 = -2.1 dBFS, RMS -11.6 dBFS, same as the original). **Honest note:** the junction points were OPTIMISED against the level-profile estimator, so that number is by design; the corroborating numbers are the curvature/jerk percentiles and the real-browser playback test below.
**Result (measured on the built loop, 5 repeats).** Seam step at the 0th-1st percentile of ordinary steps (a flat peak, natural), curvature 61st / 14th and jerk 59th / 21st percentile at the wrap / turn junctions (50 = ordinary); level at the junctions within -1.7..+1.2 sigma in every band and -1.1..+0.9 broadband (the file as delivered: -3.5..-4.2 sigma). Slow level movement (300 ms-smoothed) std 0.38 dB / peak-to-peak 2.2 dB, versus 0.64 / 2.6 for the original's clean region and 0.90 / 4.0 for the file looped as delivered, so looping adds no pulsing. (An earlier "modulation line" check was FLAWED, since any periodic signal shows strong lines at its repeat rate, and was discarded.)
**A browser finding that matters for wiring it in.** In real Chromium 141, decoding the 48 kHz WAV on a 44.1 / 32 / 96 kHz context and looping it ticks: the decoder resamples the FINITE buffer and its edge handling damages the first and last samples (wrap step 2.5x at 44.1 kHz and 12.3x at 96 kHz, curvature and jerk at the 100th percentile). At 48 kHz (no resampling) it is perfect. Mirroring the half-loop in code after decoding does NOT escape this (it inherits the damaged edges). **The fix, verified at 48000 / 44100 / 32000 / 96000 / 24000 Hz:** ship the loop with 50 ms (2400 samples at 48 kHz) of REAL audio beyond each end (the padded clip is original samples [a-2400, b+2400], 69,757 samples, with the same gain flattening applied and held constant in the pads), decode it, cut the loop from the INTERIOR of the decode (`a_idx = round(2400 x rate / 48000)`, `n = round((n48 - 1) x rate / 48000) + 1`), mirror in code (`half` then `half` reversed without its two end samples; the buffer is `2n - 2` samples), and loop that. Measured: step 0.0x everywhere, curvature 54th-68th percentile at the wrap and 17th-36th at the turn, jerk 17th-97th (the 97th is a 96 kHz turn, sub-LSB). The loop length rounds by up to a third of a sample at 44.1 kHz (and is exact at the other rates), which is inaudible at a flat peak. This is the same idea as the engineering hum's "cut from the interior" and means MP3 padding would not matter either: the padded clip as a mono 16 kHz 48 kbps MP3 is 9,333 bytes (about 12 KB in the HTML; measured, not built).
**Deliverables (in the outputs folder):** `stationaryship_loop.wav` (mono 48 kHz 16-bit, one 2.7065 s cycle, 129,912 samples: loops seamlessly in any player that loops sample-accurately at 48 kHz); `stationaryship_loop_preview_x4.wav` (4 cycles, 10.8 s, to audition the joins); `stationaryship_loop_before_after.png` (level and 0-320 Hz spectrogram of the file looped as delivered versus the new loop). **Recipe to rebuild:** the original `stationaryship1.mp3` (keep it in the project folder) -> mono (channels identical) -> take samples a..b at 48 kHz -> apply the symmetric gain `-0.87 dB/s x (t - t_mid)` -> palindrome `[s_a .. s_b, s_(b-1) .. s_(a+1)]`.
**Not verified:** how it SOUNDS (I cannot listen: the time-reversibility is measured, not heard, and whether a 2.7 s cycle shows as a faint periodic "breathing" in a long listen is a taste call; the loop can be re-cut with a shorter or longer cycle at the cost of junction quality, see the trade-off above); in Firefox / Safari (only Chromium was run); not played through the game at all.
**Open:** where it plays (a stationary / not-moving ship? which tab or phase? which factions?) and how loud (peak -2.1 dBFS, RMS -11.6 dBFS is LOUD; the game would set a gain constant, as for the other beds).

### 0.134 — What changed in v2.70-S181 (AUDIO BUILD 3: Federation bridge ambience with a one-time start-up)

**User request (2026-11-01):** the user supplied `tos_bridge_1_activate.mp3` and asked: (1) when the player is Federation and has made the pre-game selections, play it as **Engage** is pressed, and stop playing the procedurally generated "bridge sound"; (2) keep playing it when the player moves to Power Allocation; (3) Damage Control now has its own sound, which replaces the bridge sound there, and the bridge sound resumes when the player leaves it; (4) the first two or three seconds are a start-up sound, to be played only once at the beginning of the session when Engage is selected; (5) every other faction stays as designed.
**Interpretations (stated to the user; check them).** *Engage* = the setup screen's Engage button, which calls `launchGame()`; the sound starts on its first lines, before terrain generation and the sprite preload, and only for `playerFaction==='fed'` (Gorn and Orion keep the old bed: they are "other factions"). *Once at the beginning of the session* = once per Engage, i.e. once per battle (New Mission reloads the page, so a new battle plays it again); tab switches and resumes never replay it. If the user meant once per page load, say so. *The procedurally generated bridge sound* = `startTacAmbFed()` (42/84/126 Hz hum + the sensor-sweep ping) and, for Federation, the power-allocation pad `startPwrAmb()`; both are skipped for Federation and both are KEPT in the code (Gorn/Orion still use `startTacAmbFed`, everyone else keeps `startPwrAmb`, and Federation falls back to them if the recording cannot be decoded). **Only three tabs exist** (Tactical, Power Allocation, Damage Control; the "log tab — silence" comment inside `setAmbTab` is stale): the bridge plays on Tactical and Power, fades out over 0.7 s on Damage Control (whose hum, built in v2.68, fades in as before) and fades back in over 1.5 s when the player leaves it. The game's separate power-level hum (`initHum`, a 48 Hz drone scaled to the allocation) and the console chirps (§0.133) are unchanged.
**The file (measured, not assumed).** 4:17, 8.2 MB, 256 kbps stereo, 48 kHz; peak 0.349; 0.8 s of silence, then the start-up; a 15 s fade-out at the end. The start-up is a swell in the 300-700 Hz band (+20 dB above the bed at 1-2 s, +11 dB until 5 s) plus low energy at 80-300 Hz; every band is within +-2 dB of the long-term bed by **7 s**, so that is the earliest the repeating part can start. The bed (300 Hz-3 kHz; lines near 170, 227, 813-971 and 2633 Hz; wide stereo, L/R correlation -0.12) carries an irregular pulse: the loudness envelope has an autocorrelation peak at 4.3 s (0.41), and 4-6 s chunks match elsewhere only partly (0.75-0.87) at spacings of 4.2-4.7 s. **Unlike the engineering hum it is NOT a copied loop** (no exact repeat above 0.97 anywhere), so it cannot be reduced to one tiny period: a real loop has to be chosen and joined.
**Loop choice.** Splice search (stereo, 8 kHz decimated, then refined at 48 kHz): for loop start LS in 8-12 s and loop end LE giving a 14-40 s loop, maximise the normalised correlation between the 1.0 s BEFORE LE and the 1.0 s BEFORE LS (random splices score 0.00 +- 0.11; the best score 0.93-0.97 depending on length). Chosen: **LS = 9.45 s, LE = 31.5393 s of the original (a 22.09 s loop, about five pulses), match 0.965** (min of L/R; 0.927 before the full-rate refinement). Longer loops score slightly higher and cost more bytes; 22 s was the knee. To re-cut, re-run that search on the original file.
**What was built.** (1) `FED_BR_B64`: a 31.1 s clip (original 0.737-31.839 s, so the 0.8 s of silence is trimmed to 40 ms and playback starts at once; 0.3 s of margin after LE) as a **16 kHz stereo 48 kbps MP3, 187,101 bytes (183 KB; 249,468 base64 characters)**; the game grew by 254,981 bytes (now 12,260,717). In clip time the loop is `FED_BR_LS` = 8.713 s to `FED_BR_LE` = 30.802 s. (2) `buildFedBridge(ac, decodedBuffer)` (pure, in place): crossfades the last `FED_BR_XF` = 1.0 s of the loop LINEARLY into the 1.0 s that precede the loop start (linear, not equal-power: the two sides are 0.94-0.96 correlated, and an equal-power law would bump the level about +3 dB), so the loop's last sample is followed by the natural continuation (the loop head); it returns the loop points in seconds at the context's rate. The first pass through the loop region is untouched original audio, so the start-up flows into the bed with no join at all. (3) `prepFedBridge()` decodes once (when the audio engine is created and the player is Federation, and when Federation is chosen); (4) `startFedBridge()` / `beginFedBridge()` play ONE looping `AudioBufferSource` (`loopStart`/`loopEnd` set; started at offset 0, so the start-up is simply the first pass) through its own gain (0.05 s fade-in); it is NOT in `ambNodes`, so `setAmbTab`'s fade-everything step never touches it; (5) `fedBridgeFollowTab(tab)` fades its gain to 0 on `dmg` and back to `FED_BRIDGE_GAIN` elsewhere WITHOUT restarting the source (it keeps its place in the loop while muted, which is why the start-up can never replay); (6) `stopFedBridge(fade)`: called at Engage (defensively, so there are never two) and from `checkVictory()` (the only place a battle ends; 1.5 s fade); (7) `setAmbTab`: `fedBr.wanted` makes Federation skip the procedural tactical and power beds; if decoding fails, `wanted` is cleared and `setAmbTab` is re-run so the old bed starts (a Federation player is never left in silence). **Level:** `FED_BRIDGE_GAIN` = 2.0 (the file's bed is -36.1 dBFS RMS, the start-up -33.7 with a -9.1 dBFS peak; x2 gives bed ~-30, start-up peak ~-3 dBFS, no clipping; for reference the approved hum is -28.3 and the old Federation bed was about -26). One constant.
**Delay-agnostic by construction.** An MP3 decoder may or may not trim its start padding (ffmpeg and Chromium, for a file written without a gapless header, leave 1105 samples at 16 kHz = 69 ms). The loop window and the blend are both measured from the decoded buffer's own samples, so a padding shift moves them together and the geometry stays valid, provided the window stays inside the steady bed (margins: loop start is 2.4 s after the bed settles). Cost: up to ~0.11 s of lead-in before the start-up is heard.
**Encoding choice (measured).** 16 kHz stereo, 48 kbps: third-octave tonal balance within 0.8 dB mean of the original (only the 6.3 kHz band, at -102 dBFS and 40 dB below everything else, deviates, by 9 dB, which is inaudible); 10 ms envelope correlation 0.996-0.998 in the 300-700 / 700-1500 / 1500-3000 Hz bands (the pulses are not smeared); L/R correlation -0.090 vs -0.092. 64 kbps would add 62 KB for 0.4 dB. Waveform SNR is only 15-16 dB (noise-like material is expensive for a perceptual coder), so a plain "log-spectral distance" looked alarming (~20 dB) but was dominated by empty high-frequency bins; tonal balance and envelope are the meaningful measures here.
**Verification (real Chromium 141 via Playwright; ffmpeg/scipy offline).** (A) Shipped asset decoded at 48000/44100/16000/96000/32000 Hz: loop indices and lengths correct (22.089 s everywhere); wrap jump = 0.07x the largest ordinary step nearby on every rate and channel (the unblended control ranged 0.03x-0.59x, i.e. up to 4.7x the mean step, depending on rate and channel); loudness through the blend identical to the raw tail (-49..-32 dB 50 ms RMS); spectral continuity of the blended 1.0 s within 0.8 dB of the raw audio across 160-2500 Hz (max 2.6 dB at 3-4 kHz where the bed is ~16-20 dB down); stereo image unchanged (L/R -0.091 vs -0.097). (B) The real game through the real Engage button, recording the actual output for 57 s (two loop wraps): the bridge starts on Engage with ZERO procedural oscillators on Tactical and on Power; Damage Control: bridge gain 0, the hum and its reactive layers running (8 nodes), same source object; back on Tactical: gain 2.0, SAME source object, still ONE bridge start for the whole session; after victory the source is stopped (fade). **Measured from the recorded output**, projecting it on the looped buffer in 0.5 s windows: gain 2.00 through the start-up and the bed, ~0 within 0.7 s of entering Damage Control, 2.00 again within 1.5 s of leaving; normalised correlation 1.00 in every window including the windows spanning both wraps (30.8 s and 52.9 s); after each wrap the audio lines up with the loop head at lag 0 samples (NCC 1.00000), and before each wrap with the loop tail including the blend at lag 0; the seam step sits at the 56th percentile of ordinary steps within +-0.25 s (50 = typical) and the seam curvature at the 35th; planted clicks at the same spots (3x and 6x the median step) read the 98th and 100th percentile on curvature, so the detector would have caught a tick. (C) Faction diff against the previous build (v2.69) on every tab (Tactical, Power, Damage Control, Tactical again), Klingon / Romulan / Gorn / Orion: **identical oscillator sets** (the only reading that varied was the Damage Control formant oscillators, which are continuously modulated by design; masked in the comparison), no bridge started, 0 JS errors. (D) Edge paths: Engage before the decode finishes (decoder slowed 2 s): no bridge at 1.5 s and no procedural bed leaking in meanwhile, the bridge starts by itself exactly once when decoded; decode failure: Federation falls back to the old 42/84/126 Hz bed on Tactical and the pad on Power; Engage twice without a reload: the first bridge is faded out and replaced, never two. (E) Regression on this build: the hum seam test, the hum's tab logic and the console-chirp tests all pass unchanged.
**Harness notes (so they are not repeated).** There are TWO `.sc-launch` buttons (Engage is the second; the first opens the Ship Recognition Database): select Engage by `button[onclick="launchGame()"]`. The recorder is a ScriptProcessor tapped on every connection to the destination; analysis needs the game's low-frequency power hum filtered out (300 Hz high-pass) or the matches look worse than they are.
**Not verified:** how it SOUNDS (I cannot listen: the level, the start-up-to-bed hand-off as a listener hears it, and whether a 22 s loop is long enough that its repetition goes unnoticed are all taste calls; the splice is chosen so the join is smooth, not so the repetition is inaudible); Firefox / Safari (`loopStart`/`loopEnd` and `decodeAudioData` are standard, but only Chromium was run) and a real sound device; the startup latency (the recorder buffers 93 ms).
**Still open / for later (audio):** the other factions' own bridge recordings and start-ups (`FED_BR_*` and `fedBr` are Federation-named but the pattern generalises); a 'once per page load' reading of the start-up if the user prefers it; keep `tos_bridge_1_activate.mp3` in the project folder (it is the source and is NOT embedded); roadmap item C10.

### 0.133 — What changed in v2.69-S180 (AUDIO BUILD 2: Federation console chirps on commit and on Proceed to Combat)

**User request (2026-11-01):** after approving the hum ("sounds solid. good job"), the user uploaded `tos_keypress1.mp3` and `tos_keypress8.mp3` and wrote: "I'm adding two sounds for the federation side for whenever the player has assigned the power allocation as well as the finalizing button has been clicked." The message did not say which file goes with which event.
**Interpretation (stated to the user; check it if it was wrong).** The power flow has two buttons: **Commit Power Allocation** (`commitPwr`, locks the allocation) and **Proceed to Combat** (`proceedFromPower`, the finalizing button; the third button, Revise, unlocks it). "Assigned the power allocation" = the commit being accepted; "the finalizing button" = Proceed. Mapping: **keypress1 (6 notes, 0.38 s) = commit; keypress8 (11 notes, 0.49 s) = proceed** — upload order matches event order, and the longer run suits the more conclusive action. To swap them, swap the two values in `FACTION_SFX` (no file work). Revise is silent (not requested). The AI plays no sound.
**The source files (measured).** keypress1: 0.408 s, stereo with identical channels, 48 kHz, 320 kbps MP3, 6 note bursts, 23 ms of leading silence; keypress8: 0.485 s, mono, 44.1 kHz, 11 note bursts, starts at 0 ms and was cut off mid-decay (last sample 0.009, which would click). Both are normalised hot (peak -2.9 dBFS), 91-92% of their energy between 500 Hz and 2 kHz (centroids 1484 and 941 Hz), nothing above 6 kHz.
**What was built.** (1) `FACTION_SFX = {fed:{commit:'fed_commit',proceed:'fed_proceed'}}`: a per-faction table, so another faction's sounds slot in later by adding an entry (Klingon, Romulan, Gorn and Orion have none, so they stay silent). (2) `UI_SFX_B64` (two embedded clips), `UI_SFX_GAIN` (`fed_commit` 0.30, `fed_proceed` 0.365: level-matched by RMS, both -24.3 dBFS RMS, peaks about -13.5 and -11.6 dBFS) and `prepUiSfx()` (decodes both once, from the same `getAC()` hook as the hum). (3) `playUiSfx(key)` plays a one-shot `AudioBufferSource` through a gain; if the clip is not decoded yet it skips the sound (and starts the decode) rather than playing it late. (4) `playFactionSfx('commit'|'proceed')` looks up `GS.player.faction` (codes: fed, kli, rom, gor, ori; a strict `fed` test, NOT the default-to-Federation test the ambience uses, so Gorn and Orion do not get Federation chirps). (5) Hooks: the last line of `commitPwr()`'s success path (so an over-budget commit, which returns early, is silent), and the first line of `proceedFromPower()` after its guard.
