Those two functions are only called by their buttons.
**Format choice: PCM WAV, not MP3.** These are one-shots tied to a click, and MP3 encoder padding adds a browser-dependent 25-35 ms before the sound starts (the hum did not have this problem because it is a loop sliced from the middle). Each clip was made mono (keypress1's channels were identical, max difference 0), trimmed to 3 ms before the first note (keypress1; keypress8 already starts at 0) and 20 ms after the last, resampled to 22.05 kHz, given a 1.5 ms fade-in and a 15 ms fade-out (zero first and last sample, so no click), and stored as 16-bit WAV: 16,714 + 21,422 = 38,136 bytes, 51 KB as base64. The game file grew by 53 KB (12,005,736 bytes). Keep the two original MP3s in the project folder: they are the sources, not embedded.
**Verification (real Chromium 141 via Playwright, driving the real buttons).** Federation: commit starts exactly one one-shot (the 6-note clip, 16,670 samples at the 44.1 kHz context); Revise starts none; an over-budget commit starts none and leaves the allocation uncommitted; committing again starts the commit clip again; Proceed starts the 11-note clip (21,378 samples) and the game moves to the Tactical Advantage phase; zero JavaScript errors. Klingon, Romulan, Gorn and Orion (chosen through the real `chooseFaction`): commit and proceed work and start NO sounds. The not-yet-decoded path (buffers wiped before a commit): no error, the sound is skipped, the decode restarts. The ACTUAL OUTPUT STREAM was recorded off the audio graph and matched against the decoded clips: the commit clip appears twice and the proceed clip once, at normalised correlations of 0.994, 0.987 and 0.970 and exactly 1.00x the intended level (matching needed a 300 Hz high-pass, because the game's low-frequency beds sit underneath; an unfiltered first attempt found only 1 of 3 and was a measuring artifact, not a game fault). The v2.68 hum tests were re-run on this build (tab switching, one hum node, bit-exact loop lengths at five sample rates): unchanged.
**Not verified:** how the chirps SOUND, whether the mapping (keypress1 = commit, keypress8 = proceed) and the levels are what the user wants (I cannot listen), real-device latency (the recorder's own 93 ms buffer hides it; the WAV format removes the known source of lag), Firefox / Safari / a real sound card.
**Still open / for later (audio):** Klingon, Romulan, Gorn and Orion equivalents (the table is ready, the files are not); sounds for Revise and for the AI's power commit if wanted; the two original MP3s should be kept in the project; levels are two constants (`UI_SFX_GAIN`). Roadmap item C10 holds the list.

### 0.132 — What changed in v2.68-S179 (FIRST AUDIO BUILD: the Damage Control tab gets a looping engineering hum)

**User request (2026-11-01):** the user supplied `tng_engineering_hum.mp3` (3:02, 256 kbps stereo, 5.8 MB) as the replacement ambience for the Damage Control tab "for all factions", observed that it was "3 or so minutes of the exact same audio", and asked for an analysis before any change. After the analysis: *"I don't want a faint tick. I want it seamless"*, and approved the plan "short MP3 snippet at 22.05 kHz stereo, 64 kbps, 2-3 loop-lengths long; at startup the game decodes it and cuts out exactly one seamless period".
**Analysis (all measured on the real file, not assumed):** the 3:02 file is ONE 2.30417-second loop (110,600.27 samples at 48 kHz, fitted to 0.009 samples over 72 repeats) repeated 79 times; subtracting repeats from each other leaves only MP3 coding noise (~40 dB down) at every repeat tested (1, 2, 10, 30, 50, 70). Unique audio = 1.3% of the file. Loudness drift over the whole file is +-0.5 dB, the spectral centroid is 113 Hz +-5. Almost all energy is below 500 Hz (peaks near 49, 57, 64, 72, 79 Hz, then 100-200 Hz); above 2 kHz is codec noise. The stereo is wide and decorrelated (L/R correlation ~0.13, R lags L by ~171 ms) and the build keeps it stereo. The "breathing" the user may notice is a bump in the loop recurring every 2.3 s; a longer file cannot fix that, only changing the sound can (open item below).
**What was built.** (1) `DMG_HUM_B64`: ~3 loop-lengths (6.9 s) of the hum as a 24 kHz stereo 64 kbps MP3, 55,725 bytes (74 KB as base64); the game file grew by 77 KB (the original file would have added ~7.6 MB). (2) `buildDmgHumLoop(ac, decodedBuffer)` (pure) cuts ONE period out of the decoded clip: window = one period + `DMG_HUM_XFADE` (0.05 s), starting one period in (so MP3 encoder padding, trimmed or not, never matters), and linearly crossfades the overlap into the head. The last sample of the loop is therefore followed by the very next sample of the original decoded stream, so the wrap point is an ordinary sample step no matter what the codec noise does. (3) `prepDmgHum()` decodes once, when the audio engine is created (`getAC()` schedules it); (4) `startDmgHum()` plays it as a looping `AudioBufferSource` through a gain that fades in over 1.5 s, registered in `ambNodes` as `{src, gain, hum:true}`, so the existing `stopAllAmb()` fades and stops it on every tab change with no new plumbing; a `hum` flag prevents double-starts; if the tab is opened before the decode has finished, the decode callback starts the hum. (5) `startDmgAmb()` calls `startDmgHum()` first and keeps ALL the existing reactive layers on top (structural groan, crew-chatter formants, electrical buzz, red-alert klaxon). Same hum for every faction (the Damage Control tab has one code path). Level: `DMG_HUM_GAIN` = 1.0 (the loop master is about -28 dBFS RMS; the old Tactical Fed bed is roughly -26); change that one constant to re-balance. If decoding fails, nothing throws and the procedural layers still run.
**Two deviations from the approved plan, both forced by measurement.** (a) The file is 24 kHz, not 22.05 kHz, and the loop is exactly **691/300 s** (2.30333 s, -0.63 cent in pitch, far below hearing) instead of 2.30417 s: 691/300 s is a WHOLE number of samples at 24k / 44.1k / 48k / 96k, so the cut is exact whatever rate the sound card runs at (browsers resample decoded MP3 to the output rate; at 22.05 kHz the length is 50,788.5 samples, i.e. not whole). Only rates like 32 kHz or 16 kHz give a fractional length, and the crossfade absorbs that. (b) The crossfade was ADDED after the first test showed a plain cut would tick on some devices: MP3 coding noise is not periodic, so a plain cut left a wrap step of up to 143% of the loop's largest ordinary step depending on offset and rate (0% to 143% across 5 rates and 4 offsets). Bitrate does not fix that and does not help quality either: SNR plateaus at ~26 dB from 96k to 128k (normal for a perceptual coder), and 64k gives 22-24 dB with the stereo image intact (L/R correlation -0.023 vs -0.023 in the master).
**Master recipe (offline, to rebuild or re-tune).** Decode the original to 48 kHz stereo; fit the period by sub-sample cross-correlation across repeats (110,600.272 samples); low-pass at 9 kHz; cubic-spline each of the 76 clean repeats onto an exact grid of 55,280 samples (24 kHz x 691/300 s) and AVERAGE them (coherent averaging of 76 repeats removes the original's codec noise: single repeat vs average = 44.7 dB); tile the averaged period 3x; encode with libmp3lame `-b:a 64k -ar 24000 -ac 2 -write_xing 0`; base64 it into `DMG_HUM_B64`. Keep the original `tng_engineering_hum.mp3` in the project folder (it is the source; it is NOT embedded in the game).
**Verification (real Chromium 141 via Playwright, plus ffmpeg/scipy offline).** (A) The shipped function and the shipped embedded MP3, decoded by the browser at 48000 / 44100 / 24000 / 96000 / 32000 Hz: loop length equals `round(rate x 691/300)` every time (110,560 / 101,577 / 55,280 / 221,120 / 73,707); the crossfaded wrap step is 13.5-18.6% of the loop's largest ordinary step on every rate (both channels), wrap curvature 0.6-15.7% of the largest ordinary curvature. (B) The real game, a real battle (`launchGame()`), real tab switches with `sw()`: tactical tab = 0 hum nodes; Damage Control = exactly 1, looping, buffer length 101,577 (= expected at the 44.1 kHz context), gain 1.0, AudioContext running; leaving the tab = 0; re-entering = 1; three rapid in/out toggles = still exactly 1; Power tab = 0; hull at 30% = groan 0.027 and chatter 0.017 still reacting; zero JavaScript errors. The ACTUAL OUTPUT STREAM was recorded off the audio graph (a ScriptProcessor tapped on every connection to the destination, 9.75 s): the output repeats bit-for-bit every loop; the three seams were located by matching the recorded stream to the loop buffer; seam step = 0.30x and seam curvature = 0.12x of the largest value in the 200 samples either side (i.e. smaller than the waveform's own movement), identical at all three seams; control clicks planted at the same seams at 0.5x / 1x / 2x the loop's largest step read 3.76x / 7.48x / 14.9x on curvature, so the detector would have caught a tick. (C) Edge paths: tab opened while the decode was artificially delayed 1.2 s = no hum at 1 s, hum starts by itself when the decode ends, groan layer present throughout; simulated decode failure = no error, no hum, groan layer still created.
**Not verified:** how it SOUNDS to the user's ears (I cannot listen; every claim above is measured, none is auditory), whether `DMG_HUM_GAIN` = 1.0 is the right level against the other beds, and Firefox / Safari / a real sound device (only headless Chromium 141 with its null sink was available; the code uses only the long-standing callback form of `decodeAudioData`, `createBuffer`, `getChannelData`, and looping `AudioBufferSource`, which all three engines support).
**Still open / for later (audio):** the 2.3 s "breathing" is the loop itself; if it bothers the user, options are a very slow filter or playback-rate wobble in code (no file cost) or a different source sound. The Power Allocation and Tactical-map ambiences are still the old procedural oscillators (Tactical has per-faction beds and the sensor pings); candidates for the same treatment: roadmap item C10. Per-faction variants of the hum (pitch or filter in code, no extra file weight) were offered and not requested. If the game is ever distributed publicly, the clip should be checked for rights (it sounds like show audio); fine for a personal fan build.

### 0.131 — Analysis only (no change): combat log, USS Federation (Federation I Mk I) vs IKS Devisor (D-7 M (IX)), exported 2026-11-01

**User report:** "just fought as a federation dreadnought against a klingon. this seemed too early. here's the combat log" (read as: the fight ended too early; later confirmed the user only wanted to be sure there was no bug that made it an easy win; the user accepted the analysis and declined an engine-level Monte Carlo).
**Result:** NO BUG FOUND. The Federation I won in two turns because one volley was lucky. Log facts: turn 1 the D-7 AI (Captain) hit the Fwd shield (6 points absorbed) and took the Federation superstructure 50 -> 43; turn 2 phase 3 the Federation I fired six weapons at range 5 into the D-7's F-Stbd face (a 5-point shield: absorbed 2 + 2 + 1), then two FAC-3 torpedoes (12 each) both hit and BOTH penetrating hits rolled superstructure (location rolls 9 and 8): 11 + 12 = 23 against the D-7's 20 boxes. Initiative order, shield absorption sums and hull totals all check out.
**Data (registry, read live):** Federation1_MkI = superstructure 50, power 45, move ratio 5, shield ratio 0.5, max 6 per face; weapons 6x FL-6 (3, chart H, range 10; arcs fwd / port / stbd), 4x FL-3 (2, chart G, range 10), 2x FAC-3 torpedoes (fixed 12, arm cost 4, range 10). D7_M = superstructure 20, power 44, move ratio 3, shield ratio 0.5, max 12 per face; 3x KD-8 beams (7, chart U, RANGE 20), 2x KP-3 (fixed 15, chart R, range 16). **The debrief's "on paper the enemy was the stronger ship (2.0 : 1)" is correct and comes from FASA data** (SHIP_CE: Federation1_MkI D 104.5, WDF 18 -> CE 1,881; D7_M D 87.6, WDF 42.2 -> CE 3,697; ratio 1.97), because the Federation I's guns are weak apart from the two torpedoes.
**Probability (a simplified simulation, NOT the engine's dice code):** hit-location table observed in the logs: 1 shield generator, 2 beam, 3 missile, 4-6 engine, 7-9 superstructure, 10 sensors. A one-volley kill from full hull with this weapon set against a 5-point face = 2.1%; mean superstructure damage per volley 3.7; median 6 volleys to strip 20 boxes; killed within 2 volleys about 10%. So the result was a roughly 2% lucky volley, consistent with the debrief's "you beat the odds".
**Observation (a tuning idea, not a bug; logged under wishlist A14):** the D-7's beams reach 20 hexes but the Federation I's weapons reach 10, and the AI still closed to 9, 8, then 5 hexes. The Captain tier is designed to hunt blind quarters, not to kite.
**Not done:** no engine-level fairness / duration test (offered, declined); nothing changed in the game.

### 0.129 — Ship art atlas for the RPG project (no game change)

**User request (2026-10-27):** "Generate a file useable by the FASA RPG that I'm working on in another chat/thread that contains all the ship art that is usable from the tactical command game ... a single file ... as concise as possible given there's limited resources for projects."
**What was built:** `TC_ShipArt_Atlas.png` — ONE lossless RGBA PNG (2640 x 5214, **6.77 MB**) holding **92 distinct images = all 96 ship images in the game** (47 map sprites, 40 front-view portraits, 9 damage-control arts; the K-22 / D-32 / L-42 Bird of Prey trio shares identical damage-control and front-view art, so 4 duplicates are stored once and listed as `also`). Included on purpose: the 4 fixed stations (Alamo, R-1, X-3 Aviary, Z-4 Deathgame) and the 2 unused sprites (`D7Precursor`, `Federation2Precursor`, flagged UNUSED). Not included: the 4 celestial images (not ships) and the procedural (code-drawn) hull art. Why an image and not base64 text: a project reads an image file cheaply, while ~7 MB of base64 text would be enormous to store and index (this is my understanding of how project capacity works, not something I measured).
**The index travels with the file, three ways:** (1) PNG iTXt chunk `manifest` (JSON, 14.7 KB; read with `Image.open(p).info['manifest']`), (2) the same JSON zlib-packed into a pixel strip in the LAST 4 ROWS (header `STATLAS1` + 4-byte length; survives anything that strips metadata but keeps pixels), (3) each tile's key printed on a label band under it. Per tile: id (`map:`/`front:`/`dmg:` + key), rect `[x,y,w,h]`, faction code, the ships that use it (name, class, registry), `also` aliases, `text_on_hull` where lettering is baked into the art (as read by eye, §0.127: e.g. Remora NCC-3183, Chandley NCC-2301, Excelsior damage art "U.S.S. ORACLE NCC-2012"), `note` (K-22 map sprite is soft/blurry). Conventions: map and damage-control art are bow UP; front views are bow-on; the 256/512 px map canvases keep the art centred so relative scale is preserved.
**Verified (real file, not assumed):** every one of the 92 tiles is PIXEL-IDENTICAL to its original image extracted from the game; all 96 originals are covered by a tile or an alias; no overlaps; all rects inside the canvas and clear of the data strip; transparency preserved; after re-saving WITHOUT text chunks the pixel strip decodes to the identical manifest; the decoding instruction embedded in the file's `read` chunk was executed exactly as written and works.
**Rebuild:** `python3 tools/build_art_atlas.py GAME.html shipmeta.json OUT.png` (script in /mnt/user-data/outputs/tools; `shipmeta.json` = spriteKey -> faction and ships, dumped from `SHIP_REGISTRY` with jsdom). Station factions, the lettering table and the notes are hand-entered in the script.
**Size options measured, not built:** the same pixels as lossless WebP = 4.14 MB (39% smaller; less certain to survive upload and to decode everywhere); shrinking the 13 map sprites that are 512 px to 256 px saves about 1.3 MB (atlas about 5.4 MB). Share of the art bytes: map 2.68 MB, front views 2.74 MB, damage-control art 0.90 MB.
**Risk to check on the receiving side:** the project's own copy of `multi_ship_effort.png` turned out to be a JPEG (1456 x 840, RGB) saved under a .png name, so images CAN be recompressed on the way into a project. A JPEG atlas would lose all transparency and the metadata index. Check after import: `Image.open(path).format == 'PNG'` and `.mode == 'RGBA'`. If it fails, rebuild as lossless WebP, or ship only the needed tiles as text.
**Paste-ready line for the other chat:** "TC_ShipArt_Atlas.png in the project is an RGBA PNG atlas of ship art. Read its index with `import json; from PIL import Image; im=Image.open('/mnt/project/TC_ShipArt_Atlas.png'); man=json.loads(im.info['manifest'])`; each tile has r=[x,y,w,h] -> `im.crop((x,y,x+w,y+h))`. Check im.format=='PNG' and im.mode=='RGBA'. Embed only the tiles you need."

### 0.128 — Analysis only (nothing changed): multiple ships per side (1 vs 4, N vs M)  [PARKED — FUTURE GOAL, roadmap A11]

**User question (2026-10-26):** "how hard would it be to provide the option of multiple ships versus multiple ships ... with 1 versus 4 ships?" **Short answer given: a big job (the largest single feature so far) but tractable if staged; 1 vs N is a much smaller first step than N vs M.** Picture: `multi_ship_effort.png`.
**Measured (static count over the game code, images excluded; 10,821 lines, 316 functions):** the game is built around exactly TWO ships: **241 direct references to `GS.player` (151) and `GS.enemy` (90), in 72 of 316 functions (23%)**, plus 16 interface elements with ids starting `p-/e-/ps-/es-`. By area: map, viewscreen and drawing 71 (29%; `renderTac` alone 38); other 48 (20%); sidebars, panels and logs 43 (18%; `updateWpnFireBtn` 15); turn flow, initiative, victory 32 (13%; `resolveTacAdv` 10, `showEndgamePanel` 10, `checkVictory` 4); firing, damage, weapons 28 (12%); enemy AI 19 (8%; `aiAllocatePower` 5). **State stored as "the opponent" rather than per pair:** `locked` (26 uses), `detectedCloaked` (25), `hadCloakLock` (5), `_oppPrevMP` (2), `tacAdvWinner`, `playerFireDeclared`/`enemyFireDeclared` (13), `killBlow` (6), `turn_stats` (7), `debrief.faceHits/faceDmg {onPlayer,onEnemy}`, `dmgLog` sides. `launchGame` builds exactly one player ship and one enemy ship from the two selects (`player-ship`, `enemy-ship`).
**What is already reusable:** the combat core takes its ships as parameters — `resolveShipFiring(shooter,target)`, `applyDamage(ship,...,firer)`, `canFireOnTarget`, `weaponArcCoversTarget`, `getHitFace`, `computeWeaponAim`, `triggerWeaponFX`, `addShieldArcFX`, `applyExplosionDamage`, `pickWeaponLoss` (26 of 316 functions take ship parameters). So the deferred missile results, shield shimmer, hull-edge aiming, Option-A weapon loss etc. should work for any pair unchanged.
**What the rulebook says (FASA_2003_Rulebook_FULL_OCR.md):** line ~2414: the rules "are presented as though there were only two ships in combat; they may be altered slightly for more than two. Test combats were successfully run for as many as 20 captains"; ~2144: captains enjoy controlling several ships, "the practical limit is about three"; ~1048: **initiative ranks ALL vessels** ("the vessel with the highest total has won the tactical advantage, the ship with the second highest has second advantage, and so on for all vessels", ties by die roll; the loser moves first, "the next captain then moves his vessel, and so on"); ~5657 (Command & Control): the ship with more movement points in a phase moves first, ties go to the ship without the tactical advantage; ~2996 **Multiple Explosions** (several ships exploding together resolve in descending damage order); ~3500 **Multiple Ship Victories** (victory points shared among the victors); ~1492 **two or more starships may occupy the same hex** (today's hex hit-testing and drawing assume one ship per hex). The initiative screen built in §0.120-0.124 is a two-card layout and would become a RANKED LIST.
**Proposed stages (estimates in "rounds" = working sessions like the initiative screen, each with testing and the user's review):** **0 Foundation (3-5):** `GS.ships[]` and `GS.sides[]`; today's `GS.player` becomes the ship the human is commanding and `GS.enemy` the contact currently selected/targeted (aliases), so the 1v1 game keeps working while converted piece by piece; per-observer contact state (`ship.contacts[id] = {locked, detectedCloaked, ...}`). **1 vs N (8-12):** each AI ship acts against the player; target selection (map click / roster); ranked initiative; per-pair sensors and cloak detection; victory = all enemies gone; AI target choice and focus fire; the viewscreen shows the selected contact. **N vs M (8-12 more):** ship roster and per-ship power/movement/fire; AI allies; shared hexes; simultaneous explosions; shared victory points. **Hot-seat, several humans per side (5-8 more):** per-side turns/screens, secret allocations. **Risks:** the refactor touches the most code of any feature; mitigation is the existing test harness (jsdom plus a REAL Chromium via Playwright, AI-allocation regression, the 1v1 behaviour kept byte-identical at each step). **Balance:** a 1-v-4 needs fleet balancing; the game's own ratings (D / WDF / CE ratio) could drive a point-buy, which also fits the planned build-your-own-ship feature.
**DECISION (2026-10-26): the user chose to stay with 1v1 for now and asked that the effort so far be recorded and the feature marked as a future goal. DONE: this section; roadmap item A11 in Feature_Status_and_Wishlist.md rewritten as PARKED with the measurements, the rulebook findings, the staged plan, how to resume, and the open questions; A12 (hot-seat) cross-referenced as stage 3; `multi_ship_effort.png` kept. TO RESUME: read this section and A11, then start with the design note and interface mock-up for approval, before touching code.**
**Meaning of "rounds" (user asked):** one back-and-forth working session (the user sends a message, Claude returns finished, tested work and pictures, the user reacts). Examples: the deferred missile results were 1 big round; gravity-well spacing about 2; the initiative screen about 7 (mostly design feedback). The estimates are rough and rise with design iteration.
**Open questions for the user:** whether stage 1 should be "you vs 1-4 AI ships" first (recommended); whether the AI ships are allies of each other only (one enemy side) or a free-for-all. Recommended first deliverable: a short design note with the proposed roster / target-selection UI mock-up for approval BEFORE any code is touched.

### 0.127 — Analysis only (no code or art changed): baked-in names and registries on the ship art, and a hover tooltip instead

**User question (2026-10-26):** "how hard would it be to go through all the ship sprites and remove the ship registry and names? Instead we would just have a pop up tool tip stating the registry and name. Given we're going to eventually have a construction/build your own ship feature, this would just align more seamlessly."
**Inventory (read from the game file).** 96 ship images in three tables: `SHIP_SPRITES` (47 map sprites, mostly 256 px, the Baker is 512), `DMG_VIEW_ART` (9 damage-control top-down arts), `FRONT_VIEW_ART` (40 front-view portraits). Plus 4 celestial images. **Original art sources survive for only three ships** (D-4, T-5, Federation I, in /uploads); for everything else the embedded image is the only copy, so removal means editing the embedded pixels. The game already holds `name`, `reg`, `cls` for all 66 registry ships (only 10 distinct registry numbers, because marks share a ship) and already prints name and registry as LIVE text (sidebar `sb-id`, bottom bar, power panel `pwr-ship-sub`) and the ship's name as a canvas label under its hex on the map (`renderTac`).
**Where baked lettering actually is — FEDERATION ONLY.** OCR (tesseract, both polarities, 4 rotations, mirrored) found NOTHING: the lettering is upside-down, curved and a few pixels tall, so **a negative OCR result proves nothing here and was NOT used as evidence**; the art was inspected by eye instead. Map sprites: **13 of 15 Federation sprites carry lettering** (Gagarin, Northampton, Remora, Larson, Andor, Baker, Reliant, Constitution, Constitution_NCC1700 faint, Excelsior tiny, Enterprise, ChandleyClass, Loknar); Federation1 and Federation2 are clean. **All 32 Klingon, Romulan, Orion, Gorn and station sprites are clean.** Front-view portraits: clear lettering on Gagarin, Larson and Loknar, apparently on Baker and Andor. Damage-control art: Constitution_NCC1700 (large, faint) and Excelsior; Federation1 clean. **About 20 of the 96 images need work.**
**The baked text already DISAGREES with the game's data in six places (read by eye from enlarged crops; the Andor reading is the least certain):** Northampton (art NCC-3125), Remora (NCC-3183), Larson (NCC-4300) and Andor (about NCC-3350) show registry numbers while the game data says **N/A**; the ChandleyClass sprite reads NCC-2301 while the data says NCC-1838; the Excelsior damage-control art reads **"U.S.S. ORACLE NCC-2012"** while the data names the ship Excelsior. Matching: Baker NCC-2664, Reliant NCC-1891, Loknar NCC-2700, Enterprise/Constitution NCC-1701, Constitution NCC-1700, Gagarin NCC-80100.
**Size on screen:** on the map a 256-px sprite is drawn about 60 px wide, so its 7-px lettering is 1-2 px: invisible. The lettering shows in the damage-control tab (46 ships use their map sprite there at 2-3x, 3 use dedicated art), in the front-view portraits, and when zoomed.
**Removal trial (NOT applied to the game; `removal_trial_easy_cases.png`, `removal_trial_hard_cases.png`, `lettering_on_sprites.png`).** A mask of the lettering (dark pixels against a median-blurred background, inside a hand-set zone) plus OpenCV inpainting: **Larson**: registry AND the small name line removed cleanly. **Northampton**: lettering gone, but the zone also dulled the bridge outline (needs a tighter mask). **Remora**: only part of the letters caught (threshold/zone too tight). **Baker**: the lettering is made of the same dark dots as the dense panel lines, so the result is a smear and the bridge is damaged — hard. **Constitution damage-control art**: lettering is faint gray on shaded gray; the automatic method found fragments and nicked the bridge outline — fails. **Conclusion: it cannot be automated; every image needs a hand-set mask and review.** Estimated split: about 8 easy (flat light saucer, big dark lettering: Larson, Northampton, Remora, Loknar, ChandleyClass, Enterprise, Constitution 1701, Reliant), about 5 moderate (Gagarin curved tiny text on the ring, Constitution_NCC1700 faint, Excelsior tiny, Andor dark textured saucer, the portraits), about 1-2 hard (Baker; maybe the Excelsior art).
**The tooltip half is SMALL:** the map canvas already has a `mousemove` handler (`showTerrainTip`, `getHexAtEvent`) and a tooltip layer; a hover over a ship's hex can show name, registry, class and faction. Open decision: the four ships with registry N/A (show "no registry", or the name only). Suggestion for build-your-own-ship: the registry/name could be drawn DYNAMICALLY (canvas text) on the damage-control view later.
**Proposed plan (awaiting the user's go-ahead):** (1) the hover tooltip; (2) the easy sprites, delivered as before/after sheets for approval (the user's standing rule is to see art before it goes in); (3) the moderate ones; (4) decide the hard ones together; leave map sprites alone where the text is invisible unless it contradicts the data.

### 0.125 — Neutral faction colour: six options presented [DECIDED in §0.126: option 6, Obsidian, was chosen and built; the six styles are saved]

**User request (2026-10-25):** "what do you recommend for a color for a 'neutral' faction like the independent merchants? I was thinking of a crystal like -- see through, translucent like coloring. Come up with 6 options for me to choose from."
**State of the game:** no independent / neutral ships exist (the registry has only `fed` 29, `kli` 19, `rom` 13, `gor` 3, `ori` 2). The only trace is `FACTION_STYLE.ind = FACTION_STYLE.fed` (viewscreen), which would make independents LOOK LIKE THE FEDERATION there — **to be replaced when the faction is added.** On the initiative screen an unknown code (e.g. `ind`) falls back to the neutral default colours. A source comment calls the Orion blockade-runner group "INDEPENDENT / ORION / MERCHANT", so Orion ships are the nearest existing thing to merchants but remain a separate faction (purple).
**The six options (each a different MATERIAL, drawn on the same d10 as the factions; `neutral_faction_options.png`, and each beside the five factions in `neutral_options_vs_factions.png`):** (1) **Clear Quartz** — near-transparent white, edge `#f4faff`; (2) **Smoky Quartz** — translucent taupe, edge `#d8c3ad`; (3) **Moonstone (opal)** — milky with a pink/cyan/mint/lilac sheen, edge `#f2f5ff`; (4) **Aquamarine** — pale sea-glass teal, edge `#aef6ec`; (5) **Rose Quartz** — soft translucent pink, edge `#ffd3e2`; (6) **Obsidian (dark glass)** — dark glossy glass with a faint teal-violet sheen, edge `#9bb0d0`. A first draft had Silver instead of Obsidian; it looked too much like Clear Quartz and Moonstone, so the set was revised (Moonstone made milky and more iridescent, Quartz made more transparent, Silver replaced) to give a real spread.
**How a crystal die differs from the solid faction dice (for the implementation):** the faction dice are solid faces at graded `fill-opacity`; a crystal die uses per-face linear GRADIENT fills (light top-left to deeper bottom-right; Moonstone has four stops) at LOW opacity so the panel shows through, a white specular SLIVER (`polygon points="31.2,7 32.6,9.5 21.4,30.5 18.6,31.5"`, fill-opacity .38) on the front face, a bright edge, and a WHITE number with a dark outline (`paint-order:stroke; stroke:rgba(0,10,30,.7); stroke-width:2.6px`) so it stays legible on a see-through face; the winner glows in the option's glow colour, is 10% larger; the loser is `opacity .72, grayscale .2` as for the factions. Per-face opacities are listed in `opts.json` of the working copy (front face first of the five visible: `[.42,.22,.11,.11,.26]` for Clear Quartz, etc.).
**Measured on the REAL rendered dice (Chromium 141):** number contrast winning/losing — Clear Quartz 8.7/8.8, Smoky 10.6/8.5, Moonstone 6.5/4.9, Aquamarine 8.4/7.7, Rose 9.3/8.1, Obsidian 14.4/9.5 (all at or above 4.9:1, ignoring the outline, so conservative). Distance of each option's die body from the nearest faction die body (CIE76): Clear Quartz 43 (Federation), Smoky 38 (Gorn), Moonstone 53 (Federation), Aquamarine 35 (Romulan — the closest of all), Rose 43 (Klingon), Obsidian 39 (Federation); edge colour vs the nearest faction accent: 41 to 66. For comparison the five factions are at least 33 apart from each other, so every option is clearly its own thing. Among the options themselves the closest pair is Clear / Smoky at 19 (visibly cool vs warm, but both greyish).
**Recommendation given to the user:** Clear Quartz (#1) — the literal "see-through crystal" they described, achromatic so it cannot be mistaken for any faction hue, and 8.7:1 readable; runner-up Moonstone (#3) if they want more personality (distinctive in both the winning and the losing state; the one least like a "dimmed" die). **When the user picks:** add the neutral faction code (`ind`) and a crystal palette entry to `TA_FACTION` plus the crystal die rendering above; remove the `FACTION_STYLE.ind = FACTION_STYLE.fed` alias; give the neutral faction a name in the ship database list (`FAC_NAME`/`FAC_CLS` are 5-entry maps); the card's name and bar would use the option's edge colour. Nothing of this is in the game yet.
