### 0.123 — What changed in v2.65-S176 (the initiative die is a REAL ten-sided die; §0.122 was wrong)

**User feedback (2026-10-25):** "render for me what a ten side die would look like? It's not a 'kite' shape you just provided in the 'D10 faces' file." **Correction of my own mistake:** §0.122 replaced a pentagon (the face of a d12) with a single KITE — which is the shape of one FACE of a d10, not of the die. A ten-sided die (a **pentagonal trapezohedron**) has a point at the top, a point at the bottom, a zig-zag band of 10 vertices between them (5 just above the equator, 5 just below, alternating every 36 degrees) and **ten kite-shaped faces**; five kites meet at each point.
**Geometry (verified numerically in `d10geo.py`):** ring radius r = 1, ring height +-h, apex height +-H; a face (apex, two ring vertices, the opposite ring vertex of the OTHER ring) is planar exactly when **H = h(1 + cos36)/(1 - cos36)** (about 9.47 h; the build uses H = 1.12, h = 0.118; planarity error 2e-16); each face is a kite with two long edges (1.415) and two short (0.662); opposite faces sum to 9 (a physical d10 reads 0-9); a top face's normal is 38.9 degrees above horizontal.
**What the user was given.** `d10_render.png`: a shaded 3D render of the die with perspective-correct numbers (text mapped onto each face plane by an affine transform; my first render had MIRRORED numbers on some faces — a handedness bug, `right = up x normal` — found by looking at it and fixed) plus the side view, the view from above, the view from below (the mirror of from above) and one isolated face, labelled "just ONE of the ten faces". `d10_tools.zip` holds the two scripts (`d10geo.py` geometry, `render.py` renderer).
**In the game.** The die icon is now the die itself, projected orthographically at azimuth 40 degrees and elevation 22 degrees and normalised into the 64x64 viewBox: five faces are visible (three on top, two below; painter's order, Lambert shading mapped to `fill-opacity`), and the rolled number sits on the big front face at its inscribed-circle centre (30.8, 31.5; radius 12.2). The icon is 78 px (was 66), coloured through CSS variables (`--df` face, `--de` edge, `--dt` number): blue for the lower die, gold for the winner. Numbers: one digit at font-size 22; "10" at font-size 16, baseline y 39.3. Considered and rejected: the kite (one face), the pentagon (a d12 face), a hexagon with a Y (a cube = d6), a diamond (a d4 face). Nothing else on the screen changed.
**Verification.** Real Chromium 141: all values 1-10 rendered on the actual initiative screen in both styles (lower die 1-9 blue, winning die 2-10 gold; 18 renders) and every number checked against the FRONT face with `isPointInFill` on the four corners of its ink box plus a 0.8-unit margin — all inside (the first pass found the two-digit "10" marginal against the kite's narrowing upper edges; it was lowered in the face to 39.3 and re-verified), 5 visible faces per die, no JavaScript errors; `d10_faces.png` shows every value at 3x. Regression unchanged: the initiative flow with real timing (the screen stays up, background inert, Continue / Space / Enter, the double-click guard, nothing posted before the reveal), the genuine Commit -> Proceed flow with real mouse clicks, the AI/ship-data hash, deferred missile results and phase gating, weapon destruction, damage-log consistency, shield-shimmer geometry, the initiative decisions and the tie fairness (50.1%). **Still true:** the game rolls 1-10, so the die shows "10" where a physical d10 shows 0; and the view angle, size and colours are my choices — the user may want them changed.

### 0.122 — What changed in v2.64-S175 (the initiative dice are drawn as d10 dice) [SUPERSEDED BY §0.123: it drew a single kite, which is only one face of a d10]

**User feedback (2026-10-25):** after looking at the preview sheet the user said they liked panel 3 (the tie roll-off decided, dice landed) best, but "since we play with a ten side die, the shape that surrounds the numbers for the 'die roll' is incorrect. that shape would represent a 12 sided die." Correct: the die icon was a PENTAGON, which is the face shape of a d12 (a dodecahedron). A d10 is a pentagonal trapezohedron whose faces are KITES.
**Change.** `dieSvg` now draws a KITE (`<polygon class="o" points="32,2 60,26 32,62 4,26"/>`) with a smaller inner kite (`class="i"`), the number inside; CSS `.ta-die .o/.i` (and the `.win` gold state) replace the old `.ta-die polygon` rule. Considered and rejected on purpose: an elongated hexagon with a Y inside (reads as an isometric CUBE = a d6) and a plain diamond (reads as a d4 face or a rhombus). `setDie` now sizes the number: one digit at font-size 22, baseline y=38; the two-digit "10" at font-size 17, baseline y=36, so both digits stay inside the inner kite. Nothing else on the screen changed (layout, colours, wording, Continue behaviour).
**Verification.** Real Chromium 141: all ten faces were rendered on the actual initiative screen (five tie roll-offs, 1..10) and the number measured against the inner kite's width over the glyph's height — all ten fit (single digits 13.2 wide in 20.2 available; "10" 20.4 in 23), no pentagon remains in any die (`polygon` point-count check), no JavaScript errors; the dice are shown in blue (the lower die) and gold (the winner). `d10_faces.png` shows all ten faces at 3x resolution; `initiative_screen_tie_result.png` is the favoured panel at full size; `initiative_screen_preview.png` is the regenerated sheet. Regression unchanged: the initiative flow with real timing (the screen stays up, the background is inert, Continue / Space / Enter work, the double-click guard, nothing posted before the reveal), the genuine Commit -> Proceed flow with real mouse clicks (open 9 s later, Continue -> movement phase 1), the AI/ship-data hash, deferred missile results and phase gating, weapon destruction, damage-log consistency and the shield-shimmer geometry. **A d10 shows 1-10 here (the game rolls 1-10), unlike a physical d10 whose faces read 0-9; the "10" face is shown as "10".**

### 0.121 — What changed in v2.63-S174 (the initiative screen stays until the player presses Continue)

**User feedback (2026-10-25), after test play:** the initiative screen closed by itself when its progress bar finished — not enough time to read it — and the CONTINUE button "seemed pointless" because the screen vanished first. "Let's not do the progress bar and just have the player hit the continue button to move on." (The same message said the missile-result delay in the combat log "worked well".) **This SUPERSEDES the auto-advance statements in §0.120.**
**Change.** The auto-advance and the progress bar are REMOVED entirely (`TACADV_AUTO_MS` and the `.ta-prog` markup/CSS no longer exist); the screen stays up until the player presses the **CONTINUE** button, or **Space / Enter** (Esc too). The button is centred under the banner. The first press during the animation (label "SKIP") finishes it and reveals the result; the next press (label "CONTINUE") moves on. Two small decisions made to match the request: **clicking the dark background no longer does anything** (it used to advance, which would be an easy accident now that nothing closes the screen by itself), and a **450 ms guard** (`readyAt`, scaled by `TACADV_SPEED`) makes the press after the reveal be ignored if it comes straight after the skip press, so a quick double-click cannot skip the animation AND dismiss the result unread. The tutorial help text now ends "press Continue when you have read it". Nothing else changed: the result lines, badge, sidebar and sound are still posted at the reveal; hot-seat play still only needs `GS.sideLabels` (and no longer needs any timing setting).
**Verification.** jsdom with REAL timing: no `.ta-prog`/`#ta-prog-i` in the DOM and `TACADV_AUTO_MS` is undefined; after the reveal the screen is still open, and still open 7 s later; a click on the background does nothing (during the animation or after the reveal); the button continues (`enterPhase` called once); skip press -> an immediate second press ignored -> a press after the guard continues; Space skips, an immediate Enter is ignored, a later Enter continues; nothing is posted before the reveal (unchanged). **Real Chromium 141, real mouse clicks:** after the genuine Commit/Proceed flow the screen was open at the reveal and still open **11 seconds later** with 0 progress bars; a real click on the dark background left it open; a real click on CONTINUE moved the game to movement phase 1; no JavaScript errors, no dialogs. Screenshots regenerated (`initiative_screen_preview.png`). Regression unchanged: the AI/ship-data hash, deferred missile results and phase gating, weapon destruction Option A, damage-log consistency, shield shimmer geometry, and the initiative log text identical to the pre-initiative build in the 5 non-degenerate cases.

### 0.120 — What changed in v2.62-S173 (initiative shown visually; the three rule versions; a real browser is now available for verification)

**User request (2026-10-25):** "in the rules, is there a determination on initiative for each side? If so, that should be visually determined -- given that we'll be doing a multi-player 'hot seat' style of play as well as the advanced version of rules play later down the road with other RPG style die rolling." (The message began "two things" but described only this one; the second was not stated — ask.)
**Rules findings (rulebook OCR, `FASA_2003_Rulebook_FULL_OCR.md`).** Initiative is the **TACTICAL ADVANTAGE PHASE**, once per turn after Power Allocation. THREE versions: **(1) BASIC (p.12):** each captain announces his movement points; the ship with MORE wins; a tie is broken by a die roll (highest wins). **(2) INTERMEDIATE / ADVANCED (pp.22-39):** the same comparison, but a tie is settled by comparing the captains' **SKILL RATINGS** — no die roll. **(3) COMMAND & CONTROL / role-playing (pp.40-55):** no movement comparison: each captain rolls one die and ADDS it to his Skill Rating in Starship Combat Strategy/Tactics; the gamemaster does the same for the opposing captain; the higher total wins ("The Skill Roll and Tactical Advantage"). In all versions the loser moves FIRST (the winner moves last) and the winner also rolls sensors last and declares fire last.
**What the game did before this build (found by reading the code):** `resolveTacAdv` compared movement points and logged the result; a tie was settled by a d10 each — and an EQUAL roll went to the PLAYER (`pr>=er`), i.e. the player won 54.9% of ties (measured over 200,000), unacceptable for two-human hot-seat play; the tutorial help text said "a single roll decides" (wrong — movement points decide, a roll only breaks ties); the result existed only as combat-log text. **The tactical advantage is used in exactly two places in the game, both MOVEMENT ORDER** (`enterPhase` move branch, `endPhase`); the winner-rolls-sensors-last and winner-declares-fire-last parts of the rulebook are NOT modelled (the player always acts before the AI's fire is revealed), and **there are no captain Skill Ratings in the game**, so the Intermediate Skill-Rating tie-break is also settled by the Basic die roll for now. The screen therefore claims only what is real: who moves last / first.
**What was built.** `computeTacAdv(moves, rollDie)` — the pure Basic decision; an equal roll is ROLLED AGAIN (player win rate on ties now 50.1%). `computeTacAdvSkill(skills, rollDie)` — the pure role-playing decision (die + skill, higher total, equal total re-rolled); NOT wired into play (no Skill Ratings yet) but fully tested and rendered. `showTacAdvVisual(R, onDone, onReveal)` — the screen: a full-window overlay (`#tacadv-ov`, created on first use) with a card per side (label, ship, class, faction colour, big number counting up, a proportional bar), a **roll-off row of two tumbling d10 icons (kite-shaped faces since §0.122; they were pentagons before)** when the sides are tied (several rounds if the dice are equal) or always in skill mode (showing `skill + die = total`), then the winner's gold highlight and a banner ("X HOLDS THE TACTICAL ADVANTAGE", why, and what it means: moves LAST / moves FIRST). **[SUPERSEDED in §0.121: the auto-advance and the background click were removed; only the CONTINUE button / Space / Enter move on.]** The sides are generic data `{label,name,cls,faction,moves|skill}` so hot-seat play only needs `GS.sideLabels = {player:'PLAYER 1 — KIRK', enemy:'PLAYER 2 — KOR'}`. `R.mode` is `'moves'` today and `'skill'` when the role-playing rules are wired in. A header badge `#hdr-init` (new `.seg-d`; gold when the local side holds it, red-orange when the other does) keeps the holder in view all turn; the sidebar now shows the enemy's real movement points at this phase.
**The result is posted at the REVEAL, not before** (the same principle as the missile results, §0.119): `GS.tacAdvWinner`/`GS.tacAdv` are set at once (nothing else can happen while the screen is up), but the dice log lines, the "Tactical Advantage: X wins" line, "you move last…", the sidebar text, the badge and the sound are posted by `onReveal` when the winner appears — or immediately if the animation is skipped or the screen is replaced; the badge is cleared at the start of each decision. The phase continues (`enterPhase(first movement phase)`) when the screen closes (it was a fixed 800 ms). If the screen throws, it falls back to posting at once and the old 800 ms delay.
**Verification.** Pure decisions: more movement wins without any roll; ties by die; equal dice re-rolled; skill+die (6+7=13 vs 8+3=11) and equal totals re-rolled; fairness 54.9% -> 50.1%. The real `resolveTacAdv` log text and winner are IDENTICAL to the previous build in all 5 non-degenerate cases (clear wins, ties both ways). jsdom: nothing is posted while the numbers count up or the dice roll (0 lines, badge hidden, sidebar "deciding…", no sound, no phase entry) while the state is already set; one click reveals everything at once, a second continues; Space then Enter work; auto-advance works; a second screen replacing a first posts the first's result without error; the badge is cleared when the next turn's decision starts. **Real Chromium 141 (Playwright), the actual game in a real window:** no JavaScript errors, no dialogs; screenshots of a clear win, the enemy winning, a tie roll-off mid-roll and landed, a tie with an equal roll and a re-roll, hot-seat labels, the skill layout, the header badge, and a 760-px-wide window (no horizontal overflow; the header badge no longer wraps — `white-space:nowrap`); and the GENUINE flow — set the power sliders, press Commit, press Proceed to Combat: the screen appeared by itself after 0.39 s with the badge hidden and no result in the log, revealed at 1.5 s (badge, sidebar and log line appeared together), and carried on by itself at 4.5 s into movement phase 1 where the AI moved first because the player had won. All earlier suites unchanged: the deferred missile results and phase gating, shield shimmer, weapon destruction Option A (9,900 trials), damage-log hull consistency, 18,480 misses vs real hulls, the 588-allocation AI regression and the ship-data hash. `initiative_screen_preview.png` is a sheet of the REAL screenshots.
**Not done / for later:** wiring the role-playing mode (needs Skill Ratings on captains and a decision about the gamemaster's roll); the Intermediate Skill-Rating tie-break (same); making the winner roll sensors last and declare fire last (needs a decision about the fire-declaration flow, where the player currently always acts first); for hot-seat play, secrecy between the two humans' power allocations and per-side reveals (the screen already names sides generically). **Tunables:** `TACADV_SPEED`, `GS.sideLabels`, `TA_FACTION_COLOR` (`TACADV_AUTO_MS` was removed in §0.121).
**A REAL BROWSER IS AVAILABLE IN THE SANDBOX (new, important):** Chromium 141 through Playwright works (`export NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g)`; `const {chromium}=require('playwright')`; browsers live in `/opt/pw-browsers`). Load the game with `page.goto('file:///path/to/game.html')`, start a battle with `launchGame()`, drive the real buttons (`#commit-btn`, `#proceed-btn`, sliders `#sl-mv`/`#sl-sh`) and take REAL screenshots. Every earlier entry in this file that says "NOT verified: how it looks in the live game" (shield shimmer, damage-control centring and sprite fallback, weapon-fx hull emitters and misses, the labelled damage logs, the copy buttons, the deferred missile results) can now be checked for real; that pass has not been done yet.

### 0.119 — What changed in v2.61-S172 (missile / plasma results post when the projectile lands — "stage 2")

**User request (2026-10-25):** "go with the missile text delay. once there's a visual representation of a miss or hit (on the shield or ship itself) then post the results." This is the stage-2 item that had been waiting since §0.111.
**Design.** For `missile` and `plasma` weapons only (beams are effectively instant and are UNCHANGED): the die is still rolled at LAUNCH (the animation needs to know hit or miss, and the miss severity), but nothing about the shot is printed then. The whole result block — the warnings and roll line, `Damage:`, `Hits <face> shield`, `Shield absorbs`, the location roll, the damage-control hull line, the damage-log entries, the debrief face counters, `turn_stats` hits, the kill-blow record, `checkVictory`, the sidebar/damage-view refresh — posts when the projectile LANDS: on arrival at the hull edge for a HIT, and when it PASSES the ship at closest approach for a MISS (`computeWeaponAim` now returns `passFrac`, the fraction of the path at which the miss passes the target; the miss does not wait for the far end of its overshoot). The shield shimmer / hull explosion appear at the same instant: the arrival callback runs `resolveOnce()` FIRST (it posts the result and fills `fxInfo`) and only then `impactFX`. Launch bookkeeping stays at launch: `w.fired`, `playerShotsFired`, `_volleyCount`, the weapon buttons.
**Mechanics.** `triggerWeaponFX(...,info,onResolve)`: when a caller passes `onResolve` for a missile/plasma shot, `GS.pendingImpacts++` and the result runs exactly once (`resolveOnce`) from the arrival callback or, for a miss, the new projectile `pass` hook; a watchdog (`IMPACT_WATCHDOG_MS` = 9000) posts the result anyway if the projectile never lands (tab hidden, effect lost); if `GS` was replaced meanwhile the result is DROPPED (checked: nothing leaks into a new battle). Both fire paths (`fireWeapon`, `resolveShipFiring`) build `resolveOutcome` with the previous post-roll code unchanged except that its sounds go through `rsnd` (a deferred shot's explosion/shield sounds come from the impact effect; the `miss` sound still plays at the pass) and the pre-roll lines go through `emit` (buffered for a deferred shot, direct otherwise). `tickFX` collects arrivals/passes found in one tick and runs them AFTER its loop in LAUNCH order (`FX_SEQ`/`seq`), because the loop walks the list backwards — before this, two missiles landing on the same tick posted in reverse firing order (verified: third -> second -> first before, first -> second -> third now).
**Phase gating.** A fire phase must not move on while a result is still to come. `whenImpactsSettled(cb)` polls `GS.pendingImpacts`; it guards all three exits — `endPhase()` (fire branch), `declareNoFire()` and `revealFireDeclarations()` (the player's earlier missiles must post BEFORE the "End fire phase" line and before the AI's volley) — with a re-entry flag `GS._settling`, and the End Phase button reads "Resolving…" while it waits; and `resolveShipFiring`'s `finish()` (so `proceedAfterFire`/`checkVictory`/the next phase wait for the AI's own missiles). **A target already destroyed (or `GS.over`) when a missile lands:** its roll line posts followed by "but the fight is already decided; no further effect", with no damage, no second kill-blow record (`GS.killBlow` keeps the first lethal landing) and no second `checkVictory`.
**Verification (real `fireWeapon` / `resolveShipFiring` with forced dice, `tickFX` driven by hand):** (A) a missile that hits a shield: 0 result lines at launch and at 91% of its flight, pending 1; on landing the block posts in order (roll, damage, face, absorption, location, hull) with the shimmer and explosion, pending 0; (B) a miss posts at 66% of its path (pass point 65%) with the projectile NOT yet at the end, and no shimmer or explosion; (C) a beam posts immediately, pending 0; (D) AI volley of a beam + a missile: `onComplete` NOT called until the missile lands, the missile result is printed before completion, the beam result before the missile's; (E) a lethal first landing with a second missile in flight: no error, `over` set, kill-blow weapon is the first lethal landing, the second logs "already decided"; (F) End Phase pressed (twice) with a missile in flight: no "End fire phase" line and no phase advance, button "Resolving…", then after landing exactly one line (after the missile block) and one advance, button restored; (G) `declareNoFire` gated the same way; (H) watchdog: result posted after the timeout with no ticks; (I) battle replaced in flight: 0 lines leaked, new pending 0; (J) plasma defers likewise (V8 Bird of Prey, landed after 76 ticks). Regression, all UNCHANGED: shield-shimmer decisions and geometry (50,000 cases), the real player/AI beam fire paths, weapon destruction Option A (9,900 trials, 0 violations), damage-log hull consistency (4,800 events, 0 mismatches) and copy, 18,480 misses vs real hulls (0 touched), the 588-allocation AI regression and the ship-data hash.
**Timing (from the code, assuming ~60 frames per second):** a missile flies ~1 hex per 11 ticks (about 0.18 s per hex); a plasma bolt about 28 ticks per hex (about 0.5 s per hex), so a long plasma shot can hold End Phase for several seconds — that is the cost of posting at the landing, and the number is `spd` in `addPlasmaFX` if it should change. **Not verified:** how it feels in the live game (frame pacing, the length of the End Phase wait); FIRE ALL with many missiles is covered by the ordering test, not by a live run. **Known behaviour to be aware of:** the results of beams fired in the same volley appear immediately while missiles' appear later, so a volley's log lines are now in LANDING order, not firing order.
**Still open:** nothing waiting on the user from the earlier list.

### 0.118 — What changed in v2.60-S171 (range-aware misses, gravity-well steering, readable damage logs, copyable logs)

**Trigger:** a Constitution vs D-7 G play-test (log `combat_log_2026-10-25-12-29-47`, Admiral, build v2.59-S170, plus a screenshot of the "Damage dealt" log). The user reported: (1) at one hex a missed beam went "WAY WIDE" though at ten hexes it looked fine; (2) a missed beam went straight to a black hole next to the D-7 — "was that the reason? ... I do not want it to come to happy coincidence"; (3) the enemy superstructure entries looked wrong ("-3 ... then -8 with 12/20 left after that"); (4) can the log text be copied instead of screenshotted.
**1. Point-blank misses (range-aware).** Cause: the miss clearance is a SIDEWAYS DISTANCE, so at point-blank range the same distance is a huge ANGLE, and the beam then carried on a fixed 1.3-2.7 hexes. Measured with the real Constitution and D-7 sprites (misses, clear space): at 1 hex the OLD build swung misses 49 deg median / up to 64 deg off line and ended up to 2.8 hexes from the target; at 10 hexes only 1.5-4.8 deg. **Fix:** the clearance BEYOND the hull outline is capped at `MISS_MAX_GAP_PER_RANGE` = 18% of the distance to the target (about 10 deg), and the carry-on is scaled by `min(1, 0.35 + 0.2 * rangeInHexes)` so it is shorter when the shooter is close. NEW at 1 hex: median 20-36 deg, max 35.6 deg, end at most 1.4 hexes from the target, path 1.6-1.7 hexes; at 2 hexes the worst case drops 28 -> 17.7 deg; from about 3 hexes on it is unchanged. **The ~20 deg floor at one hex is geometry, not a bug:** the D-7 is wide and the ships are nearly touching, so any beam that clears its wings must swing that far.
**2. Gravity wells and shots.** Verified in the code: **nothing in `computeWeaponAim`, `triggerWeaponFX`, `fireWeapon` or `resolveShipFiring` references gravity wells** (wells affect drawing, movement cost 2, and a tooltip only). The side a miss passes on was a coin flip: with a well adjacent to the D-7, **50.4%** of old misses took the well's side (and some beams passed through the well's own hex, closest approach 0) — so the black-hole beam was CHANCE, not gravity. Because a coin flip that happens to look like gravity is misleading, a miss is now steered: `gravityWellCenters()` + `segPointDist()`; both candidate paths are solved (`solve(side)`), and if either would pass within `MISS_STEER_HEXES` = 3 hexes of a well (and they differ by more than 0.25 hex) the side keeping farther from the well is used; otherwise the side stays random. **Verified over 2,000 misses per case:** no well 50.1% north; well adjacent on one side -> 0% on the well's side, closest approach to the well 1.17 hexes minimum (was 0); wells on both sides -> the side with the farther well, 0% toward the near one; a far well (7 hexes) -> unchanged 49.2% (no steering). **If the user ever wants wells to REALLY bend shots, that is a rules/design decision and would need real mechanics (to-hit, damage path), not a visual.**
**3. Damage-log "math" (it was not wrong — it was read backwards, plus a real gap).** The screenshot's `-8 (12/20)` is turn 1 and `-3 (9/20)` is turn 4 in the combat log (12 - 3 = 9). The damage logs PREPENDED (newest at the top) while the combat log appends (oldest at the top), so reading down the panel ran backward in time. And the two CASCADE entries — `Weapon cascade -> superstructure` and `Superstructure cascade -N` — carried no amount and no hull remaining, so the running total appeared to skip. **Fix:** `addDmgLog` now appends (oldest first), scrolls to the newest, stores `turn`, and prints `T<turn> · ` before each line (turn = the Power Allocation number, as in the combat log); both cascade entries now read `... -N (hull/max)`. Every hull reduction already goes through `applyDamage` and all log (checked). **Verification:** the user's sequence prints `T1 -8 (12/20) / T4 -3 (9/20) / T4 cascade -3 (6/20) / ... / T5 -2 (1/20) / T5 cascade -5 (0/20)`; **4,800 random damage events across the registry: 1,758 hull lines checked, 0 where the printed hull differed from the real hull, 0 where the hull in the log went UP.**
**4. Copying log text.** Cause: `body{user-select:none}` for the whole page. **Fix:** a CSS rule makes `#combat-log`, `#dmg-log`, `#dmg-log-enemy` and the end-of-battle narrative/stats/debrief selectable (`user-select:text`); and there are COPY buttons on the combat log (beside EXPORT) and on each damage log. New `combatLogText()` is the single builder used by BOTH EXPORT (the .txt download) and COPY, so they cannot differ (verified: identical body text); `copyTextToClipboard()` uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText` and falls back to a hidden textarea + `execCommand('copy')` (verified both paths; the button flashes COPIED then reverts); `copyDmgLog(side)` copies the label plus the turn-stamped lines; COPY on an EMPTY combat log shows "NO LOG" and leaves the clipboard alone (my first version would have overwritten it with an empty string; caught and fixed before release).
**Verification summary:** `node --check`; headless boot 0 errors; 18,480 misses on the real Federation/D-4/T-5 sprites across 7 environments (the range cap included in the expected band): 0 touched a hull, 0 outside the band; the shield-shimmer decision table and the real player/AI fire paths re-run on the new build: unchanged; a line diff shows changes ONLY in the miss section of `computeWeaponAim` (plus its helpers), the two cascade calls in `applyDamage`, `addDmgLog`, `exportCombatLog`/the new copy functions, the damage-log and combat-log header markup, one CSS rule, and the version/log lines; the 588-allocation AI regression and the ship-data hash are IDENTICAL. **Not verified:** how any of it looks in the live game, and clipboard permission prompts in every browser. **Tunable:** `MISS_MAX_GAP_PER_RANGE`, the carry-on factor, `MISS_STEER_HEXES`.
**Still open:** the missile text/damage delay (stage 2) — waiting for the user's word.

### 0.117 — What changed in v2.59-S170 (gravity-well clearance: three FULL empty hexes)

**User clarification (2026-10-25):** "For the gravity wells, I want a minimum of three full hexes away from planets and moons. Like I said before, these can be next to a nebula." This settles the open question from §0.113 (whether "three hexes" meant two or three EMPTY hexes): it is **three full empty hexes between a gravity well and any planet or moon hex = hex distance >= 4**. v2.55-S166 had built hex distance >= 3 (two empty hexes). **Change:** `GRAV_BODY_MIN` in `placeCelestials` / `spacingOK` from 3 to 4 (the distance is still measured to the NEAREST hex of a planet's 7-hex footprint or a moon's hex, and to every gravity-well hex); the explanatory comment was updated. Unchanged: a moon must have at least one empty hex between it and a planet (`MOON_PLANET_MIN = 2`); wells carry NO restriction against nebulae.
**Verification (4,000 generated maps, old build vs new, the game's own `generateTerrain` + `placeCelestials`):** under the NEW rule the previous build had **327 well-to-planet/moon distances below 4** (it allowed 3); the new build has **0**, with the closest well-body distance seen exactly **4**; moon-planet touches 0 in both; wells still sit directly beside nebulae (170 maps before, 160 after) so that is still allowed; planets appear on 64% of maps (65% before) and 0.87 moons per map (unchanged), so the larger exclusion zone does not starve placement. A line diff shows changes ONLY to that constant, its comment, and the version/log lines; the AI and ship-data regression is identical. **Not verified:** how the new layouts look in the live game. **Still open:** the missile text/damage delay (stage 2) — waiting for the user's word.

### 0.116 — What changed in v2.58-S169 (Damage Control logs labelled and separated; per-face shield shimmer)

**Trigger:** after a Remora Mk III vs D-7 G play-test (log `combat_log_2026-10-25-11-53-46`, Captain, build v2.56-S167) the user asked (a) whose damage the Damage Control tab's "Damage Log" shows ("it should be labeled accordingly") and (b) for the shield shimmer back: on a full miss keep the fly-by; when a shot HITS but a shield takes the damage show the shimmer, "more specific to the specific hex arc that was utilized" so the player can see what was hit.
**1. Damage log (bug fix).** `addDmgLog` had ONE writer, `applyDamage`, which runs for EITHER ship — so damage to the ENEMY was written into the player's Damage Control tab, mixed with the player's own and mostly unlabelled (e.g. "Superstructure -3 (17/20)" could be either ship). It is now TWO logs, routed by the ship that took the damage (`addDmgLog(msg,cls,ship)`; a new 3rd parameter, passed from all 9 calls in `applyDamage`; no ship = the player's, as before; `GS.dmgLog` entries now carry `side`): **"Damage taken — <player ship> (your ship)"** in `#dmg-log` and **"Damage dealt — <enemy ship> (enemy)"** in the new `#dmg-log-enemy`; both labels are named at the start of each battle by the new `labelDmgLogs()`, called right after `GS` is built in `launchGame`.
`labelDmgLogs()` also CLEARS both logs: the DOM log was never cleared between battles, so entries from a previous battle in the same page session persisted (verified fixed with the real `launchGame`).
**2. Shield shimmer (new effect `shieldarc`).** The old `addShieldFX` (a full ring at the hex centre, last used on misses before stage 1) is left in place but unused. New `addShieldArcFX(target,face,pre,post,absorbed,shooter)`: a shimmering arc over the ONE 60-degree sector of the struck face, centred on `(target.facing + face) * 60 deg` (the same geometry as `getHitFace`), drawn just outside the ship's outline (radius `max(0.75 HR, hullRadius*1.12 + 0.05 HR)`), brightest at the centre and feathered to nothing at both ends, with a travelling flicker, a flare where the shot arrived, and a small label with the face name and the amount absorbed ("F-Stbd -3"). Colour by how the face is holding: **cyan** = at least half of its pre-hit strength left, **amber** = under half, **red** = that hit used it up. It fades over ~33 ticks; the label fades first.
**What a shot shows now** (`triggerWeaponFX` got a 6th parameter `info`; both fire paths create `fxInfo` and fill it after the shield is worked out: `{face, pre, post, absorbed, pen}`; the effect READS it when the shot lands — a beam ~120 ms after firing, a missile on arrival — which is always after the fire code has filled it): **miss** = fly-by only, no shimmer, no flash (unchanged); **hit, shield absorbs it all** = shimmer, NO hull explosion, `shieldhit` sound; **hit, shield absorbs part** = shimmer AND hull explosion; **hit with no shield** (generator dead, or 0 on that face) = hull explosion only; **no info supplied** = the previous behaviour (explosion). Applies to the player's shots and the AI's, beams and missiles/plasma.
**Verification:** (damage log) real page DOM: player damage lands only in the "taken" log, enemy damage only in "dealt", labels name the ships, a new battle clears both, the real `launchGame` names and clears them. (shimmer) the decision table for 8 hit/miss cases for beams and torpedoes; **50,000 random shooter/target positions and facings: the lit arc always contains the direction the shot came from** (worst offset exactly 30 deg = the sector edge); colour thresholds; the REAL `drawFX` with a recording canvas (14 outer + 14 inner segments, spanning 61 deg, centred within 0.6 deg of the face, brightest 0.74 at the centre vs 0.05 at the ends, label hidden late in the effect); the REAL `fireWeapon` (player) and `resolveShipFiring` (AI) driven end to end with forced dice: shield-takes-all -> shimmer only (enemy hull unchanged), partial -> shimmer + explosion, no shield -> explosion only, miss -> nothing; the AI case on the player lights the player's own face. `shield_shimmer_preview.png` shows what the draw code produces for all six faces, the three colours, and two later moments (drawn from the recorded canvas calls, not a screenshot). The 588-allocation AI regression and the ship-data hash are IDENTICAL to v2.57-S168.
**Not verified:** how it looks in the live game; the label size on small screens. **Tunable:** colours and thresholds in `addShieldArcFX`, segment/glow/label constants in the `shieldarc` branch of `drawFX`, duration via `dec`.
**Observations from the Remora log (not changed):** Option A weapon destruction worked as designed ("no weapon could bear on the firer — damage halved onto superstructure (-2, 5 left)" and the KD-6 beams lost when they bore). **The D-7 did no hull damage to the Remora:** all 5 of its hits were absorbed by the Remora's 14-point forward shield. Its weapon power was only 7-11 of 34-44 on most turns (the Captain-tier anticipation logic raises movement toward the player's LAST-turn move points and takes the power from weapons first) and it never gave its missile tube any power. Separately, since the shield fix the AI spreads its shields evenly, so a 14-point shield is only 2-3 points per face and nearly every hit bled through — flanking is strongly rewarded; the "concentrate shields toward the player" design (flagged in §0.110, NOT built) would change that.
**Still open:** the missile text/damage delay (stage 2) — waiting for the user's word; "three hexes" for gravity wells (built as distance 3 = two empty hexes).

### 0.115 — What changed in v2.57-S168 (miss distance retuned: tight in clear space, wider only with an outside force)

**Trigger:** after several play sessions the user said the maximum miss clearance of 2.33 HR (1.35 hexes) was too much: "with 23rd-century technology a miss could not be so severe ... not unless there's an outside force that could affect it like being in a nebula or some other specific scenario." **Design:** the severity-from-the-die mapping (`missSeverity`, §0.112) is unchanged; what changed is the MAXIMUM clearance it scales to. New constants `MISS_MAX_NORMAL_HR = 0.9` (the worst miss in CLEAR space: about half a hex, 27 px) and `MISS_MAX_ABS_HR = 2.33` (the old maximum, kept only as the ceiling). New `missSpreadFactor(shooter,target,weapon)` multiplies the normal maximum for each outside force the game ALREADY models
(the same conditions that lower the to-hit chance in `terrainToHitPenalty`/`canFireOnTarget`, so every wide miss has a rules reason): **shooter in a nebula x1.6; target in a nebula x1.6; target in an asteroid field x1.4 (beams only); detected CLOAKED target x1.5**; factors stack multiplicatively, capped by `MISS_MAX_ABS_HR`. Clearance = `(0.03 + (maxClear - 0.03) * severity)` HR, +-10% jitter (replaces the old fixed `0.03 + 2.3*severity`). A graze (severity 0) is still 0.03 HR from the real outline. Everything else about the miss (line solved against the real sprite outline, random side, carry-on 1.3-2.7 hexes, no impact flash) is unchanged.
**Resulting worst-roll clearance (HR / hexes):** clear 0.90 / 0.52; one ship in a nebula 1.44 / 0.83; both in a nebula 2.30 / 1.33; asteroid-field target, beams 1.26 / 0.73 (missiles stay 0.90); cloaked target 1.35 / 0.78; nebula both + cloak 2.33 / 1.35 (the ceiling). Clear-space clearance by severity 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1: 0.03 / 0.25 / 0.46 / 0.68 / 0.90 HR. **Verification:** the game's own `computeWeaponAim` on the REAL sprites (Federation I and II, D-4, T-5), 4 ship pairings x 7 environments x every weapon x 5 severities x 12 samples = **18,480 misses: 0 touched the target's hull and 0 fell outside the expected clearance band** for their condition. A line diff shows changes ONLY in the miss section of `computeWeaponAim`, the two new constants and `missSpreadFactor`, and the version/log lines; the AI and ship-data regression is identical.
**Corrections to earlier notes:** a code comment from v2.54-S165 (replaced in this build) and one message said the old worst miss was "about 2 hexes"; it was 1.35 hexes (2.33 HR; neighbouring hex centres are 1.73 HR apart). "0.03 of a hex" should have read 0.03 hex-radii. **Tunable in one place:** `MISS_MAX_NORMAL_HR` (clear-space maximum), the four multipliers in `missSpreadFactor`, and `MISS_MAX_ABS_HR`. **Not verified:** how it looks in the live game; other possible "outside forces" (gravity-well proximity, a damaged ship's own fire control) were NOT added because the game has no existing rule for them.
**Still open:** the missile text/damage delay (stage 2) — waiting for the user's word; "three hexes" for gravity wells (built as distance 3 = two empty hexes).

### 0.114 — What changed in v2.56-S167 (three fixes from the Andor Mk II vs Whitewind cloak log: player cloak penalty, AI cloak-turn shields, weapon destruction "Option A")

**Source:** `combat_log_2026-10-24-23-15-29` (Andor Mk II vs RIS Whitewind, Admiral, build v2.55-S166; the user first sent a duplicate of an earlier L-24 log by mistake, then this one). The user asked for fixes 1 and 2 and chose **Option A** for 3.
**1. The player's shots ignored the cloak to-hit penalty (BUG FIX).** `canFireOnTarget` returns a penalty of +3 (target moved this turn) / +5 (stationary) for a detected cloaked target under Intermediate rules; `resolveShipFiring` (AI) subtracted it from the chart's upper bound, but the player's `fireWeapon` computed `effMax = maxR - terrPen` and never did — while the weapon tooltip (`cloakNote`) promised "CLOAK PENALTY +N". In the log, torpedoes at the detected Whitewind
rolled "need 1-6" at range 5 and "1-7" at range 3 (the raw Chart R values; should have been about 1-3 and 1-4): 6 hits from 8 shots against about 2.8 expected with the penalty. **Fix:** `cloakPen` is now subtracted exactly as in the AI path, the needStr shows it (`1-6 -3 = 1-3`), and a warn line `Firing at a CLOAKED contact — to-hit penalty +N (target moving|stationary)` is logged.
Verified by driving the REAL `fireWeapon` with controlled dice: moving cloaked target needs 1-3 (roll 5 misses, 3 hits), stationary needs 1-1, an uncloaked target keeps the plain chart; the previous build reproduces the bug (roll 5 HIT at "need 1-6"). "Fire All" uses `getWeaponBlockReason` (which contains the cloak/detection gate), so it cannot bypass detection. **Consequence: cloaking is now genuinely harder for the PLAYER to beat — previous balance notes about cloakers were measured without it.** The +3/+5 values are the game's own; the project's rules data has no cloak text, so they are unverified against the rulebook.
**2. The AI wasted power on the turn it cloaked (BUG FIX, Captain/Admiral).** In the Admiral branch weapon power is sized and shields are computed from what is left; `if(cloaking) weapPwr=0` then cancelled the weapons AFTERWARD, so the power vanished (Whitewind, 44 power, cloak upkeep 22: Move 14, Shields 0, **8 unspent**; the log's "Shields 0"), and the first volley hit an unshielded ship. The branch's own comment says excess should flow to shields. **Fix:** after the cloak zeroing, for `D<6`, freed power goes to shields up to `ceil(6*maxShieldPerFace*shieldRatio)`.
**Legend (D6) is deliberately NOT changed:** its "Move-everything / Shields-0 / Weapons-0 while cloaked" is hand-authored from the user's own logs (Pattern 1). Measured old -> new on cloak turns: Whitewind D5 shields 0 -> 8, Gallant Wing 0 -> 4, Stormbird 0 -> 8; Captain, Legend and the Bird of Prey (nothing unspent) unchanged. Non-cloak AI allocations are identical (588 compared, 0 changed).
**3. Weapon destruction now follows the rulebook, "Option A".** Rules (pp.19-20): the destroyed weapon "must be one that could bear on the firer; target's owner picks if several can. If none of that type can bear, the other weapon type is hit; if nothing can bear, damage is halved onto superstructure." The old code destroyed `alive[0]` — the first living weapon of the type in list order (usually the strongest; 59 of 62 multi-beam ships list their strongest beam first) — with no bearing test, so an aft tube died to a frontal shot. **New `pickWeaponLoss(ship,loc,firer)`:**
eligible = living weapons of the wanted type for which `weaponArcCoversTarget(w, damagedShip, firer)` is true; the game picks for the owner the LEAST valuable (`weaponLossValue`: beam = maxPower, missile = fixedDmg; ties keep the first listed); none of that type bears -> the other type (logged: "no beam could bear on the firer — a missile is hit instead"); nothing bears -> `ceil(dmg/2)` onto superstructure (logged). `applyDamage` gained a 5th parameter `firer`; passed from the AI fire path and the player fire path (`shooter`) and the single-face explosion hit (`exploder`); the all-faces explosion passes none (any living weapon is eligible).
**Option C (let the player choose which weapon to lose) was NOT built**; this is the automatic version of "the owner picks". Plasma weapons (type `plasma`, 8 in the registry) are not covered by the beam/missile location, as before. **Verification:** scenarios from the logs — Federation I Mk VI hit from dead ahead loses FH-8 F/P/A, FH-8 F/S/A, then FH-10 Fwd 1 (weakest first; it used to lose both FH-10s); Whitewind hit from the front loses RP-2 Fwd 1, Fwd 2, then falls through to beams while RP-2 Aft survives (it used to lose Aft too); hit from behind it loses RP-2 Aft; a Gagarin hit from astern (nothing bears) loses no weapon and takes half damage on the hull; with no firer the weakest beam goes. **9,900 randomized trials across all 66 ships (random facing, firer position, dead weapons, hit type): 0 violations of the rule** (3,606 normal, 2,441 fallback, 3,853 cascade). The explosion-damage path was run in both branches without error.
**Balance consequences — please re-test:** ships keep their strongest weapons longer; a ship can now be hit "through" a flank it has no guns on without losing guns (it takes half damage on the hull instead); cloakers are harder for the player to hit; Admiral/Captain cloakers are sturdier on their cloak turn. **Verification summary:** `node --check`; headless boot 0 errors; a line diff shows changes ONLY in `fireWeapon` (cloak penalty), `aiAllocatePower` (cloak-turn shields), `applyDamage` + the new `pickWeaponLoss`/`weaponLossValue`, and the three call sites; the 1,056-allocation shield sweep still has 0 negative shields and 0 bad faces; ship-data hash identical. **NOT verified:** a live battle.
**Still open:** the missile text/damage delay (stage 2) — waiting for the user's word; whether "three hexes" for gravity wells meant two or three EMPTY hexes (built as distance 3 = two empty).

### 0.113 — What changed in v2.55-S166 (Damage Control falls back to the ship's own sprite; space-object spacing rules)

**Trigger:** a Chandley Mk III play-test (the attached log is Chandley vs RIS Stormbird Type 5, though the user described a D-7). The user confirmed the dice-based miss effect "works well" and reported (a) the Damage Control tab drew a PROCEDURALLY generated ship even though the game has a top-down image of it — "all of these need to be addressed" — and (b) two spacing rules for space objects.
**1. Damage Control fallback (bug fix).** Measured with the running game: 20 registry ships have dedicated `DMG_VIEW_ART`; **46 of 66 have a top-down map sprite but NO damage-control art**, and `dmgDrawShip` fell through to `drawFedShip/drawRomShip/drawKliShip` for all 46 (every Chandley mark, Federation II, Gagarin, L-24, the Birds of Prey, etc.); no ship has neither. **Fix:** when `getDmgImg(spriteKey)` is null, `dmgDrawShip` now uses `shipImages[spriteKey]` — the same sprite the map draws — CROPPED to its own outline
(`dmgContentBox(key, img, 'spr:', 512)` reads the alpha at up to full resolution, +1% margin so thin nacelle tips are not clipped; the sprite canvas has a transparent margin) and passes the cropped source rectangle to the 9-argument `drawImage`. It is fitted and centred exactly like dedicated art (the fitted rect fills its box, so `dmgPlaceImage` gets the box {0,1,0,1}). **Dedicated damage art, where it exists, still wins**, and the hand-tuned `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE` (D7RSM) is untouched. `dmgContentBox` gained `(imgIn, tag, maxDim)` parameters and a tag-prefixed cache key so sprite and damage-art boxes cannot collide.
**Verification (the game's own `dmgDrawShip`, a recording canvas, the REAL sprite pixels for 8 sprite-only ships + Excelsior as the dedicated-art control):** all 8 draw via the cropped 9-argument path; the crop contains the whole hull and is within 3% of tight; content centre vs ring centre = (0.00, 0.00) U for all 9; every one fits the 32x40-unit box; **0 calls to the procedural drawers**; Excelsior still takes the 5-argument dedicated path and is centred. `damage_view_sprite_fallback.png` shows the result for 8 ships, drawn from the game's computed crop and placement (not a screenshot).
**Known limits:** (i) map sprites are 256 px (some 512), drawn about 2x larger here than on the map, so they look softer than dedicated damage art (Constitution is 283x652); better art can be added per ship via `DMG_VIEW_ART` and it will take over automatically. (ii) `spawnDmgParticles` places damage sparks/smoke at FIXED offsets tuned to the procedural silhouette (e.g. nacelles at `cx +- nacX`), so on any ship with real art — dedicated or sprite — those effects may not sit on the actual hull parts. That was already true for dedicated art and is NOT fixed here.
**2. Space-object spacing (user rules).** Gravity wells ('G' hexes, 0-2 per battle) are laid down in `generateTerrain()`; planets and moons later in `placeCelestials()`, which previously checked only overlap with other celestial bodies and the start lanes — never wells. Measured over 4,000 generated maps BEFORE: **115 moons touched a planet (distance 1)** and **436 well-to-planet/moon distances were under 3, including distance 0 (a well on the same hex as a planet or moon)**.
New in `placeCelestials`: `spacingOK(type,hexes)` — (1) a MOON must be at hex distance >= 2 from every PLANET hex (planets occupy 7 hexes, so this is measured from the nearest planet hex, i.e. at least one empty hex between them; "not adjacent"); (2) every planet and moon hex must be at hex distance >= 3 from every gravity-well hex (so two empty hexes between). Wells carry NO restriction against nebulae (verified: wells still sit directly beside nebulae, 168 of 4,000 maps). Moon-vs-moon and planet-vs-planet are not covered by the user's rules and were left alone.
**Interpretation to confirm with the user:** "three hexes from" was read as hex distance 3 (two empty hexes between); if three EMPTY hexes were meant, change `GRAV_BODY_MIN` to 4. **Verification:** AFTER, 4,000 maps: **0 moon-planet touches, 0 well-body distances under 3**; closest moon-planet gap seen 2; closest well-body distance seen 3; planets appear on 66% of maps (65% before) and 0.90 moons per map (0.89 before), so the rules do not starve placement.
**Verification summary:** `node --check`; headless boot 0 errors; a line diff shows changes ONLY in `placeCelestials` (new spacing), `dmgContentBox` and `dmgDrawShip`; the 588-allocation AI regression and the ship-data hash are IDENTICAL to v2.54-S165. **NOT verified:** how the Damage Control tab and the new map layouts look in the real game.
**Stage 2 (missile text and damage held until impact) is STILL NOT built** — the user said they will give the word.

### 0.112 — What changed in v2.54-S165 (dice-based miss distance; damage-control art centred on its ring)

**Trigger:** a play-test log (Constitution Mk II vs D-7 M at Captain). The user reported the stage-1 miss effect "looks pretty good" (missiles too), suggested making the MISS DISTANCE depend on the die roll, and reported that in the Damage Control tab the top-down ship is not centred in the hex "in any game lately".
**1. Dice-based miss distance (graphics only).** `missSeverity(roll,minR,effMax)` returns 0 (one pip beyond the number needed) .. 1 (the worst roll): steps = pips beyond `effMax` (or below `minR`), severity = (steps-1)/(maxSteps-1). It is passed as a new last argument to `triggerWeaponFX` from BOTH call sites (`resolveShipFiring` for the AI, `fireWeapon` for the player; the roll,
the hit test and the log text are unchanged). In `computeWeaponAim` the miss line is solved so that its closest approach to the target's REAL outline is exactly `gap = (0.03 + 2.3*severity)` hex-radii (+-10% jitter): a graze is ~0.03 of a hex clear of the hull, the worst roll ~2.3 hex-radii clear. New helper `hullExtentAlong(ship,nx,ny)` measures the
outline's reach along the direction from the ship to the line (so a slim ship's near miss is tangent to the real hull, not to a bounding circle, which was the first version and would have let a graze pass visibly wide of a slim ship like the D-4). The line still carries on 1.3-2.7 hexes past the ship. Fallback for sprite-less ships: the bounding-radius estimate.
**Verification (headless, REAL sprites for Federation I/II, D-4, T-5, L-24; the game's own functions):** 8,800 sampled misses (4 scenarios x every weapon x 5 severities x 40): the clearance between the shot and the target's actual hull pixels was min/mean/max 0.027/0.030/0.033 HR at severity 0 .. 2.097/2.335/2.563 HR at severity 1, tracking `gap` in every band; **0 shots touched the hull, 0 failed to carry past the ship.**
**2. Damage-control centring (BUG FIX; confirmed by measurement before changing anything).** `dmgDrawShip` centres the shield ring (rx=18.5U, ry=24.0U, "the hex") on a fixed point but placed the ship art by a fixed rule: top-aligned in a 32x40-unit box, then shifted DOWN 4 units by default. Where the ship landed therefore depended on the art's empty margin. Measured with the real art: Constitution, Excelsior, Federation I, T-5 and D-4 (tall narrow art) sat **4.0 U (8.3% of the ring height) LOW**;
K-22 / D-32 / L-42 (wide art, aspect 1.54, top-aligned) sat **5.6 U HIGH**; D7RSM (hand-tuned override) sat -2.0 U. **Fix:** `dmgContentBox(key)` reads each art's opaque bounding box from its alpha (cached; same canvas approach as the sprite silhouettes) and `dmgPlaceImage` centres that box on the ring centre. **A ship with an entry in `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE` (currently only D7RSM)
keeps its hand-tuned placement EXACTLY as before** (verified: tx=0, ty=-2, x=-10.397, y=-15.4 before and after). Ships whose box cannot be read fall back to the old placement. After the fix all 8 non-override arts measure (0.00, 0.00). `dmg_centering_before_after.png` shows old (red ghost) vs new (solid) for seven ships. **Caveat on "centred":** this centres the art's BOUNDING BOX on the ring. The user's own D7RSM tuning landed 2 U above that,
so their eye may weigh the visual mass (e.g. a heavy saucer) differently; if a ship still looks off, add an entry to `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE` (scale, cxShift, cyShift) as D7RSM has. Also untouched: the FWD/AFT face labels and the box tracks, which are positioned from the same ring constants.
**Verification summary:** `node --check`; headless boot 0 errors; a line diff shows changes ONLY in `computeWeaponAim`/`triggerWeaponFX`/`missSeverity`/`hullExtentAlong`, the two added call arguments, and `dmgDrawShip` plus its new helpers; the 588-allocation AI regression and the ship-data hash are IDENTICAL to v2.53-S164. **NOT verified:** how any of it looks in the real game (canvas frames), and the Damage Control tab is checked from the placement numbers and a drawn diagram, not a screenshot.
**Stage 2 (missile text and damage held until impact) is STILL NOT built** — the user said they will give the word.

### 0.111 — What changed in v2.53-S164 (WEAPON VISUALS, STAGE 1: hull-based emitters, hull-edge impacts, real misses)

**Trigger:** the user noticed (from a Federation I Mk VI vs L-24 log) that (1) beams did not appear to come from the ship model but from points on the hex, (2) a missile's hit/miss text appeared in the log before it reached the target, and (3) every shot looked like a hit.
The user chose to do (1) and (3) first ("stage 1", graphics only) and (2) afterwards, on their word ("stage 2", NOT built yet). **Findings before changing anything:** beams started 0.62 hex out in the direction of the centroid of the weapon's arcs (and `proc`-style beams such as Klingon KD / Romulan RB, and
all torpedoes, started at the hex CENTRE with no offset at all); every projectile ended at the exact centre of the target hex whether it hit or missed; the only hit/miss difference was an explosion vs a shield ripple at that same spot, which read as an impact. The map uses a pointy-top hex layout
where facing 0 = East (the older comment "facing 1=E" in `launchGame` is stale), and sprites are drawn nose-up, rotated by `facing*60deg + 90deg`, as a square of side `2*HR*scale`; the FX code already used the same facing convention, so the geometry was consistent — only the choice of points was wrong.
**What was built (effect code only: the `add*FX` constructors, `drawFX`, and `triggerWeaponFX`; NO change to hit rolls, damage, `resolveShipFiring`, `fireWeapon`, or any log text — confirmed by a line diff):**
`shipSilhouette(key)` reads each sprite's transparency (cached at 128x128; not cached until the image has loaded); `hullEdgePoint(ship, dir, lateral, inset)` ray-casts from the sprite centre along a ship-local direction and returns the farthest opaque point, as a world offset rotated by the ship's facing;
`clampDirToArcs` pulls the bearing to the target into the weapon's own firing arcs (each arc = a 60-degree sector centred on arc*60); `oldMountOffset` is the previous emitter, kept as the fallback for ships with no sprite; `hullRadiusWorld` gives the hull's bounding radius; `computeWeaponAim` returns {emit, tOff, impact, pathHexes}.
**Emitter:** on the shooter's hull edge on the side facing the target, spread across the hull width per weapon (beams `((idx%5)-2)*0.13` of the half-size, torpedoes `((idx%3)-1)*0.10`). **Hit:** the shot ends on the TARGET's hull edge on the side facing the shooter (inset 12% of the half-size, spread `((idx%4)-1.5)*0.12`) and the explosion is drawn there, not at the hex centre.
**Miss:** the shot is aimed at a point BESIDE the ship — `m=(hullRadius+0.12*HR)*1.15 + rand*0.45*HR` perpendicular to the line of fire, random side — and carries on `1.3-2.7` hexes past it (torpedo speed stays ~1 hex per 11 ticks via `pathHexes`); a miss draws NO impact flash and no shield ripple (the `miss` sound still plays from the fire code).
`drawFX` now honours `emitOff`/`tOff` for `beam`, `bluebeam`, `goldpulse`, `torp`, `plasma`, and `off` for `expl`. **Verification (headless, against the REAL sprites for Federation I/II, D-4, T-5 and the L-24 art, using the game's own `computeWeaponAim`):** 44/44 emitter points lie on the shooter's hull boundary; 44/44 hit points lie
on the target's boundary on the shooter-facing side; **2,640/2,640 random misses (60 per weapon) never touch the target's outline and end beyond it**. The first version used a fixed miss distance of 0.95-1.5 hex, which cleared every ship but looked like "nowhere near" for slim ships (the D-4); it was changed to scale with the hull radius. A first hit-impact test was too strict (6px) because impacts are deliberately inset ~7.7px;
the threshold was corrected to match the design, not the design to the test. A diagram of the result drawn from the game's own numbers is `weapon_fx_geometry_check.png`. **NOT verified:** how it looks in the real game — frame-by-frame appearance, beam thickness against the sprites, whether the shield bubble (drawn after the hull) hides the last part of a beam, and the feel of the near-miss distance. Needs the user's eyes.
**Known limits:** the emitter is "farthest opaque pixel along the ray", so on ships with nacelles a beam can leave from a nacelle tip; this is an approximation of true hardpoints (per-ship hardpoint data would be better but is 66 ships of work). **Stage 2 (NOT built):** defer the missile roll-reveal, log lines, damage and sidebar updates until the torpedo arrives — needs a pending-projectile counter so a phase cannot end while a missile is in flight, changes in BOTH `resolveShipFiring` (AI) and `fireWeapon`/`fireAllWeapons` (player), and handling a ship that dies to an earlier missile before a later one lands. The existing `onArrive` hook is the natural attachment point.

### 0.110 — What changed in v2.52-S163 (AI SHIELD BUG fixed: the Captain/Admiral/Legend AI entered battle with an empty or NEGATIVE forward shield; plus a cloak over-allocation bug)

**Trigger:** the user supplied two combat logs (Federation I Mk I vs D-7 M at Captain; Constitution Mk II vs L-42 at Admiral) and asked whether the enemy forward shield failing looked like a bug. In BOTH logs the enemy's very first
hit on its forward face had no "shield absorbs" line — it went straight to a location roll (and both rolled "shield generator", which is just the 10% roll, made likely because every first hit penetrated fully and so got a location roll at all).
**Bug 1 (real, pre-existing, NOT caused by any recent change):** `aiAllocatePower()` (~line 5173, the `if(D>=4)` "concentrate shields toward player" branch) computed `spare = shields - sum(dist)` — shield POWER minus shield POINTS.
Points = power / shieldRatio, so for any ship with `shieldRatio < 1` (56 of 66 registry ships) `spare` was hugely NEGATIVE and was ADDED to face 0, leaving the AI's front shield at zero or below at Captain (D4), Admiral (D5) and Legend (D6).
Reproduced headlessly for log 1: D-7 M, 15 shield power, ratio 0.5 -> distribution **[-10,5,5,5,5,5]** (one tier lower, Lt. Cmdr: a normal [4,4,4,4,4,4]). `resolveHit` absorbs only when `shields[face] > 0`, so a non-positive face absorbs nothing and prints
no absorb line. A sweep of 1,056 allocations (every ship x 2 player ships x 4 tiers x 2 ranges) found **447 with a negative front shield** before. **Fix:** `spare` now uses POINTS (`spts - sum(dist)`, floored at 0).
**IMPORTANT caveat recorded honestly:** with correct units `spare` is only ever > 0 when the per-face cap clipped EVERY face, so face 0 gains nothing — the "boost forward" intent was never a working feature; the AI's D>=4 spread is now simply EVEN (same as D3).
A genuine "concentrate toward the player" (shift points from rear faces to the face toward the player) is a separate design decision and was NOT made. **Bug 2 (found by that sweep, also pre-existing):** a ship that just CLOAKED has the cloak
upkeep deducted from `tot`, but several tier branches size movement from the full budget (e.g. `move=range>5?14:6`), so a cloaked Admiral allocated more than it had and the shortfall appeared as NEGATIVE shield power (Romulan Bird of Prey: 26 power, cloak cost 15,
Move 14, Shields -7; 17 of the 1,056 runs). **Fix:** after `if(cloaking) weapPwr=0`, `shields=max(0,shields)` and any overspend is trimmed from movement. The guard also trimmed 4 of 588 normal allocations: the 22-power Gagarin spending 24 as an AI
(fixed shields 12 + move 12 at Lt. Cmdr; 16 + 7 at Commander+). **Verification:** `node --check`; headless boot, 0 errors; after the fix the same 1,056-allocation sweep has **0 negative front shields, 0 out-of-range faces, 0 negative shield-power allocations**; the log-1 matchup now gives [5,5,5,5,5,5];
588 non-cloak allocations compared old vs new: move/shield/weapon power identical except the 4 Gagarin trims; ship data hash identical. **Balance consequence — please re-test:** the top three tiers are now genuinely tougher (a real forward shield on the face that usually points at you). Every earlier win at Captain+
and every balance note in §0.104 / §0.108 / §0.109 was measured against the weakened AI. Not tested: a live battle, or how the AI feels at the top tiers after the fix.

### 0.109 — What changed in v2.51-S162 (Federation II weapons corrected: the dreadnoughts carry TWO complete beam sets; Federation I re-verified)

**Trigger:** the user explained that the dreadnoughts carry **two separate sets of beam weapons, each with its own specification** (both classes), and asked for every entry of both classes to be re-examined against the original design,
expecting the power-allocation tab to need changes. **What was found:** (a) the *Federation II registry was wrong*, not the UI: it modelled the two beam sets as 3 + 3 entries where the source has **6 + 6** (Mk I: FH-11 x6 "2 f/p, 2 f, 2 f/s" chart Y max 10 + FH-9 x6
"2 f/p/a, 2 f/s/a, 2 a" chart X max 6; Mk II: FH-11 x6 + FH-14 x6 chart T max 12; torpedoes FP-4 x2 forward chart S arm 1 dmg 20), and it gave set 2 the arcs [1,2,3,4,5] (no forward arc). It is now **14 weapons per mark** (6 + 6 beams + 2 tubes, one entry per beam).
Arcs: set 1 keeps the established f/p = [0,5], f = [0], f/s = [0,1]; set 2 uses the user's reading (the same as the Federation I): f/p/a = [0,5,4,3], f/s/a = [0,1,2,3], a = [3]. (Note "port" is read slightly differently in "f/p" [0,5] vs "f/p/a" [0,5,4,3]
— flagged for the user; adjust after play-testing.) Every Federation II weapon type was checked against the game's own tables (FH-11 Y/10, FH-9 X/6, FH-14 T/12, FP-4 S/1/20): all match. (b) **The power-allocation panel needed NO change:** it builds one row per weapon from
`ship.weapons` (`s.weapons.forEach` -> `.wpn-row`, each with its own `MAX n`, arcs and name), so two beam types on one ship works as-is. (c) **Two beam types per ship is NOT unique to the dreadnoughts** — 13 registry ships already carry 2+ distinct beam types
(Excelsior Mk I, L-24, L-9, D-10, D-18 Gull, Whitewind, the Federation II, and now the Federation I marks); the Nova has 20 weapons and the L-24 16, so 14-weapon ships fit. (d) **Weapon ids are unique after `mkShip`** for every registry ship (checked), so arming individual rows
works even with 12 beams of one type. (e) **Federation I re-verified, all six marks, against the user's source tables** (read back from `Federation_I_Dreadnought_Stats.xlsx`): beam types, counts and torpedoes match on every mark — no change needed. **Clarification worth keeping:** the user
mentioned "FH-11 and FH-9" for the Federation I Mk I; those are the **Federation II Mk I**. The Federation I Mk I carries **FL-6 x6 + FL-3 x4**. **Balance note:** the Federation II now fires up to 12 beams instead of 6, so its in-game strength rises substantially; its D/WDF ratings
(exact from the source) were always computed for 12 beams, so matchups should now agree better with the ratings. The earlier balance pairings in §0.104 (e.g. Fed II Mk I vs the L-24) were observed with the HALVED ship — **re-play-test them**. Catalog entries needed no change (they already listed 6 + 6 and all-six
arcs for the Federation II second set). **Verification:** `node --check`; headless jsdom boot 0 errors/warnings; both Federation II marks read back 14 weapons with the expected types/arcs; every registry ship still builds; a SHA-1 over every OTHER ship's registry, ratings, sprite/front/damage art, rosters, SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE and the Federation II's non-weapon stats is IDENTICAL old vs new. Not tested: a live
battle with a 14-weapon ship, or how the 14 rows lay out on a small screen.

User request: the Federation-class dreadnoughts were "playable but not in the recognition database" (that was the Federation II), and the TOS-style **Federation I** (Franz Joseph, *Star Fleet Technical Manual*)
was not in the game at all. **Federation I:** registry `Federation1_MkI`...`MkVI` (fed roster +6), spriteKey `Federation1`, name 'USS Federation' / reg 'NCC-2100' — **identical to the Federation II by the user's choice**; the
`cls` label ('Federation I Mk n' vs 'Federation II Mk n') tells them apart. Stats (supplied by the user from the fasaststcs.com page, a fan STCS conversion — NOT in the project's recognition-manual files):
hull 50, move 5:1, 3x FWC-1 warp @13 = 39, impulse 6/9/8/8/16/16, power 45/48/47/47/55/55 (warp + impulse sums to the listed power on all six), shields ratio 1/2 (1/3 on Mk VI), max 6/14/14/14/14/12.
Beams: bank 1 x6 "2 f, 2 p, 2 s" = FL-6/FH-2/FH-3/FH-9/FH-9/FH-10; bank 2 x4 "1 f/p/a, 1 f/s/a, 1 p/a, 1 s/a" = FL-3/FH-2/FH-2/FH-4/FH-5/FH-8; torpedoes x2 forward = FAC-3/FAC-3/FP-1/FP-1/FP-5/FP-5.
**Every one of the 9 beam types and 3 torpedo types was cross-checked against the game's own weapon tables (chart, max power, damage-modifier ranges, arm cost, damage): all match exactly.**
D/WDF (exact, from the page): 104.5/18, 118.5/20.8, 117.5/48.8, 117.5/54, 122.5/67, 136/79.6 in `SHIP_CE`. **Art:** the user's flat-vector sheet (navy panel, three views; its caption reads "Federation Class Block II
Dreadnought" — probably the artist's label; the user confirmed it is for the Federation I). Top view bow was on the RIGHT -> rotated 90 deg COUNTER-clockwise -> 256px sprite at the house ~67% fill (width 29%, no scale override);
front view 286px native upscaled 1.6x -> 458x299; DMG_VIEW_ART = the top view bow-up at native size (292x684). Cutout used a flood-fill-from-the-border background (so dark parts INSIDE the ship are never mistaken for
background) plus mask smoothing to remove JPEG ringing. **ARC READING (the user's; "we can adjust it if testing shows it doesn't make sense"):** "port" = BOTH port-side arcs [5,4], "starboard" = BOTH starboard-side arcs [1,2],
f = [0], a = [3]. So p = [4,5], s = [1,2], f/p/a = [0,5,4,3], f/s/a = [0,1,2,3], p/a = [5,4,3], s/a = [1,2,3]. Beams are one registry entry PER BEAM (10 per mark: 2 fwd, 2 port, 2 stbd, then the four bank-2 beams),
torpedoes one entry per tube. **Recognition Database:** new catalog entries `fed_Federation` (Mk I-VI; canon default Mk II = 6 built, 'most-produced') and `fed_Federation2` (Mk I, II only — the two marks in the game; the source also lists Mk III and
Mk V, recorded in §0.104 but NOT added; canon default Mk II, 'documented'); role 'Battleship', `page` null (no manual page exists — the UI only reads `fasa.page`), `built` null for the Federation II (source says "Refit");
`SPRITES.fed_Federation`/`fed_Federation2` linked; `VARIANT_KEY_MAP` entries for BOTH so Select-for-battle works on all 8 marks.
**KNOWN ISSUES FOUND (not fixed — need the user's decision):** (1) **Three inconsistent readings of port/starboard arc letters** exist in the registry: older ships read "p/a" as [5,3] and a bare "p" as [5] (the V-30 precedent);
the Nova reads "a/p" as [3,4] (from the user's physical rulebook); the Federation I (this build) reads "p" as BOTH port arcs. The Federation II's second bank, whose source says "2 f/p/a, 2 f/s/a, 2 a", is [1,2,3,4,5] in the registry
(no forward arc) but is listed with all six arcs in the NEW catalog entry — **catalog and registry disagree for the Federation II's second bank** — RESOLVED in v2.51-S162 (§0.109). The rulebook's firing-arc diagram should settle one rule for every ship.
(2) **[RESOLVED in v2.51-S162, §0.109 — it was a real data error, not a modelling choice] Entries per beam vs per bank is inconsistent:** Larson, Remora, the T-5, L-9, D-4 and the Federation I use one entry per BEAM; the Federation II has 6 beam entries for the source's 12 beams (3 FH-11 + 3 FH-9) and some older
ships likewise — the Federation II may be under-armed by half. (3) **Select-for-battle is dead for most ships**: a headless audit found 72 of 88 variant buttons on "Playable" ships did nothing; only the ships in
`VARIANT_KEY_MAP` work (now Constitution, Enterprise, D-7, Romulan Bird of Prey, D-4, and both Federation classes). **Verification:** `node --check`; headless jsdom boot, 0 errors/warnings; all six marks' stats, engine sums,
weapon counts, charts and arcs read back; `mkShip` builds all 8 dreadnought marks; the database UI was driven for both entries (Playable + Sprite live + live sprite + correct variant buttons) and Select-for-battle was clicked on every
variant (8/8 chose the right registry key); a SHA-1 over every OTHER ship's registry, ratings, sprite/front/damage art, rosters and SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE is IDENTICAL old vs new; the catalog differs ONLY by the two added entries.

## 0. MASTER STATE (read first)

**SEPARATE FROM THE GAME FILE — UI/UX MOCKUP EXPLORATION EXISTS, CHECK IT BEFORE**
**REDOING THIS WORK:** a multi-session UI redesign exploration (TOS-era vs. TMP-era bridge
console concepts — power allocation, a hex-grid combat map, a six-arc enemy-bearing radar
plot, damage/subsystem readouts) lives entirely in a separate Claude Artifact, NOT in this
game file, and NEVER touched `SHIP_REGISTRY`/`SHIP_SPRITES`/`CATALOG`/anything else here.
Artifact URL: `https://claude.ai/artifact/BJqhxdvA7gvFzuUdWqo1ZV` (five boards: `TOS.dc.html`,
`Bridge.dc.html`, `Main.dc.html`, and — added 2026-09-23, see §0.66 —
`DamageControl_TOS.dc.html` and `DamageControl_TMP.dc.html`). Two standalone, portable HTML exports of the same design
also exist outside the artifact (self-contained, no platform dependency) — ask the user for
these if picking the work back up. As of this note, the agreed next step there is translating
FASA's own "Master Control Panel" record sheet (four displays: Engineering, Helm, Weapons,
Damage Control — see the FASA rulebook OCR for the real mechanic detail, including a 5-tier
per-system repair-difficulty track and a Stress mechanic not yet represented in the mockup)
into that same visual language, one display at a time. **Damage Control is DONE for both eras
(2026-09-23, §0.66)**; the remaining three displays (Engineering, Helm incl. Stress charts,
Weapons) are not started — Helm was offered as the next step. This is exploratory/approved-as-mockup-
only work — it does not authorize touching this file's actual game systems on its own.

**HARD RULE — READ BEFORE TOUCHING ANY SHIP DATA:** never modify `SHIP_REGISTRY` — no
weapon added, removed, or re-arc'd, no stat changed — unless the user explicitly asks for
that specific change, by name, in that message. This includes when a combat log seems to
show a ship losing badly *because of* a gap in its loadout (e.g. a hull with no aft-arc
weapons getting flanked and gutted). That is not evidence of a bug to patch. Several ships
in this project (Enterprise-class, Constitution-class, confirmed directly against
`SHIP_REGISTRY` — likely others) are built by design with zero aft coverage, matching their
FASA source data; a player exploiting that by maneuvering onto their tail is playing the
matchup correctly, not finding an oversight. **A combat log attached with no other request
is asking the AI opponent to get smarter within the ship it has — never a request to change
the ship.** See §0.58/§0.59 for two builds that correctly drew this line (AI-only fixes,
`aiAllocatePower()`/`aiDoMove()`, ship data untouched and verified untouched afterward) and
treat those as the template for how to respond to this kind of log.

**SOUND PROJECT (owner's goal, 2026-11-06) — READ §0.164 BEFORE TOUCHING ANY SOUND:** replace ALL procedurally generated sounds. Done: 13 embedded clips and 6 ambience recordings (setup, Damage Control hum, and the bridge beds: Federation TOS, Federation TMP, Klingon, Romulan). Still generated: the 10 sounds of `snd()` (phaser, torpedo, explosion, shieldhit, miss, move, phase, tactical, victory, defeat) and 4 ambience systems (Gorn and Orion tactical bed and Power pad, Power tab hum, Damage Control layers); silent: commit and proceed for non-Federation players, and arming for most non-Federation weapons. Do not change a sound in the game unless the owner asks; design it in the tools first, check it is distinct, encode, level by measurement, then hook it in (the standing rule at the top of this file).

**RULESET ROADMAP DECISION (owner, 2026-11-07) — READ §0.168 and the wishlist's "Ruleset roadmap":** the goal is to build the game in its entirety, in stages. The book's Advanced Course (A1), Graduate Course (A19) and Command & Control Course (A20) are official wishlist items, each a separate setting. **"Intermediate" stays exactly as it is, as a PLACEHOLDER for the Advanced Course until Advanced is fully built out; no game change is planned for now.** Graduate is a totally separate setting after that.


## COMBAT LOG LEDGER — every user-submitted combat log, what it found, what changed

**STANDING RULE (added 2026-09-24 after the user rightly asked whether their logs were being
wasted):** every combat log the user submits gets a row here IN THE SAME SESSION — even when no code
changes — with the difficulty tier identified from the log's raw AI power numbers (never assumed),
the finding, and the outcome. The game's AI does NOT learn at runtime (no stored state, no
localStorage); logs only make it smarter when a session turns them into code in `aiAllocatePower()` /
`aiDoMove()` and records it here. Before analysing a new log, READ THIS TABLE and the tier formulas
first, so a tier's deliberate simplicity isn't misreported as a bug. (The 2026-09-24 session failed
this once — it critiqued a Lt. Cmdr log as if the tier should behave like Admiral, and didn't log it
here until the user asked. Don't repeat that.)

**Identify the tier from the log, not the user's memory:** the difficulty slider defaults to Ensign
(`value="2"`) and "New Mission" is a full reload, so it RESETS EVERY GAME (still true at v2.20-S131).
Signatures: Ensign = `Move 8, Shields 10` every turn; Lt. Cmdr = `Shields 12` flat with Move 12 (range
>6) / 6 (close) or 12 when no weapon bears; Captain = shields ≈35% of power; Admiral = range/threat
branches; Legend = hand-authored from this user's own logs; Cadet = random.
