### 0.18 — What changed in v1.71-S82 (user found the original high-res Constitution sheet —
resolved the resolution gap from §0.17, plus a full hull-text relettering pass)

**Directly closes the limitation flagged one build earlier.** The user located and uploaded
`constitution_class_starship___high_resolution_01.jpg` (1069×747, six panels: top-down,
profile, bottom-up, front, a description panel, and aft) — the actual original this ship's
art was always meant to come from. Re-processed the top-down panel fresh (~480×310 before
rotation, versus the 73×172 that v1.70-S81 had been stuck reusing) and used it to replace
both `SHIP_SPRITES.Constitution_NCC1700` and `DMG_VIEW_ART.Constitution_NCC1700`.

**The user then asked to incorporate the other panels too, which surfaced a real question
answered by reading the code, not assumed:** the reserve-file panels (profile, bottom-up,
rear) are the wrong *projection* for the damage-control view specifically — that view needs
a straight top-down, bow-up silhouette, and profile/bottom/rear are different angles
entirely, even though they're the right ship. This was explained to the user directly rather
than silently substituting a different source. The correct top-down panel was used for the
sprite/damage-view replacement above; the other panels were refreshed into the reserve file
instead, since no in-game system currently consumes that projection.

**A full hull-text relettering pass, done properly this time — arc geometry measured from
real pixels, not guessed:** the source sheet's stock art reads "U.S.S. Brindabella" /
"NCC-1861" (confirmed this is the same underlying stock render noted in this file's own
original header comment — not a new/different source ship). For each occurrence:
1. Measured the exact pixel geometry of the old text — arc radius and angular span for
   curved instances (e.g., the top-down saucer text measured at radius ≈114, spanning
   141°–169°), a tight bounding box for the straight nacelle instance — using brightness
   thresholding *and* distance-from-center to isolate letters from the ship's own hull
   detail and rim outline, which share similar brightness and would otherwise get
   swept into the same mask.
2. Removed the old text with OpenCV inpainting (`cv2.INPAINT_TELEA`), constrained tightly
   to the measured region — never a blanket threshold across the whole image.
3. Drew new text — "NCC-1700" and "U.S.S. Constitution" — with DejaVu Sans Condensed Bold.
   Curved instances use a real per-character arc renderer (each glyph individually rotated
   to the tangent angle at its position along the measured arc), not a straight label
   rotated to look approximately right.

**A real mistake made and caught mid-task, worth keeping in the record honestly:** the first
inpaint attempt on the profile view's nacelle text broke the ship's red accent stripe — the
algorithm tried to blend color across a genuine gap in the stripe (where the old text had
always interrupted it) and produced a warped, tapered shape instead of a continuous line.
Caught this by inspecting the result before moving on, rather than shipping it. Fixed by
abandoning inpainting for that specific band and instead directly copying a confirmed-clean,
decoration-free segment of the same stripe from elsewhere on the nacelle, tiling it across
the gap, and only then inpainting the much smaller residual ghosting left above the
reconstructed stripe. A second near-miss on the same view: the first "clean" source patch
chosen for that tiling accidentally included a decorative yellow chevron marking, which
duplicated it further down the hull when tiled — caught by inspecting the result again,
fixed by choosing a genuinely plain patch further along the stripe.

**Bottom-up view has two separate registry instances** (upper and lower on the visible disc,
since the view is from underneath) — both measured and relettered independently. One was
initially rendered reading backwards ("0071-CCN") because the arc's start/end angles were
in the wrong order for that particular instance; caught by inspection, fixed by reversing
the angle direction for that one arc specifically.

**Front view deliberately NOT touched.** Checked its current resolution (345×224) against
the fresh source panel (330×290) — close enough that re-doing it would have been a wash, not
an improvement, and no defect was found on inspection. Re-processing everything just because
a better source arrived would have been scope creep without a clear benefit.

**`Constitution_integration.js` (the reserve file) fully rewritten**, not patched — new
profile/bottom-up/rear images from this same high-res source, replacing the older, lower-
resolution versions that used to live there, with header documentation updated to describe
the actual relettering methodology used (previous versions of this file described relettering
in generic terms; this rewrite documents the specific arc-measurement/inpaint/stripe-rebuild
approach in enough detail that it could be reproduced or debugged later without re-deriving
it from scratch).

**Verified at every step, not just at the end** — this build involved more manual image
manipulation than any single build so far this session, so each stage (mask geometry, inpaint
result, stripe reconstruction, curved-text placement, reading direction) was visually checked
before moving to the next, exactly because two of those checks caught real mistakes (the
broken stripe, the reversed arc) that would otherwise have shipped.

### 0.19 — What changed in v1.72-S83 (two real defects in v1.71-S82's Constitution art,
caught by the user after deployment — should have been caught before shipping)

**Both defects were genuine, and both should honestly have been caught in §0.18's own
verification pass rather than shipped:**

**Defect 1 — warp nacelle aft tips cut off, in both `SHIP_SPRITES.Constitution_NCC1700` and
`DMG_VIEW_ART.Constitution_NCC1700`.** Root cause traced precisely: the very first crop taken
from the source JPEG in §0.18 (`(0, 0, 480, 310)`) was simply too narrow — measured the
source directly and found real nacelle content extending out to x=669, well past the old
crop's x=480 boundary. Re-cropped wide (`(0, 0, 671, 310)`) to include the complete tapered
nacelle caps. This crop boundary is upstream of everything else (inpainting, text, rotation),
so the fix required redoing the full pipeline on the wider image, not just patching the
final output.

**Defect 2 — hull registry text sat too close to the bow.** The user's own description ("if
front is noon, it's approximately at 10 or 11 o'clock") was checked directly rather than
assumed correct: overlaid actual clock-position rays on the deployed v1.71-S82 art and
confirmed by eye that the text really did span roughly 10:30 to nearly 12 o'clock — a
genuinely poor position, sitting almost on top of the bow direction. Shifted the arc's
pre-rotation start/end angles (same radius, same ~28° span, just rotated to a different
part of the rim) and re-verified with the identical clock-overlay method on the corrected
art: text now sits cleanly between 9 and 10 o'clock.

**A verification method tried and abandoned mid-task, worth recording honestly:** first
attempted to quantify both the old and new text positions with an automated pixel-centroid
measurement (median position of dark pixels in a bounding region, converted to an angle).
This gave a plausible-looking but wrong answer — inspecting the actual mask showed it was
dominated by the saucer's curved rim outline and hull shading, not the letters themselves,
because the rim line is a long continuous feature that outweighs the comparatively small
letter strokes in a simple threshold mask. Caught this by visualizing the mask before
trusting the numbers it produced, discarded the automated measurement, and fell back to
the direct clock-overlay comparison instead — which is what's actually behind the "9 to 10
o'clock" and "10:30 to nearly 12" claims here, not a fabricated-sounding precise degree
figure. Worth remembering for any future geometric measurement on this kind of art: a
simple brightness-threshold mask over a region is not automatically clean just because it
excludes obviously-wrong areas — it can still be dominated by *legitimate* nearby structure
(rim lines, panel edges, shading) that isn't the thing being measured, and the only reliable
check is to visualize the mask itself before trusting anything computed from it.

**Both fixes reused the same inpainting mask coordinates from v1.71-S82 without changes** —
the crop only became wider (added area to the right, toward the nacelles), and the region
containing the old "U.S.S. Brindabella / NCC-1861" text did not move, so there was no new
text-removal work required, only new text-*placement* work.

**Not touched, and correctly so:** checked whether `Constitution_integration.js`'s
profile/bottom-up reserve views (refreshed in §0.18 from separate crops with different
boundaries) had the same nacelle-cropping problem. They did not — visually re-inspected both
and confirmed their crops were already wide enough to include full nacelle tips. No
unnecessary rework was done on files that weren't actually broken.
