### 0.21 — What changed in v1.74-S85 (the v1.73-S84 "hexagon icon" mystery solved — it was
never a separate UI element; plus a real, separate D-7 dossier sprite bug)

**The user solved their own mystery from §0.20 and reported back precisely.** The "hexagon
icon extra S" was never a distinct UI component at all — it was the tactical map's F/S/P/A
hex-facing labels (`labelDefs` in the ship-rendering loop, drawn at radius `sz*1.22`,
rotating with `s.facing`) landing visually on top of the ship-name label (drawn at a fixed
screen-space offset, `sy+sz*.9`, that does **not** rotate with facing). Since the arc labels
rotate to show relative Forward/Starboard/Port/Aft based on the ship's actual heading, any one
of the four can end up pointing into the same screen area the name occupies, depending on
which way the ship happens to be facing — and with a long name like "USS Constitution", a
stray "S" or "F" landing mid-word reads exactly like a typo. **This affects every ship, not
just Constitution** — the user explicitly confirmed this and it's obvious once the geometry
is understood: nothing about it was Constitution-specific.

**Fix:** pushed the name label's offset from `0.9x` to `1.55x` hex size. Verified this
actually clears the arc labels' worst-case reach by computing it, not assuming: the arc
labels use `textBaseline='middle'` at radius `1.22x` with a font roughly `0.18x` tall, so
their farthest possible downward extent (a label pointing straight down, in the one facing
where that happens) is about `1.22 + 0.09 = 1.31x`. The new `1.55x` name offset leaves a
genuine `~0.24x` gap, not a coincidental near-miss. This does not address crowding from the
name's own *width* (a very long name could still visually approach an arc label positioned
to its side rather than below it) — only the specific vertical-collision failure mode that
was actually reported.

**Second, unrelated bug found in the same conversation: Klingon D-7 marks M/R/S showed the
older A/C/G art in the ship-database "Recognition File" view**, regardless of which specific
mark was selected. Root cause, confirmed by reading the code rather than guessing: the
Recognition File catalog groups all six D-7 marks (A/C/G/M/R/S) under one entry (`kli_D7`),
and its sprite lookup table (`SPRITES`, a separate, parallel table from the real in-game
`SHIP_SPRITES`) had exactly one image registered per catalog id — `kli_D7: SHIP_SPRITES.D7`
— with no awareness that `SHIP_REGISTRY` assigns A/C/G the `D7` spriteKey but M/R/S the
distinct `D7RSM` spriteKey (confirmed both sprites are genuinely different art — `D7RSM`'s
front view already looks like a proper movie-era refit, more angular with a raised bridge
module, not a placeholder). **Fixed `siloInner()` to resolve through the same
`VARIANT_KEY_MAP` → `SHIP_REGISTRY` → `spriteKey` path the real game uses** for the currently
selected variant, falling back to the old `SPRITES[s.id]` lookup only when no variant-specific
registry entry exists — so this is a general fix for any future multi-sprite catalog entry,
not a D-7-specific patch.

**Two side questions answered directly, no code change needed:**
- **"IKS Devisor" is simply a fixed, hardcoded name** — `SHIP_REGISTRY.D7_A` through `.D7_S`
  (all six D-7 marks) share the literal string `name:'IKS Devisor'`. It is not randomly
  generated or unique per instance; every D-7 the player fights is named this.
- **The D7RSM art already functions as the "K'tinga" viewscreen** the user asked about, even
  though nothing in this file uses that literal name — FASA's own D-7 M/R/S designations are
  the in-universe equivalent of the movie-era refit. No separate "K'tinga" asset exists or is
  needed; `FRONT_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` already is that ship, and was already correct — the dossier
  bug above was the actual problem, not missing art.

### 0.22 — What changed in v1.75-S86 (user supplied the actual K'tinga reference sheet — a
real art inconsistency turned up that §0.21 didn't catch, plus a new "armed tube" glow feature)

**§0.21's claim that `FRONT_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` "was already correct" needs a correction, in the
interest of an honest record.** It was correct in the narrow sense that it depicted the right
*ship* (a proper movie-era refit silhouette, not the classic D-7). What it missed: that asset
was a completely different **art style** — a photorealistic grey 3D render — while every other
piece of this ship's art (the top-down sprite) is a flat green vector illustration. The user
supplied the original reference sheet this session, confirmed the top-down panel matches what's
already live (so that stayed untouched), and supplied a front-on panel in the same vector style
as the top-down. Replaced `FRONT_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` with it — this is a stylistic consistency fix,
not a resolution fix like every previous art correction this session, and it wasn't something
that showed up by comparing resolutions or checking for a wrong-ship mixup — only a direct
side-by-side against the top-down sprite revealed the mismatch.

**New feature, not a bug fix: the forward torpedo/plasma emitter now glows red on the
viewscreen when armed and ready.** Implementation, built to generalize past this one ship:
- `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS` — a lookup keyed by spriteKey, storing the emitter's position as a
  fraction of that ship's own `FRONT_VIEW_ART` image dimensions (measured directly from the
  new art at (0.494, 0.508), radius 0.06 — not guessed), so the glow lands correctly regardless
  of how `vsFitSize()` later scales that image into the viewscreen canvas. Only ships with a
  visible emitter in their front-view art should get an entry; ships without one simply never
  show anything, no special-casing required elsewhere.
- `shipHasArmedFrontTube(s)` — a helper gating the glow on a real condition: an alive, armed,
  not-yet-fired weapon of type `missile` or `plasma` whose `arcs` includes `0` (forward).
  Explicitly does **not** trigger for an armed forward beam (a beam isn't a "tube" and has no
  visual home on this art) or for a torpedo that only covers aft/side arcs.
- Verified with six standalone test cases before shipping (armed-and-ready, unarmed, already
  fired this phase, aft-only arc, forward beam instead of a tube, and a destroyed tube) —
  all six behaved correctly, not just the one obvious "happy path" case.
- Rendered a static mockup of the glow at the measured position before shipping, specifically
  because this is a purely visual feature with no way to verify placement from the code alone —
  confirmed it sits centered on the emitter and doesn't obscure the ship silhouette.
- Currently `D7RSM` is the only entry in `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS`. Adding this effect to another ship
  is exactly one more entry (measure that ship's own emitter position, add it to the lookup) —
  no other code changes needed, since `renderViewscreenInline()` already checks the lookup
  generically for whichever ship is currently the enemy contact.

### 0.23 — What changed in v1.76-S87 (v1.75-S86's shipped glow defaults were wrong per the
user — built a real tuning tool instead of guessing again, then wired in the user's exact
tuned values)

**The user's own verdict on the shipped default: "too diffuse... too big... needs to be
more concentrated with the halo glow more defined."** Rather than adjust the numbers blind a
third time — the same mistake pattern already seen twice this session with the Constitution
hull-text position (§0.18 → §0.19 → §0.20, three corrections before it was actually right) —
built `torpedo_glow_tuner.html`, a standalone tool with live sliders (position, core radius,
halo radius, halo sharpness, intensity, pulse) rendering the exact real K'tinga art with the
exact same gradient math the game uses, plus click-to-reposition and a live code-block output.
Handed this to the user instead of another static mockup, since a static image only answers
"does this one specific set of numbers look right" — a live tool answers the actually useful
question of "what numbers look right" without a fourth round-trip.

**User tuned it and returned exact values**, which needed two things done correctly, not just
copy-pasted:
1. **`TORPEDO_GLOW_POS.D7RSM` reshaped** — the old entry only had a single flat `r` (radius).
   The tuner's richer model (`coreR`, `haloR`, `sharpness`, `intensity`, `pulse`) is what
   actually let the user separate "how big the bright center is" from "how far the halo
   reaches" from "how sharply one becomes the other" — three independently-useful controls
   that a single radius could never express. Any future ship added to this lookup should use
   the same five-field shape, not the old single-`r` one, or it'll silently produce a default
   `undefined` for the new fields and likely draw nothing (`NaN` radius).
2. **The in-game gradient code itself replaced**, not just the lookup values — the render
   function's gradient math had to be swapped for the tuner tool's exact formula (same
   stop positions, same pulse formula using the live `t*6` phase already used elsewhere in
   this function) so that what the user approved in the standalone tool is *precisely* what
   now renders in the actual viewscreen, rather than a hand-reimplemented approximation of it
   that could subtly drift from what was actually tuned and confirmed.

**Verified by rendering the final shipped numbers as a static image before deploying** —
not just confirming the code parses, but confirming the actual pixel result: a tight,
well-defined bright core with a small contained halo, matching what a correctly-tuned result
should look like and clearly tighter than the v1.75-S86 default it replaces.

### 0.24 — What changed in v1.77-S88 (two real defects: jagged front-view edges, and a
destroyed enemy still showing an intact viewscreen portrait forever)

**Defect 1 — `FRONT_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` had visibly jagged, speckled edges.** The user noticed
this directly: the top-down sprite (same reference sheet) looked clean, but the front view
didn't, despite both supposedly going through the same white-background transparency process.
Root cause, found by compositing the actual asset onto the real viewscreen background color
rather than trusting the raw PNG's appearance: the source reference sheet is a **JPEG**, and
JPEG compression produces ringing/mosquito-noise artifacts right at hard color edges — pixels
that are neither pure background-white nor the ship's actual color. The original transparency
threshold (pure brightness, >240) correctly caught clean white background but left this
edge-noise band behind as visible opaque speckle. Fixed with a saturation-aware method
instead: a pixel counts as background if it's both bright AND desaturated (grayish/whitish),
regardless of its exact brightness value — this catches the JPEG ringing that a pure
brightness threshold misses. Followed by a 1px erosion (eats any straggling fringe pixels)
and a small Gaussian feather on the alpha channel (smooth anti-aliased edges instead of a
hard jagged cutoff). Verified detail wasn't lost by checking the full image after
reprocessing, not just the one edge that prompted the fix.

**Defect 2 — a destroyed enemy ship kept showing a fully intact portrait on the viewscreen
forever, even after visibly exploding and vanishing from the tactical map.** Reported
directly by the user right after watching the K'tinga blow up. Root cause: the tactical-map
ship-rendering loop already correctly checks `s.superstructure<=0` and stops drawing a
destroyed hull (this was fixed back when `playDestructionSequence()` was built), but nothing
in `renderViewscreenInline()` — a completely separate render loop — ever checked the same
condition. Fixed generically for every ship, not specific to the K'tinga:
- `playDestructionSequence(ship, onComplete)` now stamps `ship.destructionStartedAt =
  performance.now()` as its very first action, before anything else runs. This exists purely
  so the viewscreen loop (which runs independently and continuously via its own
  `requestAnimationFrame`) can derive its own local elapsed time from this timestamp, without
  being coupled to `playDestructionSequence()`'s own animation timing or callback structure.
- `renderViewscreenInline()` now checks `enemy.superstructure<=0` before doing anything else.
  If destroyed and less than `VS_EXPLOSION_MS` (1100ms) has elapsed since
  `destructionStartedAt`, it plays its own scaled-down flash + growing/fading fireball
  sequence — deliberately **reusing the same preloaded `explosionImages` frames** as the
  tactical-map explosion (not a separate art asset), so both displays show a visually
  consistent detonation rather than two different-looking effects for the same event. The
  tactical map's hex-accurate shockwave lines are intentionally not reproduced here — they
  have no meaning off the hex grid, so this is a simplified version, not a straight copy.
- Once the explosion window elapses, the viewscreen settles into a permanent "◈ CONTACT
  DESTROYED — NO SIGNAL ◈" static state and never reverts to showing the dead ship's portrait
  again, regardless of how long the fight screen stays open afterward.
- Verified the frame-index and fade-alpha math holds across the full 0→1 progress range
  before shipping (frame index never goes out of bounds, alpha reaches exactly 0 at
  completion) — a standalone check, not just "it validated."

**Forward-looking note, not yet built:** the user is now interested in a broader "ship FX"
system — navigation lights, warp nacelle/Bussard collector animation, etc. — generalizing the
pattern established by `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS` + `torpedo_glow_tuner.html` into something that
could drive multiple simultaneous effects per ship. No code exists for this yet; flagged here
so the next session has context on where that conversation left off, rather than starting
cold. A reasonable shape discussed: a per-ship list of effect entries (position, type,
color/timing, and a game-state condition function name) plus a generalized version of the
tuning tool that can add/edit multiple effect points rather than just one.

### 0.25 — What changed in v1.78-S89 (a full playthrough surfaced a real layout bug, a
related sync bug caught while fixing it, and a missing tooltip — plus several bigger asks
deliberately deferred, not ignored)

**Defect 1 — the damage-control panel's AFT label (and sometimes the bottom of the ship
image) was clipped off, invisible.** Reported directly as "aft is not there." Confirmed by
computing the actual layout math by hand before touching any code: `dmgDrawShip()`'s
height-scaling assumed the ship's drawn content (image + face labels) spanned 36 units
top-to-bottom, but the FWD and AFT labels' own coordinates put the true span at about 47
units — a genuine ~30% understatement, not a coincidental tight fit on one unlucky panel
size. Because `#dmg-wrap` has `overflow:hidden`, that understatement meant real content was
silently drawn past the visible bottom edge on a wide range of panel proportions. Fixed by
scaling and centering against the measured true span (`contentH=47.5`, `contentMid=2.955`)
instead of the old guessed numbers. Verified numerically across five different panel
width/height combinations before shipping — the old math overflowed on some of them (up to
~18px past the edge) and the new math held with margin on all five, not just the one that
prompted the report.

**Defect 2 — found while fixing Defect 1, not reported separately:** the damage-particle
system (`spawnDmgParticles`, the sparks/smoke) computed its own *independent* approximation
of this same ship-layout math, using different constants (`31/35`, multiplier `0.984375`)
than `dmgDrawShip`'s real ones (`32/36`, multiplier `1.0125`). One comment in the code even
claimed "U matches dmgDrawShip exactly" — it didn't; the two were only close enough by
coincidence not to look broken. Left unsynced, the Defect 1 fix alone would have introduced
a *new*, more visible bug: sparks and smoke spawning at the old (wrong) position while the
ship image moved to its newly-corrected one. Both locations now use the literal same formula
as `dmgDrawShip`, not two independently-hand-tuned approximations of it.

**Missing feature, not a bug: added a ship-hover tooltip explaining the red damage-tint
circle.** The user saw this directly on a heavily-damaged Constitution and had no way to
find out what it meant — reasonably read as a bug even though the underlying feature
(`drawShipSprite`'s damaged-tint branch, hull below 60%) has existed since well before this
session. Added by extending `showTerrainTip()` (the existing terrain/celestial hover-tooltip
handler, already wired to `#ship-tooltip` and `tac-cv`'s mousemove) to check both ships'
hexes first, before falling through to terrain — hovering any ship now explains its current
hull percentage and, once below 60%, explicitly names the red tint and confirms it's purely
visual (doesn't itself change any stats).

**Several other items from the same feedback round are real requests, not dismissed, but
deliberately not rushed into this build:**
- **Extend the torpedo-glow effect to other Klingon ships with forward tubes** — real work,
  since each ship needs its own emitter position measured against its own front-view art
  (the same process done for D7RSM originally), not just a copy-paste of one entry.
- **Bussard collector dimming when power is critically low** — the user explicitly tied this
  to the "ship FX" system already flagged above as a future dedicated session, not an
  immediate fix.
- **Context-specific damage effects** (smoke/sparks tied to which *specific* system is hit,
  not just overall hull percentage) — worth being precise about what already exists here
  rather than overclaiming a gap: `spawnDmgParticles` already ties nacelle sparks
  specifically to `dmgSystems.engine<40`, so engine damage already produces a different
  visual than shield or weapon damage. What it does *not* do is vary the three main
  hull-breach effects by which specific system is damaged — those trigger off overall
  `dmgPct` and always appear at the same three fixed hull locations regardless of which
  system is actually hit. That's the real gap, and it's naturally the same kind of
  per-condition effect system the "ship FX" idea above is meant to generalize, so it belongs
  in that same future pass rather than a one-off patch here.
- **Shield-arc red marking in the damage-control view, "like on the playing mat"** — this
  already exists in a basic form: `dmgDrawShip`'s face labels turn red with an X-mark when
  `dmgSystems.shields[i]` is dead (see the `faceLabels.forEach` block). Worth confirming with
  the user whether that's sufficient or whether they specifically want a drawn arc/ring
  matching the tactical map's hex-edge shield rendering rather than a colored text label —
  didn't assume which and build the wrong one.
- **"Are transporters powered?" / "life-signs" sensor questions — why do these exist, is
  this RPG-flavored?** Answered directly, not deferred: these are two of the canonical FASA
  tactical-rules "sensor questions" (`Q8`/`Q9` in the existing `SENSOR_QUESTIONS`-style list),
  asked during the Sensors Phase against a locked target — the same mechanism as "how much
  power is available" or "how are the weapons powered." They're part of the base tactical
  ruleset already implemented this session, not something added for or gated behind the
  DESIGN-ONLY "Advanced" tier discussed in §3.3 — that section is about a *separate*,
  not-yet-built decision (new difficulty/complexity tier, surrender house-rule), and these
  questions predate and are unrelated to it. They do carry narrative flavor (crew casualties,
  anticipating a boarding action) simply because the original tabletop rules were written
  that way, not because this project added an RPG layer on top of the tactical combat.

### 0.26 — What changed in v1.79-S90 (two feature additions the user asked for directly,
scoped down from the §0.25 deferral list rather than left there indefinitely)

**Feature 1 — a generic "hot tube" glow on the tactical map for Klingon KP-series torpedoes,
inspired by (not copied 1:1 from) the viewscreen's torpedo glow.** The user was explicit that
a literal 1:1 copy of the viewscreen effect would be "ludicrously too big" at tactical-icon
scale, and asked for it scaled down and applied to *every* Klingon ship carrying a KP-weapon
(KP-1 through KP-6), not just D7RSM. Deliberately built differently from the viewscreen
version rather than reusing its per-ship, per-image-measured `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS` system:

- `shipHasArmedKlingonTube(s)` checks specifically for `w.desig` starting with `"KP"` (the
  Klingon missile-tube family) with a live, armed, unfired, forward-arc weapon — narrower
  than the viewscreen's `shipHasArmedFrontTube()`, which also allows plasma torpedoes, per
  the user's own explicit scoping to just the KP series.
- `drawKlingonTubeGlow(g, s, sz, t)` draws the same gradient *shape* (core/halo/sharpness
  stops) as the viewscreen effect, hand-scaled down, at one fixed position relative to the
  ship's own bow. This works for every Klingon hull with no per-ship art measurement because
  of where it's called from: by the time this runs, the ship-rendering loop has already done
  `g.translate(sx,sy); g.rotate(s.facing*Math.PI/3+Math.PI/2)`, so every ship is drawn
  "nose-up" in a consistent local space regardless of its actual facing on the map. A fixed
  bow-relative position in that space is automatically correct for any ship, without needing
  the viewscreen's approach of measuring each ship's own art individually.
- Verified the KP-detection logic against five cases (armed KP forward, armed plasma
  specifically excluded, non-Klingon faction excluded, destroyed tube, aft-only arc) before
  wiring it in, and rendered a proportional mockup at a realistic icon size to confirm it
  reads as a small accent, not an oversized blob, before shipping.

**Feature 2 — an actual drawn shield arc in the damage-control view, matching the tactical
map's convention, replacing the previous text-label-only indicator.** The user specifically
asked for "an actual drawn arc like the tactical map has," not just confirmation that the
existing red-label-and-X was sufficient. Implementation:

- Projects the tactical map's per-facing hex-edge convention (dead=red, charged=green scaled
  by strength, alive-but-uncharged=white, ±30° span per facing) onto an ellipse sized to this
  ship's own silhouette instead of a hex's uniform 6 sides.
- Positioned using the *exact* angles the existing FWD/F-P/F-S/AFT/A-P/A-S face labels
  already sit at — computed directly from those labels' own coordinates (`-90°, -141.7°,
  -38.3°, 90°, 144.9°, 35.1°`), not a forced uniform hexagon that wouldn't actually match
  this elongated silhouette's real proportions. Each arc segment therefore lines up with its
  corresponding label rather than sitting at an idealized position nearby.
- Required a real data change, not just a rendering one: `dmgSystems` previously only carried
  `shields` as an alive/dead boolean per face (from `s.shieldGenAlive`). Extended it with
  `shieldStrength` (`s.shields`, the actual current points per face) and `maxShieldPerFace`,
  since the tactical map's three-state coloring needs actual shield strength to distinguish
  "charged" from "alive but uncharged," which alive/dead alone can't express.
- Verified with a rendered mockup showing a deliberate mix of all three states (some dead,
  some charged at different strengths, one alive-uncharged) before shipping, confirming the
  hexagonal ring forms correctly and each segment's color/position matches its label.

**Rulebook page reference, requested directly:** the Sensors Phase's nine questions
(including Q8, life-forms status, and Q9, transporter activity) are on **PDF page 27** of
the rulebook — the general automatic sensor-contact information immediately preceding them
starts on page 26, and the numbered Q1–Q9 list itself runs entirely on page 27, confirmed by
locating the page-break markers directly in the rulebook OCR rather than estimating.

### 0.27 — What changed in v1.80-S91 (correcting a real misunderstanding from v1.79-S90,
not refining it)

**The "red glow on Klingon torpedoes" request was misread in §0.26.** The user meant the
fired projectile's own flight animation as it travels across the map — the actual "weapon
animation itself," their words — not the ship-icon "armed and ready" indicator §0.26 built.
Worth stating plainly rather than glossing over: this was a genuine misunderstanding of the
original request, not a follow-up refinement of something already correct.

**Fixed at the actual source, not by adding a parallel system:** `addTorpFX()` — the single
function that already draws every missile-weapon projectile in the game, for every faction —
previously hardcoded one fixed color (`#ffcc44`) for all of them. It now takes an explicit
color parameter (defaulting to that same original color, so nothing else that calls it
changes behavior). `triggerWeaponFX()` computes red specifically when `shooter.faction==='kli'`
**and** the weapon's own `desig` starts with `"KP"` — the same KP-series scoping already
established for the (different) v1.79-S90 feature, so Klingon plasma torpedoes and every
other faction's missiles are correctly unaffected and keep flying their original color.
Verified against four cases (Klingon KP, Klingon plasma, Federation, Gorn) before shipping.

**Deliberately left unresolved, not overlooked:** the v1.79-S90 ship-icon bow glow has not
been removed. The user's correcting message was cut off before saying whether they want it
kept alongside this fix or taken out now that the actual request is understood — flagged
directly rather than guessing at a deletion, since removing a shipped feature on an
assumption is a worse mistake to make twice in a row than asking one direct question.

### 0.28 — What changed in v1.81-S92 (the §0.27 open question answered; a second real gap
found and fixed while addressing it)

**Question from §0.27 answered — the v1.79-S90 tactical-map bow glow is removed.** The user
confirmed directly: they only ever wanted a glow on the K'tinga's viewscreen front-view (the
one hand-tuned via `torpedo_glow_tuner.html`), never a generic indicator on the top-down
tactical icon for any ship. `shipHasArmedKlingonTube()` and `drawKlingonTubeGlow()` are
deleted outright, not just unhooked — there's no reason to carry dead code for a rejected
design direction. The user also noted that if other ships need a *viewscreen* glow like the
K'tinga's, that will be handled case-by-case (measure that ship's own art, tune it with the
same tool) rather than as a generic system — consistent with how the K'tinga's own glow was
built in the first place. **`shipHasArmedFrontTube()` and `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS` — the
viewscreen's own, differently-named and differently-scoped machinery — are untouched** and
still drive the K'tinga's viewscreen glow exactly as before; don't confuse the two on a
future read of this code, the similar names are coincidental (one was inspired by the other,
per §0.26, not derived from it).

**Second, separate gap found and fixed in the same message: the K'tinga's damage-control
panel had no real art at all.** `DMG_VIEW_ART` had no `D7RSM` entry, so this view was
silently falling back to the generic procedural `drawKliShip()` silhouette — confirmed by
checking the actual object's keys directly rather than assuming a fallback existed
elsewhere. **(Correction, v1.82-S93: the claim below that no high-resolution source existed
was wrong — see §0.29. Left here unedited for an honest record of what was actually believed
at the time, not retroactively cleaned up.)** No separate high-resolution source exists for
this ship's top-down view from earlier in the project (it predates this session, and no
wider reference sheet was ever supplied for it the way the Constitution's was). Matching the
exact precedent already established for the three Klingon Bird-of-Prey-hull ships in
v1.70-S81 — use the ship's own live tactical sprite when no higher-resolution source exists,
rather than leaving a procedural mismatch in place — extracted and tight-cropped the
already-embedded `SHIP_SPRITES.D7RSM` sprite itself and added it as `DMG_VIEW_ART.D7RSM`.
Decoded the result straight from the saved file to confirm it before shipping, the same
verification habit used for every art change this session, not just checking that the
object key exists.

### 0.29 — What changed in v1.82-S93 (the K'tinga's new damage-control panel had four real
problems, all found by actually looking closely rather than assuming last build's fix was
complete)

**Correction to §0.28's "no high-resolution source exists" claim — it was wrong.** A crop
from the user's own original K'tinga reference sheet (`new_topdown.png`, 460×430, processed
earlier this session for the front-view work but never used for the top-down since the
already-live tactical sprite matched it) was sitting unused in the same workspace the whole
time. `DMG_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` now uses a properly transparency-processed, bow-up-rotated crop
of that source (408×424) instead of the 110×159 extraction from the already-downscaled
tactical sprite — which is what was actually causing the reported blurriness, not a
resolution limitation with no available fix. Worth remembering: "no higher-res source
exists" is a claim worth actually searching for, not assuming, especially on a project with
this much accumulated intermediate art across sessions.

**Ship image was too large and positioned too low, overflowing the shield-arc envelope.**
Diagnosed by rendering the exact canvas math (image-fitting + arc ellipse) as a Python
mockup rather than reasoning about it abstractly — confirmed the wingtips extended past the
F-P/F-S arcs and the hull sat low and off-center within the hexagon, exactly matching the
user's own description. Fixed with a new `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE` lookup (`{scale, cyShift}` keyed
by spriteKey) applied only to `D7RSM`, not a global change to the image-fitting math —
conventional saucer-and-hull designs (Excelsior, Constitution) already fit the existing
`shipW`/`shipH` assumptions reasonably well, and shrinking every ship's art to accommodate
one unusually wide "batwing" silhouette would have made correctly-fitting ships unnecessarily
small for no reason. Iterated the scale/offset numbers against the rendered mockup rather
than guessing once and shipping it.

**Shield arcs overlapped each other, and the AFT arc was hard to see.** The six face labels
sit between 52° and 73° apart on this elongated hull, not an even 60° — v1.81-S92's fixed
±30°-per-arc span therefore made adjacent arcs overlap wherever two labels sat closer than
60° apart (confirmed exactly matching the reported "Forward arc crosses over forward-port
and forward-starboard") and left visible gaps wherever they sat farther apart. This is also
the most likely explanation for the AFT arc being hard to see — not a separate bug, just the
combination of the overlap/gap pattern plus the oversized ship image both landing in the
same area. Fixed by computing each arc's actual boundary as the angular midpoint to its
neighbor on each side (precomputed into a `faceArcBounds` array, index-matched to
`faceAngDeg`) rather than a fixed span from each label's own angle — the six segments now
tile the full circle exactly once, no overlap, no gap, still each centered on its own label.

**`dmgSystems.sensors` was referenced in existing code but never populated — a real,
previously-invisible bug.** The `SYSTEM STATUS TEXT` block already had a
`dmgSystems.sensors<80` check, but since that field was never added to the `dmgSystems`
object, the comparison was always `undefined<80` (false in JS), so a sensors status line
could never appear no matter how badly a ship's sensors were actually damaged. Fixed by
adding `sensors:Math.round(s.sensors)` to the object. Separately, confirmed against the
rulebook (PDF p.11–12) that a dedicated sensors repair-status track is authentically part of
the Damage Control Display's "Systems Repair Status Tracks," alongside the superstructure
track already shown — so added persistent `POWER` and `SENSORS` status bars, styled to match
the existing superstructure box track, replacing power's old behavior of only appearing as
conditional text once damage exceeded 12% (and sensors not appearing at all, per the bug
above).

**Verified as a whole, not just fix-by-fix:** rendered one combined mockup with all four
fixes together — including simulated dead/charged shield states across different faces —
before touching the live game file, to catch any interaction between the fixes (e.g., the
new status bars colliding with the repositioned ship image) that checking each in isolation
could have missed.

### 0.30 — What changed in v1.83-S94 (v1.82-S93 shipped a reversed ship, and one root cause
that looked like three separate bugs)

**The ship was reversed — bow pointing toward the AFT arc — a real mistake, not a matter of
taste.** Root cause: on a D-7/K'tinga hull the small "head" section is the bow and the wide
wing-spread is the aft engineering section, the *opposite* of a Starfleet saucer-forward
layout — and v1.82-S93's rotation was chosen assuming the wrong end was the bow, by analogy
to how the Constitution's art had been handled. Caught and fixed by checking against a
ground truth that already existed rather than re-guessing: the already-live, already-correct
`SHIP_SPRITES.D7RSM` tactical sprite shows the small tip at the top (bow), confirming the
source crop's bow was on the *right* side, not the left — so the correct rotation is +90°
(counterclockwise), not the −90° used before.

**The same message's other two complaints — "boom and command pod cut off" and "power/
sensors/superstructure overlapping" — turned out to be downstream symptoms of this one
mistake, not separate bugs needing separate fixes.** With the ship reversed, its thin bow
section landed at the *bottom* of the display, directly where the new status bars and
superstructure track from v1.82-S93 were also positioned — three unrelated-looking
complaints, one actual cause. Worth remembering when triaging a cluster of visual reports on
the same view: check whether they share a root cause before treating each as independent.

**Re-tuned, not just re-rotated:** the `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE` scale/offset for `D7RSM` was
originally tuned against the *reversed* image, so it needed re-verification against the
corrected orientation too, not just a rotation fix — the visual balance of "thin part on
top, wide part on bottom" is different from what was tuned before. Re-rendered the
scale/position mockup against the corrected art and confirmed the same values (`scale:0.60,
cyShift:-4`) still held up, rather than assuming they would.

**Separately, per direct feedback — "there's plenty of space on the sides of the screen...
not everything needs to be all tightly consolidated" — the `POWER`/`SENSORS` bars were moved
out of the crowded central column entirely.** They're now vertical fill bars in the left and
right side margins, outside the shield-arc ring, rather than stacked in the same narrow band
as the superstructure track. Added a width-based clamp (`Math.max`/`Math.min` against the
panel's actual `W`) so they degrade gracefully inward on a narrower panel instead of running
off-canvas entirely — verified numerically (an unclamped position of screen x=−84 correctly
pulled to x=2 under the clamp) rather than only checking it looked fine at one test size.

### 0.31 — What changed in v1.84-S95 (v1.83-S94 completely broke the damage-control panel —
a real gap in this project's verification process, not just a coding mistake)

**The damage-control panel went from "has real bugs" to "displays nothing at all."** Root
cause: `rx`/`ry` (the shield-arc ellipse radii) were declared with `const` *inside* the
`if(dmgSystems.shields){...}` block, but v1.83-S94's new `POWER`/`SENSORS` side bars — added
in the same build, further down in the function, outside that block — referenced `rx` for
their positioning. `const` is block-scoped, so this was not a rare edge case: it threw
`ReferenceError: rx is not defined` on **every single animation frame**, crashing
`dmgDrawShip()` before it could finish drawing anything. That's the whole explanation for why
the panel was reported as completely blank rather than partially broken — the function never
got past that line.

**This is the important part, worth being direct about: this class of bug cannot be caught
by `check.js`.** That script confirms the file parses as valid JavaScript (via `new
Function(...)`), which a block-scoping mistake like this satisfies perfectly — the code is
syntactically correct, it only fails when that specific line actually *executes* with real
data. `check.js` passing was never a meaningful signal that this build's damage-control
changes actually worked, and citing it as verification in the v1.83-S94 changelog was
misleading, even though it wasn't intended that way at the time.

**Fixed the immediate bug** by hoisting the `rx`/`ry` declaration above the `if` block, so
both the shield-arc drawing and the side bars can see it.

**Built and validated an actual runtime test, not just another visual mockup:** extracted
`dmgDrawShip()` with a mock canvas 2D context (every drawing method as a no-op, including
`createRadialGradient()` returning a real gradient-like stub with `addColorStop`) and
executed it — not just parsed it — against four realistic scenarios (no game active, a
healthy ship, a heavily damaged ship with mixed dead/charged shields and degraded sensors, a
ship with no `DMG_VIEW_ART` entry falling back to the procedural silhouette) across two panel
aspect ratios, eight runs total. Then, as a check on the test itself, ran the *same* harness
against the previous (broken) code first and confirmed it failed with the identical
`"rx is not defined"` error the user actually saw — proof the test would have caught this
before it shipped, not just a plausible-sounding test that happened to pass.

**Going forward: any change to canvas-drawing code involving conditionally-scoped variables
should get an executed runtime test like this one, not just `check.js` and a visual mockup.**
A mockup built in Python (as several previous entries in this log describe) verifies the
*visual result* looks right; it does not exercise the actual JavaScript execution path and
would not have caught a scoping crash like this one, since the Python reimplementation
never shared the buggy code's actual variable scope in the first place. The two techniques
catch different classes of bugs and neither substitutes for the other.

### 0.32 — What changed in v1.85-S96 (three more real problems after v1.84-S95: an ugly
bar design, a positioning fix that still wasn't enough, and a near-miss caught mid-edit)

**Problem 1 — the PWR/SENSORS bars looked like "just a big block of vertical green."**
Rather than guess at a better-looking design, checked the rulebook directly: both the
Engineering Display's Power Tracks and the Damage Control Display's Systems Repair Status
Tracks are explicitly described as rows of boxes crossed off as damage accrues — the exact
same visual language already used for the superstructure track in this same panel. A
continuous fill bar was never the right shape for this UI, regardless of color choices.
Rebuilt both as ten-segment box tracks matching that existing style. Verified with a test
that **records actual `fillRect` calls** rather than only checking for a thrown error —
confirming the number of filled boxes and their color genuinely track the underlying
percentage (tested at 100%, 50%, 10%, and 0%) rather than a bug making it always render as
full regardless of value, which is a distinct failure mode a crash-only test cannot catch.

**Problem 2 — the boom and command pod were still getting cut off near the FWD arc despite
v1.84-S95's fix.** The previous adjustment (`scale:0.60, cyShift:-4`) was checked against
only two panel sizes and turned out not to generalize. This time, made the override
substantially more conservative (`scale:0.50, cyShift:6` — smaller and shifted further
down) and swept the resulting ship-image position across **ten** different panel aspect
ratios, not two, confirming real margin at the top in every case via an executed test rather
than assuming a couple of spot-checks would generalize to whatever proportions the user's
actual browser window produces.

**Problem 3 — an internal near-miss caught before it could become a fourth regression.**
While replacing the old continuous-bar code with the new box-track version, a leftover
fragment of the old code briefly remained, preceded by a stray `return;` statement that
would have exited `dmgDrawShip()` early, skipping the superstructure track and the closing
`g.restore()` call entirely — likely a new, different blank/broken-panel bug, from a
completely different cause than v1.84-S95's. Caught by rereading the actual diff before
testing, not by the test suite catching it afterward. Worth remembering: a large,
multi-fragment `str_replace` on a long function is exactly the kind of edit where a stray
leftover line is easy to miss, and rereading the result is not optional.

**All three fixes verified with both an executed runtime test (crash-safety across four
game-state scenarios and two panel sizes, plus the ten-size sweep above) and a rendered
visual mockup** (confirming the box-tracks fill proportionally with correct colors and the
ship clears the arcs with real margin) before deploying — applying the lesson from
v1.84-S95 throughout this pass rather than trusting `check.js` and a single mockup again.

### 0.33 — What changed in v1.86-S97 (v1.85-S96's scale/position fix still wasn't enough,
and this time the root cause could not be pinned down — recorded honestly rather than
papered over)

**The user's screenshot showed the K'tinga's boom and command pod essentially absent**,
despite v1.85-S96's ten-size sweep having shown comfortable margin in every tested case.
This time, investigated thoroughly *before* touching any code, in this order:
1. Decoded the actual base64 image from the live deployed file directly (not a local copy)
   — confirmed 408×424, full boom and command pod clearly present in the source art itself.
2. Re-read the actual deployed `dmgDrawShip()` code line-by-line against the Python
   simulation used for testing — confirmed an exact match, no discrepancy in the formula.
3. Confirmed `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE`'s lookup key (`'D7RSM'`) genuinely matches this ship's
   `spriteKey` in `SHIP_REGISTRY` (all three D-7 M/R/S entries checked directly).
4. Measured the user's actual screenshot pixel-by-pixel (found the box-track column bounds,
   back-calculated the implied `U` value, and searched for ship-colored pixels in the
   boom's expected column) to characterize the real symptom precisely rather than guess from
   a description.

**None of this turned up an explainable root cause.** The math checks out in isolation; the
user's actual rendered result didn't match what that math predicts. Rather than keep
guessing at a discrepancy that couldn't be located, made the fix unambiguously conservative
instead of precisely tuned: `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE.D7RSM` scale dropped from `0.50` to `0.35`,
`cyShift` increased from `6` to `10` (further down) — trading on-screen size for a much
larger safety margin against whatever unidentified factor is at play.

**Verification this time swept sixteen panel sizes, not two or ten** — including several
extremes (150×180, 1017×735 matching the user's actual screenshot dimensions directly,
600×800, 800×600) — computing the ship image's absolute top and bottom position against
each canvas's real height programmatically and confirming zero overflow in every single
case, a stronger check than the visual-mockup-based verification used in earlier attempts.

**Recorded honestly, not glossed over:** the actual mechanism behind why v1.84-S95 and
v1.85-S96's "verified safe" calculations didn't match the user's real-world result remains
unconfirmed. Possible explanations not yet ruled out: a devicePixelRatio or browser-zoom
interaction not reflected in `cv.width`/`cv.height`; a panel aspect ratio far outside
anything tested; or some other environmental factor specific to the user's actual setup.
If this build's much-more-conservative sizing still doesn't resolve it, the next diagnostic
step should be obtaining the user's actual browser window dimensions (or a zoomed-in
screenshot of just the `#dmg-wrap` element) rather than continuing to estimate panel
proportions from a full-screen capture, which is what every attempt so far has had to do.

### 0.34 — What changed in v1.87-S98 (the actual root cause, finally found — it was never
positioning; plus a new standalone tool built at the user's suggestion)

**The user sent a properly zoomed screenshot (just the damage-control panel, not the full
app window)**, which made pixel-level measurement possible instead of estimation from a
full-screen capture as every prior attempt had been limited to. Measured directly:
- The boom's pixels **are** present exactly where the geometry predicts — rendering at
  roughly 8/255 brightness, effectively invisible against the black background.
- The same region in the full-resolution *source* art (`DMGVIEW_D7RSM_highres_v2.png`,
  decoded straight from the file, not a local copy) is clearly visible at 60–90/255
  brightness.

**This is a canvas image-minification artifact, not a positioning or clipping bug at all.**
`imageSmoothingQuality` was never explicitly set anywhere in this entire file — confirmed by
grepping for it and finding zero matches — meaning every browser's own default minification
quality was being used when scaling the ship image down. A thin, bright detail (the boom)
scaled down significantly with low-quality smoothing can average into near-black. **All
three previous fix attempts (v1.84-S95, v1.85-S96, v1.86-S97) were chasing the wrong theory**
— each shrank the ship further to "fix overflow" that pixel measurement now shows was never
actually happening; shrinking the art repeatedly only made the real problem (a thin detail
minifying poorly) worse, not better. Fixed by explicitly setting
`g.imageSmoothingEnabled = true; g.imageSmoothingQuality = 'high';` at the top of
`dmgDrawShip()`. The live game's `D7RSM` scale/position values were deliberately left
unchanged (still `0.35`/`10` from v1.86-S97) pending the user tuning the new tool below and
reporting back their preferred numbers now that the actual defect is fixed, rather than
guessing a fourth specific value.

**Built `damage_control_designer.html`, a standalone interactive tool, per the user's own
suggestion** that this become the template for every future ship's damage-control layout,
not a one-off fix for this one ship. Live sliders for: ship image scale, vertical offset,
and a smoothing-quality toggle (so the exact defect just fixed can be demonstrated and
compared directly); shield arc radius (rx/ry) and line width; superstructure track box count
and height; PWR/SNS side-track segment count and distance from the arc ring; and full color
control for every element (charged/dead/uncharged shield states, superstructure alive
color), plus one-click Federation/Klingon/Romulan color presets (blue/green/teal
respectively) since this needs to work across factions, not just Klingon hulls. A live code
block at the bottom mirrors the exact constants used in `dmgDrawShip()`/`DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE`,
intended to be copied directly back into the game rather than requiring translation.

**Also includes a repair-mechanic mockup section** (explicitly labeled non-functional —
it doesn't touch real game state), added per the user's request to review the rulebook's
crew/repair rules as a basis. Grounded directly in the rulebook's actual **System Shaken**
rules (not invented): each shaken system is assigned to a specific responsible officer (the
mockup shows Chief Engineer for Superstructure, Science Officer for Sensors, matching the
rulebook's system/officer table), who attempts a percentile **Skill Roll** against their own
skill rating — success if the roll is ≤ their rating — with a rulebook-specified retry
structure (reroll next Firing Phase at a cumulative +5% penalty) noted but not yet modeled
in the mockup's dice logic. This is seed material for the "Advanced" tier repair mechanic
already discussed as DESIGN-ONLY in §3.2 above, not a parallel or competing design — if that
design work resumes, this mockup's officer-assignment/skill-roll structure should inform it
directly, and its visual style is a reasonable starting point for the real UI.

### 0.35 — What changed in v1.88-S99 (the v1.87-S98 tool had two real bugs of its own,
both caught by the user directly; the live game's scale is restored on the strength of the
corrected evidence)

**The user asked directly: "Is there an invisible object that is overlaying the ship?"** Yes
— confirmed by rereading the tool's own render code line-by-line. Two distinct bugs, both in
`damage_control_designer.html`, not in the actual game:

1. **The shield-arc radius sliders (`rx`/`ry`) were used as raw, unscaled pixel values.**
   Their default values (18.5, 24) were chosen to match the original formula's coefficients
   (`SR*1.42`, `SR*1.85`) at `U=1` — i.e., they were meant to be multiplied by `U` before use,
   the same way the correctly-working face labels already do. The render code never did that
   multiplication, so the arcs drew as a tiny, fixed-size hexagon near the ship's center,
   completely disconnected from the correctly-U-scaled labels — visible in the user's
   screenshot as a small red/green hexagon sitting almost exactly on top of where the boom
   should be. This is very likely why the tool's own preview looked broken even independent
   of whatever was happening in the live game.
2. **The superstructure box-height slider was computed but then silently discarded** — the
   actual `drawBoxTrack()` call used a different, hardcoded value instead of the slider's
   result. The "Box height" control did nothing.

Both fixed: `rx`/`ry`/`arcW` now multiply by `U` (matching the labels' own scaling), and
`bH`'s computed value is what actually gets passed to `drawBoxTrack()`.

**Also corrected a real omission, not just a bug:** the user pointed out the tool only had
three factions (fed/kli/rom) when the game has five. Added Gorn and Orion, and while doing
so, read `FACTION_STYLE` directly rather than re-guessing colors for the existing three too
— this caught a real mistake: the first version's Klingon preset used green (matching this
one ship's own hull paint), but the game's actual established Klingon UI accent
(`FACTION_STYLE.kli.accent`) is red/crimson. A ship's paint scheme and its faction's UI color
are two different things and shouldn't have been conflated. All five presets now use the
exact accent colors already live elsewhere in the game, not colors invented for this tool.

**Rendered a corrected mockup with the fixed math**, which showed the K'tinga's boom and
command pod fully clear and visible at `scale:0.60` — meaningfully larger than the `0.35`
left in the live game pending this investigation. Combined with the tool bugs just found
(which plausibly explain why testing looked broken independent of the live game's own
state), this is real evidence the v1.87-S98 `imageSmoothingQuality` fix works correctly at a
reasonable scale. On that basis, **restored `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE.D7RSM` from `0.35`/`10` back to
`0.60`/`-2`** — re-verified with the same 16-panel-size overflow sweep established in
§0.33 (all clear, comfortable positive margin in every single case), rather than assuming
the earlier "conservative and safe" reasoning still applied unchanged now that the actual
defect behind the original complaint is understood and fixed.

### 0.36 — What changed in v1.89-S100 (the ACTUAL root cause, after five straight wrong
guesses — the source image itself was incomplete, nothing to do with rendering at all)

**This is the real fix. §0.34's "found the actual root cause" claim was wrong** — not a
bad-faith claim, `imageSmoothingQuality` is a genuine, independently worthwhile improvement
that's still correctly in place, but it was never going to fix this specific report, because
the reported content (the command pod) was never in the source file to begin with. Five
consecutive builds (v1.84-S95 through v1.88-S99) all guessed at rendering-side causes —
clipping, scale, position, minification — because that was the more interesting technical
theory each time, when the actual answer was far more mundane.

**The user asked the right diagnostic question directly: "did you truly grab the already
validated art that is currently being used on the space map?"** Checked, honestly: no.
`SHIP_SPRITES.D7RSM` (correct on the tactical map) and `DMG_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` (broken) were two
completely different image files — the damage-control one was a separate reprocessing from
the original reference sheet done earlier this session, never validated against the
already-working tactical sprite. Tracing that reprocessing to its origin found the actual
bug: the very first crop taken from the reference JPEG (originally made while extracting the
*front*-view art, then reused for the top-down without rechecking) was bounded at `x=460`.
Overlaying a coordinate grid directly on the source image showed the command pod actually
spans `x=530` to `x=630` — the original crop cut it off before any transparency, rotation, or
scaling work even began. **No amount of scale, position, or smoothing adjustment could ever
have fixed this** — the pixels simply were not in the file.

**Confirmed before accepting this as the answer, not just inferred:** zoomed into the
previous asset's very top pixels and found a hard, flat, abruptly-cut edge with no natural
taper — the visual signature of a crop cut, clearly distinct from what a genuine rendering
or minification artifact would look like. This check should have been the *first* thing
tried across the whole saga, not the sixth.

**Fixed at the actual source:** re-cropped wide from the original reference JPEG
(`(0, 20, 650, 420)`, capturing the complete boom and pod with margin), reprocessed through
the exact same transparency/rotation pipeline already established for this ship, and
confirmed visually — a complete, naturally-terminating command pod with visible internal
(deflector dish) detail, not another abrupt cut. Replaced `DMG_VIEW_ART.D7RSM` in both the
live game and `damage_control_designer.html` with this corrected image. The corrected
image's aspect ratio is meaningfully different from the broken one (0.68 vs 0.96 — taller,
since it now includes the full boom length it was missing before), so the existing
`0.60`/`-2` scale/position values were re-verified against it with the full 16-panel-size
overflow sweep rather than assumed to still be safe — they are, with comfortable margin
in every case, purely by fortunate coincidence rather than by having been tuned for this
specific image.

**Lesson recorded plainly:** when a piece of art is reported as "missing" content rather
than "misaligned" or "wrong color," check whether the content actually exists in the source
file *before* investigating anything about how it's drawn. A rendering pipeline cannot
display pixels that were never captured, and this should be page one of the debugging
checklist for exactly this failure mode, not page six.

### 0.37 — What changed in v1.90-S101 (applied the user's own tuned values from the design
tool; confirmed — not fixed — that the ship-art system was already fully generic; fixed a
real layout bug the user found in the tool itself)

**On "DO NOT JUST RENDER A D-7 K'TINGA FOR ALL FACTIONS" — checked and can show directly this
was never happening.** `getDmgImg(GS.player.spriteKey)` keys off whichever ship the player
actually selected, not a fixed value, and the procedural fallback
(`drawFedShip`/`drawKliShip`/`drawRomShip`, dispatched by `s.faction` at the existing call
site) already handles any ship with no `DMG_VIEW_ART` entry correctly, per-faction. This
wasn't a bug that got fixed — it's confirmation of a design that was already correct,
demonstrated with the actual code rather than just asserted.

**Added real new capability to `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE` to match what `damage_control_designer.html`
now supports:** entries can now include `cxShift` (horizontal offset) and `angleDeg`
(rotation) alongside the existing `scale`/`cyShift` — previously the live game had no way to
apply either, even though tuning them was already possible in the tool. Applied the user's
own exact tuned output for `D7RSM`: `{scale:0.77, cxShift:0, cyShift:-2, angleDeg:0}`
(notably larger than the `0.60` from v1.89-S100 — re-verified against the full 16-panel-size
overflow sweep, still clear in every case). Also applied their refined shield-arc radius
(`rx=SR*1.423`, `ry=SR*1.846`, both essentially unchanged from the previous defaults),
arc line-width baseline (`U*.273`, replacing the old `.5`/`.32` split), and superstructure
box-height factor (`U*.477`, replacing `.68`) — all general layout refinements, not
per-faction or per-ship values, so applied directly to the shared constants.

**Deliberately did NOT make shield-arc charged/dead colors or the superstructure health
color per-faction**, despite the user's tuned tool output including a "Klingon" color
preset. Reasoning: these colors carry *safety meaning* (charged/safe vs. dead/danger), and
the tactical map already uses a fixed green/red convention for exactly this reason — varying
it by faction would mean the same color means different things depending on which ship is
selected, which risks real confusion rather than adding useful flavor. The tool's per-faction
color presets remain useful for previewing *decorative* choices (like a ship class's general
UI accent), but this distinction was preserved rather than collapsed for consistency with
the rest of the game's UI language. If this reasoning turns out to be wrong, it's an easy
policy to reverse — the per-faction color values are already sitting in the tool.

**Fixed a real layout bug in the tool, reported directly:** the superstructure track was
positioned inside the ship-group hexagon at `bY2 = sY + ry` — almost exactly the AFT arc's
own radius — so the box track and the AFT arc line visually crossed each other. Moved
superstructure into the right-side status column entirely, as the first item above Systems
Repair Status, rather than living inside the ship graphic. While making room for it,
increased canvas height and capped a box-height calculation that had been silently scaling
with `U` (which itself scales with canvas size) — a feedback loop where naively increasing
canvas height never actually created slack, since the content grew proportionally too.
**Also caught and fixed a flaw in the verification itself**, not just the layout: an initial
overflow test kept reporting "exactly zero margin" at every canvas height tried, which turned
out to be the test accidentally measuring the full-canvas background fill (which by
definition always equals canvas height) rather than the actual right-panel content. Corrected
the test to exclude that fill before trusting any of its output, and confirmed the real
content fits with substantial genuine margin (~380px), not the previously non-existent
margin the flawed test was reporting.

### 0.38 — What changed in v1.91-S102 (three playtesting reports investigated; one real
bug found in movement validation, two reports confirmed as correct existing behavior via
rulebook and code review, plus a UI fix for reviewing combat logs)

**Report 1 — apparent contradiction: a ship fired successfully despite a planet blocking
sensor lock earlier the same round.** Traced through the actual code rather than assuming
either the sensor check or the firing check was wrong: `canFireOnTarget()` already calls
`losBlocked()` — the *same* function the sensor-lock code uses — evaluated fresh against
current ship positions every time either check runs. In the reported log, the sensor block
happened in Sensors Phase 1 at that round's starting positions; the successful shot happened
in Firing Phase 3, after three movement phases had shifted both ships enough to clear the
line of sight between them. **Not a bug** — both systems already use identical logic and
are consistent with each other; they were just evaluated at genuinely different moments as
the tactical picture changed. Worth documenting precisely since it's easy to misread a log
like this without walking through the phase-by-phase position changes.

**Report 2 — planets, moons, and enemy ships should be impassable to movement.** Checked
the actual rulebook text before assuming this was correct: it explicitly states *"Two or
more starships may occupy the same hex, but they may not fire at one another while they are
in that hex. Ships may neither ram nor collide with one another."* — ship-into-ship movement
is **explicitly allowed** by the rules, not a bug. For planets/moons, the rulebook blocks
weapons fire and sensor line-of-sight through them but never states they block movement —
however, this project's own existing code already goes beyond the rulebook's letter here in
a reasonable way: `reachableHexes()` (the click-to-move system) has always correctly treated
them as impassable via `celBlocked()`. **What was NOT consistent, and is a real, now-fixed
bug:** `playerStep()` — the separate "move forward/reverse one hex" button, a completely
different code path from click-to-move — never called `celBlocked()` at all, letting a ship
step directly into a planet or moon's hex through that specific control. Fixed to match the
behavior `reachableHexes()` already had. Deliberately scoped to celestial bodies only, not
extended to block ship-into-ship movement, since the rulebook explicitly allows that.

**Report 3 — the end-of-combat panel blocks reviewing the scrolled combat log.** Confirmed:
`#eg-panel` can cover up to 78% of the combat-log column's height when shown (victory/defeat,
narrative, stats, New Mission button), directly on top of the scrollable log entries.
Added a minimize toggle (`toggleEgMinimize()`) that collapses the panel down to just its
title bar, letting the log underneath become visible/scrollable again, then restores on a
second click. No drag-repositioning was added — minimize directly solves the stated problem
(reviewing dice rolls that the panel was covering) with much less new interaction surface
than a full drag system would need.

**Combat log review, requested for Legend-tier AI tuning:** worth being direct that none of
the three logs provided show adaptive Legend-tier behavior worth analyzing as such. One
repeats the well-documented "Move 8→2, Shields 10" Ensign-tier fixed formula for its entire
duration; the other two show different but equally static per-round formulas (unchanging
across many turns within each game). This is consistent with the difficulty-reset issue
already tracked elsewhere in this project's notes, not new information — flagged rather than
writing up a Legend-specific tuning analysis that the underlying data doesn't actually
support.

### 0.39 — What changed in v1.92-S103 (a confirmed weapon-arc data bug on three Klingon
ships, found from a user's combat log and their own skepticism about the diagnosis)

**Source:** user-submitted combat log, `combat_log_2026-09-14-11-23-44.txt` (v1.91-S102) — a
Federation dreadnought vs. an Ensign-difficulty IKV Ever-Victorious (L-24 battleship), where
the Klingon ship fired only a handful of times across the whole match. The user's own
observation was sharp on two counts and wrong on none: they noticed the enemy repeatedly
"tried" to fire and failed, and — critically — pushed back directly on an initial claim that
the ship's rulebook stats themselves were the problem, saying *"I find it hard to believe the
Klingons would design a battleship that has such weapons firing limitations."* They were
right to push back.

**What the first pass got wrong:** reading the rulebook's `Beam 1: KD-8 ×8, arcs 4f/p 4f/s`
notation as meaning each individual weapon covers only the narrow diagonal *between* forward
and port (or forward and starboard) — i.e. that compound arcs are more restrictive than a
plain single arc. The rulebook says the opposite, explicitly: *"if the weapon is mounted on
the front of the ship, its Firing Arc will be f, if it can also fire to the starboard (right),
its Firing Arc will be listed as f/s"* (FASA rulebook, Firing Arcs section) — a compound arc
means the weapon **additionally** covers the second named arc, a broader combined arc, not a
narrower one.

**The actual, confirmed bug**, found by reading `StarTrek_TacticalCommand_GAME.html` directly
rather than continuing to reason from the rulebook alone: the *live, playable* IKV
Ever-Victorious's weapon list (search for `L24_EverVictorious`) gave every one of its 8 KD-8
beams and 4 KD-13 beams exactly ONE arc index each (`[5]`, `[1]`, `[4]`, or `[2]`) — never
arc 0 (Forward) on any KD-8, never arc 3 (Aft) on any KD-13. That means this ship's entire
beam armament genuinely could not fire directly ahead or directly astern of itself, at any
facing, for the whole match. This is inconsistent with three independent sources at once:
the rulebook's own definition above; this project's own `CATALOG` reference data for the
same hull (`kli_L24`, which correctly lists KD-8 `arcs:[0,1,5]` and KD-13 `arcs:[2,3,4]` —
full three-arc unions); and this project's own pattern for building other Klingon ships'
quarter-arc mounts elsewhere in the same file (e.g. `kli_K22`'s KD-8 mounts are individually
`[0,5]` and `[0,1]`, always including the pure arc alongside the named quarter). All three
agree with each other and disagree with what `L24_EverVictorious` actually had.

**Fix:** Ever-Victorious's 12 beam mounts now carry two arc indices each, matching the
catalog's known-correct aggregate exactly — F/P mounts `[0,5]`, F/S mounts `[0,1]`, Port-Aft
mounts `[3,4]`, Stbd-Aft mounts `[2,3]`. (Its KP-6 missiles were already correct — pure `[0]`
Forward ×2 and pure `[3]` Aft ×2 — the rulebook's plain "2f 2a" notation for missiles was
never compound, so there was nothing to misinterpret there.)

**Swept the rest of the live roster for the same authoring pattern** rather than fixing only
the reported ship: found it on two more — `D18_Gull`'s KD-5 F/P and F/S mounts, and
`L9_Saber`'s KD-8 and KD-13 F/P and F/S mounts. Both fixed the same way (each now includes
arc 0 alongside its named quarter). Worth being precise about severity, though: on these two
ships the bug was much milder than Ever-Victorious's. Both already carry separate,
dedicated Forward-only mounts alongside their F/P/F/S ones, so their *ship-level aggregate*
arc coverage already matched the catalog even before this fix — a target dead ahead could
still be hit by the dedicated Fwd mounts. Only the *per-weapon* arc data on the F/P/F/S
mounts specifically was incomplete (each should individually be able to bear forward too,
per the rulebook's own definition, and now can). No other ships in the live roster matched
this pattern — checked via `grep` for every single-arc mount whose own label contains F/P,
F/S, Port-Aft, or Stbd-Aft; none remained after the fix.

**Deliberately left UNCHANGED, flagged for whoever next tunes AI difficulty:** the same
combat log's power-allocation signature (`Move 8, Shields 10`, unchanging every round) is the
literal Ensign (`D===2`) formula in `aiAllocatePower()` — confirmed by reading the function
directly, not inferred. At Ensign, `aiDecideFire()` fires on any armed-and-alive weapon with
no arc check at all (explaining the log's repeated `Enemy=FIRE` followed immediately by every
mount failing its arc check), and the arc-aware re-facing correction already built into
`aiDoMove()` for exactly this symptom (see §3.1 item 3 and its comment citing this same class
of combat log) is scoped to Admiral (`D===5`) only — Ensign's movement just turns toward a
generic "optimal range" heading with no regard for its own arcs. Both read as plausibly
intentional difficulty-tier scaling (a "basic," easier AI is expected to fire less
intelligently) rather than bugs, so neither was touched here. Flagging directly: the
Ever-Victorious fix alone will noticeably improve this ship's firing rate at any difficulty,
but at Ensign specifically, a human should still expect to see occasional declared-but-wasted
fire phases and non-arc-optimized facing — that is current difficulty-tier design, not a
remaining defect, unless a future session decides otherwise.

### 0.40 — What changed in v1.93-S104 (a new, high-quality colorized reference sheet
replaced a placeholder sprite, a viewscreen art gap was filled, and a fourth ship turned
out to have the same arc-data bug fixed in v1.92-S103)

**Source:** user-supplied `L24_and_T5_Klingon_colorized_3views.jfif` — a professionally
colorized three-view reference sheet (profile, top-down with front-to-left, front-on) for
the same L-24/T-5 hull the earlier line-art schematic covered. The user's own framing note
("the front view is good for use as a screen/monitor view during the game") turned out to
point at a real, already-built feature (`FRONT_VIEW_ART`, the viewscreen art table) that
this ship pair had simply never had an entry in.

**Sprite replaced.** `SHIP_SPRITES.T5_ThroneSeeker` — shared by both `T5_ThroneSeeker` and
`L24_EverVictorious` via `spriteKey` — was, on inspection, a rough 256×256 placeholder of a
visibly different ship design, not art for this hull at all. Replaced with the top-down
panel from the new reference sheet. Two real technical problems had to be solved to do this
correctly, not just cosmetic cropping:

1. **The source file has no usable transparency.** `.jfif` (JPEG File Interchange Format)
   cannot store an alpha channel at all — the checkerboard pattern that *looks* like
   Photoshop's transparency indicator is actually baked into the pixel data as literal
   grey/white squares. Naive "keep everything, it's already transparent" would have shipped
   an opaque checkerboard box around the ship. Detected it instead via an achromatic
   (low-saturation) + brightness test, with a border-connectivity pass (a small morphological
   closing first, `border_value=1`, to survive JPEG noise breaking the connection right at
   the image edge) to distinguish true outer background from any coincidentally
   grey/neutral-toned ship parts (this hull's warp-nacelle bodies and console housings are
   genuinely dark grey, so a cruder color-key would have punched holes in them).
2. **Orientation.** This file's `drawShipSprite()` already carries its own comment stating
   the expected convention precisely: *"The image is drawn nose-up in local space."* The
   reference sheet's top-down panel is drawn nose-**left** (per the user's own framing), so
   the isolated ship was rotated 90° before being squared off and resized to 512×512.

**Viewscreen art added.** New `FRONT_VIEW_ART.T5_ThroneSeeker` entry (also shared by
`L24_EverVictorious`), built from the same sheet's front-view panel via the same
checkerboard-removal process, cropped to its natural aspect ratio rather than forced square
(`vsFitSize()` already fits arbitrary aspect ratios into the viewscreen canvas, so no
padding was needed here the way the square sprite needed it).

**A fourth ship had the v1.92-S103 arc bug.** While reading `T5_ThroneSeeker`'s weapon list
to confirm — per the user's request — that it was actually playable before considering
whether to build it from recognition-manual data, found it already was: full stats, 6
weapons, already present in the live `kli` roster. It was not, however, correctly armed.
Its two KD-1 Fwd-Port mounts and two KD-1 Fwd-Stbd mounts each carried only their single
named quarter-arc (`[5]` and `[1]`), with **no dedicated Forward mount** to compensate —
unlike D-18 Gull and L-9 Saber in v1.92-S103, which had the same per-weapon gap but stayed
ship-level-correct because they each have separate Fwd-only mounts. T-5 has none, so this
was the same *total* forward blind spot Ever-Victorious had. Fixed identically: Fwd-Port
mounts now `[0,5]`, Fwd-Stbd mounts now `[0,1]`, matching `kli_T5`'s own catalog arcs
`[0,1,3,5]` exactly. Swept the rest of the live roster again afterward (see §0.39's method)
— no further instances found.

**Deliberately left undone:** `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS` has no entry for this ship pair.
`L24_EverVictorious` has forward-arc KP-6 missiles that would now qualify for the viewscreen
glow effect (see `shipHasArmedFrontTube()`), but this file already has a dedicated
calibration tool for this exact purpose (`torpedo_glow_tuner.html` — see the existing
`D7RSM` entry's comment, v1.75-S86) specifically because guessed coordinates read as
"too big and too diffuse" the one time this project tried that. Whoever adds this next
should use that tool against the actual new art, not estimate a position from the source
sheet by eye.

### 0.41 — What changed in v1.94-S105 and v1.95-S106 (sprite overflow fix plus a
centering bug caught in the process; individual hull names decided for later)

**v1.94-S105 — sprite overflow.** User reported the new `T5_ThroneSeeker` sprite (shipped
in v1.93-S104) extended past its hex on the tactical map, with a screenshot showing the
nose and flared nacelles bleeding into neighboring hexes. Measured it directly rather than
guess: the ship's nose-to-tail content fills 98.6% of its own 512×512 canvas, so at the
shared `sz*2` draw diameter every ship uses, the flared nacelles pushed past the hex's side
edges even though the nose alone roughly reached the vertex. Added `SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE`
(a new per-sprite scale-down map) rather than shrinking the shared `sz` constant, which
would have under-sized every other ship's art to fix one sprite. `T5_ThroneSeeker` set to
`0.75`. **Not independently verified against a live render this session** — if that value
still overshoots or undershoots, it's a one-line number to adjust, not a structural fix.

**Real bug caught while making that change:** `drawShipSprite()` drew at a fixed
`-sz, -sz` offset regardless of the diameter actually being drawn — correct only when that
diameter equals `sz*2`. Introducing a smaller, scaled diameter without also correcting the
offset to `-d/2, -d/2` would have shifted the sprite toward the hex's upper-left corner
instead of shrinking it in place around the hex's center. Fixed alongside the scale change.

**v1.95-S106 — individual hull names decided, not yet implemented.** See §3's new backlog
entry for the full decision: the two commissioned L-24 hulls are named **Chargh'wI'**
("The Conqueror") and **Grethor Vann** ("Hell for the Dishonored"), but the live
`L24_EverVictorious` entry stays named after the class ("IKV Ever-Victorious") until
multi-ship support exists to actually field two separately-named hulls. Documented both in
HANDOVER and directly in the ship data's own comment, specifically so this doesn't become
another recovered-fragment incident like §3.2's self-destruct design.

### 0.42 — Investigation only, no code changed (a suspected weapon-ID collision bug,
ruled out; user-shared combat log reviewed for AI-tuning patterns)

**User shared a Constitution-vs-Throne-Seeker combat log** and asked whether it might be
useful for AI tuning. It didn't surface anything new to fix, but it triggered a real
investigation worth recording so it isn't re-run from scratch later.

**False alarm, fully chased down: does `buildWeapon()`'s shared `.id` (e.g. every FH-11 bank
gets `id:'fh11'` regardless of bank number — `id` is derived from the weapon TYPE string, not
the unique bank name) cause `weapons.find(x=>x.id===wid)` lookups (`fireWeapon()`,
`s.alloc.weapons[w.id]`, the manual-fire button's `onclick`) to always resolve to the first
matching bank, silently breaking every other bank of the same type?** Reproduced this exact
failure in isolation, faithfully extracting and running the real `fireAllWeapons()`/
`fireWeapon()` source in Node — it *does* fail that way if `SHIP_REGISTRY`'s static template
IDs are used as-is. But that's not what actually happens at runtime: `mkShip()` (the function
that turns a static `SHIP_REGISTRY` template into a live `GS.player`/`GS.enemy` instance —
distinct from the templates themselves, and easy to miss if you only read the templates and
`buildWeapon()`) already de-duplicates on the way in:
```
weapons: (()=>{ const _seen={}; return tmpl.weapons.map(w=>{
  let id=w.id;
  if(_seen[id]===undefined){ _seen[id]=0; } else { _seen[id]++; id=w.id+'_'+_seen[id]; }
  return {...w, id, armed:false, poweredWith:0, fired:false, alive:true};
}); })(),
```
So the five live FH-11 banks actually get `fh11`, `fh11_1`, `fh11_2`, `fh11_3`, `fh11_4` —
genuinely unique per instance. Confirmed no bug exists here. If a similar concern comes up
again, check `mkShip()` first, not just the templates.

**Why "KD-1 Aft 2" never appears in that log, or most Throne Seeker logs**: not a bug either.
Ensign's fixed power formula gives this ship `weapPwr=20` of its 38 total, and
`aiAllocatePower()` arms weapons in array order until the budget runs out. T5_ThroneSeeker's
array is `[Fwd-Port 1, Fwd-Port 2, Fwd-Stbd 1, Fwd-Stbd 2, Aft 1, Aft 2]` — with each KD-1
costing enough that only 5 of 6 can be armed, the LAST array entry (Aft 2) is the one that
consistently goes unpowered. Worth flagging for whoever eventually revisits AI power
allocation: because arming is strictly array-order-dependent, this ship's second Aft mount is
functionally dead weight at Ensign difficulty specifically — every reviewed Ensign-tier log
for this ship shows the identical pattern.

**Pattern worth carrying into any future AI-tuning pass**, consistent across every Ensign-tier
log reviewed so far (this one, and the two Ever-Victorious logs in §0.39/§0.41): the AI parks
in roughly one location, never re-faces for arc coverage (that fix is Admiral-only, §0.39),
and fires whatever happens to bear. The player, moving last with a free hand to maneuver, wins
mainly by choosing engagement geometry rather than by superior firepower. This isn't a bug —
Ensign is supposed to be the easy tier — but it's worth having on record as the actual
behavioral signature of "Ensign" if that tier's balance is ever revisited.
