### 0.45 — What changed in v1.98-S109 (real art for the Romulan V8BirdOfPrey, first time; a

black-backdrop/white-canvas removal technique that recurs through §0.50)

User supplied real top-down and front-view art for the Romulan `V8BirdOfPrey` (RIS Talon),
filling the gap confirmed in §0.44. Same general class of problem as the T5/L24 art before it
(§0.40), but inverted: these PNGs had real alpha (uniformly opaque, 255 throughout) with NO
actual transparency encoded — the apparent transparent background was a flat black backdrop
sitting inside a white canvas, baked into the pixels. Removed both via brightness thresholding
(near-black and near-white) plus connected-component analysis, keyed on the LARGEST black blob
specifically so smaller genuinely-dark ship detail wouldn't be stripped out.

**One real, disclosed limitation, not silently absorbed**: the top-down art's thin sensor-boom
line has a tip rendered in a color pixel-identical to the black backdrop (verified by direct
pixel sampling, not assumption) — there is no way to distinguish "line" from "background" at
that exact spot by color alone, so that tip is very slightly shortened in the final sprite.

Replaced `SHIP_SPRITES.V8BirdOfPrey` (rotated 90° to match this file's nose-up convention, same
as T5 before it) and added the missing `FRONT_VIEW_ART.V8BirdOfPrey` entry. Also checked
proactively this time rather than waiting for a bug report: the new sprite's content fills
97.6% of its own canvas width, essentially the same overflow risk T5_ThroneSeeker had (§0.41) —
added `SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE.V8BirdOfPrey = 0.72` up front.

**This build's brightness-thresholding technique is the direct ancestor of a real bug that
took until §0.50 to actually fix** — see that section before reusing this exact method on a
similarly-sourced black-backdrop/white-canvas image.

### 0.46 — What changed in v1.99-S110 (V8BirdOfPrey's ship-select preview pointed the wrong

way — a genuine convention mismatch, resolved empirically)

User reported the new `V8BirdOfPrey` sprite (§0.45) did not point the same direction as other
ships in the player/enemy ship-select preview. Confirmed by reading `updateShipPreview()`
directly: it renders `SHIP_SPRITES[spriteKey]` raw with zero rotation, so this preview shows a
sprite's stored orientation exactly as authored — unlike the tactical map, which rotates a
sprite per live facing.

Extracted and compared the actual stored `Constitution_NCC1700` sprite directly rather than
assume a convention: its saucer sits at the absolute top edge of the frame, nacelles trailing
down. The Bird of Prey sprite from §0.45 had its main hull mass sitting in the upper-middle with
only a thin sensor line reaching the top edge — a real mismatch, not just a perception issue.
Checked `K22BirdOfPrey` (Klingon) as a second reference point and found it genuinely ambiguous
for bird-shaped, non-saucer hulls (wingtips at top, head/hull drooping down) — did not treat it
as a conclusive convention either way.

**Resolved empirically, not by lore argument**: rotated the `V8BirdOfPrey` sprite a further
180° so its hull mass sits at the top edge like Constitution's saucer does, then rebuilt an
exact replica of the actual 56×56 preview thumbnail (matching the real CSS: `object-fit:contain`,
6px padding) to confirm the fix directly before shipping it, rather than assert correctness from
the full-resolution image alone. `FRONT_VIEW_ART.V8BirdOfPrey` is unaffected — that asset has no
rotation convention to violate, it's only ever shown as a static head-on viewscreen image.

### 0.47 — What changed in v2.00-S111 (a real, confirmed cloak position leak fixed; the

V8BirdOfPrey halo *claimed* fixed here — see §0.50, it wasn't; new cloak/decloak shimmer)

Three things from user screenshots plus a combat log.

1. **A confirmed and fixed position leak** — separate from the ghost-marker code checked, and
   cleared, in §0.44. The firing-phase "highlight enemy hex if targetable" indicator drew
   directly at `GS.enemy.col/row` completely unconditionally, with no cloak check at all — the
   bright green in the user's screenshot matched that code's `eInArc` fill color exactly. Gated
   it with the same cloak-and-undetected condition used elsewhere.
2. **The V8BirdOfPrey front-view white-line artifact (from §0.45/§0.46) — claimed fixed here.**
   Traced (at the time) to pixels around brightness 20-50 falling between the near-black and
   near-white thresholds during background removal, and "rebuilt with a saturation-aware
   threshold that closes that gap." **This did not actually hold** — the user reported the same
   artifact again after this build, and §0.50 found the real cause and the real fix. Don't trust
   this entry's fix as done; §0.50 supersedes it.
3. **New feature**: a cloak/decloak shimmer (expanding ring plus a brief hull sparkle, ~900ms)
   plays for either side, in either direction, from three trigger points — `toggleCloak()` for
   the player, the AI's engage decision in `aiAllocatePower()`, and the automatic decloak every
   cloak underwent at turn end in `endTurn()` at the time (this last trigger point was itself
   removed in §0.48, once decloak stopped being automatic). Purely cosmetic — briefly keeps a
   ship visible so the effect has something to play over, does not change detection or fog-of-
   war logic. Caught and fixed a self-inflicted mistake while wiring this in: an edit briefly
   deleted the `renderTac()` function declaration itself, caught immediately by syntax
   verification before it went any further — a good example of why the syntax-check-before-
   trusting-anything discipline exists.

### 0.48 — What changed in v2.01-S112 (a real rules misread found and fixed via direct rulebook

check — cloak was auto-decloaking every turn, and shouldn't have been)

User reported cloak auto-decloaking every turn, contrary to how they recalled it being designed.
Checked the actual FASA rulebook text directly (p.29-30) rather than assume either side was
right: confirmed a cloak, once activated, **persists turn to turn** until the captain actively
decloaks or fails to keep paying its upkeep — it does not automatically switch off at end of
turn. The previous code did exactly that (`endTurn()` force-reset `s.cloaked=false` every turn
for both sides), silently undoing a chosen sneak-attack posture and forcing a full re-payment of
the cloak cost every single turn just to stay hidden.

Fixed by no longer resetting `s.cloaked` in `endTurn()` — it now only changes via
`toggleCloak()` (player) or the AI's own decision. Restructured `aiAllocatePower()`'s cloak
logic into two genuinely different branches instead of one: already-cloaked now asks "decloak
to strike, or keep paying to stay hidden" (replacing the old anti-perma-cloak probability
penalty, which no longer made sense once staying cloaked stopped requiring a fresh re-engage),
while not-cloaked keeps the original "engage fresh" decision. Also removed a shimmer trigger
call placed in `endTurn()` in §0.47 — with decloak no longer automatic there, that call would
have fired the shimmer every single turn a ship simply remained cloaked, rather than only on a
real transition.

### 0.49 — What changed in v2.02-S113 (the final cloak-effect look, ported from the user's own

design-tool prototype)

Replaced the placeholder cloak shimmer (§0.47) with the exact combination the user landed on via
the standalone `cloak_effect_designer.html` proof-of-concept tool: a dark hull-concealment veil
(500ms) plus three stacked effects — Sparkle Burst (700ms, low intensity), Radar Ping (900ms, 2
rings), and Distortion Ripple (900ms). Ported directly from that tool's own effect renderers,
adapted to this file's hex-based `sx`/`sy`/`sz` coordinates instead of the tool's fixed
`CX`/`CY`/`SHIP_R`.

Also had to fix, in this file, the exact same architectural bug the user caught in the tool
itself: hull visibility can't be nested alpha scaling (this file's own hull-drawing code sets
its own absolute `globalAlpha` for damage tinting, which overwrites rather than multiplies with
anything applied around it) — so "hull reveal" is rendered as an opaque concealment veil over
the ship rather than true transparency. This deliberately reads as "a distortion swallowing the
ship" rather than a plain fade, which is arguably more correct for a cloak anyway.
`triggerCloakFx()` now takes an explicit `mode` (`'engage'`/`'decloak'`) instead of inferring
direction from `ship.cloaked` at draw time, matching the tool's own fix for the same reported
bug (decloak was starting from a fully visible ship instead of a clear one).

**The exact settings JSON this effect was built from** (kept here in case the effect is ever
re-tuned and this specific combination needs to be reproduced or compared against):
```json
{
  "hullReveal": { "delay": 0, "duration": 500 },
  "effects": [
    { "effect": "sparkle", "delay": 0, "duration": 700, "intensity": 25, "color": "#24c3eb", "count": 60, "size": 2.5 },
    { "effect": "radar",   "delay": 0, "duration": 900, "intensity": 80, "color": "#7affe4", "rings": 2, "spacing": 65, "maxRadiusMult": 1.2 },
    { "effect": "ripple",  "delay": 0, "duration": 900, "intensity": 60, "color": "#c0a0ff", "amplitude": 6, "freq": 4 }
  ]
}
```

### 0.50 — What changed in v2.03-S114 (the V8BirdOfPrey halo, ACTUALLY fixed this time — §0.47's

fix didn't hold, and here's why, and how it was verified for real)

The `V8BirdOfPrey` viewscreen white-line artifact, claimed fixed in §0.47 ("saturation-aware
threshold"), was reported **still present** by the user, and confirmed still present by direct
pixel decode of the live file — the earlier fix did not hold, and per this file's own standing
lesson (§0.28, restated at the top of §0), was never independently re-verified by decoding and
viewing the actual shipped bytes after the change. This is the clearest real-world example on
record of why that lesson exists: a fix that sounds specific and technical ("saturation-aware
threshold") shipped without anyone actually looking at the resulting pixels against the real
background color, and it didn't work.

**Root-caused for real this time**: the halo was not the ship's edge at all — it was leftover
anti-aliasing from the ORIGINAL source image's black-backdrop/white-canvas seam (the same class
of source problem §0.45 first encountered). Confirmed by sampling: a band of pixels immediately
outside the ship silhouette carries pure white (255,255,255) color at low-to-mid alpha (2-190),
forming a soft rounded halo shaped like the *source canvas's crop box*, not like the ship. Both
§0.45's and §0.47's brightness thresholds left this transitional band only partially classified.

**Fix**: any `FRONT_VIEW_ART.V8BirdOfPrey` pixel with alpha under 200 is now fully transparent,
and any pixel at or above that is snapped to fully opaque — eliminating the soft halo band
outright rather than re-tuning where its gradient starts (re-tuning the threshold is exactly
what §0.47 tried, and it wasn't enough). **Re-verified by decoding the base64 back out of the
actual shipped file** (not the source PNG used to build it) and compositing it against the real
viewscreen background color (`#050608`) — no visible ring at any zoom level tested.
`SHIP_SPRITES.V8BirdOfPrey` (the top-down tactical sprite) was checked and confirmed clean —
this defect was isolated to the `FRONT_VIEW_ART` entry only.

**If a future ship's art shows a similar soft light-colored ring around it**: check for exactly
this pattern (a band of low-to-mid-alpha pixels near-matching the *original canvas's* color,
not the ship's) before assuming it's a simple background-removal miss — a partial-alpha
gradient needs a hard cutoff, not a better-tuned soft one.

### 0.51 — What changed in v2.04-S115 (IKV Sting Tongue gets real art for the first time — a

hard-alpha extraction method that's now the default for future checkerboard-JPEG sources)

`IKV Sting Tongue` (D-2, `spriteKey D2_StingTongue`) received real reference art for the first
time: user supplied a 3-view colorized sheet (profile/top-down/front elevation stacked in one
image). Only the top-down and front-elevation panels are used by this game — no profile-view
slot exists anywhere in the asset pipeline, and none was added for this.

Source was a flattened JPEG with a baked-in gray/white checkerboard standing in for
transparency (`.jfif`/JPEG has no real alpha channel — unlike the PNG-based art used everywhere
else, including §0.45's black-backdrop source). Extracted each panel via a saturation+brightness
background mask (checkerboard cells are all near-neutral gray, R≈G≈B, brightness 187-255; every
ship pixel tested falls outside that band), producing **hard 0/255 alpha with zero partial-alpha
pixels by construction** — i.e. structurally immune to the soft-halo class of bug just fixed in
§0.50, since there is no gradient band left to mis-threshold. **This hard-mask approach is now
the default method for any future checkerboard-JPEG source** (see §0.52/§0.53 for two more
ships done the same way) — it is simpler than the black-backdrop method in §0.45 and doesn't
carry that method's halo risk at all.

Top-down source had the ship lying nose-left; rotated 90° clockwise to match this game's
universal nose-up sprite convention, then scaled to fit a 512×512 canvas at near-edge-to-edge
fill (505px tall of 512), matching the low-padding convention already used for the other
large/detailed hulls (`T5_ThroneSeeker`, `V8BirdOfPrey`) rather than the more-padded convention
used by the smaller 256×256 sprites. Front-elevation source was already a natural head-on view —
cropped tight with a small (6px) margin, no rotation needed, left at its native aspect (591×158)
rather than forced into another ship's canvas proportions (front-view art sizes already vary
ship-to-ship, spanning 1.5:1 to 7.7:1 across the roster — there is no fixed convention to match).

`SHIP_SPRITES.D2_StingTongue` (previously real but lower-detail placeholder art) was REPLACED;
`FRONT_VIEW_ART.D2_StingTongue` is a NEW entry — this hull had no viewscreen art before, it was
rendering the generic procedural silhouette. Both re-verified by decoding straight out of the
shipped file and compositing against the actual viewscreen background (`#050608`) before calling
this done — the §0.50 discipline, applied from the start this time rather than after a bug
report.

### 0.52 — What changed in v2.05-S116 (IKV Saber gets real art — top-down only, viewscreen still

open)

cleaner**, re-check Baker's superstructure and arc fields against it.

Verified both `buildWeapon('FH-8',...)` and `buildWeapon('FP-2'/'FP-1',...)` resolve against the
existing `FED_PHASERS`/`FED_MISSILES` tables with no "Unknown weapon" console warning before

ships, just never previously referenced by name. Added `'Baker_MkII'`,`'Baker_MkIV'` to the
`fed` roster array; both now selectable in-game. Art re-verified by decoding straight out of the
shipped file, same discipline as §0.50 onward.

**New tool, not tied to any one ship**: `generate_ship_art_master_list.py`. Standing problem it
solves — every prior art-status summary (which ships have real top-down art, which have
viewscreen art, which are still on the procedural fallback) had to be hand-assembled by
re-reading the game file each time, which is exactly the kind of manual bookkeeping that goes
stale the moment anyone forgets to redo it. This script instead parses `SHIP_SPRITES`,
`FRONT_VIEW_ART`, `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS`, the faction roster arrays, and `SHIP_REGISTRY` (handling
both literal weapon objects and `buildWeapon()` calls) directly out of whatever game file it's
pointed at, and emits `Ship_Art_Master_List.html` — a styled, faction-grouped table with each
ship's top-down sprite, viewscreen art (or a "PROCEDURAL FALLBACK" flag), and a TO-ADDRESS
column covering both missing art and un-tuned `TORPEDO_GLOW_POS` entries. **Run this after any
future art or weapon-arc change** — `python3 generate_ship_art_master_list.py
StarTrek_TacticalCommand_GAME.html`. It has no state of its own to go stale; it only reflects
whatever the game file currently contains. See §4 for its listing alongside the other tools.

### 0.56 — What changed in v2.09-S120 (RIS Stormbird's viewscreen, closing the ORIGINAL

three-item list this whole art-fixing thread opened with — plus a new colorization technique)

`RIS Stormbird` (V-11, `spriteKey RomulanStormbird`) received new `FRONT_VIEW_ART`. **This was
the very first asset gap ever raised in this project's ongoing art-completion thread** — "the
front view for the viewscreen of the Romulan Stormbird is not present, it's procedurally
generated" — and the last of the original three-item list (Stormbird front view, the RIS Talon
halo fixed for real in §0.50, and the cloak-effect settings finalized in §0.49) to actually get
closed.

Per explicit user instruction, `SHIP_SPRITES.RomulanStormbird` (the top-down sprite) was **NOT
touched** — verified byte-for-byte identical against the pre-edit file both before and after
this change, not just assumed correct. Source sheet supplied all four standard views plus a
separate faction emblem graphic; only the front-elevation panel was extracted, per instruction
— top-down, profile, and the emblem were all left alone.

**New technique, worth remembering for any future request like it**: the user asked for the new
front view to carry hints of the *existing* top-down sprite's color scheme (a vivid
green-to-purple-to-orange-to-gold-to-green-to-teal-to-blue vertical gradient already baked into
that sprite — sampled directly from it in bands rather than guessed at) without matching its
full vibrancy. Built a per-row gradient matched to the sampled palette, then applied it as an
HSV hue/saturation blend (hue mostly replaced, saturation blended toward a capped target, value/
brightness left almost entirely from the source line art) rather than a flat RGB tint — blending
in RGB space just muddied the source's dark green linework into brown mush on the first attempt.
Tint is skipped entirely for near-black outline pixels and near-white highlights so linework
stays crisp. Tried three strength levels side by side against the actual top-down sprite before
picking the middle one. Re-verified by decoding straight out of the shipped file and compositing
against the real viewscreen background before calling this done.

### 0.57 — What changed in v2.10-S121 (the in-game Recognition Database was found genuinely

stale, not just theoretically driftable — new `--fix-catalog` reconciliation tool)

`generate_ship_art_master_list.py` (§0.53) gained a `--fix-catalog` mode and was run against
this file. The in-game Recognition Database (`CATALOG` array + its `SPRITES` image-lookup
table) is a SEPARATE data structure from `SHIP_REGISTRY`/`SHIP_SPRITES`/`FRONT_VIEW_ART`, with
its own `sprite`/`live`/`ingame` flags per entry, and nothing kept it in sync with the actual
game state. Confirmed genuinely stale on inspection, not just theoretically driftable:

- `fed_Constitution`'s `SPRITES` entry pointed at the known-generic `SHIP_SPRITES.Constitution`
  placeholder (see §0.1/§1) instead of the real `Constitution_NCC1700` art the playable
  Constitution Mk I/II/III ships actually use.
- `fed_Reliant`, `fed_Chandley`, `fed_Baker`, and `kli_D10` were all flagged not-live/
  not-playable in the Recognition Database despite being fully playable with real art.
- `fed_Loknar`'s `CATALOG` flags were already correct, but it was missing from the `SPRITES`
  lookup entirely — so the database would have shown no image for it regardless of what its
  flags claimed.

**Fix**: added a `CATALOG_ID_TO_SPRITEKEY` correspondence table to the generator script (the
one fact that can't be mechanically derived from names alone — Recognition Database ids like
`kli_K22` don't map cleanly to spriteKeys like `K22BirdOfPrey` by string matching) and a
reconciliation pass that verifies each mapped spriteKey actually exists in `SHIP_SPRITES` AND is
actually used by a roster-reachable `SHIP_REGISTRY` entry before trusting it — a wrong or stale
line in that table gets flagged as a warning, not silently believed. Verified sprite/live/ingame
now `True` for exactly the 6 stale entries above (`kli_K23`, a genuine not-yet-built gap,
correctly left untouched) and the `SPRITES` object was fully rebuilt from the verified set.
Replaced the hand-written comment above `SPRITES` (which described it as a manually-audited
block) with one pointing at the script instead, since hand-editing it now just means it gets
silently overwritten — and drifts again — the next time the script runs. Validated with
`node --check` before calling this done; ran the script a second time afterward and confirmed
"already in sync — no changes needed" as a correctness check.

The script now has its own standalone `README_generate_ship_art_master_list.md`, kept alongside
it rather than in this file, since the user keeps this tool in a separate directory from the
game project. See §4 for the tool summary; see that README for full usage, including the
`CATALOG_ID_TO_SPRITEKEY` table and when to add a line to it.

### 0.58 — What changed in v2.11-S122 (a real, previously-deferred AI gap confirmed by direct

evidence and fixed — plus a now-routine sprite-scale correction)

Two things from a user-submitted combat log (D-7 vs Enterprise-class, Captain difficulty,
decisive Klingon win).

**Sprite overflow, confirmed and fixed the routine way**: the Enterprise art added in §0.54
fills 98.2% of its own 512×512 canvas (measured directly), the same overflow class as
`T5_ThroneSeeker` (§0.41, 0.75) and `V8BirdOfPrey` (§0.45, 0.72). Added `SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE.
Enterprise = 0.74`, interpolated between those two known-good values rather than guessed fresh,
since Enterprise's fill ratio sits almost exactly between them. Same disclosed caveat as the
original T5 entry: not independently verified against a live render in this environment — a
one-line number to adjust further if it's still slightly off.

**The real find**: a genuine, previously-flagged-and-deferred AI gap, now confirmed by direct
evidence. `aiDoMove()`'s arc-aware re-facing correction — the logic that checks whether a chosen
heading actually keeps a surviving weapon's arc on the target, not just the right distance/angle
— was scoped to Admiral (`D===5`) only. The §0.39-era build log (v1.92-S103) had already flagged
this exact scoping question as an open item: *"plausibly intentional difficulty-tier scaling
rather than a bug... flagged here for whoever next tunes AI difficulty."* This log is that
evidence. Checked directly against `SHIP_REGISTRY` rather than taken on the user's word alone:
the Enterprise-class genuinely carries **no aft weapons whatsoever** — every mount is arcs
`[0,1,5]` or `[0]`. Once the Klingon reached its aft quarter at close range, Captain-tier
(`D===4`) AI kept choosing facing by pure angle-to-target with no arc verification at all, and
separately, its close-range power formula allocated a flat `move=4` (often converting to just 1
actual move point) — leaving it structurally unable to complete even one re-facing correction
even if it had wanted to. The log shows the Enterprise absorbing unanswered hits to its Aft
shield face for the rest of the match, weapons destroyed one by one, ending in total power
failure.

**Fix**: extended the arc-aware facing correction to `D>=4` (Captain and up — Admiral already
had it), and added a companion check to `aiAllocatePower()`'s `D===4` branch: when no surviving
weapon currently bears on the target at all, movement power is boosted to at least 12 (up from
the flat 4) so the ship actually has the points needed to act on the facing correction, not just
the theoretical logic to want to. Scoped narrowly to the exact condition diagnosed — arc
coverage lost, this tier only; the close-in/back-off branches and every other difficulty tier
are unchanged. Validated with `node --check`; **not independently playtested in this
environment**, per the standing browser-testing limitation — the user's next Captain-difficulty
match against a forward-arc-limited ship is the real test of whether this holds up in play.

### 0.59 — What changed in v2.12-S123 (the v2.11 flanking fix confirmed one tier further down —

plus the standing rule this whole line of fixes needed stated explicitly)

A third combat log (BH-2 vs USS Constitution Mk II) showed the identical failure mode fixed in
§0.58, one difficulty tier lower. Difficulty was identified from the raw power-allocation
numbers themselves, not asserted — a flat `shields=12` and `move=6/12`-by-range are the literal
Lt Cmdr (`D===3`) formula, not Captain's. Confirmed against `SHIP_REGISTRY` (not assumed from
the user's description) that `Constitution_MkII` has the identical structural trait as
Enterprise-class: every weapon is arcs `[0,1,5]` or `[0]`, zero aft coverage. Two distinct
Federation hulls now confirmed built this way — worth treating as a real, intentional trait of
this ship era rather than a gap.

**Fix**: extended both halves of §0.58's remedy down to `D>=3` — `aiDoMove()`'s facing
correction now applies from Lt Cmdr up (was Captain up), and `aiAllocatePower()`'s `D===3`
branch now boosts move to at least 12 when no surviving weapon bears on the target, mirroring
the `D===4` branch exactly. Cadet (`D===1`) and Ensign (`D===2`) remain untouched, consistent
with their own doc comments describing those tiers as intentionally basic/random. Validated
with `node --check`; not independently playtested — now two confirmed difficulty tiers await
real-match confirmation instead of one.

**The line this build was careful to hold, and the user then stated explicitly as a standing
rule** (now at the very top of §0 — read it before touching `SHIP_REGISTRY` for any reason):
`Constitution_MkII`'s and `Enterprise_MkI`'s weapon/arc data were checked and confirmed
byte-identical before and after this change. **A combat log showing a ship losing badly because
of a real gap in its loadout is never, by itself, a request to close that gap.** These ships
have no aft weapons on purpose, matching their FASA source data — a player getting behind one
and winning easily is playing the matchup correctly, not exploiting an oversight. Every fix in
§0.58 and this section touched only `aiAllocatePower()`/`aiDoMove()` — the AI's judgment, never
the hardware it's given. Any future session reading a combat log cold should treat that
distinction as settled, not rediscover it.

### 0.60 — What changed in v2.13-S124 (Orion Wanderer gets real art — a new background type

that broke every prior extraction method, fixed with a flood-fill approach)

`Wanderer` (spriteKey `Wanderer`) received real high-detail art, replacing its previous
real-but-lower-detail sprite. `SHIP_SPRITES.Wanderer` REPLACED; new `FRONT_VIEW_ART.Wanderer`
added (no viewscreen art before, procedural fallback until now).

**A background type that broke every extraction method used so far**: a light graph-paper grid
rather than white, checkerboard, black-backdrop, or navy schematic panel. The grid lines and
large areas of this ship's own silver/gray hull are nearly identical in color and brightness, so
a global color threshold — the method behind every background type up through §0.59 — would
have eaten large chunks of hull along with the grid. Switched to a flood-fill approach instead:
classify a generous, low-saturation/bright-enough band of pixels as background-CANDIDATE, then
keep only the connected regions of that candidate mask that actually touch the image border,
discarding any that don't. Since this art's dark outline strokes fully enclose each hull panel,
background-toned pixels INSIDE the hull are never connected to the border through other
background-toned pixels, so they survive untouched while the true grid/white background — one
continuous region reaching every edge — gets removed in one pass. Zero partial-alpha pixels by
construction. Front was on the LEFT (the more common convention) — rotated 90° clockwise to
nose-up. Fit to a 512×512 canvas at near-edge-to-edge scale. Both re-verified by decoding
straight out of the shipped file before calling this done.

**This completes the Orion faction** — both playable Orion hulls now have real top-down and

### 0.62 — What changed in v2.15-S126 (a genuinely new entity type: the first fixed, deliberately

non-playable station — and a real tool gap this exposed)

**NEW ENTITY TYPE**: Starbase Alamo, a Federation Defense Outpost, added to the Recognition
Database — not another playable ship. Confirmed against FASA source (2003 Combat Data p.66-right;
2302 Federation Ships Data) before building anything: Alamo is real, immobile, moved only by
tugs, 287 positioned. Two marks transcribed directly from source (Mk III: ss 64, pwr 179, FH-3
×12, FP-1 ×6, 161 built; Mk IV: ss 72, pwr 204, FH-9 ×18, FP-4 ×6, 126 built). Both marks' weapon
batteries are explicitly "all-arc" per source prose ("per-arc firing, see the arc diagram p42") —
represented as covering all six arcs, since the `CATALOG` schema has no per-arc-count field and
this entry isn't used for live combat math.

Added `SHIP_SPRITES.AlamoStation` (from the sheet's dorsal plan view, kept in its natural
orientation — a fixed station has no direction of travel to align to a nose-up convention) and
`FRONT_VIEW_ART.AlamoStation` (from the assembled "starstation configuration" view — the open
lattice/truss sections between the station's stacked modules are genuinely transparent in the
source render, and the flood-fill extraction correctly punched alpha through those gaps rather
than treating them as solid; confirmed this is accurate to the source, not an artifact, before
accepting it).

**The real find**: added a new `CATALOG` entry, `fed_Alamo` — `sprite:true`, `live:true`, but
`ingame` DELIBERATELY left `false`, per explicit user instruction ("does not need to be playable
just yet"). This is the first `CATALOG` entry ever added with real art but no corresponding
`SHIP_REGISTRY` entry, and it exposed a real gap in `generate_ship_art_master_list.py`: its
`--fix-catalog` reconciliation required roster-reachability before trusting any id→spriteKey
mapping — correct for playable ships, but it would have permanently warned-and-skipped a
deliberately-non-playable entry forever. **Fixed by adding a second, separate table**,
`CATALOG_ID_TO_SPRITEKEY_NONPLAYABLE`, verified only against `SHIP_SPRITES` existing (no roster
check), which never touches the `ingame` flag in either direction — keeping "playable-ship
reconciliation" and "art-only/non-playable reconciliation" structurally distinct rather than
overloading one table with an exception flag. Ran `--fix-catalog` afterward to wire `fed_Alamo`
into `SPRITES` properly rather than hand-editing that auto-generated block (which would have been
silently overwritten the next run — see that block's own comment).

**If a future session adds another station or scenario-only entity**: use
`CATALOG_ID_TO_SPRITEKEY_NONPLAYABLE`, not `CATALOG_ID_TO_SPRITEKEY` — and only promote an entry
from one table to the other if the user explicitly asks for it to become playable, per the
standing `SHIP_REGISTRY` rule at the top of §0.

### 0.63 — What changed in v2.16-S127 (a second station, R-1 — weaker source data handled

honestly, and a real extraction snag from the station's own geometry)

Second fixed station: R-1 (Federation Orbital Defense Outpost), same non-playable-but-real-art
category established in §0.62. **Weaker source than Alamo**: only one FASA table exists (2003
Combat Data p.66-left, no cleaner parallel entry in the 2302 doc), and several fields are
OCR-flagged uncertain in the project's own reference transcription (superstructure "40(?)",
damage table "C(?)", both weapons' arc notation "f/arc(?)"/"q/arc(?)"). Transcribed as given
rather than guessing a cleaner number, and disclosed here rather than presented with false
confidence: R-1's all-six-arcs representation is the WEAKER of the two stations' arc inferences
— Alamo's source explicitly says "all-arc" in prose, R-1's is just an OCR gap next to "arc" that
could have said anything. Only one variant exists in the source (no multiple marks like Alamo's
III/IV). Added `nick:'Investigator'` from the user's own submitted artwork title ("R-1
Investigator Research Station") — explicitly NOT FASA sourcebook text, and disclosed as such
rather than folded in as if it were.

Source sheet had two profile views (one labeled with leader lines and OCR-garbled callouts
"SANSOR"/"SAUCOR", one clean) plus a top-down at the bottom. Per instruction, used the clean
top-LEFT profile for `FRONT_VIEW_ART` — **a profile/side angle used as the viewscreen image, not
a head-on shot, a first for this pipeline but user-directed, not a mistake** — and the bottom
view for `SHIP_SPRITES`. Same grid-paper background as §0.60/§0.61; reused that flood-fill
extraction.

**A new extraction snag, specific to this station's geometry**: the top-down view's four outer
pods connect to the central hub through thin struts, and at the standard 4-iteration dilation
used everywhere else, those struts didn't reliably bridge — the pods and hub fragmented into
disconnected pieces, which would have extracted only part of the station. Fixed by increasing
dilation to 8 iterations for this component specifically, confirmed empirically (tried 4/8/12/16)
that 8 closes the station's own internal gaps while the sheet's external text labels
(BIO-LAB/GEOLOGY/HULL/HULL) remain correctly separate — 12+ starts merging the labels in too.
**If a future station or ship has thin connecting struts and fragments during extraction, try
this before assuming the flood-fill approach itself doesn't apply — it's a dilation-amount tuning
problem, not a method failure.**

### 0.91 — What changed in v2.39-S150 (hex-overflow/underfill audit — 9 sprites fixed, policy established)

**Trigger:** user played the newly-added Federation II Mk II dreadnought against RIS Nova and
reported two visual complaints in the same message: Federation2's sprite visibly exceeded its hex
boundary, and Nova (a Class XIII battleship) looked too small for its hex given how big the ship
actually is. The user also stated a standing policy: **no ship sprite may exceed its hex boundary
unless explicitly directed to, and any such deliberate exception must be disclosed to the player via
an on-hover tooltip explaining why.**

**Root cause, Federation2:** `SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE` already had three entries (T5_ThroneSeeker,
V8BirdOfPrey, Enterprise) compensating for an older art-batch convention — sprites built on a 512px
canvas with real ship content filling ~96-99% of it, versus this session's own convention of a
256px canvas at 67% fill. Federation2 is from that same older batch (512px canvas, 97.1% fill) but
had never been given a compensating scale — a straightforward oversight, not something the user
had asked for.

**Full audit, not a single patch:** rather than fix only the reported ship, every sprite in
`SHIP_SPRITES` was measured (actual alpha-content bounding box vs. canvas size) and rendered against
a real hex outline to check for overflow. This found **eight more sprites sharing the same uncaught
issue** — L9_Saber, Wanderer, D2_StingTongue, Lightning, Baker (all real playable-ship sprites), plus
RomulanAviary/AlamoStation/Z4Station/R1Station (confirmed via a `spriteKey` grep to be used by ZERO
`SHIP_REGISTRY` entries — orphaned or scenery art, left alone, not in scope). All six real overflow
cases were fixed with measured `SPRITE_SCALE_OVERRIDE` values, each verified against a real hex
outline and, for the tightest case (Federation2 at 0.69), a close-up crop confirming genuine
clearance rather than a near-miss.

**The audit also caught the opposite problem:** K22BirdOfPrey's sprite content fills only ~19.5% of
its canvas (heavy transparent padding from an old extraction), so it rendered as a tiny speck
regardless of scale. Corrected with a large compensating increase (3.4).

**Nova, separately — not a bug.** Nova's own fill ratio (67.2%) exactly matches roughly 30 other
ships built this session; it was never technically broken. Its wide, tapering delta-wing shape just
leaves a lot of empty space inside its own bounding box, so at the standard scale it reads as small
for a Class XIII battleship. Increased to 1.32 (verified with real margin left on all sides). **This
was NOT extended to any other large-class hull** (Excelsior, Gallant Wing, etc.) — the user flagged
one specific ship, and "should bigger FASA classes render bigger by default" is a real design
decision to make deliberately later, not one to sneak in ship-by-ship while fixing something else.

**CORRECTION, same build, no version bump (user caught this immediately):** the K22BirdOfPrey
"fix" above was wrong and has been reverted. K22, D32StrongerBird, and L42GreatBird share one piece
of art scaled to represent a real in-universe size family — a K-22 Bird of Prey (Class V Scout,
~12 crew), a D-32 Stronger Bird (Class VII Cruiser, ~145 crew), and an L-42 Great Bird (Class IX-X
Frigate, ~240 crew) — and K22's small render was the whole point, not an extraction artifact. The
registry comment already said `// Class V Scout — ~12 crew (smallest)` right next to the entry;
this session's sprite audit measured canvas fill ratios in isolation and never cross-checked that
comment before "correcting" it. Reverted by deleting the `K22BirdOfPrey` override entirely — with
D32 and L42 never touched in the first place, this restores the exact original hierarchy
(fill ratios 0.195 / 0.527 / 0.820 — smallest to largest, matching the crew-size family). Verified:
rendered all three side by side against real hex outlines (small, medium, large read correctly at a
glance); re-ran a live K22 battle with no render errors.

**Lesson for any future sprite-sizing pass: a small render is not automatically a bug.** Check the
registry's own comments and any stated in-universe rationale (crew size, class, a named art family)
*before* treating an outlier fill ratio as something to fix — this is the second time in this
project a "smaller than the others" observation was actually correct and the "larger than the
others" one was the mistake (see also: this same audit correctly left several genuinely-scoped
overflow bugs alone rather than fixing them all at once with one formula).

**Open item, not yet resolved: tooltip verbiage for `SPRITE_OVERSIZE_REASON`.** The map is still
empty — no ship needs it yet — but the user asked for candidate wording for whenever it's used.
Proposed options, none chosen yet:
- *"Drawn slightly oversized for visibility — this doesn't change the ship's position, arcs, or hex."*
- *"This hull's art extends past its hex border by design; combat position is still exactly centered."*
- *"Rendered larger than scale so the design reads clearly — has no effect on movement or firing arcs."*
The common thread across all three: reassure the player the visual size is cosmetic only and doesn't
touch anything mechanical, since that's the natural worry a player would have on seeing a ship
visibly overlap its neighbor's hex. Whichever wording is chosen, it belongs in `SPRITE_OVERSIZE_REASON`
keyed by `spriteKey`, per the mechanism already wired into `showTerrainTip()`.

**Policy implementation:** added an empty `SPRITE_OVERSIZE_REASON` map alongside the scale table,
and wired it into the existing `showTerrainTip()` hover handler (which already resolves "what hex is
the mouse over, and is a ship sitting on it" for the red-damage-tint tooltip) — if a ship's
`spriteKey` has an entry here, the tooltip appends the reason. **Currently empty by design**: every
overflow case found in this audit turned out to be a bug that got its scale corrected, not a
deliberate exception, so no ship uses it yet. The mechanism exists and is documented so that any
FUTURE deliberate oversize choice has an obvious place to put its justification, rather than the
question resurfacing as "why didn't this get a tooltip like the policy said."

Verified: rendered all nine fixed sprites together at real hex proportions (see the QA renders in
this session's transcript); ran a live battle for Federation2 vs Nova and for K22BirdOfPrey with no
render errors; confirmed the new `SPRITE_OVERSIZE_REASON` map exists, is empty, and
`showTerrainTip` is still callable.

### 0.103 — What changed in v2.45-S156 (setup screen redesigned for real monitors)

**Trigger:** the start menu was a 480px column with 9-11px type centred on a 27-inch screen (about 18% of a 2560px width), the D/WDF
readout was too wordy, and more panels are coming (multiplayer, fleet-vs-fleet, Advanced/RPG options).

**Layout.** `#scenario-screen` is now a responsive dashboard. A header, then a 3-column **stage** (`.sc-stage`: your ship | matchup |
enemy ship), then `.sc-lower`, an `auto-fit` grid of `.sc-card` panels (AI difficulty, ruleset, terrain & house rules), then the action
row (Ship Recognition Database, Engage). **ONE scalable unit `--u`** (`clamp(10px, min(.5vw + 4px, 1.4vh), 24px)`) drives every size on the
screen via `calc(var(--u)*k)`: width scaling gives readable type on big monitors, the height cap guarantees it fits without scrolling.
Below 1000px wide it stacks to one scrolling column (`--u:13px`), which also makes the SETUP screen phone-usable (the battle screen is
still not: see roadmap B1).
**Adding a panel** (game mode / multiplayer, fleet builder, advanced & RPG options) = add one `.sc-card` inside `.sc-lower` (there is a
comment marking the spot); the grid wraps it automatically. For fleets, a side card's single ship slot becomes a list.

**Matchup readout (compact).** `updateMatchupBalance()` now renders a short verdict (`fairnessShort`: EVEN MATCH / SLIGHT EDGE - YOU /
LOPSIDED - ENEMY / MISMATCH, or NOT RATED), the ratio with an "approx." mark, a you-vs-enemy balance bar, and a 3-row table (armour D,
firepower WDF, CE) with the leading value highlighted. The explanations (what D, WDF and CE mean, "rates ships not pilots", approximate-rating
reasons) moved into an info popover (`.mb-info` / `#mb-pop`) that opens on hover AND keyboard focus (so tap works). New `updateSideInfo()` fills
per-ship stat chips (hull, power, shield, guns, cloak) and the enemy faction badge. `renderCustomPanel()` now fills two cards
(`#sc-ruleset`, `#sc-terrain`) instead of the old `#sc-custom`. Difficulty tick labels are clickable (`setDiff`) and the current tier is highlighted.
Faction chips lost the hex glyph and wrap instead of truncating (flex-basis in `--u`, NOT `em`: `em` there was the chip's own smaller font).

**Verification, in a REAL browser (Playwright + Chromium), not jsdom.** Fit without scrolling and no horizontal overflow at 3840x2160,
2560x1440, 2560x1080, 1920x1080, 1680x1050, 1600x900, 1440x900, 1366x768, 1280x720, 1100x800, 1024x768; 800x1000 and 390x844 stack and scroll by
design. At 2560x1440 the panel is 94% of the width (was 18%). A 26-check interaction script clicks every control (all five faction chips,
matchup for rated / approximate / unrated pairs, popover on hover and focus, every difficulty tick, both rulesets, every terrain toggle and
ALL ON/OFF, the Ship Database button) and then Engage, confirming the chosen ruleset, AI tier and terrain reach the battle (`GS.rules`,
`aiDifficulty`): 26/26. Extensibility test: injecting 2-3 stand-in panels wraps them to a second row and still fits at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440;
at 1366x768 with 5+ panels it scrolls instead of breaking (graceful fallback). No game logic changed.

**Tooling note (environment).** The sandbox was reset between sessions: the old working copy, jsdom and the AI harness were gone (only
`/mnt/user-data/outputs` persisted). **Playwright with Chromium IS available** (`/home/claude/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/playwright`,

### 0.102 — Scoring-mechanics analysis for a future Construction Manual feature (analysis only, no code change)

**Context.** The user once heard (decades ago, story only, nothing preserved) that an actuary reverse-engineered FASA's D/WDF scoring and
concluded some of it was not derivable. The aim: when the Construction Manual feature is built, let the player design engines, weapons
and ships and score them. These tests were run to see how feasible an approximate scorer is. Nothing was changed in the game.

**D (Defense Factor).** The rulebook says D comes from warp+impulse power units, the movement and shield point ratios, maximum shield
power and superstructure; the formula is in the *Ship Construction Manual*, which is NOT in the project files. Fits on 46 exactly-matched
ships (`ce_drivers.js`, `d_forms.js` in the tools zip): hull + power + max shield alone R^2 0.77 (roughly 1 D per hull box, ~1 per power
unit, ~2 per point of max shield per face); adding the ratios 0.83; richest form with efficiency interactions and the warp/impulse split
0.89, typical error +-12 on values from 53 to 198. Outlier: Orion Wanderer (actual 148, fit about 80). **Strongest evidence of irregularity:
D-7 M and D-7 R list identical values for every input the rulebook names (hull 20, power 44, 3:1, KWE-3 x2 (20), KIC-2 (4), KSK 1/2 max 12)
yet print D 87.6 vs 84.6.** Their only listed differences are the R's cloak (KCC/32), crew, cargo and weapons. So either D uses inputs the
rulebook does not list, or it was adjusted by hand. This supports the actuary's story but cannot distinguish hidden input from judgement.

**WDF (Weapon Damage Factor).** Not reproducible from weapon counts (a simple fit gave nonsensical negative coefficients), consistent with
the rulebook saying it uses each weapon's max range, hit ability across the range and max damage, i.e. the FIRING CHARTS. It does respond to
weapon specs: the KP-3 appears as chart R / arm 2 / dmg 15 on the rulebook page but chart E / arm 10 in the Klingon book, and the D-7 M's
WDF differs accordingly (42.2 vs 33.4). **Verified: the game's KP-3 uses chart R**, so the page value (42.2) in `SHIP_CE` is the correct one.

**Feasibility.** FASA's own "nearly equal" tolerance is about 25%, so a scorer needs roughly +-10%, not exactness. Most promising route:
model WDF from first principles using the firing charts (in the project's rules data) with a few fitted constants, test against the ~87
printed WDF values; improve D by finding the unlisted inputs (cloak, engine type, etc.). **Not yet attempted for WDF.** Honest status: D is
about +-12% today; WDF is untested.

**Also needed:** the Ship Construction Manual's component tables and design rules (not in the project; the user may own the book).
Tracked as roadmap item A16.

### 0.101 — v2.44-S155: the missing D/WDF ratings were in the project's data after all (correction to §0.100)

**What went wrong.** §0.100 said 13 ships had no rating data. The user asked me to double-check (specifically the Chandley and the
Federation dreadnought). I had only searched the game's CATALOG, not the project's book data files. The rulebook ship data
(`FASA_2003_Starship_Combat_SHIPS_DATA.md`) prints D/WDF for 35 ships, and the Federation/Klingon/Romulan books
(`FASA_2302/2301/2303`) have them per mark. **Lesson: for any "do we have this data?" question, search ALL the project data files
(rulebook ship data, the three recognition-manual files, the OCR text), not just the game's catalog.**

**Method (`ce_reconcile.js`, in `tools/ai_harness.zip`).** For every ship, compare the game's power and hull strength against the
rulebook page and the catalog variants, and use the source that actually matches. Policy now written into the `SHIP_CE`
comment: (1) game ship matches a RULEBOOK PAGE exactly -> page values; (2) else a CATALOG/book variant exactly -> those;
(3) matches except hull strength -> rated but marked `approx` with the reason (shown in the UI as "approximate"); (4) else
unrated. **Result: 52 of 54 selectable ships rated (7 approximate). Unrated: Federation II Mk I and Mk II only** -- no D/WDF for
the dreadnought exists in any project file, and nothing in the history records the stat block's source (the code says "FASA stat
block"; the user believes it came from a screenshot). **Needs D and WDF for the Federation II from the book.**

**Validation.** The rulebook says the Constitution, D7-M and D-10 are "nearly equal" and the Reliant matches the L-9. Final CE ratios:
Constitution Mk II / D7-M **0.986**, Constitution Mk II / D-10 (Mk D) **0.945**, Reliant Mk II / L-9 **1.242**. Before the corrections
these were 1.25, 0.55 (wrong D-10 mark) and 1.24 -- the D-10 and D-7 M fixes are what make the rulebook's claim come out right.

**Corrections made to ratings that were already in the table.** D-7 M: WDF 33.4 -> **42.2** (the game's stats match the rulebook
PAGE exactly and the page prints 42.2; the Klingon catalog says 33.4). D-10: the game's "Mk D" matches the Klingon book's Mk D
exactly (power 46, hull 24, shields 1/2 max 15) -> **85.3 / 45.2**, not the Mk G values an earlier pass used.

**Added:** Northampton Mk II 124.0/84.3 (p.64, exact); L-9 101.8/59.4 (p.70, exact; page model letter "B" flagged); CS-2 75.4/26.0
(p.72, exact); Whitewind 88.5/49.8 (catalog Type 3 matches the game exactly; the rulebook scan prints D 83.5 -- sources differ,

Mk III (137.5/102.2), Mk IV (170.0/102.2) -- identified by power, shield ratio, impulse and missile type (the game's labels

### 0.100 — What changed in v2.43-S154 (matchup balance, plus fixes from the Andor vs Great Bird log)

**Trigger:** combat log #18 (ledger) and a feature idea: the game has no way to say whether a fight is fair.

**1. Matchup balance (first cut) — `SHIP_CE`, `shipRating`, `compareSides`, `fairnessVerdict`, `updateMatchupBalance`, `#matchup-balance`.**
Uses FASA's own method (rulebook "Balancing Scenarios", read directly, not invented): two ships -> Combat Efficiency
CE = D x WDF ("the ship with the greater CE will, in general, last longer"); two sides -> compare TOTAL D and TOTAL WDF
(FASA's published-scenario method) or each side's total D x total WDF. `compareSides(keysA, keysB)` takes arrays, so the
same code carries to fleet-vs-fleet (roadmap A11). The rulebook gives no numeric tolerance; its own examples put
"nearly equal" near 25% (Constitution Mk II vs D7-M = 1.246; Reliant vs L-9 about 1.24), so: <=1.25 even, <=2 slight edge,
<=4 lopsided, >4 mismatch (OUR bands, a judgement call). Shown on a new "Matchup" row of the setup screen (updates on ship or
difficulty change), with a note that it rates ships not pilots (arcs, cloaks, AI tier not counted); and the debrief compares
the pre-battle verdict to the result ("you beat the odds" / "you lost a fight the numbers favoured you in").
**(SUPERSEDED by §0.101: 52 of 54 are now rated.) Data: only 41 of 54 selectable ships were rated at first.** D/WDF live in the CATALOG variants; there is NO clean link from a
playable ship to its catalog variant (`VARIANT_KEY_MAP` covers only 14), so `SHIP_CE` was built by matching faction + power +
hull and checking names, and every row carries its source in a comment. **Unrated on purpose (13):** Federation II Mk I/II
(not in the catalog), Nova (ours is a Type 2, catalog only has Type 1), K-22 (no catalog D/WDF), Whitewind (catalog D 88.5
vs the rulebook scan's 83.5 -- unresolved), CS-2 (genuine unmatched variant), L-42 (registry hull 18 vs catalog 22), L-9 and
D-10 (several candidate variants), Chandley Mk I-III, Northampton Mk II. Rating these needs a check against the physical
book. The generic legacy keys `Constitution`/`D7` are not selectable and were not rated (a power+hull match to the L-6 was a
coincidence and was rejected). **The first-load default pairing (Constitution Mk II vs D7-M) is rated and reads "Even match".**

**2. AI: never turn the stern to a ship you can already shoot.** The legacy branch "Too close: turn away and back off"
(`range < targetRange-1`, D>=3) rotated the AI's stern to the target (ships cannot reverse) for several phases, exposing its aft
arc and forfeiting shots. Now it only backs off when NO gun bears; otherwise it falls through to the optimal-range branch (hold the
arc). The v2.42 planner got the same guard, plus **self-preservation: below 40% hull it does not plan flanks** and
`aiExploitMoveBoost` no longer shifts power into movement. Measured: static targets unchanged; vs a closing-in player
Captain -0.05..-0.10 (was -0.11..-0.12), Admiral -0.02..-0.11 (was -0.08..-0.14); v2.41 was -0.23. Reproduction of the logged
situation (`repro4.js`, decloak forced): v2.42 moved to 16,10 facing 1 (away), v2.43 stays facing the player.

**3. Debrief fixes (the user asked what "too brief ... guard your blind arcs" meant while having won).** (a) Cloaked
windows were excluded wholesale, leaving 1 usable window in a 4-window fight; it now says "most of this fight (3 of 4 windows)
was against a cloaked ship" and counts the cloaked windows separately. (b) "You denied it a blind quarter, and won" was printed
with no data (blindW was empty only because N<2); outcome lines now require >=2 open windows. (c) "Lesson of this tier"
read like criticism after a win; renamed "What this tier tests:" with neutral phrasing, and the "Next time" advice only appears
when >=2 blind windows were recorded. (d) The debrief used to be logged the instant the kill registered, i.e. mid-volley; it is
now built and logged in `showEndgamePanel`, so it lands at the END of an exported log.

**Open (not changed):** the Captain's allocation ignores its own hull state (anticipation strips shields into movement even at 11%
hull; the Admiral has a survival branch, the Captain does not) -- roadmap D8, needs a decision. Observed also: shots in a volley
are still resolved after the kill registers (simultaneous fire, so arguably correct).

**Tooling:** `tools/ai_harness.zip` gained `ce_audit.js`, `ce_match.js` (the data audit used for the ratings table) and the
tests used here (`fair_test.js`, `debrief_cases.js`, `repro_decloak_case.js`).

### 0.99 — What changed in v2.42-S153 (SMARTER AI TIERS: exploit layer, tier descriptions, tactical debrief)

Implements roadmap item A14 (design agreed in §0.98). Three player-visible pieces, plus one internal test harness.

**1. Exploit layer (`AI_EXPLOIT`, `aiPlanExploit`, `aiExploitMoveBoost`) — Captain, Admiral, Legend only.**
- **Gated on a sensor lock** (user decision): `!interMode() || s.locked || s.detectedCloaked`. Basic rules have no lock
  mechanic, so there the AI is treated as having contact. A successful hit on a ship already breaks its lock (existing
  rule), which is the player's counterplay. Skipped when the player is cloaked (its weapons are offline) or the AI is
  patrolling for a lost target.
- **How it decides.** For candidate ring hexes (preferred range +-1 around the player) it values a position as
  `my bearing firepower - B * (player's bearing firepower, RELATIVE to the best available on the ring) * rangeWeight
  - 0.12*|range - preferred|` (+ Admiral/Legend extras: turns the player needs to cover it, weakest/knocked-out shield
  facing). Weapon "firepower" = `weaponPowerCap`. It then does a COST/BENEFIT over a per-tier horizon: a flank costs T
  phases of reduced effectiveness and pays off for the remaining `horizon-T`; only trips with gain >= `baseGain` are taken.
  The route is a hazard-weighted Dijkstra over (hex, facing) states (1 pt per rotate or step = the real movement rules)
  that swings wide rather than cutting through point-blank range; it commits to the path, then spends leftover points
  rotating to keep guns on the target. Uses the existing `weaponArcCoversTarget` on hypothetical positions.
- **Plan-aware movement budget.** At power allocation, if a worthwhile flank exists at the move budget the tier would
  buy (Captain 4, Admiral 5, Legend 4 pts/phase), power is shifted from WEAPONS to MOVEMENT for the turn, never below a
  third of full firepower. Without this a flank took more phases than any horizon justified and was never attempted.
- **Flank feedback (first piece of in-match adaptation).** If the goal chosen last phase has stopped being blind (the
  player turned to cover it) that is a failed flank; each failure raises the required gain, and after `failLimit`
  (Captain/Admiral 3, Legend 2) it stops flanking for the rest of the match. Successes reduce the count.
- **Tiers.** Cadet/Ensign untouched. **Lt Cmdr deliberately has NO exploit entry** (deviation from the agreed ladder):
  tested in three start geometries it never found a flank worth taking, and an entry that never fires only risks
  changing behaviour, so Lt Cmdr keeps legacy movement exactly. Lt Cmdr's description says "no flanking". Revisit only
  with a concrete idea for what it should do.
- **When there is nothing worth doing the layer steps aside** (returns null -> legacy `tryMove`), except that Captain+
  HOLD station once at preferred range (better than legacy's random one-hex sidestep, which was measurably self-harming).

**2. Tier descriptions (`DIFF_DESC`, `updDiffLabel`, `#diff-desc`).** Shown under the slider for every tier, naming the
tier's lesson and what it actually does. **Rule: keep `DIFF_DESC` in step with the AI code; never describe behaviour
that is not built.** (Legend's description does NOT promise habit-adaptation because that is not built.)

**3. Tactical debrief (`debriefSnapshot`, `buildDebrief`, `renderDebriefHTML`, `logDebrief`, `#eg-debrief`, `GS.debrief`).**
A snapshot at the start of every fire window records where the enemy sits relative to the PLAYER's arcs, how many guns
of each side bear, and lock state; `resolveShipFiring` tallies hits/damage per shield facing. The end screen shows a
debrief (arc discipline, blind-quarter windows, shield-facing concentration, lock coverage, range, outcome flavour, the
tier's lesson) and the same lines are written into the combat log so EXPORTED logs carry it. Cloaked windows are excluded.

**Verification (headless harness, `tools/ai_harness.zip`, see its README).** "adv" = AI firepower bearing minus player's.
| Player | Tier | v2.41 | v2.42 |
|---|---|---|---|
| static Constitution | Captain / Admiral / Legend | +0.47 / +0.44 / +0.64 | +0.73 / +0.87 / +0.87 (real start) |
| static Constitution, other starts | Captain / Admiral / Legend | +0.34..+0.39 / +0.32..+0.38 / +0.38..+0.54 | +0.76..+0.76 / +0.79..+0.85 / +0.85..+0.97 |
| responsive (slow-turn / advance) | Captain / Admiral | -0.20..-0.24 | -0.05..-0.14 |
| responsive | Legend | -0.02..-0.06 | -0.01..-0.10 (slightly worse in one geometry) |
Lock forced OFF reproduces the old numbers within noise (gate works); Basic rules exploit is active. Stress test: 7,776
phases across all tiers x 6 enemy ships x 3 player ships with random obstacles, cloaks and damage: 0 exceptions, tiers 3-6
never off-map / on an obstacle / on the player / overspending points; 3.6 ms average, 64 ms worst per phase.

**Bugs found and fixed while building (all caught by the harness, not by reading):** (a) a one-step planner was inert
(never reached a blind arc); (b) planner active at long range made Captain/Admiral stall outside weapon range; (c) goal
flip-flop because the player's per-phase remaining points differed by who moves first (now the turn's average points);
(d) "hold station" off-station froze the AI (now defers to legacy pursuit until at preferred range); (e) a
`Float32Array` of distances vs double heap keys silently discarded valid Dijkstra nodes (use `Float64Array`);
(f) early versions were measurably WORSE than v2.41 against players who turn to answer (fixed by flank feedback, a
steeper hazard near the player, and a stricter trip valuation).

**Known limits / honest caveats.** The test "players" are scripts that always make a sensible choice; a human is both
better and worse. Only Constitution/Fed-II vs D-7M were measured in depth. Against a perfectly responding player the new
tiers do not exploit anything ("a timely turn beats it" is the intended lesson). Legend is a touch behind v2.41 in one
geometry against a perfect responder. NOT built: Legend/Admiral habit tracking beyond flank feedback (A14 stays open).

**CORRECTION (same build): the "pre-existing bug" I first logged here (roadmap D7) was NOT a bug.** FASA's Basic
movement rules say two or more starships may occupy the same hex, that ships may neither ram nor collide, and that ships
in the same hex may not fire at one another (rulebook movement and firing sections; also summarised in
`FASA_2003_Starship_Combat_RULES_DATA.md`). The game implements exactly that: `celBlocked` covers only planets/moons, for
the player's movement as well as the AI's, and `weaponArcCoversTarget` returns false at range 0. My stress test's
"ON-PLAYER" check wrongly treated stacking as a violation, and I described it as a bug without first checking the rules.
What IS true: the new Captain+ planner chooses never to END a phase on the player's hex -- a deliberate AI preference, not
a rule -- while legacy tiers (and the player) may stack, as the rules allow. D7 was removed from the roadmap.
**Lesson: check the rulebook before calling engine behaviour a bug.**

### 0.98 — Roadmap correction: B4 withdrawn, new item A14 (smarter AI tiers) — documentation only, build stays v2.41-S152

User clarified that B4 (remember the AI difficulty between games) was a misreading: resetting to Ensign
on reload is expected behavior, the player chooses a difficulty each game, and no change is wanted.
B4 is withdrawn (§0.97's localStorage note stands only as background). What the user actually wants is
that **each difficulty setting should behave in a meaningfully different, instructive way**, e.g. higher
tiers exploiting that Constitution-type ships have no aft weapons, and responding to the player's style.

Code-verified findings (v2.41-S152), recorded so the design starts from fact:
- `aiDoMove()`: the movement goal is always the player's hex (`goal = track.col/row`); the AI holds a
  per-tier range (Ensign 6 / Lt Cmdr 5 / Captain+Admiral 4 / Legend 2) and faces the player. At D>=3 it
  verifies its OWN weapons bear (the "flank fix" from §0.59/v2.12 is purely defensive, it stops the AI
  being flanked; there is no offensive mirror of it).
- It never reads the player's weapon arcs or downed shield facings, so every tier approaches on the same
  line and meets a forward-armed player's bow. The Captain+ "lateral drift" is a random 50% one-hex
  sidestep, always toward heading+1, not a purposeful flank.
- The only adaptation is `_oppPrevMP` (the player's previous-turn move points, used by the anticipation
  rule in `aiAllocatePower`). The AI also reads the player's true hull directly rather than via sensors.
- Needed geometry already exists: `weaponArcCoversTarget(weapon, shooter{col,row,facing}, target)` and
  `arcOfTargetFrom()` accept hypothetical positions, so scoring candidate hexes needs no new geometry.

Written up as roadmap item **A14** (design only; layers: exploit, adapt, optional tier descriptions and
after-action debrief; open decisions listed there). Nothing built; no game file changes.

### 0.95 — Mobile support: code audit documented (no code changed, build stays v2.41-S152)

User asked what it would actually take to make the game work on mobile, given the game currently
only "technically" runs there. Rather than answer from general mobile-dev knowledge, audited the
real file directly: grepped every `addEventListener` call (zero touch events of any kind — mouse
only), checked for a `<meta name="viewport">` tag (absent), counted `:hover` CSS rules (33, several
of them tooltips added THIS session), counted `@media` queries (2, against panels hardcoded up to
780px wide), and measured the file's own byte composition (10.6 MB total, 9.4 MB / 89% of it is
embedded base64 ship art).

**The headline finding, and the reason this isn't just "needs polish": ship movement is a hard
blocker, not a rough edge.** `playerStep()` and `playerRotate()` are called from exactly two
`keydown` handlers (WASD/arrows) and nowhere else in the entire codebase — no button, no touch
path. On a touch-only device there is currently no way to move or rotate a ship at all.

Full findings, in priority order, written up properly in `Feature_Status_and_Wishlist.md`'s new
"Mobile Support — Detailed Findings" section rather than just left in this conversation: (1) the
movement blocker above, (2) zero touch listeners / wheel-only zoom, (3) missing viewport meta tag,
(4) hover-dependent tooltips including this session's own oversize-disclosure and hull-lineage notes,
(5) fixed-pixel layout against almost no responsive CSS, (6) the 10.6 MB/89%-art payload, (7)
desktop-density panel layout, (8) no orientation handling. That document is the one to read for any
future mobile work — this entry just records that the audit happened and why its conclusion is
sharper than the old "5-phase plan" placeholder it replaced.

No game file changes in this entry — documentation only. `Feature_Status_and_Wishlist.md` updated
and delivered; its own header timestamp now notes the v2.41-S152 addition.

### 0.93 — What changed in v2.40-S151 (Klingon Bird-of-Prey hull-lineage note, two places)

Follow-up to the §0.91 correction: the user liked having the K-22/D-32/L-42 size family explained,
but wanted it player-visible rather than just a code comment, and asked for in-universe flavor text
rather than a plain technical note. Wording (user's own, chosen from three offered drafts):

> "One hull, three scales — the design proved so sound the Empire never replaced it, only grew it:
> barely a dozen officers and men crew the K-22 scout, while the same silhouette scales up into the
> D-32 cruiser and the L-42 frigate."

(The "dozen officers and men" phrase is the user's own reference to Sulu's line in *Star Trek III:
The Search for Spock* about a Bird-of-Prey's crew complement — kept in the in-universe text itself
without a meta citation, matching how the rest of the game's flavor text reads.)

**One shared string, two lookup tables, two surfaces** — this is a different mechanism from
`SPRITE_OVERSIZE_REASON` (§0.91), which discloses a *rendering* choice; this is *lore* about a
shared design family, so it doesn't belong in that map:
- `SHIP_LORE_NOTE` (keyed by `spriteKey`) — wired into the existing `showTerrainTip()` hex-hover
  handler, right after the oversize-disclosure line, in its own distinct style (teal italic with a
  🖖 marker, vs. the oversize line's amber ⚠) so the two kinds of note are visually distinguishable

### 0.85 — The CATALOG "verify" flag: contradiction found, partially resolved (2026-09-25, comment-only)

**The contradiction.** Two places in this project disagree about what a catalog variant's `verify:
true` field means:
- The Recognition DB's own UI tooltip (shown for a not-yet-playable variant) reads: *"This mark is
  flagged **Verify** — confirm vs master scan before promoting."* → reads as a CAUTION: not yet
  checked.
- An earlier handover note (when the Loknar was added) reads: *"none carry FASA's own 'verify:true'
  flag, so Mk II isn't more 'official,' just the chosen standard variant"* → treats it as a mark of
  SPECIAL CONFIDENCE.
Nothing else in the file settles which reading the original catalog author intended. **This session's
own build comments for Larson (§0.79) and Nova (§0.82) cited `verify:true` as a confidence booster,
following the second reading — flagged to the user as potentially backwards.**

**Empirical evidence gathered since, from real book checks (not from the code):**
- Nova: catalog's Type 1 entry (verify:true) gave RB-11 chart V and maxPower 9. User's physical
  rulebook check confirmed both.
- Larson: catalog's Mk VII entry (verify:true) gave moveRatio 2, shieldRatio 0.5, maxShieldPerFace 10
  (the last of these wasn't even flagged uncertain in the OCR scan, so it's a weaker data point, but
  the first two were genuinely disputed OCR cells resolved via this catalog entry). **User confirmed
  all three against their physical FASA Starship Combat Simulator rulebook, 2026-09-25 — no changes
  needed, entry was already correct.**

**Where this leaves things:** two independent real-book checks of verify:true-derived values both
came back correct. That favours the "confirmed/reliable" reading over the UI tooltip's "still needs
checking" reading — but **it is not proof**, and the user explicitly noted other marks may need
checking against other sources in the future. **Do not treat this as fully settled for a NEW ship.**
Continue disclosing when a value depends on a verify:true catalog entry (as every ship built this
session already does), just note that the flag has held up twice so far. The UI tooltip text itself
was NOT changed (still says the "needs checking" version) — that's a separate small task if the user
ever wants it addressed, since fixing the copy without being sure of the intended meaning risks
making the contradiction worse, not better.

**Game-file change:** none, other than updating the `Larson_MkVII` registry comment from "conflicting
sources, resolved by house precedent" to "user-confirmed 2026-09-25, no change needed" — pure comment
edit, stat values verified byte-identical before/after (`totalPower:28, moveRatio:2, shieldRatio:0.5,
maxShieldPerFace:10, superstructureMax:16`, unchanged). No build-number bump; not a gameplay change.
