### 0.74 — What changed in v2.24-S135 (AI: smart weapon arming + close-range anticipation)

**Trigger:** combat log #14 (ledger), sent with no other request → per the HARD RULE, a request for
the AI to get smarter within its ship. Template followed: §0.58/§0.59 (AI-only; ship data verified
untouched afterwards). This also closes the anticipation gap logged from #13.

**Fix 1 — smart arming (Lt. Cmdr and up, D≥3), in the "Arm weapons" block of `aiAllocatePower()`.**
Root cause (every tier): `s.weapons.filter(alive).forEach(...)` funded each beam at `maxPower` in
REGISTRY ORDER until `weapPwr` ran out. For a K-23 (bank, bank, fwd, fwd, aft, aft) any budget under
~26 left both aft KD-9s unpowered — log #14's mysterious 3-pt shot was Fwd 2 getting the last 3 units.
Now weapons are funded in order of arc distance to the target (`arcOfTargetFrom`; 0 = in arc, 1 = one
arc away, …; registry order breaks ties; cloaked target → `s._lastKnown`). Cadet/Ensign (D 1–2) keep
list order DELIBERATELY (green crews; keeps the ladder meaningful). Legend gets smart arming (arming,
not movement — its hand-authored movement is untouched).

**Fix 2 — anticipation (D 3–5 only; Legend excluded), just before the final `weapPwr` clamp.** Within 4
hexes, raise movement toward the opponent's move points from LAST turn (`s._oppPrevMP`, recorded at the
end of each allocation). NEVER this turn's: the player commits first, so reading `p.movePts` for the
current turn would be cheating. Cap: 40% of power (Lt. Cmdr) / 50% (Captain, Admiral). Extra power comes
from NON-bearing weapon power first (bearing guns' full cost is protected), then shields, then bearing
guns only as a last resort. (A first version took from all weapons and left Captain's second aft gun at
3 power — rejected in test.)

**Verification.** Structure + `node --check`. Log #14 geometry recreated (K-23 at 17,6 facing 5,
Loknar astern at range 1, arc 3): OLD Lt. Cmdr / Captain / Ensign all funded 0 to the aft pair, 0 guns
able to fire; NEW Lt. Cmdr & Captain fund Aft 1/2 at 5/5 (2 guns bear), Ensign unchanged. Target dead
ahead → forward guns first, as before. Ran the real `resolveShipFiring(GS.enemy, GS.player, …)`: OLD
tried only the four forward guns (all "Target not in arc"); NEW fired both aft KD-9s. SHIP_REGISTRY (all
48 hulls, every stat and weapon) and PLAYABLE_BY_FACTION compared as live objects old vs new:
identical. Fuzz 6 tiers × 260 random states: no NaN/negative allocations introduced.

**Pre-existing bug FOUND, NOT fixed (needs the user's call — it changes difficulty):** several tiers
request fixed amounts regardless of remaining power (e.g. Lt. Cmdr `move 12 + shields 12` even when an
engine-damaged ship has < 24 total; Cadet's random draws likewise). `weapPwr` clamps to 0 but move +
shields can EXCEED `currentPower`, so a badly crippled AI ship gets phantom power. Same-seed fuzz: over-
budget counts identical in old and new builds (Cadet 27, Ensign 3, Lt. Cmdr 65, Captain 45, Admiral 50,
Legend 0 of 260 each) — confirmed pre-existing. Fix would be a final normalisation (trim shields, then
move, to fit `currentPower`). Logged in §3.

### 0.73 — What changed in v2.23-S134 (NEBULA: Wispy + ROLLING BOIL, user's second pick)

**User feedback that drove it:** the v2.21 "moving cloud" (3-phase crossfade + few-pixel sway) felt off —
the user wanted the cloud to STAY IN POSITION and ROLL, "like there's inner currents moving the mist
around like a rolling boil," with "some rolling less, some more active." Prototyped in the Nebula Lab
first (same artifact URL as §0.69) as a new motion mode; user then exported this config, now stored
verbatim as `NEB_RENDER`: style `wispy`, edgeSpreadPct 90, filamentDetailPct 100, densityPct 100,
glowPct 53, motion `boil`, boil {intensityPct 150, speedPct 110, calmActiveVarietyPct 85}, lightning
{100, 140}, outline always. (`gasMotionSpeedPct` 30 retained but only used by `motion:'drift'`.)

**Rolling boil — how it works (keep these properties):**
- `nebBuildFlow(cl)` (async, after phase 0): per cache pixel, a **curl-noise** current (divergence-free
  → closed eddies ~1.15 HR across) as a unit vector × local strength; an **activity** value (slow fbm,
  ~2.6 HR) for calm vs active pockets; an **edge weight** `smooth(0.2,0.85,field)^1.5` so currents are
  zero at the rim (outline never moves); a per-pixel **phase jitter** (low-freq fbm) so pockets don't
  pulse in sync.
- `nebBoilFrame(cl, t)`: two-phase flow map — each pixel samples cached phase 0 from upstream at
  offsets `v·D·p0` and `v·D·p1` (p1 = p0+0.5), triangle-weighted, period `T = 5/speed` s,
  `D = intensity·0.95·HR·renderScale·edge·activity`, activity = `1 − variety·(1 − smooth(.3,.72,A0))`.
  Offsets run 0..D (NOT centred — a centred −D..+D version was tried in the lab and mostly shimmered);
  closed eddies keep the gas circulating inside its own pocket, so the cloud as a whole stays put.
- Throttled to ~30 updates/s per cloud (`cl.flow.t`); stops under prefers-reduced-motion. Lightning
  masks against the boiled frame, so flashes light the moving gas. In boil mode the drift phases 1–2
  are NOT rendered; glow is still baked from phase 0.
- `nebRenderCloud` now stores `cv._img` / `cv._field` and supports `style:'wispy'` (ported from the
  lab) alongside `'billow'`. Swap back = change `NEB_RENDER.style` / `.motion`.

**Measured (game sizes, 8-hex + 5-hex clouds at 90% spread):** battle-start sync render 45 ms;
background flow+glow build 26 ms; boil update ~0.7 ms per 8-hex cloud, ~1.3 ms for both → ~37 ms of
work per second at 30 updates/s. Metrics from the lab: rim changes ~11× less than interior; active
pockets move ~3× more than calm ones.

**Verification:** structure + `node --check`; jsdom boot + launchGame until nebulae exist — flows
built, drift phases skipped, glow baked, 120 frames with a boil-call counter confirming the 30/s
throttle, zero errors; real frames from the shipped code over ~4 s via `@napi-rs/canvas`. Not tested
in a real browser.

### 0.72 — What changed in v2.22-S133 (GRAVITY WELLS → black-hole art; rules unchanged)

**Why this build exists:** in §0.71 the session published the lab and then WAITED for a style pick
even though the user had said "we're just updating the art" — the user had to point out that neither
the game nor the README changed. Lesson: when the user says to update something and a sensible
default exists (the lab's default + the style the session itself recommended), BUILD IT and offer
the swap; don't stall on a choice the user didn't ask to make. Also: README gets updated in the same
pass whenever the game changes.

**What:** style = Accretion vortex at lab defaults, well-hue colour (`GRAV_RENDER` holds it all).
**Rules untouched** — a `'G'` hex still only costs 2 MP to enter (verified the reachable-cost line is
unchanged). Rule ideas remain BOOKMARKED in §3, not approved.
- New block above `generateTerrain()` (after the nebula block; same TDZ reason): `GRAV_RENDER`,
  `gravWells`, `gravColourAt`, `gravDiskTex` (reuses `nebMakeNoise`/`nebFbm`), `gravBuildWells`,
  `gravOutline`, `drawGravWells`. `gravBuildWells()` is called right after `nebBuildClouds()` at the
  end of `generateTerrain()`; one well per 'G' hex (each is an isolated single hex).
- `renderTac()`: 'G' hexes now fill with `TC.S` (no green hex tint), the per-hex `drawGravHex()` call
  is removed (function left in place, unused), and `drawGravWells(g, ts, ox, oy, W, H)` runs right
  after `drawNebulaClouds(...)` — before any tactical overlay or ship.
- **Live lensing:** reads back the already-drawn canvas around each well (`getImageData`, patch radius
  2·HR·ts), applies the point-lens map (θE = 0.62·HR·ts at defaults, black inside the shadow,
  Einstein-ring brightening, identity at the patch edge), `putImageData`s it back, then RE-STROKES the
  hex grid over that area so the grid never looks warped (lab "warp grid" was off). Works because the
  tactical canvas is 1:1 CSS px with no transform. The lens also bends adjacent nebula gas.
- Outline = the pronounced two-pass spec from §0.71 (dark underlay + bright dashed `[6,3]`).
- Motion (rotation, photon-ring shimmer) stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

**Verification:** structure + `node --check`; jsdom boot, `launchGame()` until a map had wells, one
well per G hex, `renderTac()` ×60 with a lens read/write per well per frame, zero errors, movement
rule unchanged; real frames rendered from the shipped code via `@napi-rs/canvas` (old vs new with a
nebula beside a well, plus a zoomed lensing on/off comparison). Lensing is subtle at default zoom
(sparse tactical starfield) — true to life; if the user wants it more obvious, raise
`GRAV_RENDER.lensingPct` or add a faint background dust layer near wells. Not tested in a browser.

### 0.71 — Gravity well art prototype, 2026-09-24 (no game-file change; build still v2.21-S132)

**Current gravity-well facts (read before touching them):** 0–2 per battle, each a SINGLE hex
(`terrain[k]==='G'`), `terrainStyle` `{hue ∈ GRAV_HUES [210,285,34], spin 0.35–1.0}`. The ONLY rule:
entering costs 2 MP (same as asteroids, `renderTac` reachable-hex cost + movement). No effect on
neighbours, to-hit, or sensors. NOTE the Customization description ("Warp-distorting singularities
that bend movement near them") overstates this. FASA has no gravity wells — all house rules.
**User decision (2026-09-24): KEEP THE CURRENT RULE for now — art update only.**

**Gravity Well Render Lab** (published artifact `https://claude.ai/artifact/W3pan2C6wuXzTHBvgHE9b6`,
downloads → `gravity_well_render_config.json`). Styles: Current (game, reproduced exactly), Accretion
vortex (face-on, differential rotation), Gargantua (tilted band + lensed halo + Doppler beaming),
Dormant singularity (shadow + photon ring + lensing only), Quasar (tilted disk + jets). Colour: well
hue or physical blackbody ramp. Every non-current style uses **real point-lens gravitational
lensing** of the background: a pixel at radius r samples the source at `r − θE²/r` (θE ≈ 0.62·HR at
defaults, fading to identity at 2.4·HR; inside the shadow = black; Einstein-ring brightening), cached
per well at 2× supersampling — optional "warp the hex grid" lenses the grid too. First pass was too
timid (lensing couldn't bend the grid, tilted disks invisible at map scale) — retuned before
publishing. Cache build ~2–2.5 s for 3 wells in the lab (supersampled); the game has ≤2 single-hex
wells — still build it off the critical path like the nebula phases.
**Outline requirement (user):** the gameplay-hex outline is MANDATORY in-game (same reason as
nebulae), and must be MORE PRONOUNCED than the nebula one because the art sits on the hex centre
and spills across its edges: two-pass stroke — dark underlay `rgba(0,0,0,.7)` width 3.6, then
`terHSL(hue,.9,.84)` at .95 alpha, width 1.9, dash `[6,3]`, round joins. Awaiting the user's style
pick / export before building it into the game.

### 0.70 — What changed in v2.21-S132 (NEBULA CLOUDS in the game + viewscreen target-only rule)

**User picked, verbatim config** (from the Nebula Render Lab export): style `billow`, edgeSpreadPct
56, filamentDetailPct 48, densityPct 100, glowPct 53, animateGas true, gasMotionSpeedPct 30,
lightning {enabled, frequencyPct 90, brightnessPct 130}, gameplayHexOutline `always`, renderScale 0.5.
Stored as `NEB_RENDER` — **all nebula-look tuning lives in that one object.** The user called the
outline "mandatory" so players always know exactly which hexes have an effect — do not make it
optional in-game without asking.

**Implementation.**
- New block **above `generateTerrain()`** (it must be above: `generateTerrain()` runs at file load,
  so constants below it would hit the TDZ): `NEB_RENDER`, `nebCloud` state, `nebMakeNoise`/`nebFbm`,
  `nebRenderCloud` (billow only — the other lab styles were not ported), `nebBuildClouds`,
  `nebFlashEnv`, `drawNebulaClouds`.
- `nebBuildClouds()` is called at the end of `generateTerrain()` (so both the load-time call and
  `launchGame()`'s call rebuild). Clouds = nebula hexes grouped by their shared `terrainStyle` object
  (one per connected blob, assigned by generateTerrain) — verified cloud count == distinct blobs and
  every N hex covered. Each cloud gets a bbox-sized cache at half resolution in WORLD coords; phase 0
  renders synchronously, phases 1–2 + baked glow via setTimeout, guarded by `nebCloud.gen` so a
  terrain regen discards stale work (verified).
- `renderTac()`: nebula hexes now fill with `TC.S` (no hex-shaped tint) and the per-hex
  `drawNebulaHex()` call is removed (function left in place, unused). `drawNebulaClouds(g, ts, ox,
  oy)` runs right after the hex loop and before `if(!GS) return;` — above the map, below every
  tactical overlay and ship. Screen transform is the same `world*ts + (ox,oy)` the loop uses, so
  zoom/pan just work.
- Motion: 3-phase churn blended with `'lighter'` on a per-cloud scratch canvas (exact lerp, no
  mid-fade dimming) + few-pixel sway; driven by `tacT`. Lightning: per-cloud rate
  `0.085·freq·√(hexes/6)·(0.6+0.4·min(2,density))` per second, flare masked to that cloud's gas with
  `'destination-in'`, two-pass additive bloom. Motion + lightning honour prefers-reduced-motion.
- Outline: dashed `[4,3]`, `terHSL(hue,.75,.75)` at 0.7 alpha, width scales mildly with zoom.

**Viewscreen change (user rule from §0.69):** `vsNebulaDim()` now counts only `GS.enemy` standing in
a nebula; the player's own position no longer thins the viewscreen stars. Map-wide nebula thinning
unchanged. Measured: player in a 1-hex nebula → 0.049 (map term only); enemy in it → 0.299.

**Verification.** Structure + `node --check`; jsdom boot + `launchGame()` until a map with nebulae;
clouds/blobs/hex coverage checked; async phases complete; `renderTac()` ×120 frames with lightning
forced frequent, no errors; double terrain regen discards stale work; viewscreen rule measured;
real frames rendered from the shipped code (old vs new vs mid-flash) via `@napi-rs/canvas`. Not
tested in a real browser — watch battle-start latency on slow machines (phase 0 renders
synchronously; if it stutters, move it async too and draw nothing until ready).

### 0.69 — Docs + prototype session, 2026-09-24 (no game-file change; build still v2.20-S131)

**(1) Combat log #13 (ledger above) — Constitution Mk II vs K-23, Lt. Cmdr, player win.** Tier
identified from the numbers: `Shields 12→24pts` flat every turn; Move 12 at long range, 6 at range ≤6
— the literal `D===3` formula. What happened: the AI lost Tactical Advantage every turn (3 vs 8, then
1 vs 4 move pts) so it moved FIRST each phase; its 24 shield points spread evenly (4/face); in turn 3
it rotated to facing 2 on 1 move point and the player, moving last, parked on its aft-starboard
quarter at range 2 — a K-23 blind arc (its KD-9s cover [0,1,5], [0], [3]; nothing covers arcs 2 or 4)
— and one alpha strike (3× FH-3 + FP-1) took superstructure 16 → 0.
**Why the §0.59 flank fix didn't fire:** it checks weapon coverage only at ALLOCATION time; at range 2
the player was still inside the forward bank's arc, so `covered` was true and move stayed 6. The
failure happened after, when the AI moved first with 1 MP. **New lesson:** coverage-at-allocation is
not enough when the opponent has more movement points and moves last — the AI should anticipate
(e.g. match/exceed opponent's recent move points when close and outmanoeuvred, or reserve turn
capacity to keep a blind quarter covered). Even shields and loitering are Lt. Cmdr's deliberate
simplicity, not bugs; any fix must respect the tier ladder (candidate: apply the anticipation rule at
Captain+ first, a milder version at Lt. Cmdr). **User has not yet approved an AI change** — this is
logged per the new ledger rule.
**Also from the same log (viewscreen feedback):** the user wants the viewscreen nebula star-thinning
to react to the TARGET ENEMY being in a nebula only — not the player's own ship. Map-wide nebula
thinning stays. Pending next build (one-line change in `vsNebulaDim()`). Drift behaved as designed
(start still until power committed; ~52% then ~12% of max from both ships' averaged MP); user fine
with it; offered option: use the faster ship instead of the average.

**(2) Nebula Render Lab (prototype, not in the game):** published artifact
`https://claude.ai/artifact/N6fND9onoPjrus2s5Wty4x` (downloads capability → `nebula_render_config.json`).
Game-accurate pointy-top hex map (same odd-r geometry, `NEB_HUES`), five clouds of 16/10/6/4/3 hexes
with per-cloud density; styles: Current (game, reproduced exactly — per-hex clip + tiled 64px
`nebTex` + radial pulse), Wispy filaments, Billowing cloud, Emission knots, Dark dust, Ionized veil;
controls for edge spread, filament detail, density, glow, gas motion, grid, gameplay-hex outline.
**Technique to reuse in-game:** each connected cloud is ONE shape — a gaussian soft-union (metaball)
field Σexp(−d²/1.15) over its hex centres, perturbed by domain-warped fbm plus a large-scale wobble,
so edges bleed past hex borders without per-hex scallops (plain nearest-centre distance left visible
hex scallops — first render rejected on inspection). Rendered at half resolution into a cache
(~0.9 s for all five clouds here; in-game this happens once per battle at terrain generation), glow
baked once as a blurred additive layer, motion = slow crossfade between two cached noise phases.
Gameplay hexes are unchanged in every style. Awaiting the user's style pick.

### 0.68 — What changed in v2.20-S131 (VIEWSCREEN STARFIELD, game-state driven)

**Origin.** User asked for "a bit of realism" on the viewscreen: stars behind the contact, a few red
or blue, none over 5–7px across. Built first as a standalone proof of concept, then as the
**Viewscreen Starfield Tuner & Exporter** (published artifact
`https://claude.ai/artifact/4DtiLSoaVZRCcPJzwMA6R8`, `downloads` capability for saving
`viewscreen_starfield_config.json`; also copy-as-JS, import/restore, seed box, same-sky vs
new-sky-per-battle, brightness, drift speed, reset). The user explored both extremes, then asked
for it in-game with the MAP and GAME STATE driving it, and set these rules explicitly:
- **Nebulae → fewer visible stars** (many nebulae, or one large one).
- **Movement power → relative drift** (more power into movement by either ship = faster drift;
  both stationary = still).
- **No twinkle** — scintillation needs an atmosphere (user's own mirage analogy).
- **Colour, diameter, brightness do NOT react to game state** — "randomly determined with each
  game," held for the battle. Do not add state-driven brightness/haze without asking.

**Implementation (one new block right above `renderViewscreenInline()`, + 2 one-line hooks).**
- `VS_STARFIELD` config — `perBattle` ranges (starCount 70–140, coloredSharePct 5–14,
  maxDiameterPx 5–7, brightnessPct 85–115), `sizeWeights`, `coloredMinDiameterPx: 2`, `palette`,
  `nebula` weights, `drift` limits. Generator `mulberry32-v1`, identical to the Tuner's, so a Tuner
  export's sizeWeights/palette are drop-in. **All tuning lives in this one object.**
- `vsStarfieldNewBattle()` — called right after `generateTerrain()` in `launchGame()`; rolls a seed
  and the perBattle params, builds the stars, ranks them by prominence (bright×diameter).
- `vsNebulaDim()` → fraction hidden: `mapWeight 0.45 × min(1, Σ nebula-hex density / 20)` +
  `cloudWeight 0.15 × min(1, largest cloud hexes / 10)` + `shipInNebulaWeight 0.25` per ship standing
  in a nebula (scaled by that cloud's density; same endpoint rule as `terrainToHitPenalty`), capped
  at `maxDim 0.8`. Clouds are identified by their shared `terrainStyle` object (generateTerrain
  assigns one style per connected blob). Faintest stars are hidden first; each star fades.
  Measured: clear 0.00 · small thin cloud 0.15 · one big dense cloud 0.60 · + player inside 0.80.
- `vsDriftTargetPct()` → `maxSpeedPct 200 × avg over both ships of min(1, Σ movePts /
  floor(totalPower/moveRatio))`. During `GS.phase==='power'` it HOLDS the previous target (movePts
  are zeroed at end of turn until recommitted — without this the stars stall every turn). Eased,
  and applied as an accumulating offset (speed changes never make stars jump). Parallax: bigger
  stars move faster (`1.2 + d×0.9` px/s at 100%).
- `vsDrawStarfield(g,W,H)` — called right after the black fill in the normal (alive-contact) path of
  `renderViewscreenInline()`, i.e. BEFORE the ship art, so the hull occludes stars. NOT drawn in
  the destroyed/"no signal" path. Stars stay crisp in the no-lock state (only the contact blurs).

**Art fix riding along (flagged, minimal).** The starfield exposed stray opaque extraction debris in
`FRONT_VIEW_ART.Constitution_NCC1700` — two dark blobs pinned to the image's left margin that would
block stars as dark patches. Removed exactly those (279 px, all within x 6–15); hull region
verified pixel-identical. A scan of all 26 viewscreen images flagged other "detached" pixels, but a
visual check showed they are REAL PARTS (V8 Bird of Prey wingtip pods/lower hull, R-1 antenna mast,
running lights on Aviary/Alamo/Federation2/Baker/Chandley) — **do not auto-clean by connectivity**
(see §2.2 lesson below). Nothing else touched.

**Verification.** Structure + `node --check`; jsdom boot + `launchGame()` run twice (per-battle
re-roll confirmed); terrain rewritten live to exercise every nebula case; `movePts` driven to
exercise drift (0% still · 100% one ship full burn · 200% both · held through power phase); zero
runtime errors over ~38k star draws; real frames rendered from the shipped code via
`@napi-rs/canvas` for clear / big-nebula / ship-in-nebula. Not tested in a real browser.

### 3.1 — Admiral-tier AI tuning (playtest observation) — FIXED in v1.58-S69

**Status: implemented and verified — see §0.5 for the fix detail.** Left here, unedited below,
as the original diagnosis/evidence trail; do not delete this history when a future session
revisits Admiral tuning again.

**Source:** user-submitted combat log, `combat_log_2026-09-02-10-50-51.txt` (v1.56-S67) — a
Klingon D-7 M (IX) vs. an Admiral-difficulty USS Constitution Mk II, ending in a clean Klingon
kill. Three concrete weaknesses were traced to actual code, not just inferred from the log:

1. **Admiral's aggression check reads the wrong ship's hull.** `aiAllocatePower()`'s `D===5`
   branch computes `hullPct = p.superstructure/p.superstructureMax` — the *player's* hull, not
   its own (`s.superstructure`). An Admiral-tier AI never adapts its own power split to its own
   damage state; it only ever reacts to how hurt the player is. Confirmed by hand-running the
   formula (`move=6; weapPwr=floor(tot*0.45); shields=tot-move-weapPwr`) against the log's
   shrinking power totals (44→37→34 from engine hits) — it reproduces the log's near-static
   "Move ~6, Weapons ~15-19, Shields ~13-19" split almost exactly, even as the Constitution
   lost its shield generator and three of five weapons over the course of the fight.
2. **Weapon power isn't capped to what's actually armable.** `D===1` (Cadet — the *weakest*
   tier) correctly caps weapon power at `Math.min(tot-move-shields, sum of alive weapons'
   maxPower)`. Admiral (`D===5`) has no equivalent cap — it takes a flat 45% regardless of how
   many weapons survive. By the log's final turns the Constitution had one weapon left, then
   none ("No armed weapons to fire"), while still nominally being allocated ~15 power for
   weapons with nothing to arm — power that a smarter AI would have redirected to shields.
3. **Facing logic optimizes for range, not surviving-weapon arc, at point-blank.** `aiDoMove()`'s
   `tryMove()` turns toward an "optimal range" heading (`targetRange` by difficulty) but never
   separately verifies that heading still keeps its *specific remaining* weapon arcs on target.
   The log shows three consecutive fire phases logging "Target not in arc [F/F-Stbd/F-Port]" /
   "[F]" while both ships sat essentially in the same hex — the Klingon had flanked after the
   forward shield generator died, and the Constitution's movement never corrected for it.

### 3.2 — Surrender / self-destruct design (recovered fragment — still incomplete)

**Status: recovered from the user's memory, not from any prior session's written notes.**
The game code has referenced this design since before v1.54-S65 — the "SHIP EXPLOSIONS" block
(`calculateExplosionDamage`, search for `Phase 1 of 4`) has carried the comment *"See HANDOVER
for the full self-destruct/surrender design — this is Phase 1 of 4"* pointing at a document
that, as of v1.56-S67, contained no such design. This is the same failure mode as the
documentation-gap incident in §0.1: a real design discussion happened in some earlier session
and did not survive into the handover doc. The user was able to recall the following from
memory (2026-09-02); it is captured here in full for the first time. **Treat this as a partial
recovery, not a complete spec** — per-faction behavior for Gorn, Orion, and Independent
factions beyond the one guess below is still unconfirmed, and "Phase 2/3/4" (whatever they
were meant to cover beyond the explosion-damage table) remain unknown.

**Mechanical anchor (confirmed against the actual FASA rule, not just recalled):** the
rulebook's Superstructure Damage Track section states that when the superstructure counter
reaches 0 or below, the ship can no longer fire or move, and *"usually this means that its
captain will surrender unless he feels that he will be able to repair the damage or inflict
more damage on the enemy by self-destructing."* A related rule requires a Science Officer
skill roll to prevent an unintentional explosion if the counter goes negative. This is the
FASA-literal trigger point the surrender/self-destruct decision should hang off of — distinct
from the existing `powerKill` state (engine damage dropping current power to 0), which
currently produces only flavor-text capture narratives, not an actual decision.

**Cross-reference, added after a user question during actual play (2026-09-06):** the user
fought a game where the enemy's power hit zero (hull otherwise intact) and asked directly
whether the resulting "VICTORY — SURRENDER" ending meant the game had some real surrender
mechanic already. It doesn't, and it's worth being precise about the distinction for whoever
picks up this design next: `checkVictory()` already treats `currentPower<=0` as a complete,
separate ending condition from hull destruction, and `buildPowerKillNarrative()` already
writes a full, faction-pair-specific prose paragraph about capture/prisoner treatment when
that happens (six distinct fed/kli/rom-vs-fed/kli/rom variants, already well-written, already
shipped, not a stub). None of that is "surrender" in the sense this section is designing —
it's automatic narrative dressing for a specific *involuntary* ending (the ship went dark),
with no decision on either side. The surrender/self-destruct design above is about a
*voluntary* choice made at the FASA-literal trigger point (superstructure ≤ 0), which is a
different moment, a different condition, and would need its own trigger separate from
`powerKill`. If this design is ever built, it should almost certainly reuse
`buildPowerKillNarrative()`'s prose style and per-faction-pair structure rather than
inventing a second narrative system from scratch — but the trigger conditions and the
presence of an actual choice are what make these two things genuinely different features,
not two names for the same one.

**Per-faction surrender disposition, as recalled:**
- **Klingon — will not surrender, essentially ever.** Fights to destruction rather than yield
  the ship. Signature line, coined by the user in the lost prior session: **"Death First!"** —
  intended to be used somewhere in the surrender-offer/refusal flow for a Klingon captain
  (exact placement — a log line, a UI prompt response, both — not yet decided).
- **Romulan — also will not surrender**, for a different reason than Klingon pride: strongly
  prefers self-destruct specifically to deny their technology (especially the cloaking device)
  to whoever just defeated them. This should probably link into the existing explosion-damage
  table (`calculateExplosionDamage`) as the mechanism, i.e. a Romulan hitting the surrender
  trigger point rolls to self-destruct rather than being offered/accepting surrender at all.
- **Federation — will surrender**, conditioned on the captain weighing crew survival. This is
  the one faction where surrender is a live, sympathetic option rather than a near-never/never
  case — likely the faction where a genuine player-facing surrender choice matters most if this
  is ever built as an interactive decision rather than a dice-driven one.
- **Independent/merchant — not from the recalled discussion; the user's own new guess this
  session**, offered as speculation rather than a settled design: likely to surrender readily,
  leaning cowardly/self-preserving rather than fighting on. Flagged here as *unconfirmed* —
  don't treat it with the same confidence as the three factions above.
- **Gorn — surrenders only on a cold, calculated assessment of zero chance to win.** Not
  reflexive or emotional about it, the opposite temperament from Klingon pride — purely a
  rational read of the odds. Will self-destruct instead, but only as a rare exception: when they
  judge the resulting blast would cripple or take the enemy out along with them. Otherwise
  defaults to surrender once the odds are truly zero.
- **Orion — surrenders by default.** Explicitly pragmatic/mercantile reasoning: better to live
  to see another day, another opportunity for profit. This is the one faction whose baseline
  leans toward surrender rather than fighting to the end.
- **Orion's default is opponent-dependent, though — this took the most detail of any faction.**
  Surrendering only makes sense if the *other side* is actually going to let them live, so the
  calculus flips per enemy:
  - **vs. Klingon → self-destructs instead of surrendering, essentially always.** Reasoning as
    given: an Orion crew being defeated by Klingons knows there's no "another day of profit" on
    the other side of that surrender — Klingons won't take them alive/spare them — so the
    default pragmatic logic (surrender to live) doesn't apply and self-destruct becomes the
    better play.
  - **vs. Romulan → roughly 50/50** between surrender and self-destruct. Genuine uncertainty
    about whether Romulans would actually spare them.
  - **vs. Gorn → roughly 70/30 in favor of self-destruct.** Not because Gorn are known to be
    merciless specifically, but because so little is known about them at all — the Orion crew
    doesn't know what they'd be surrendering *to*, and that uncertainty itself pushes toward
    self-destruction more often than not.
  - (vs. Federation is presumably the "surrenders" default case, matching the general Orion
    disposition, though this wasn't stated explicitly and shouldn't be assumed confirmed.)

**Not yet designed:** how a surrender is actually offered/triggered in play (automatic at the
superstructure-0 threshold vs. a player-initiated action), what "faction responses" beyond
accept/refuse/self-destruct means mechanically (a captured-ship/prize mechanic already exists
narratively via `buildPowerKillNarrative()`'s `fates` text — whether surrender should route
into that same system or be a separate, earlier decision point is unresolved), and whether any
of this is meant to be an interactive prompt to the player or purely narrated/dice-resolved for
both sides symmetric with the AI. Next session picking this up should design the state machine
before writing any code, and should write it down here immediately rather than trusting it'll
survive to the next session by memory alone.

**2026-09-02 addendum — blast damage is dead code, and a real win-logic bug was waiting behind
it.** While mocking up an explosion shockwave visual, checked whether a ship that "wins" by
destroying its opponent could itself then be killed by that opponent's blast damage (per the
rulebook's Damage From Explosions table — same hex 2x/1hex 1x/2hex ½/.../7-10hex flat 1 point,
scaling with the exploding ship's own Total Power Units Available at ranges ≤6 hexes, fixed at
range 10 max regardless of ship size beyond that). Traced `applyExplosionDamage()` and its
helper `calculateExplosionDamage()` (search `calculateExplosionDamage`) — both are fully
implemented and match the book's table, but **`applyExplosionDamage` still has zero call sites
anywhere else in the file, as of v1.58-S69.** It is dead code. No ship currently takes blast
damage from another ship's death, at any range, ever — the mechanic exists on paper only.
**Update, v1.57-S68:** the *win-logic half* of this addendum has since been fixed, independent
of wiring up the blast damage — `checkVictory()` had no branch for both ships hitting
superstructure ≤0 simultaneously and silently declared the player the loser in a true mutual
kill; it now shows "MUTUAL DESTRUCTION" and narrates both sides (see §0.4). This fix did NOT
require `applyExplosionDamage` to be wired up, since mutual destruction can already happen from
ordinary simultaneous combat resolution. `applyExplosionDamage` itself remains untouched, dead
code, and would need its own separate wiring-up pass whenever blast-damage-to-other-ships
becomes a priority — see §3.3 below for how this now relates to the Advanced ruleset tier.

### 3.3 — Ruleset-tier decision + surrender house-rule toggle (2026-09-03, DESIGN ONLY — not
implemented, explicitly deferred by the user for a later coding pass)

Follows directly from a full rulebook verification pass (grepping the actual OCR text, not
relying on memory) done in response to the user asking "is any of this really in the rulebook,
or am I hallucinating." Findings, then decisions.

**What's confirmed real, with exact rulebook grounding:**
- **Surrender is genuinely in the book, but it's one sentence, not a system.** Superstructure
  Damage Track section: *"When the counter gets to 0 or below, the ship is no longer able to
  fire weapons or move. Usually this means that its captain will surrender unless he feels that
  he will be able to repair the damage or inflict more damage on the enemy by self-destructing."*
  No dice roll, no morale check, no negotiation mechanic, no player-initiated hail of any kind.
  Anything resembling an interactive surrender *offer* is entirely custom — there is nothing in
  the source text to extend, only this one narrative default to build on top of.
- **Self-destruct / ship explosions are real and substantial, and live under the Advanced
  Course specifically** (its own intro: *"the section on Firing Weapons tells about Romulan
  plasma bolts and ship explosions"*). The per-faction guidance, quoted exactly since it matters
  for accuracy: self-destruct is *"used to keep a vessel from capture... limited to a ship with
  secret components or information on board that would jeopardize the safety of the
  governmental body."* Then: Romulans self-destruct "except in extreme cases" (rare); Klingon
  self-destruction "might bring dishonor to their family line" (reluctant, not eager); and
  **Federation, Gorn, and Orion "will never destroy their own vessels,"** preferring to "run
  away and live to fight another day." **This directly contradicts the Gorn/Orion disposition
  matrix recorded in §3.2 above** (Gorn calculated self-destruct, Orion's opponent-dependent
  self-destruct matrix) — that matrix is confirmed, deliberate house-rule territory, not a
  reading of an ambiguous rule. Both versions are preserved (see the toggle below), not one
  overwriting the other.
- **The rulebook itself only names two tiers — "Basic Course" and "Advanced Course."** [**Corrected 2026-11-06 (§0.167): this was wrong. The book has FOUR courses: Basic (pp. 6-21), Advanced (pp. 22-33), Graduate (pp. 34-39) and Command & Control (the role-play course), and mentions an Expert Course only in passing; "Intermediate" is still the game's own name for a cut of the Advanced Course.**] There is
  no official "Intermediate Course" heading anywhere in the OCR text. The game's own existing
  `RULESETS` array (`id:'basic'`/`id:'inter'`, search `const RULESETS`) already labels a middle
  tier "INTERMEDIATE" covering sensors phase / sensor locks / cloak detection — this is real
  rulebook content, just content that is technically part of the book's own "Advanced Course"
  (its cloak/sensors section), pulled forward into its own lighter middle tier by whoever built
  this feature. That naming is already shipped and working; nothing about it needs to change.
- **Captain's Skill Rating / Crew Efficiency / Campaign Advancement is real, fully specified,
  and 100% unimplemented in code** (grepped for every term — zero hits). Lives under the
  Advanced Course's "Campaign Rules" section. Captain's Skill Rating: 3d6+45 (range 48–75, avg
  60), used for skill checks and to resolve simultaneous-movement ties. Crew Efficiency Rating:
  3d6+25 (range 28–55, avg 40), checked once per turn before Power Allocation — a percentile
  roll under the rating grants a one-time-per-turn bonus, captain's choice of: +1 to-hit on one
  weapon, +1 power from each working engine, +1 shield power (can exceed max), or 1 point of
  repair. Campaign Advancement: Victory Points = defeated ship's starting Total Power Units
  Available ÷ 10 (rounded down), split captain/crew (book recommends 50/50), added permanently
  to the ratings **after** the scenario ends. Persistence rule, quoted exactly: *"The captain's
  rating is his until he is killed, no matter what ship he commands. The crew's rating is only
  good for the specific ship designated, no matter who commands."* — i.e. the captain's
  progression follows the *person* across commands; the crew's progression is tied to the
  *hull* and is explicitly lost if the crew has to abandon ship.
- **The game currently renders ship explosions for every death regardless of ruleset** — there
  is no gate checking Basic vs. Intermediate vs. (future) Advanced before playing
  `playDestructionSequence()`. Worth deciding whether to leave this as permanent "eye candy for
  everyone" (defensible — it's just a visual, arguably fine even in Basic) or gate it once
  Advanced exists, when this actually gets built.

**Decisions made this session (design only, confirmed by the user, not yet coded):**
1. **Keep "Intermediate" exactly as it is today** — same scope (sensors phase, sensor locks,
   cloak detection), same name, no changes. Do not fold anything below into it.
2. **Add a new "Advanced" tier to the existing `RULESETS` array**, sitting above Intermediate.
   Per the real Advanced Course's own stated relationship to Basic (*"adds to the rules... does
   not replace"*), Advanced here should be additive/inclusive of Intermediate's rules, not a
   parallel alternative to them — Basic ⊂ Intermediate ⊂ Advanced. Advanced houses: the ship-
   explosion mechanic properly gated to this tier (currently ungated, see above), the self-
   destruct rule, and the full Captain's Skill Rating / Crew Efficiency / Victory Points /
   campaign-persistence system described above — "with all the other options available" per the
   user's own phrasing, meaning Advanced is the tier where the complete, unabridged ruleset
   lives, matching how the real Advanced Course is positioned in the actual book.
3. **Surrender gets its own independent toggle, using the existing `HOUSE_RULES` array pattern**
   (search `const HOUSE_RULES`, same shape as the existing `nebula`/`gravwell`/`planets`
   entries: `{id, label, hr, def, desc}`). Two modes, both fully preserved rather than one
   replacing the other:
   - **"By the Book"** — matches the rulebook's actual (thin) text as closely as a game system
     can: no player-initiated offer, resolved automatically/narratively once a ship is disabled
     (superstructure ≤0 or, per §3.2's existing scope question, possibly the `powerKill`
     threshold too — still unresolved, see §3.2's original "not yet designed" list, unchanged
     by this session). Uses the book's own per-faction self-destruct leanings verbatim: Romulan
     rare-exception self-destruct, Klingon reluctant self-destruct (dishonor), Federation/
     Gorn/Orion never self-destruct, defaulting to surrender instead when disabled.
   - **"House Rule"** (the user's own design, from §3.2, unchanged, just now explicitly framed
     as the *alternate* mode rather than the only version) — a one-time, known-to-the-player
     surrender offer ("Wanna give up?"), which the AI resolves by checking its own status and
     faction disposition: Klingon essentially never surrenders ("Death First!"), Romulan
     self-destructs to deny their tech to the victor, Federation surrenders based on a
     crew-survival calculus, Gorn makes a cold, calculated zero-chance-of-victory assessment
     with self-destruct as a rare exception when it would cripple or take out the enemy, and
     Orion surrenders by default but with the opponent-dependent override matrix (vs. Klingon:
     self-destructs almost always, since surrender is pointless; vs. Romulan: roughly 50/50; vs.
     Gorn: roughly 70/30 toward self-destruct, out of not knowing what surrender would even mean
     against an opponent this unknown).
   - **Resolved 2026-09-03: the toggle is independently selectable regardless of ruleset
     tier** — available and functional under Basic, Intermediate, and Advanced alike. Not
     gated behind Advanced. The user was explicit about this: "truly toggleable," the player's
     free choice in any ruleset, not a privilege unlocked by picking Advanced.

**Explicitly not to be coded yet** — this entire subsection is a save-and-analyze pass, per the
user's direct instruction. The trigger-mechanism questions already open in §3.2 (automatic vs.
player-initiated, how it interacts with the existing `powerKill`/capture-narrative system) are
still open and are not resolved by this session's ruleset-tier decision — they still need
answering before either surrender mode is actually implementable as code.

### 3.4 — Character portraits + cross-project RPG import/export (2026-09-03, DESIGN ONLY —
not implemented, not even scoped in detail yet)

Two more additions from the same conversation, both explicitly "for safe keeping" — save and
analyze, not build. Both depend on the Campaign/crew-skill system in §3.3 existing first (there
is no "character" to export, portray, or persist until Captain's Skill Rating / Crew Efficiency
Rating / Victory Points are actually implemented) — treat this as riding on top of §3.3, not a
parallel, independent feature.

**Cross-project character import/export with a separate RPG project.** The user is building a
Star Trek RPG in a different, entirely separate conversation thread — **this session has zero
visibility into that project.** No knowledge of its character data model, file format, tech
stack, or even whether it's also a single-file HTML artifact like this one. The ask: a
character created/leveled in this combat simulator (via the §3.3 Campaign Advancement system —
Captain's Skill Rating, Crew Efficiency Rating, accumulated Victory Points) could be **exported**
from here and **imported** into the RPG, and vice versa. This is a real, reasonable idea, but it
is **not scopeable from this thread alone**. Whoever picks this up will need the user to either
(a) bring the RPG thread's own character-data documentation/schema into this conversation, or
(b) describe the RPG's character fields directly, before any export/import format can be
designed here — guessing at a shared schema without seeing the other side would likely produce
a format that doesn't actually match what the RPG expects. Plain JSON is the obvious starting
guess for a transfer format (human-readable, easy to version, easy to validate) but this is a
default assumption, not a decision — do not treat it as settled.

**Character portraits.** The user has existing portrait art (already in use in the RPG project)
they'd like to reuse here rather than commission/generate anything new. Same dependency as
above: portraits need a character to attach to, which needs §3.3's crew/captain system built
first. Not yet discussed: how portraits would be selected (a fixed roster the player picks
from, procedurally assigned by faction/species, or explicitly tied to the imported-from-RPG
character's own portrait) or the art's format/dimensions/licensing status for reuse across the
two projects. All open.

### 3.5 — Damage Control Designer fixes + hotspot/mobile roadmap discussion (2026-09-11,
MIXED — fixes below are IMPLEMENTED and shipped; everything after "Discussion only" is
DESIGN ONLY, explicitly not built)

Two distinct halves this session: a batch of real fixes to `damage_control_designer1.html`
(the standalone damage-view calibration tool from §0.34 onward), and a long open-ended
design conversation about hotspot-based damage effects, mobile support, and a possible
future "Construction System" tool. Note: this is a different file from the earlier
`damage_control_designer.html` (no "1"), which holds the repair-skill-roll mockup
referenced below — that file was not opened this session.

**Fixed: faction colors reset on every tab switch.** `applyFactionPreset()` was
unconditionally overwriting the 4 color inputs from a hardcoded table on every faction-tab
click, silently discarding any manual tuning for that faction. Added `factionColorState`,
an in-memory per-faction cache — a faction's colors seed from the hardcoded preset only
the first time it's visited, then persist across tab switches. Added a "Reset THIS
faction's colors" button (clears just the current faction); the existing full-reset
button now also clears the whole cache.

**Added: independent box border colors.** Box borders were previously derived from fill
colors or hardcoded, with no separate control. Added "Box border (filled)" / "Box border
(empty)" pickers, wired into `drawBoxTrack()` and, later in the session, the Systems
Repair Status grid too (see below) — every box border in the tool now comes from these
two pickers, never from the shield-arc Charged/Dead colors.

**Added: Label Styling panel.** Per-label position (x/y offset), font size, bold toggle,
and font family (stock fonts + several Google Fonts + real custom font import via the
browser's `FontFace` API, client-side only, nothing uploaded). Implementation note for
future reference: rendering-time style lookups (`getEffectiveStyle`, called every frame)
deliberately do NOT persist a default into storage — only actual edits
(`ensureCustomized`) do. This keeps "only labels you've touched" true in the reset button
and the copyable JS output; an earlier pass of this logic would have silently marked all
~19 labels "customized" within the first rendered frame.

**Added: click-and-drag directly on the canvas.** Following feedback that dropdown+slider
editing was cumbersome, labels can now be grabbed and dragged on the canvas itself, via
`labelHitboxes` (approximate bounding boxes rebuilt every frame) and standard
`mousedown`/`mousemove`/`mouseup` handlers. Mouse-only — no touch handlers exist yet,
which matters directly for the mobile discussion below. Hitboxes are approximate, not
pixel-perfect; if two labels end up very close together the later-drawn one wins a click.

**Fixed: Systems Repair Status grid overlap, plus resizing and border decoupling.** Root
cause of a screenshot showing what looked like far too many boxes in the Sensors row:
boxes were drawn at `cellW*3` width but spaced only `cellW+gap` apart, so the 5
side-by-side Sensors boxes visually overlapped into a smear. Fixed by making box
width/height slider-controlled (new "Status box width/height" sliders, default 50×16px)
and making drawn width always match spacing exactly. Also split the grid into two
independently-movable groups per direct request — Sensors (horizontal, 5 boxes) and
Shield-facing + Engineering (vertical, 7 single-box rows) previously shared one offset.
And: this grid turned out to be the one place still tying box borders straight to the
shield-arc Charged/Dead colors — now fixed to use the independent border pickers like
everywhere else in the tool.

**Discussion only, nothing built below this point.**

**Repair mechanics — verified against the rulebook, not memory.** The Systems Repair
Status / Percent Casualties / Casualty Modifier tracks are real, rulebook-grounded
content confirmed to belong to Intermediate/Advanced play (hence this tool's own
"ADVANCED TIER — PREVIEW ONLY" labeling). The *display* and the actual repair *mechanic*
(officer-per-system assignment, percentile skill roll, retry-at-a-penalty) are two
different things — the mechanic was only ever sketched in the separate, older
`damage_control_designer.html` (no "1"). Per §3.3, the whole Advanced tier this would
live under is confirmed real but 100% unimplemented in the live game, and doesn't yet
exist as a selectable ruleset option at all. Net: flipping on "Advanced" someday would
NOT make any of this functional by itself — it would need (1) Advanced added as a
selectable tier, (2) the actual repair mechanic built from the older mockup's sketch, (3)
this display's placeholder boxes wired to real game state instead of preview sliders.

**Damage visual effects (smoke, sparks, glow) tied to ship location.** Discussed four
options, cheapest to priciest: tie effects to the existing UI status boxes (no per-ship
knowledge needed); generic zones from a sprite's own bounding box (front/aft/sides);
sampling a sprite's alpha channel for particle placement; or a manual hotspot-pinning
tool. Conversation moved toward the pinning tool as the long-term direction, with the
cheaper options as fallback for ships nobody's pinned yet.

**The hotspot-pinning tool, tentatively named "Construction System"** (renamed from
"Construction Manual" — see naming note below). Confirmed as an explicit two-step
pipeline: import artwork, then separately mark where each system lives on that specific
image — never inferred automatically. Should extend the existing designer tool rather
than be standalone, since pins only make sense after a ship's `DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE`
scale/offset/rotation is already locked in. Pins must be stored relative to the artwork
(normalized position within the sprite's own bounding box), never as raw canvas pixels,
or they break the moment the fit is retuned. **Real gap found, verified against the live
game's `dmgSystems` tracking:** impulse, warp port/stbd, life support, and sensors already
have real tracked damage state — pins for those hook into something real. Torpedo
launchers and beam emitters do NOT, despite the rulebook genuinely supporting individual
weapon damage (its own Damage Location Table) — pins for weapons would be built ahead of
a mechanic that doesn't exist in the live game yet. Needs two pin modes: point pins
(click once) and drag-boxes (click-drag a rectangle, for area damage like hull sections).

**Image format guidance for future ship art.** PNG confirmed as the right primary choice
(lossless, real alpha, already what `SHIP_SPRITES` uses); WebP a reasonable secondary;
JPEG/GIF actively discouraged (no/limited transparency, artifacts or palette flattening
work against precise pinning). Multi-angle art (sprite sheets vs. separate files per
angle) is a layout question, not a format one, and would need its own crop-rectangle step
in the tool. Flagged as new territory for the live game too, not just the tool — it
currently only ever renders one fixed view per ship, no rotation-driven art-swapping. And
hotspots never transfer between angles automatically; each image needs its own full
pinning pass.

**Lit/animated effects (nav lights, engine glow, bussard collectors).** Each pin would
need an effect type (static glow / blinking / spinning), a link to a real damage
variable, and a still-open design question — binary vs. gradient damage-to-effect mapping
— explicitly deferred rather than guessed at. Symmetry mirroring should be an opt-in
checkbox, OFF by default (corrected mid-discussion: many Fed ships are single-nacelle,
many alien designs have none at all). Layering (front/behind hull) and spin direction
should be per-pin, designer-set choices, set visually rather than inferred. Fleet
rendering performance flagged as a live-game tactical-view concern specifically (the
designer tool only ever shows one ship, so it's cheap there) — proposed direction is full
animation for the player's own/selected ship, simplified/static for others on the board,
if a multi-ship battle with several animated effects ever proves to be a real cost.

**Mobile feasibility for the player-facing game**, prompted by the user testing the live
game on a phone and finding it functional but not designed for touch. Tech stack itself
(HTML/CSS/JS/Canvas) isn't a blocker. Concrete gaps identified: layout assumes
desktop-width side-by-side panels (this session's tool is a live example of the pattern);
**the drag-and-drop built this session is mouse-only and will not fire at all on
touch** — would need parallel `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend` handlers; tap targets
need to be larger than mouse-click targets (~44×44 CSS px guideline); several labels
already sit at 8–11px, worse on a smaller closer-held screen; canvas DPI/orientation need
real handling, not just scaling down; multi-MB embedded base64 art is heavier on mobile
data; animation cost ties back to the fleet-rendering concern above. Important scoping
split: designer/authoring tools can stay desktop-only forever since players never touch
them — only the player-facing tactical game needs mobile work. Proposed phased path (none
started): (1) baseline touch/tap-target hygiene, (2) responsive layout pass, (3) a real
mobile-first HUD redesign, (4) PWA packaging, (5) native wrapper only if app-store
presence specifically matters. Open, not-yet-acted-on offer: review the live game's
actual file directly for concrete mobile-breakage points, rather than reasoning about it
from memory.

**Scoping philosophy**, agreed across all of the above: hotspots and effects only get
built for ships where a player has actually invested in good art — no procedural
fallback needed, and ships without that investment just keep using plain art (or the
cheap generic-zone effects). Nobody is blocked waiting for every ship in the roster to be
manually pinned before anyone sees a single spark.

**Preview control wishlist** for a future hotspot/effects tool, not yet built: per-hotspot
individual damage toggle (not just aggregate counts), continuous 0–100% severity range
per system, animation speed/scrub/freeze control, quick-jump presets (pristine / moderate
/ critical / derelict), and a global "all effects off" baseline toggle.

**Community/construction-manual angle — changes a real design requirement, not just
flavor.** If players eventually add their own ship art and hotspots, the current
`DMG_IMG_OVERRIDE`-style pattern (copy a JS snippet, paste into one shared game file by
hand) doesn't scale to multiple contributors editing one shared object. Implication for
later design: per-ship hotspot data should likely live in its own small standalone file
per ship, loaded independently by the game, rather than one big shared table — worth
designing for from the start.

**Naming: "Construction Manual" → "Construction System."** Checked, not just a vibe:
"Ship Construction Manual" is the actual title of a specific FASA sourcebook, referenced
by name repeatedly in the rulebook OCR and in this project's own house-rule notes
("Recognition Manuals win over the Construction Manual" — see §4, Source materials &
environment, below).
Reusing that exact name for an in-house tool would create real confusion between the book
and the tool. Landed on "Construction System." Other names left on the table if wanted
later: Ship Builder, Fleet Yard / Shipyard, Hull Designer.

**Suggested next steps, whenever picked back up** (no priority order implied — this
wasn't decided): prototype the point-pin/drag-box hotspot mode as an extension of
`damage_control_designer1.html`; or do the "what breaks first on a phone" pass against
the actual live game file; or pin down the binary-vs-gradient damage-to-effect mapping
question before building anything that depends on it.

### §0.209 v2.111-S222 (from combat log 2026-11-18-22-26-40, Constitution vs Devisor)
- **Run fix:** `scnAiFlee` stores one escape point (`s._runGoal`, prefers nearer edges); `csCanRun` now requires the ship can reach an edge with its available move points.
- **Narrative:** `csPrePara()` (via `endLead` wrapper) describes the run and `csG().firedOnRun` (player shots at a running enemy). Federation player firing on a runner gets a "not very Starfleet" line; holding fire is praised.
- **Option:** new Intermediate house rule `command` "Surrender & Self-Destruct" (off by default, `noAll`). `commandOn()` gates `csCanYield`/`csCanBoom`/`csDemand`/COMMAND button. Run stays tied to Warp Out. Scenarios keep only run.
- **Cut scene:** `playWarpOutScene(ship,who,done)` for any successful warp-out (AI/player/scenario), skippable (Esc), generated whoosh audio; `scnFieldExit` shows result after it.
- Tests: pt16 (scene, narrative, option off hides COMMAND), pt17 (goal persists, ship reaches edge), pt2 regression clean.

### §0.210 v2.112-S223 (owner: clean Federation registry data and baked-in art; name/designation pop-up and display change)
- **Names:** `launchGame()` now wraps `launchGame0()`. For a Federation player (not in a scenario) `fedNameDialog` asks for ship name + designation (optional; RANDOM / SKIP; Enter confirms, Esc skips; last entry remembered in `customState.fedNames`). `applyFedNames(ps,es)` runs after `mkShip`: player gets the typed name ("USS " added if missing) or "Starfleet <Class>-class" and an empty reg; an AI Federation ship gets a made-up name from `FED_NAME_POOL` and a random NCC number. **SHIP_REGISTRY is untouched** (Recognition Database still shows FASA names). Test flag `customState.skipNamePrompt` bypasses the dialog.
- **Display:** `regTxt(s)` guards every reg display (power tab sub-line, shield centre, sidebar id, class line); ship pickers show the class only for Federation hulls (`shipOptionHTML`); matchup notes use `shipLabel(key)`.
- **Art:** lettering inpainted out (OpenCV) of map sprites Andor, Baker, ChandleyClass, Constitution (shared with the Enterprise record), Enterprise, Larson, Loknar, Northampton, Reliant, Remora; front views Larson, Loknar, Gagarin; damage views Constitution_NCC1700, Excelsior. Baker and Enterprise show a slight smudge where the text was. Not touched: Federation1/2, Gagarin and Excelsior map sprites, Constitution_NCC1700 sprite (no readable text), other front views.
- Scenario (Big Bad Wolf) keeps USS Hood / its own names. Source for the block: `/home/claude/cs/names.js`.

### §0.212b — Select-for-battle audit (2026-11-19)
Real-click audit of the Recognition Database (`audit_b5.js`): 21 of 96 playable variant buttons did nothing because `VARIANT_KEY_MAP` lacked their ships. Added: fed_Chandley (Mk I, Mk III -> Chandley_MkII, Mk IV -> Chandley_MkIII), fed_Excelsior, fed_Baker, fed_Andor ('Mk II'), kli_L24 ('A'), kli_K22 ('Standard' -> K22BirdOfPrey), rom_WingedDefender (V30WingedDefender_Type1/2), rom_Stormbird (Type1/2/5), rom_Nova ('Type 1' -> Nova_Type2), gor_BH2/MA12/SS3 and ori_Lightning/Wanderer ('Standard'). Result: 96/96 buttons select the right ship, no duplicate targets. No database button for Gagarin_MkI (no catalog entry, D4) or K22_B. Same build number v2.114-S225 (delivered file replaced). Regression pt2b and pt32 clean.

### §0.213 — v2.115-S226: four fixes from the 2026-11-20 combat log (K-22 B vs Gorn MA-12, Captain, mutual destruction)
1. **Cloak upkeep.** In `applyDamage`'s engine branch, if a cloaked ship's `currentPower` falls below its `cloakCost` the cloak drops at once (decloak effect, a log line 'the cloaking device fails', a damage-log line, Power tab refresh). Applies to either side; it does not wait for the next power phase.
2. **Blast narrative.** `applyExplosionDamage` tracks `target._blastAbsorbed`; `GS.blastKill.shieldHeld` (both creation sites) selects between 'the shields flared and fell' and 'There was no shield up on that facing...'.
3. **Enemy picker by faction.** New `#enemy-factions` buttons (`efb-*`), `chooseEnemyFaction`, called from `populateShipSelectors` and `scnApplyShips`. The player's own faction is dimmed and disabled (the existing rule that you cannot fight your own faction is kept).
4. **Mutual-destruction order.** `ssLose` stamps `ship._deathSeq` (`GS._deathCtr`); the `checkVictory` mutual branch plays the first-dead ship's `playDestructionSequence` first.
Tests: pt40 and pt41 (new), pt2b regression, B5 audit still 98/98. Backup before the fixes: `game_v2114b.bak`.

### §0.214 — v2.116-S227 (2026-11-20): evasion, cloaked ping, 3-D keys, log header, Mutara cut-scene proof of concept
1. **AI dodge (`aiEvadeChoice`, Captain and up).** Old test: hull damage saved > shots given up + 2. A 30% dodge saves about 1 point of a 10-damage torpedo, so it never passed. New: gain = pHit x 0.3 x ((hull pen now - hull pen after) + 0.4 x (shield points spared)); dodge if gain >= fixed + share x expected damage of declared fire (Captain 0.6 / 0.5, Admiral 0.45 / 0.4, Legend 0.35 / 0.3). Holding fire means it dodges; three beams declared means it keeps shooting. Lt Cmdr (weak facing shield) and Ensign (1 in 4) unchanged; the 1-hull guard stays. Test pt44.
2. **Cloaked AI sensors.** `aiDoSensors` no longer calls `addScanFX` while `en.cloaked` (both the no-lock ping and the cloak-hunt sweep). Test pt45.
3. **Keys.** The Orion -1 degree tilt on Commit and Proceed is gone. Raised bevel (inset highlights, 6 px drop) for `#commit-btn`, `#proceed-btn`, `#revise-btn`; `:active` and a `.pressed` class (set by a capturing `pointerdown` listener for 240 ms) sink the key 5 px with an inset shadow. The faction rules (Klingon cut corners, Gorn pill, Romulan border, TMP glow) keep their shapes; their overrides sit AFTER the faction lines, because those lines set `box-shadow:none`. Test pt42 and pt43 (screenshots).
4. **Log header.** `combatLogText()` adds `Rules:` (ruleset, AI tier, scenario) and `Options ON:` / `Options OFF:` from `HOUSE_RULES`; Asteroid Fields is read from `customState` (it is not in `GS.rules`).
5. **Surrender, checked, not changed:** the Stormbird kept one of four RB-10 banks, 13 of 21 hull; `csAssess` hull trigger needs <= 25% for Captain, odds needs ratio <= 0.25. Open observation: with one bank left it allocated Weapons 2 and held fire for two turns (not investigated).
6. **Mutara Approach**, a separate tool (not in the game): https://claude.ai/artifact/TJ6v8Z6ABmpgwA2Hjxa63X, source in `/home/claude/cine/mutara_src.html` plus `imgs.json` (the game's Enterprise and Reliant top-down and front art). Four scenes (the pursuit, the Reliant viewscreen, into the nebula with half power meters and lightning, the hail) and an end card with the scenario rules. Dialogue is ORIGINAL, written on the film's story beats; the screenplay's lines are not reproduced. All lines sit in one `SCENES` table. Sound is generated placeholders behind a Sound button.
Regression: pt40, pt41, pt2b, pt32 and the B5 audit (98/98) clean.

### §0.214b — Mutara Approach v2 (2026-11-20, owner feedback)
Owner wanted two scenes in one cut: the Reliant's surprise attack with the Enterprise damaged, the Enterprise's return fire driving the Reliant off, fade out; then the Enterprise running for the nebula past a moon and the station; real sounds; no transparency gaps in the Reliant art; no generated bridge sound. Built in the same artifact (https://claude.ai/artifact/TJ6v8Z6ABmpgwA2Hjxa63X, version 2; file `/home/claude/Mutara_Approach_v2.html`). Scenes: Title, 1 Ambush (42 s, one cut with four shots: calm approach, the Reliant on the viewscreen charging, the Reliant's phasers and torpedoes hitting the Enterprise with shake, smoke, hull meters and red alert, the Enterprise's return fire, the Reliant turning and running), 2 The Run (36 s: the game's Moon_2 sprite and the Alamo outpost sprite passing, a damaged Enterprise trailing smoke, nebula glow growing, dialogue with an outpost voice), 3 Into the Mutara, 4 The Hail (both unchanged apart from the art fix). Art fix: near-black connected regions of 90 px or more in the front-view PNGs (Reliant and Enterprise) were made transparent (scipy label), so the arch and strut gaps show space. Sound: ONLY the game's own recordings at the game's own levels (`UI_SFX_GAIN`): `fed_phaser` .20, `fed_torp_fire` .55, `ship_explosion` .40 (used x.6 to x1 for hits, since the game's hit sound is generated), `fed_commit` and `fed_proceed` as console chirps, and the `BR_ENT_B64` Motion Picture bridge bed looped at .218 with a 3 s fade in (as `BRIDGE_BEDS.fed_tmp`). No generated sound. MP3 onsets are trimmed as in the game. Sound starts from the 'Play with sound' button (browsers need a click). Sound cues sit in `SCENES[].sfx`. Dialogue is still original.

### §0.214d — Mutara Approach cut scene FINAL (2026-11-20, owner; not in the game, kept as a file for the future expert-rules Mutara scenario)
Delivered as `StarTrek_Mutara_Approach_Cutscene.html` (artifact version 6). Scenes: Title, 1 Ambush (97 s), 2 The Run (72 s), 3 Into the Mutara, 4 The Hail. Owner-directed story: the Reliant approaches the Enterprise's PORT side and fires from its own port side at her aft (two phasers, then ONE torpedo, nothing more); Khan gloats and demands Genesis; Kirk stalls and the prefix code drops the Reliant's shields; the Enterprise answers with three short phaser bursts, no torpedo; the Reliant arcs away. The chase passes the moon and Regula One (the game's R-1 art); Khan: "Explain it to them." (one torpedo passes very close to the saucer); Kirk's rematch taunt; Khan orders full impulse. Reliant drawn at 1.138x the Enterprise's sprite width so the two saucers are the same diameter (measured: 0.402 vs 0.458 of sprite width). Dialogue follows the owner's two script excerpts, trimmed. Sound: only the game's recordings and the TMP bridge bed. Kirk is an Admiral throughout; the hail scene now repeats the chase's rematch and may be cut. Working source: /home/claude/cine/mutara2.html (session scratch; the delivered file is the copy to keep).


### §0.215 — v2.117-S228 (2026-11-21): the queued fixes, built together
From the logs 11-21 13-29-42 (Winged Defender vs BH-2) and 11-21 15-20-58 (Great Bird vs MA-12).
- **Double explosion (owner saw it twice; he was right).** Causes: (1) a torpedo that lands after its target is already dead ran `impactFX` with empty `fxInfo`, drawing a second fireball and sound (log line "HIT — but the fight is already decided"); (2) generated `snd('explosion')` calls in `resolveShipExplosions` and the `applyDamage` superstructure branch stacked on the recorded `ship_explosion`. Fix: `fxInfo.dead=true` at both early returns (AI path, player path), `impactFX` returns at once when `info.dead`, the generated sound is removed from `resolveShipExplosions` and skipped on the kill blow. Test `pt43.js`.
- **A29** Gorn hail lines (the set approved by the owner, wishlist A29 text) in `CS_WHY.gor` and `CS_FRAME.gor`.
- **A31** Damage Control: `dmgSpawnMap()` samples the art's alpha once per ship and every spark/smoke point is snapped to an opaque pixel (centre of the art is the minimum); procedural hulls keep the old spots. `DMG_AXIS_FIX` straightens the Gorn top-down art (SS3 -2.8, MA12 -5.0, BH2 -2.1 degrees, measured by spine and principal axis). Test `pt42.js` and screenshot.
- **A32** New log kinds `lg-bad` (red), `lg-good` (green), `lg-miss` (yellow) with a left bar and bold for red/green (not colour alone). Used on both fire-roll lines (hit by the enemy red, player hit green, any miss yellow), cloak detections (player detects enemy green, failed scan yellow, enemy detects the player red). Export text stays plain.
- **A33** `evPlayback` no longer auto-closes one second after the result; it waits for Continue / Space / Enter.
- **A34** `csRunRefuse()` and `CS_REFUSE`: the run hail now has LET HER GO and a faction-voiced refusal (Starfleet stay on her, Klingon hunt her down, Romulan, Gorn, Orion). Cosmetic for now: it logs the choice, records `csG().refusedRun` and carries on; no pursuit mechanic.
- **Not built:** A30 (3-D panels); the unapproved idea that an AI ship with no weapon able to bear should yield or turn.
- Tests: pt2b, pt32, pt40, pt41, audit_b5 (98/98), pt42, pt43 clean.

### §0.217 — v2.119-S230 (2026-11-22): the wishlist 'easy wins' build
Owner approved all of them and answered the open questions: D2 all tiers; D3 one field; C11 pulse + flash; A17 full book.
- **Cascade kills** (`noteCascadeKill`, `GS._lastShot`): a kill through a dead-generator cascade or a weapon cascade now sets `GS.killBlow` (`cascade:'shield'|'weapons'`); `buildKillNarrative` adds a clause for each. Fixes the stock 'lost in the chaos' ending seen in log row 40.
- **Log**: both fire paths say 'X shield is at 0 points (nothing to absorb) — full N penetrates' when a live generator had no points; a location roll of shieldGen adds a note (and says if the generator was already dead and cascades); the allocation line adds 'Shields by facing: Fwd 4 · F-Stbd 2 ...' (DEAD for a destroyed generator).
- **Debrief**: Ship Explosions roll (`GS.explLog`, written by `resolveShipExplosions`), and 'You refused to let a retreating ship go' (A34).
- **D2**: `aiAllocatePower` trims weapons, then shields, then movement so the total never exceeds current power (all six tiers tested at power 12).
- **D3**: the Recognition Manual printed 'Class undefined' for 11 variants that have no class in the data (Romulan Nestar/Aviary types, Orion, Gorn); it now omits the class text (CATALOG untouched). The K-22 itself already carried class V since v2.114.
- **C11**: Damage Control gauge columns (Power and Sensors): CRITICAL breathes, OFFLINE flashes and blinks the word, boxes just lost flash for 1.1 s (`_dmgGaugeMem`); `prefers-reduced-motion` gets a steady red outline instead.
- **A17**: `GS._aiSensPending`, `flushAiSensors()`: when the AI holds the Tactical Advantage its sensor roll waits until the player ends the Sensors Phase (the player-wins case is as before). Fire: with Evasive Maneuvers off and the AI holding the advantage its fire decision (`ensureAiFireDecided`) waits until the player acts; with Evasive Maneuvers on the existing declare-last flow (v2.92) is unchanged. NOTE: there is no declaration step with Evasive Maneuvers off, so this ordering is not visible to the player; it matters only if the AI ever reacts to the player's shots.
- A6 (blast damage) is built (v2.99-S210): wishlist entry closed.
- Tests: pt46 (cascade kill, D2 cap, gauges), pt47 (four full scripted turns with the AI holding the advantage), pt2b, pt32, pt40-pt45, audit_b5.

- **Faction UI labels**: `PA_TX` is now one standard set (`PA_TX_STD`: Power Allocation / Weapons / Deflector Shields / Motion / Shields) for every skin; the Orion scope dial labels are MOTION / SHIELDS / WEAPONS. - **v2.120-S231b**: `playMapWarpAway` skipped itself when `#tac-wrap` had no usable size (narrow/squeezed layout: 0 px wide at 420 px) and ended instantly. Now it falls back to `playWarpOutScene` in that case, wraps the frame in try/catch and has a safety timer. Test pt50 (hail Accept at 420/800/1100/1500 px).
